output.summary: Reviewed trigger persistence, eligibility, merge checks and delivery. Reproduced a dropped-trigger defect. The land-store test passes; conflict-round tests cannot initialize because installed Zod lacks .overwrite, used by unchanged code.

findings.title: Stale cached observations permanently discard valid conflict triggers
findings.detail: Whenever githubPrData exists, `seen` ignores the supplied current observation. An older cached head therefore causes a valid trigger to be permanently marked skipped with `PR head moved`. The queue and startup consumers also use cached snapshots without refreshing them. Reproduction command: `bun -e 'import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const repo=s.upsertRepo({slug:"test/repo",kind:"github",url:null,localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); const url="https://github.com/test/repo/pull/1"; const old="a".repeat(40), head="b".repeat(40); const owner=s.createRun(repo,{repo:repo.slug,prompt:"Feature"}); s.updateRun(owner.id,{status:"succeeded",branch:"limitless/feature",baseBranch:"main",baseSha:old,prUrl:url}); s.saveGithubPr({url,repo:repo.slug,runId:owner.id,nodeId:null,data:JSON.stringify({state:"OPEN",isDraft:false,headRefOid:old}),delivered:1},false,[],1000); s.recordConflictTrigger(url,head,"land",2000); const trigger=s.pendingConflictTriggers()[0]; const run=s.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id,{state:"OPEN",isDraft:false,headRefOid:head},2000); console.log(JSON.stringify(s.db.query("SELECT state,reason FROM conflict_triggers").all())); assert.ok(run,"fresh OPEN head should start the conflict round"); s.close();'`. Output: `[{"state":"skipped","reason":"PR head moved"}]`, followed by `AssertionError: fresh OPEN head should start the conflict round`.
findings.suggestion: Use the current validated observation with the existing observation-version safeguards. Refresh cached observations when consuming pending triggers, and preserve pending state when freshness cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A. A review round pushes head B, which is approved for landing before the next poll. Landing B conflicts with the base and records a trigger for B. The cached snapshot still names A, so the trigger is permanently skipped and no conflict round starts.

output.summary: Found two reproducible defects in trigger handling and comment delivery. Isolated checks failed as described below. The targeted conflict-round suite could not run because the installed Zod lacks .overwrite(), used by existing schema code. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Do not permanently discard land triggers using stale snapshots
findings.detail: Any cached snapshot bypasses the live lookup, even when its head predates the landing approval. startConflictTrigger then permanently marks the valid trigger skipped as 'PR head moved'. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-stale-conflict-trigger.ts"` produced `{"lookups":0,"rounds":0,"triggers":[{"state":"skipped","reason":"PR head moved"}]}` and `AssertionError: 0 !== 1`.
findings.suggestion: Refresh stale observations before consuming land triggers, and leave triggers pending when current eligibility cannot be confirmed. Ensure startConflictTrigger does not replace a fresh observation with older cached data.
findings.failure_scenario: The poll cache records H1, a review round pushes H2, and an approval at H2 reaches a landing conflict before the cache refreshes. The H2 trigger is discarded against H1. With polling disabled, the conflict remains unresolved indefinitely.

findings.title: Recheck the comment marker inside the retry
findings.detail: The supplied gh wrapper retries transient failures, but the marker lookup occurs outside that retry. If GitHub creates the comment and its acknowledgement is lost, the retry posts an identical comment. An isolated execution of the production delivery function with fake boundaries, `bun "$TMPDIR/review-conflict-comment-retry.ts"`, produced `{"comments":2,"identical":true}` and `AssertionError: 2 !== 1`.
findings.suggestion: Put marker reconciliation and comment creation inside one bounded retry operation, using the raw runner so each retry checks whether the preceding attempt already posted.
findings.failure_scenario: The first comment POST succeeds remotely but returns a retryable timeout or HTTP 502. Delivery retries the POST without rereading comments, producing duplicate resolution summaries.

output.summary: Found a reproducible local retry regression and two incomplete executor integrations. Targeted suites, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies. Focused probes ran successfully and exposed the reported failures; diff whitespace checks passed.

findings.title: Restore local retry prerequisites after restart
findings.detail: On resume, oneRound calls checkoutCommitted, removing ignored dependencies and build output. Returning the cached initial result here skips setup, while the pending regression retry's stored request has setup: []. The retry therefore fails because its prerequisites disappeared. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-executor-probe.ts". Output: `uninterrupted local retry: pass`, followed by `resumed local retry: {"ok":false,"output":""}` and `AssertionError: resumed retry should retain/recreate its setup prerequisites`.
findings.suggestion: Make local retry resume restore the setup and build prerequisites that cleanup removes. Add a restart test using real setup artifacts and dependent checks.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup installs node_modules, a check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts after persisting the regression-retry handle. Resume deletes node_modules, skips the completed initial execution, and reruns only the check without reinstalling dependencies.

findings.title: Persist landing execution handles before attaching
findings.detail: Landing calls executeGate without either a stored handle or a persistence callback. Its handle is consequently discarded by the default no-op callback, violating the required durable start/attach contract. After restart, the queue starts another execution instead of attaching to the existing one.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing handle before attach, restore it when resuming the same landing attempt, and clear it after consuming the result.
findings.failure_scenario: A landing execution starts and the daemon restarts before its result is recorded. The resumed checking entry calls start again because no execution handle was saved.

findings.title: Consume execution events through the shared executor path
findings.detail: executeGate awaits only execution.result and never reads execution.events. Local hooks happen to work through a separate closure, but injected executors cannot deliver check events to pipeline events or landing logs. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-executor-events.ts". Output: `{"streamed":0,"reported":0}` and `AssertionError: executor check events should reach gate hooks` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.suggestion: Consume events alongside the result, route check and status events to the caller, and avoid duplicating local notifications.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits a completed check through events and returns a passing GateRun. The stage succeeds, but no gate notification or landing log entry is produced.

output.summary: Found a reproduced retry-resume regression and missing landing-handle durability. No repository files changed. Most targeted suites were blocked by incompatible Zod or missing dependencies; 21 gate-slot tests passed. Lint and typecheck were blocked by missing Biome and Bun types.

findings.title: Restore setup prerequisites before replaying a local retry
findings.detail: On restart during a regression retry, the gates stage calls checkoutCommitted(), which deletes dependencies and generated files. This cached-result return then skips the initial execution, including setup, while the persisted retry request has setup: []. The resumed retry therefore runs without its prerequisites. A temporary reproduction using the production helpers, run with `bun "$TMPDIR/gate-executor-resume-repro.ts"`, printed `uninterrupted retry ok: true` and `resumed retry ok: false`, then failed with `error: resumed retry fails because setup output was cleaned`.
findings.suggestion: Restore the setup and prerequisite execution environment when replaying local retries after restart. Add a restart test with real setup output and a check that depends on it.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup installs dependencies or creates build output; an initial check fails transiently; the daemon restarts after persisting the regression-retry handle. Resume cleans the worktree, skips cached setup, and incorrectly reports another gate failure.

findings.title: Persist and reattach landing execution handles
findings.detail: The landing caller supplies neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback to executeGate(), so its handle is discarded through the default no-op callback. Restarting a checking entry consequently calls start() again instead of attach(). This leaves the landing path outside the requested durable executor contract.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle before attaching, restore it when resuming the same checked commit, and clear it after consuming the result. Test a restart between start and result.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an injected executor is running landing checks. The resumed queue has no execution handle and starts duplicate work instead of attaching to the existing execution.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and sandbox entry points and reproduced the Cargo credential allowance in generated policy. Targeted tests recorded 11 passes; remaining checks were blocked by sandbox restrictions or unavailable dependencies. Real Seatbelt probes could not run inside this sandbox.

findings.title: Gate allowlist leaves Cargo registry credentials readable
findings.detail: Allowing the entire Cargo home reopens reads of `$CARGO_HOME/credentials` and `$CARGO_HOME/credentials.toml`, which store registry tokens. Neither file appears in the credential denies. A temporary-home probe produced a home-wide deny followed by `(allow file-read* (subpath "…/home/.cargo"))` with no credential exception. Candidate tests or dependency scripts can therefore still read and exfiltrate these tokens, contrary to the requirement that credential stores remain outside the gate allowlist.
findings.suggestion: Limit Cargo allowances to the toolchain and cache paths gates actually need, excluding both credential files. Add temporary credential stand-ins to the policy tests and real gate read probes.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner has run `cargo login`, creating ~/.cargo/credentials.toml. An untrusted gate command reads that absolute path and sends its registry token over the unrestricted network.

output.summary: Found a reproducible Codex editor launch regression. Sandbox tests passed with temporary HOME (15 passed, 9 skipped). Real Seatbelt probes were unavailable inside this sandbox; other targeted suites were blocked by incompatible Zod and missing MCP dependencies. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Credential files make every Codex editor probe inconclusive
findings.detail: Preserving the editor's denyRead list feeds regular files such as .netrc and .npmrc into canaryRoots. It returns writable files as canary locations, and sandboxProbe then calls mkdtemp inside them, raising ENOTDIR before any sandbox command runs. The catch converts this into 'probe inconclusive', preventing editor launch. A temporary-home verify reproduction returned {"ok":false,"reason":"probe inconclusive","sandboxCalls":0}. Exact minimal command: `bun -e 'import {canaryRoots} from "./src/harness/codex.ts"; import * as fs from "node:fs"; import {tmpdir} from "node:os"; const h=fs.mkdtempSync(tmpdir()+"/netrc-"); try { const f=h+"/.netrc"; fs.writeFileSync(f,"fixture"); for(const p of canaryRoots([h,f],{tmp:h,tmpdir:h,home:h})) fs.mkdtempSync(p+"/canary-"); } finally { fs.rmSync(h,{recursive:true,force:true}); }'`. Output: `ENOTDIR: not a directory, mkdtemp '…/.netrc/canary-…'` (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Restrict canary creation locations to directories. Verify denied regular files through the existing read probes, and add a regression test that runs CodexReaderProbe with a stand-in .netrc.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's home contains a writable .netrc or .npmrc, or sandbox.deny_read names another writable regular file. Every uncached Codex editor confinement probe fails before launch.

output.summary: Found two durability gaps in the executor seam. A focused probe confirmed retry resume starts replacement work. Targeted suites could not load because dependencies are missing or incompatible; lint lacked Biome, and typecheck lacked Bun types.

findings.title: Resume persisted retry executions instead of replacing them
findings.detail: The purpose whitelist excludes baseline, regression and timeout retries. Their saved handles are discarded, and the engine restarts the initial execution before dispatching another retry. This violates the required attach-without-start behavior; the new tests explicitly expect replacement work. Reproducer command: bun -e 'import {mock} from "bun:test"; import {resolve} from "node:path"; mock.module(resolve("src/git/repos.ts"),()=>({headSha:async()=>"h"})); const {runGateExecution}=await import("./src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts"); let starts=0; const attached=[]; const ctx={state:{round:0,gateExecution:{stage:"gates",round:0,purpose:"regression-retry",sha:"h",handle:{kind:"lan",id:"old",startedAt:1}}},deps:{gateExecutor:{kind:"lan",async start(){starts++;return {kind:"lan",id:"new",startedAt:2}},attach(h){attached.push(h.id);return {events:[],result:Promise.resolve({setupOk:true,setup:[],checks:[]}),async cancel(){}}}}},repo:{slug:"r"},run:{},signal:new AbortController().signal,checkCancelled(){},async save(){}}; await runGateExecution(ctx,"gates","regression-retry",".",{checks:[]}); console.log(JSON.stringify({starts,attached})); if(starts)throw Error("Expected attach without start");'. Output: {"starts":1,"attached":["new"]}, followed by 'error: Expected attach without start' (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Persist the retry phase and preceding results so resume can attach to the pending retry and preserve first-attempt evidence. Keep setup replay specific to local execution.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a retry has a persisted handle. Resume discards that handle and starts replacement work rather than observing the existing execution.

findings.title: Persist landing-check execution handles
findings.detail: Landing calls executeGate without a stored handle or persistence callback. Its default persistence callback does nothing, so attach and result consumption begin without any durable execution identity. Unlike pipeline gates, landing checks cannot reattach after restart.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the landing execution handle with the entry and checked SHA before attaching, then reuse it on resume and clear it after recording the result.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after landing starts a gate execution but before pushedSha is recorded. The resumed queue starts another execution because the original handle was never saved.

output.summary: Found three gaps in execution durability. Dependency-light probes confirmed duplicate starts on resume. Targeted tests could not load because installed dependencies lack Zod .overwrite() and an MCP SDK module. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Resume saved retry executions instead of discarding their handles
findings.detail: The purpose whitelist excludes baseline-retry, regression-retry and timeout executions. On restart, their persisted handles are discarded and new work starts; cancelGateExecution cannot cancel an execution absent from the process-local map. Running `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-executor.ts"` with saved handles produced `{"purpose":"regression-retry","calls":["start(new)","attach(new)"]}`, with identical behavior for baseline-retry and timeout. The new tests explicitly assert this behavior, contrary to the requested reattachment contract.
findings.suggestion: Persist the attempt context and preceding results needed to resume each retry, then attach its saved handle. Keep rerunning local work inside the local executor's attach implementation.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after a retry handle is saved while the executor still owns that retry. Resume starts another execution and loses the original execution's identity.

findings.title: Persist landing execution handles before awaiting checks
findings.detail: Landing calls executeGate without its stored-handle and persistence arguments, so the default persistence callback does nothing. Unlike pipeline gates, landing checks never record their execution identity and cannot reattach after restart. This leaves one explicitly required daemon gate path outside the durability implementation.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the landing execution handle against the landing attempt and checked SHA, and supply it on resume.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while landing checks are running. The recovered checking entry calls start again because no execution handle was saved.

findings.title: Checkpoint the result before clearing its execution handle
findings.detail: The gate-result checkpoint removes the handle before returning the GateRun to the caller, which has not yet persisted the baseline or stage result. A crash in this window loses both result and identity. The probe command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-executor.ts"` reported `durable state after result: {"round":0}` followed by `result-checkpoint restart: ["start(0)","attach(0)","start(2)","attach(2)"]`.
findings.suggestion: Retain the handle until the caller durably consumes the result, or atomically store the result and attempt context when clearing it.
findings.failure_scenario: An initial execution completes and gate-result is saved, then the daemon crashes before the caller records its result. Resume starts a duplicate execution instead of recovering the completed one.

findings.title: Backfilled merge metadata never reaches the merge feed item
findings.detail: The new backfill updates the run row, but the existing run.merged feed item permanently retains null metadata. Thus the feed inconsistency reported in item 1 survives when the immediate post-merge lookup fails or lacks metadata. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const p=s.upsertRepo({slug:"test/repo",kind:"github",url:"unused",localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); const r=s.createRun(p,{repo:p.slug,prompt:"fix"}); s.updateRun(r.id,{status:"succeeded",prUrl:"https://github.com/test/repo/pull/1",merged:true}); s.resolveMergedRun(r.id,"owner",123456); console.log(JSON.stringify({run:s.getRun(r.id)?.mergedBy,feed:s.readFeed().items.find(x=>x.kind==="run.merged")?.data.mergedBy})); s.close();' Output: {"run":"owner","feed":null}.
findings.suggestion: Make later metadata enrichment visible through the feed without recording a duplicate merge, and test the feed fields after reconciliation.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue merge succeeds, but its metadata lookup fails or returns missing fields. The queue emits run.merged with null fields. A later saved MERGED observation supplies complete metadata; reconciliation updates the run while the feed continues reporting null.

output.summary: Reviewed all changed paths. GitHub notifier tests passed (62 tests); four other targeted files could not load because MCP SDK modules were missing. An isolated probe confirmed a new feed-publication regression.

findings.title: Publish landing feed events after the outer transaction commits
findings.detail: The new outer database transaction suppresses feed publication: both landFeed and resolveMergedRun attempt publication while db.inTransaction is true, and nothing flushes after this transaction commits. Live feed consumers therefore miss the landing until another operation publishes. Targeted command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-land-feed.ts"` invoked landed with an in-memory store and subscriber. Output: `{"stored":["run.pr_opened","run.succeeded","land.landed","run.merged"],"published":[]}`, followed by `error: Landing did not publish run.merged` (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Move the atomic landing operation behind a Store method that buffers publications and flushes them after the outermost commit. Add a subscriber regression test.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue entry lands and the optional metadata lookup fails, times out, or returns no metadata. With no subsequent publishing store operation, land.landed and run.merged remain stored but never reach feed subscribers.

findings.title: Merge metadata corrections are invisible after the feed cursor advances
findings.detail: The queue records the merge with null metadata before awaiting its metadata lookup. Enrichment then updates the existing feed row, but feed reads and publications only deliver IDs greater than the consumer's cursor. An agent that reads the initial merge never receives the corrected fields. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const p=s.upsertRepo({slug:"test/repo",kind:"github",url:"unused",localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); const r=s.createRun(p,{repo:p.slug,prompt:"fix"}); s.updateRun(r.id,{status:"succeeded",prUrl:"https://github.com/test/repo/pull/1"}); s.resolveMergedRun(r.id,null,null,{confirmedAt:1}); const cursor=s.readFeed().nextAfter; s.fillMergedRunMetadata(r.id,"owner",2); console.log(JSON.stringify(s.readFeed({after:cursor}).items)); s.close();' Output: []
findings.suggestion: Make metadata enrichment observable to consumers whose cursors have advanced, and test reading the initial merge followed by enrichment and another incremental feed read.
findings.failure_scenario: An MCP consumer reads and acknowledges run.merged while the queue's metadata request is pending. The request later succeeds, but subsequent feed reads never deliver mergedBy or mergedAt.

output.summary: Found a file-selection defect that can expand targeted retries beyond their slot-bypass bounds. All 32 retry-files tests passed; two other test files could not load installed dependencies, and lint was blocked by sandbox temp-directory permissions.

findings.title: Pass exact paths to Bun instead of filename filters
findings.detail: Only filenames beginning with '-' receive a './' prefix. Bun treats other bare filenames as filters, so a targeted retry can execute additional files. In a temporary fixture containing a.test.ts and nested/a.test.ts, the exact command `bun test a.test.ts` reported `2 pass` and `Ran 2 tests across 2 files`; `bun test ./a.test.ts` reported `1 pass` across one file. This violates the targeted-file requirement and can run substantially more work outside the gate slot than the checked file-count and duration bounds permit.
findings.suggestion: Prefix every validated relative filename with './' before shell quoting, and add a regression test with matching filenames in different directories.
findings.failure_scenario: JUnit identifies root-level a.test.ts as the sole failing file with a short duration, while nested directories contain additional a.test.ts files. The generated unslotted command runs all matching files rather than only the reported failure.

output.summary: Reviewed retry selection, classification, configuration provenance and slot handling. All 32 parser/slot tests passed. Two other test files could not load because local Zod and MCP SDK dependencies were incompatible or missing. A real Bun probe confirmed incorrect targeted file selection.

findings.title: Pass explicit paths to Bun instead of substring filters
findings.detail: Ordinary filenames are substituted without a ./ prefix. Bun treats these arguments as substring filters, so the targeted retry can execute additional files that were excluded from its file-count and duration bounds. In a temporary fixture, `bun test test/a.test.ts` returned exit 1 with `1 pass`, `1 fail`, and `Ran 2 tests across 2 files`: it also selected test/a.test.ts-extra.test.ts. `bun test ./test/a.test.ts` returned exit 0 and ran only one file. An unrelated failure can therefore falsely confirm a regression and suppress the required full retry.
findings.suggestion: Normalize substituted filenames to explicit relative paths, including a ./ prefix for Bun, and add a regression test with overlapping filenames.
findings.failure_scenario: The report lists test/a.test.ts, which passes on retry. Another file named test/a.test.ts-extra.test.ts fails intermittently. The generated retry selects both, incorrectly confirms a regression, and may run the extra file outside the gate slot despite its duration being unknown.

findings.title: Bind the pairing code to the coordinator's TLS identity
findings.detail: The initial request accepts any certificate, and the displayed code is an independent coordinator-generated random value. A TLS-intercepting relay can forward pairing and claim responses unchanged: the owner's code comparison succeeds, while the relay learns the approved token and the worker permanently pins the relay's certificate. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-pair-relay.ts". Output: {"codeMatches":true,"attackerHasApprovedToken":true,"victimPinnedAttacker":true}. This exercised the actual pairing client and SQLite-backed WorkerStore with a mocked relay transport.

findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the first pairing connection using its own TLS certificate and relays requests to the genuine coordinator. The owner approves the matching code, granting the attacker a usable worker token and causing the worker to trust the attacker thereafter.

findings.title: Bind pairing approval to the authenticated TLS identities
findings.detail: The initial request accepts any certificate, and the displayed code is simply returned by the coordinator. An intercepting proxy can relay the pairing request and response unchanged, so the owner and worker see identical codes while the proxy learns the claim secret. After approval, it can claim the worker token itself. The submitted worker fingerprint provides no protection because claiming and authentication require no proof of possession of its private key. A direct protocol probe confirmed: `relay can claim and authenticate without worker private key: true`.
findings.suggestion: Cryptographically bind the compared pairing code to both certificate identities and require proof of possession of the worker key when claiming credentials, or authenticate the coordinator fingerprint through a trusted channel before pairing.
findings.failure_scenario: A network attacker intercepts the worker's first pairing connection, forwards traffic to the real coordinator, and steals the approved token despite the owner comparing matching codes. The worker also pins the attacker's certificate.

findings.title: Protect persisted worker credentials independently of listener lifetime
findings.detail: The TLS key's read deny is registered only when the listener starts and released when it stops. Restarting with workers.listen unset leaves the existing key on disk without a sandbox deny; the shared credential policy contains no worker paths. Mode 0600 does not prevent agents running as the same user from reading it. A policy probe reported `reader denies TLS key while listener holds registration: true` and `reader denies persisted TLS key after listener is disabled: false`.
findings.suggestion: Register persisted worker credential paths in the shared sandbox policy at daemon startup, regardless of whether the listener is enabled. Cover worker tokens and fingerprints across separate processes as well.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner enables workers once, then disables the listener and restarts the daemon. A subsequent tool-enabled agent can read the retained coordinator private key and use it to impersonate the coordinator to paired workers.

findings.title: Preserve check failures across infrastructure retries

findings.title: Revalidate ownership immediately before publication commands

Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/land-claim-review.test.ts"` failed with `error: expect(received).toEqual(expected)`: expected `[]`, received a `gh pr merge ... --squash --delete-branch --match-head-commit ...` command after ownership was revoked during the preflight lookup.

findings.title: Recovery must discover descendants forked before freezing completes
findings.detail: Recovery kills only persisted members, then deletes the invocation record without repeating discovery. A claimed process can fork between the discovery snapshot and SIGSTOP; live cleanup normally catches that child on its next sweep, but recovery never does. I reproduced this with a real subprocess, pausing inspection to arrange the fork and killing the supervisor after SIGSTOP. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/cleanup-fork-review.ts"`. Output: `descendant recorded before crash: false` followed by `{"nextStepExitCode":0,"previousDescendantStillAlive":true,"pendingRecords":0}`. Recovery therefore declares cleanup complete while an old descendant remains able to write to the checkout.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation discovery context to resume the freeze-and-rescan protocol after a crash. Discover and identity-check remaining descendants before deleting the ownership record or allowing another invocation.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked process forks after the cleanup discovery snapshot but before receiving SIGSTOP. The daemon crashes after that SIGSTOP and before the next sweep. Recovery kills the recorded parent, misses its unrecorded child, clears all records, and starts the next command.

findings.title: Do not declare cleanup complete without recovering unfinished discovery

findings.title: Timeout cleanup leaves detached test subprocesses running
findings.detail:
Both cleanup signals target only the timeout process group. The suite's runProcess implementation (src/util/proc.ts:541) starts subprocesses with detached: true, so those children escape both signals. The new test covers only children sharing the group. Targeted probe command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, signal, subprocess, time
p = subprocess.Popen(['bash', '-c', '''trap ':' TERM
bash scripts/ci-check.sh --monitor $$ python3 -c 'import os,time; os.setsid(); print(os.getpid(),flush=True); time.sleep(60)' &
m=$!; sleep 0.3; kill -TERM "$m"; while :; do wait; done
'''], start_new_session=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
child = int(p.stdout.readline())
try:
    time.sleep(0.6)
    os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
    p.wait()
    os.kill(child, 0)
    print('FAIL: detached child survived TERM and group KILL')
finally:
    if p.poll() is None: os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL); p.wait()
    os.kill(child, signal.SIGKILL)
PY
Output: FAIL: detached child survived TERM and group KILL
findings.suggestion: Ensure timeout cleanup also stops owned descendants in separate process groups, and extend the helper test with a detached child matching runProcess behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: A test hangs waiting on a subprocess created through runProcess. At 20 minutes the wrapper terminates Bun, but the detached subprocess survives the TERM and KILL cleanup, violating the requirement to stop children.

findings.title: Preserve known cache measurements for single-round evals
findings.detail: Every eval with recorded rounds loses its input/cache split, including a single-round implementation trial whose details contain the exact measurements. This also makes aggregate cache totals null when mixed with otherwise measurable work. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { computeProviderStatistics } from "./src/db/stats.ts"; const s = new Store(":memory:"); const run = s.createEvalRun({role:"implement",models:["m"],k:1,maxUsd:10},[]); s.recordEvalTrial({evalRunId:run.id,effort:null,caseId:"case",modelId:"m",trial:0,cacheKey:"k",harness:"fake",status:"error",output:null,pass:false,score:0,details:{provider:"p",invocationStatus:"ok",cacheReadTokens:2,cacheWriteTokens:1,rounds:[{round:0,provider:"p",modelId:"m",effort:"default",status:"error",pass:false,reason:"hidden-test command failed",costUsd:0.5,costEquivUsd:1,tokensIn:10,tokensOut:4,durationMs:100}]},tokensIn:10,tokensOut:4,costUsd:0.5,costEquivUsd:1,durationMs:100,createdAt:1}); const totals=computeProviderStatistics(s)[0]?.eval?.totals; console.log(JSON.stringify(totals)); s.close(); if(totals?.successfulShare !== 1 || totals?.cacheReadTokens !== 2 || totals?.cacheWriteTokens !== 1 || totals?.inputTokens !== 7) throw new Error("Expected successfulShare=1, cacheReadTokens=2, cacheWriteTokens=1, inputTokens=7 for one successful provider invocation followed by a grader failure");' Output included inputTokens:null, cacheReadTokens:null, cacheWriteTokens:null and exited 1 with the stated assertion error.
findings.suggestion: Use trial cache measurements when attribution is unambiguous, including single-round trials. Add a regression test with recorded rounds and known cache totals.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation eval stores one round with 10 prompt tokens and trial details recording 2 cache-read and 1 cache-write tokens; statistics report all three input/cache measurements as unknown instead of 7, 2 and 1.

findings.title: Do not treat grading failures as failed provider invocations
findings.detail: Recorded round status is not necessarily the invocation status: src/evals/runner.ts:1208–1212 overwrites it with error or timeout when implementation grading fails after a successful provider call. Using that status here reports a provider failure caused by local grading. The reproduction command in the preceding finding also printed successfulShare:0 despite details.invocationStatus:"ok", then failed its successfulShare=1 assertion.
findings.suggestion: Use stored invocation status where it is available, including single-round trials, and distinguish grading outcomes from provider outcomes. Mark genuinely unavailable historical outcomes as unknown rather than assuming they represent provider failures.
findings.failure_scenario: The provider returns successfully, then implementation grading errors or times out. A single-round eval records invocationStatus="ok" and rounds[0].status="error"; the endpoint reports a successful share of 0 instead of 1.

findings.title: Preserve exact-field redaction for short credentials
findings.detail: Padding the selected field with surrounding log text defeats redactCredentials' exact-match protection for credentials shorter than eight characters. Previously, an image value equal to a registered short credential was redacted; now it survives in image and signature and is persisted. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {expect} from "bun:test"; import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("REVIEW_SHORT", "abc123"); expect(ciSignature("test", "Image: abc123\n(fail) real failure", "failure").image).toBe("[redacted]");' Output: Expected: "[redacted]"; Received: "abc123".
findings.suggestion: Retain exact-field credential matching alongside context-aware redaction, and add a regression test for a short registered credential used as the complete image value.
findings.failure_scenario: Register credential abc123, then inspect a failing log containing 'Image: abc123'. The previous implementation redacts the image; this implementation stores the credential in runner_image and the serialized signature.

findings.title: Report event rejection before discarding the job
findings.detail: A rejected events request aborts the job controller. The catch block then skips POST failure because jobSignal.aborted is true. Consequently, a 400 or 413 rejection leaves the coordinator job leased until expiry, losing the actual failure reason and delaying reassignment.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish event-delivery failure from coordinator cancellation and report its sanitized reason using a separate bounded signal when the lease is still held.
findings.failure_scenario: The events endpoint returns 400 or 413 while the harness is running. The harness aborts and its checkout is removed, but no failure is posted and the coordinator continues showing a leased job.

findings.title: Keep event batches within the endpoint's byte limit
findings.detail: Batching limits event count but ignores serialized size, whereas the coordinator limits event bodies to 1 MiB. Harness tool results can each contain 20,000 characters. A standalone `bun -e` payload-size probe with 60 such events returned {"events":60,"bytes":1203670,"eventEndpointLimit":1048576,"rejected":true}. Valid session output can therefore produce a 413 and abort the session.
findings.suggestion: Flush before the serialized batch reaches the endpoint limit and define explicit handling for an individually oversized event.
findings.failure_scenario: A harness emits 60 tool-result events containing 20,000 ASCII characters each within one batching window. The worker posts a 1,203,670-byte body, exceeding the coordinator's 1,048,576-byte limit.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding worker, lease, and harness code. Targeted tests (`bun test test/workers.test.ts test/agent-test.test.ts`) could not load: missing package `entities` and `TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function`. Found a failure-reporting defect.

findings.title: Report rejected event batches as job failures
findings.detail: Rejecting an event batch aborts the job controller. The catch handler then skips POST failure because jobSignal is aborted. The coordinator retains a leased job until expiry, delays reassignment, and records a generic lease-expiry reason instead of the event rejection. The new rejection test only checks that the job is not done, allowing this behavior to pass.
findings.suggestion: Track event-post failures separately from external cancellation, abort the harness, and send a bounded failure report using a signal independent of the aborted job controller. Assert that the coordinator records the rejection promptly.
findings.failure_scenario: The events endpoint returns 400 or 413 while the worker remains connected and holds a valid lease. The harness stops and its checkout is removed, but no failure report is sent; the coordinator still counts the job as leased until expiry.

output.summary: Reviewed restart reconciliation, adoption, orphan cancellation and late reporting. Found a lease-renewal gap after fencing. A source-derived probe confirmed fenced jobs disappear from heartbeats. Targeted tests could not start because the entities dependency is missing; git diff --check passed.

findings.title: Keep renewing the lease while a pushed result awaits delivery
findings.detail: The independent result signal survives fencing, but heldJobs() excludes every job whose controller is aborted. After the fence fires, subsequent heartbeats therefore omit this job and never renew its lease. If result delivery remains delayed beyond the restart grace period, sweepAgentJobs() expires and requeues it; the eventual report receives 409 despite the worker remaining reachable. The pushed commit then has no accepted report and can end the run NeedsHuman.
findings.suggestion: Track pending reports for pushed commits and keep those jobs in heartbeat lease renewals until reporting finishes or the attempt deadline expires. Add coverage that delays result delivery beyond one lease period while heartbeats succeed after fencing.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes during coordinator downtime and the fence fires. After restart, heartbeats succeed but result POSTs encounter transient failures for over 60 seconds. The job is omitted from heartbeat jobs, its lease expires, and its accepted-report recovery fails.

findings.title: Connect production complexity lookup to the CLI
findings.detail: The documented generator command never supplies lookupRun. Consequently, every CLI-generated case defaults to medium, even when its PR footer identifies a production run whose triage complexity is available locally. The injectable helper supports the requirement, but the actual command cannot use it.
findings.suggestion: Wire an injected run lookup into the CLI through the existing daemon API or another existing run-record interface. Retain the documented fallback when the record is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a replay for a PR with a Run footer whose available production record has complexity small. The CLI writes complexity medium and notes 'lookup not configured' instead of preserving small.

output.summary: Found two defects affecting whether generated cases are usable by the runner. A real-git probe confirmed the validation/grading mismatch. Targeted tests could not start because `entities` is missing; lint could not run because Biome is absent.

findings.title: Mandatory snapshot preparation excludes the intended repository's replays
findings.detail: Every generated case uses snapshot mode, which removes evals/, and must pass the full baseline before validation. This repository's configured test gate runs tests such as test/evals-cases.test.ts that load the committed datasets. Those tests fail when evals/ is removed, so prepareImplement rejects recent Limitless PRs before checking their hidden tests. Documenting this exclusion leaves the central use case—replaying the factory's own merged PRs—unimplemented.
findings.suggestion: Provide a contamination-safe preparation strategy that allows this repository's baseline checks to run, and cover generation with a fixture whose baseline loads committed eval datasets.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a replay from a recent Limitless PR whose hidden tests fail at its parent and pass at its squash commit. Snapshot preparation removes evals/, dataset-loading baseline tests fail, and the otherwise valid replay is excluded.

findings.title: Validate hidden tests with the grader's cleanup semantics
findings.detail: Validation injects hidden tests immediately after setup, preserving untracked setup outputs. gradeImplement instead runs `git reset --hard` and `git clean -fdq` before injection. Consequently, the generator accepts cases whose reference solution fails actual grading. The new fixture itself depends on an untracked `ready` file. In a scratch real-git reproduction, `bun test ./test/hidden.test.ts` returned 0 after setup but returned 1 after `git reset --hard -q HEAD` and `git clean -fdq`, with output `error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'ready'`.
findings.suggestion: Share the grading preparation sequence with validation, including cleanup before hidden-file injection, and verify that an accepted reference solution passes the actual implement grader.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR's setup creates an untracked generated file required by its tests. Both generator validation outcomes qualify, but grading removes the generated file and rejects even an exact implementation of the reference solution.

output.summary: Found a reproducible validation/grading mismatch and missing CLI metadata lookup. Targeted tests could not start because the entities dependency is missing. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Validate hidden tests against the state grading actually uses
findings.detail: Validation injects hidden files immediately after setup, preserving untracked setup outputs. gradeImplement instead runs gates, resets tracked changes, and runs git clean -fdq before injection. Consequently, validation can accept cases whose reference solution fails grading. I reproduced this with the new fixture's pattern: setup creates untracked ready and the hidden test reads it. `bun test ./hidden.test.ts` initially returned 0; after `git reset --hard -q HEAD` and `git clean -fdq`, reinjecting the test and running the same command returned 1 with `error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'ready'`.
findings.suggestion: Share the grading preparation lifecycle with validation, including cleanup before hidden-file injection, and test that an accepted reference solution passes actual grading.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR's hidden tests require an untracked file created by setup, such as the ready file in the newly added fixture. The generator accepts the case, but grading rejects even the reference implementation.

findings.title: Connect the CLI to production run complexity lookup

Therefore every CLI-generated case defaults to medium, even when the report identifies a run whose triage complexity is available locally. The injectable lookup is exercised by tests but cannot be reached through the requested command.
findings.suggestion: Wire a read-only production run lookup into the CLI and retain the explicit unknown/default behavior when the record genuinely cannot be found.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a replay on the factory host for a PR whose footer references an available run with complexity small. The resulting case records medium and 'lookup not configured' instead of the production complexity.

output.summary: Reviewed snapshot creation, gate execution, reuse, and evidence paths. Found two defects in failure handling. Nine session tests and mode parsing passed. Integration checks were blocked by missing/incompatible dependencies and sandbox socket restrictions.

findings.title: Preserve timed-out gate executions for reuse
findings.detail: The completed() predicate excludes timed-out results, so these factory executions are never recorded. When the round commits the identical tree, the gates stage runs the suite again without preserving the earlier timeout. A subsequent pass becomes clean evidence rather than retaining the failure and retry history required by the request. The new timeout test explicitly expects this duplicate execution.
findings.suggestion: Record completed factory timeout outcomes with their classification and retry history, and reuse them for the matching key. Apply the normal timeout policy before finalizing the recorded result if necessary.
findings.failure_scenario: The snapshot test gate times out, the implementer changes nothing afterward, and the gates-stage rerun passes. The suite runs twice and the final evidence loses the timeout.

findings.title: Return failure when confinement invalidates a zero exit
findings.detail: The returned status uses exitCode without checking result.ok or confinementFailed(result). The normal gate executor can mark a result as failed with exitCode 0 when its raw output contains a confinement launch failure. This path prints FAIL but returns status 0, and AgentTestSession consequently emits gate-pass.
findings.suggestion: Return a nonzero status whenever the factory result is not ok, preserving an existing nonzero exit code where appropriate. Add coverage for confinementError: true with exitCode: 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A test command reports a nested sandbox launch failure but its outer process exits zero. The factory rejects the gate, while the session command succeeds and its event reports gate-pass.

Reviewed the diff and restart, lease, cancellation, and retry paths. Found three lifecycle defects. The targeted command `bun test test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts` could not load: `Cannot find package 'entities'`; behavioral tests remain unverified.

findings.title: Process existence does not establish executor freshness
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth identity. There is no heartbeat timestamp or freshness check. A hung executor remains available indefinitely; after its job lease expires, fallback waits in waitStopped forever because the owning process still exists.
findings.suggestion: Implement executor heartbeat freshness and bounded, fail-closed stop handling. Treat stale executors as unavailable for dispatch and resume without authorizing overlapping processes.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor stops servicing its event loop while a gate runs. The lease expires, sweep fails the job, and the daemon waits indefinitely for stopped=1 instead of completing recovery or reporting an actionable failure.

findings.title: Restart cancels surviving targeted retries
findings.detail: Resume accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A surviving baseline-retry-targeted or regression-retry-targeted job is therefore cancelled on restart, even with matching stage, round, SHA, environment, and lease. The resumed engine enters the initial gate path and reruns the suite, contrary to the requested targeted-retry coverage.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress and first-attempt evidence to resume the recorded retry purpose, then attach to its existing job.
findings.failure_scenario: Restart the daemon while an executor is running a targeted regression retry. The new engine requests purpose initial, cancels the live retry, cleans its output, and starts the full gate sequence again.

findings.title: Leasing does not enforce exclusive worktree ownership
findings.detail: leaseInplace atomically claims a job ID but never checks for another running or unconfirmed job in the same worktree. The daemon-side scan occurs before asynchronous checkpointing and enqueueing, so it cannot enforce exclusivity across concurrent starts. Multiple executor processes can lease different jobs for the same cwd and run them simultaneously.
findings.suggestion: Enforce worktree exclusivity inside the lease transaction, including jobs whose processes have not been confirmed stopped.
findings.failure_scenario: Two starts for the same cwd both scan before either enqueues. With two executor processes and two available slots, each executor leases one queued job and both checks mutate the same worktree concurrently.

output.summary: Found three recovery and confinement defects. Database slot tests passed 20 cases. Executor tests could not load because `entities` is missing; gate-slot tests encountered an incompatible Zod API. No files were modified.

findings.title: Preserve confinement failures instead of retrying them locally
findings.detail: The catch converts every exception, including ConfinementError, into an ordinary failed job. The in-place attachment then unconditionally runs failed jobs in-process. A subsequent successful run can therefore produce passing gate evidence after confinement verification failed, violating the existing fail-closed behavior.
findings.suggestion: Persist a distinct terminal confinement failure and propagate it through attachment without executing a fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor's confinement probe detects ineffective enforcement and throws ConfinementError. The daemon reruns the job, its probe succeeds, and the resulting passing GateRun can populate the baseline cache.

findings.title: Reattach surviving targeted retries
findings.detail: The purpose whitelist excludes baseline and regression retries, including targeted retries. Even when stage, round, SHA, environment and lease match, a restart cancels these surviving jobs. The engine also resumes through the initial execution path, so removing the whitelist alone would not preserve the retry.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress and evidence for the engine to resume the recorded retry purpose directly, retaining its setup artifacts and first-attempt classification.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a regression-retry-targeted job is running. The resumed stage requests purpose initial, cancels the retry, cleans its worktree and starts the original gates again.

findings.title: Bound recovery from an unresponsive live executor
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth identity; there is no heartbeat freshness. If the executor stops servicing its event loop, lease expiry marks its job failed, but waitStopped continues waiting indefinitely because that process identity remains alive. Pickup and lease timers consequently cannot complete failover.
findings.suggestion: Track executor responsiveness and apply freshness checks. Bound stop confirmation and surface an explicit recovery failure when processes cannot be confirmed stopped, rather than waiting indefinitely or starting overlapping gates.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor becomes unresponsive during a leased gate. Its lease expires, but the daemon remains stuck in waitStopped forever because executor(worker, false) still recognizes the live PID.

findings.title: Validate the key at startup using the signing-time checks
findings.detail: Startup uses statSync, which follows symlinks, and never checks ownership or actually opens the file. Signing instead uses O_NOFOLLOW and verifies ownership. Consequently startup accepts configurations whose key can never be used, leaving every App-backed GitHub operation broken until configuration is repaired. The isolated probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/github-app-startup-review.ts"`, exercising the extracted startup validator with a symlink to a 0600 file, failed with `AssertionError: startup must refuse a key path that signing rejects` and `false !== true`. Opening that same path with the signing flags returned ELOOP.
findings.suggestion: Share the secure open/fstat validation between startup and signing so startup rejects symlinks, wrong ownership, and unreadable keys with a clear reason.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure private_key_path as a symlink to an owner-owned 0600 PEM file. The daemon starts successfully, but its first App GitHub call fails with 'symlink refused'. A foreign-owned 0600 file similarly passes startup metadata validation but cannot be used.

output.summary: Reviewed identity routing, approval handling, secret registration, configuration and tests. Found inconsistent key validation that permits startup with unusable App credentials. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies, including entities and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, are absent.

findings.title: Reject unsupported key paths during startup
findings.detail: Startup uses statSync, which follows symlinks, whereas signingKey opens the same path with O_NOFOLLOW and rejects it. Consequently, configuration and daemon startup accept a symlink to a valid 0600 key, but every App-authenticated call subsequently fails. The added daemon test explicitly accepts this configuration. An isolated execution of the actual validation and signing functions produced: `startup validation accepted symlink: true` and `signing rejected: GitHub App private key <scratch>/link.pem: symlink refused`. Filesystem reproduction command: `bun -e 'import * as fs from "node:fs"; import {tmpdir} from "node:os"; import {join} from "node:path"; const d=fs.mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),"key-probe-")); try {fs.writeFileSync(join(d,"key"),"fixture",{mode:0o600}); const p=join(d,"link"); fs.symlinkSync(join(d,"key"),p); const key=fs.statSync(p); console.log("startup refuses:",!key.isFile() || (key.mode & 0o077)!==0 || !(key.mode & 0o400)); try {fs.closeSync(fs.openSync(p,fs.constants.O_RDONLY|fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW|fs.constants.O_NONBLOCK));} catch(e) {console.log("signing open:",e.code);} } finally {fs.rmSync(d,{recursive:true,force:true});}'`. Output: `startup refuses: false\nsigning open: ELOOP`.
findings.suggestion: Share the descriptor-based key validation between configuration loading and signing so unsupported paths, ownership and readability fail at startup. Change the symlink startup test to require rejection.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure private_key_path as a symlink to an owner-owned 0600 PEM file. The daemon starts successfully, but all GitHub operations for configured App repositories fail with 'symlink refused'.

Reviewed the diff and surrounding admission, notification, and persistence code. Isolated Bun probes reproduced two defects. Targeted tests could not start because entities and the MCP SDK are missing from this checkout.

findings.title: Persist lifecycle events before polling can lose them
findings.detail: Terminal events are inferred solely from the current status, and their durable checkpoints are created only during polling. A needs_human or failed transition followed by resolution before the next poll disappears entirely. The `bun -` lifecycle probe returned only the started comment and `"needsHumanCheckpoint":null` after needs_human → resolved between polls. Existing pending-event recovery does not cover events the poller never observed.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle intents durably when transitions occur, or consume persisted transition records with a durable cursor. Preserve each event's original reason until publication succeeds.
findings.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human, then the owner resolves it within the polling interval, possibly across a daemon restart. Neither the needs-you label change nor its reason comment is ever published.

findings.title: Do not release a failed issue before re-approval protection exists
findings.detail: The label loop removes in-progress before adding failed. If adding failed fails, the same poll continues into queue admission with neither blocking label present. Failed CLI/MCP runs linked through Closes directives have no latestIssueRun protection because that query considers only issue source references. An actual Store probe confirmed both claim and latest are null for a failed MCP Closes run. A `bun -` lifecycle/admission probe rejecting the failed-label POST returned `{"labels":["priority:1"],"admission":{"eligible":true,"priority":1}}`.
findings.suggestion: Install the failure label before removing in-progress, and extend the existing latest-run admission evidence to cover the same linked issues as lifecycle reconciliation. Keep failed writes retryable without permitting re-pick.
findings.failure_scenario: An MCP or CLI run containing Closes #7 fails. Removing in-progress succeeds, but adding failed returns HTTP 503. The queue immediately picks issue #7 using its old priority approval, without any owner re-approval.

output.summary: Found missing lifecycle coverage and lost lifecycle events. Dependency-isolated probes reproduced three failures. Targeted suites could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates incorrectly require queue enrollment
findings.detail: lifecycleManaged restricts all updates to repositories with an enabled, trusted issue queue. The request requires lifecycle updates for every start path; CLI, MCP and issue-triggered runs outside queue repositories receive no lifecycle labels. The reconciler also stops entirely when the queue is disabled. Dependency-isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts"` exited 1 with `FAIL: queue-disabled linked run has no lifecycle updates`.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission and manage eligible issue-linked runs regardless of queue enrollment.
findings.failure_scenario: With githubQueue unset, start a CLI run containing Closes #7. No in-progress label, lifecycle start comment or later failure label is written.

findings.title: Persist lifecycle events when transitions occur
findings.detail: Events are synthesized from the status observed at polling time, rather than durably recorded at each transition. A needs_human state resolved before the next poll permanently loses its reason comment. Additionally, comment checkpoints keyed only by status suppress every subsequent episode of that status. Dependency-isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts"` exited 1 with `FAIL: needs_human between polls loses its comment` and `FAIL: second needs_human episode has no new reason comment`.
findings.suggestion: Persist lifecycle events and publication bodies when transitions occur, with a durable identifier per status episode. Let polling deliver and checkpoint those recorded effects.
findings.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human and is resolved between polls, so no needs-you comment is posted. Alternatively, retry a run after its first needs_human comment; if it needs human attention again for a different reason, the existing done checkpoint suppresses the new comment.

output.summary: Found missing reasons, discarded notifications, lost transitions, and incomplete repository coverage. Targeted tests could not load: `bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts test/github-notifier.test.ts test/land-queue.test.ts` reported missing package `entities`. Isolated probes confirmed the notification defects.

findings.title: Include sanitized reasons in failure and needs-human comments
findings.detail: These comments always use fixed text, even when the reason is safe to publish. The request requires the reason, with a fixed fallback when publication checks reject it. Probe command: `bun --eval 'const s=await Bun.file("src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts").text();const emit=new Function("run","link","events",s.slice(s.indexOf("    if (run.status ==="),s.indexOf("    for (const [event")));for(const status of ["failed","resolved"]){const events=new Map();emit({status,error:"disk full"},"UI",events);console.log(status,JSON.stringify([...events]));}'`. Output: `failed [["failed","failed: see UI."]]` and `resolved []`.
findings.suggestion: Build comments from the recorded reason, redact and check it, and substitute fixed text only when necessary. Update tests that currently require reasons to be absent.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails with the public reason `disk full`; its issue comment provides no explanation despite the reason passing publication checks.

findings.title: Post a safe fallback when publication checks reject a comment
findings.detail: The catch marks the effect done without posting anything. The delivery-time validation catch does the same. This permanently loses the notification instead of posting the fixed message explicitly required by the request.
findings.suggestion: Persist and deliver a checked, fixed fallback body when the original text is blocked; do not mark an undelivered notification done.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured private string occurs in the UI URL. The failure comment is rejected and permanently suppressed, leaving issue watchers without the required failure notification.

findings.title: Checkpoint lifecycle events when transitions occur
findings.detail: Events are derived exclusively from the current run snapshot at poll time. A failed or needs-human state that becomes resolved before the next poll leaves no lifecycle effect to deliver. The isolated command reported above produces `resolved []`, demonstrating that the reconciler cannot recover the prior event. Existing restart tests first poll the failure, so they do not cover this gap.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle intents durably with run transitions, then let polling deliver those intents independently of the current status.
findings.failure_scenario: Immediately after a poll, a run reaches needs_human and the owner resolves it before the next 180-second poll. No needs-human comment is ever recorded or posted, including after a restart.

findings.title: Support issue lifecycle updates independently of queue admission
findings.detail: Lifecycle management requires the repository to appear in githubQueue.repos with trusted accounts configured, and the reconciler starts only with the issue queue. Consequently CLI, MCP, and webhook issue runs outside queue-enabled repositories receive none of the new lifecycle labels or durable comments. The request explicitly covers any start path without this queue-configuration restriction.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation for issue-linked runs independently of queue eligibility configuration, while retaining repository identity and discreet settings.
findings.failure_scenario: With the issue queue disabled, an owner starts `limitless run` containing `Closes #7`. The run starts and fails without adding in-progress or failed labels or posting lifecycle comments.

output.summary: Reviewed lifecycle reconciliation, persistence, eligibility, and notifier wiring. Found four requirement gaps. Targeted command `bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts test/github-notifier.test.ts` could not load: `Cannot find package 'entities'`; no tests ran. Read-only observation probes also confirmed omitted reasons, suppressed fallback comments, and lost transitions.

findings.title: Include sanitized reasons in failure and needs-you comments
findings.detail: Both comments always contain fixed text and a UI link. The implementation never reads the run's reason, even when it is safe to publish. This contradicts the explicit requirement to comment with the reason; the new tests instead assert that reasons are absent.
findings.suggestion: Include the reason after credential redaction and publication checks, using fixed text only when publication is blocked.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails with error `lint failed in src/example.ts`; its issue receives only `failed: see <UI link>` and gives watchers no explanation.

findings.title: Post the required fallback when publication is blocked
findings.detail: When checkBody rejects a comment, the effect is marked done without posting anything. The delivery-time validation catch does the same. The request requires a fixed public message when the private-strings check blocks text, so these checkpoints permanently discard a required notification.
findings.suggestion: Persist and deliver a safe fixed fallback body instead of completing the effect without a comment.
findings.failure_scenario: The configured UI URL contains a private string. A failed run gets its label, but its failure comment is permanently suppressed, including after restart.

findings.title: Do not restrict lifecycle delivery to queue-enabled repositories
findings.detail: lifecycleManaged requires queue configuration and membership, and the reconciler starts only when the issue queue is enabled. Consequently CLI, MCP, label-triggered, and comment-triggered issue runs outside that configuration receive none of the new lifecycle labels or durable notifications. The request covers any start path without imposing this restriction.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission and include supported issue-linked runs regardless of queue membership.
findings.failure_scenario: With github.queue disabled, an owner starts `limitless run` with `Closes #7`. The run never adds in-progress or failed labels and never posts the required lifecycle comments.

findings.title: Checkpoint lifecycle events when transitions occur
findings.detail: Events are derived exclusively from the current run snapshot when polling occurs. No durable lifecycle effect is recorded at the actual status transition. If a run fails or reaches needs_human and is resolved before the next poll, that event disappears permanently. Persisting observations before delivery only protects events the poller has already seen.
findings.suggestion: Record pending lifecycle events durably alongside status transitions, then let polling deliver those recorded effects.
findings.failure_scenario: Immediately after a poll, a run fails and the owner resolves it before the default 180-second interval expires. The next poll sees resolved, records no failure effect, and never posts the failure comment or applies its failure label.

Allowance smoke checks and git diff --check passed. Targeted gate and pipeline tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency, so runtime verification remains incomplete.

Inspected the diff, rollback handling and scheduler recovery. Found that real daemon restarts skip unfinished rollback. Targeted tests could not run: `bun test test/pipeline-delivery-restart.test.ts` failed to load the missing `entities` package.

findings.title: Keep unfinished rollback eligible for startup recovery
findings.detail: This write marks the run needs_human before rollback finishes, but Scheduler.start only recovers running and waiting_input runs, and its queue only executes queued runs. A daemon restart therefore never reaches rollbackRejectedMerge for this checkpoint. The new tests bypass this defect by calling executeRun directly rather than restarting the scheduler.
findings.suggestion: Persist the rejection while retaining a recoverable status until rollback completes, or explicitly recover rejected runs with unfinished rollback during scheduler startup. Test recovery through a fresh scheduler.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops immediately after reset --hard. On restart, the run is already needs_human, so the scheduler skips it: clean never runs, headSha remains the merged SHA, and pendingRebaseSha/preRebaseHead remain uncleared. A stop immediately after recording rejection also leaves the checkout on the rejected merge.

output.summary: Reviewed rejection persistence, rollback and scheduler recovery. A focused scheduler probe confirmed terminal rejections are skipped on startup. The targeted restart tests could not load because the entities dependency is missing.

findings.title: Keep rejected runs recoverable until rollback finishes
findings.detail: Persisting needs_human before rollback prevents automatic restart recovery. Scheduler.start only recovers running and waiting_input runs, and tick only executes queued runs. Consequently, rollbackRejectedMerge is never reached after a daemon restart at this checkpoint. A focused scheduler probe returned no updates or active runs for a needs_human rejection. The new restart tests bypass this problem by invoking executeRun directly.
findings.suggestion: Persist the rejection while retaining a recoverable status until rollback completes, or explicitly recover unfinished rejection checkpoints during scheduler startup. Cover the reset and state-save interruptions through scheduler restart.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after the rejection checkpoint, including immediately after reset. On startup the scheduler ignores the needs_human run, leaving cleanup and persisted rollback state unfinished. If stopped before reset, the checkout remains at the rejected merged SHA.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, surrounding code, migration, and tests for transactional deduplication, enable boundaries, webhook hints, and retry behavior. No concrete defects found. git diff --check passed. Could not run test/issue-queue.test.ts: it failed to load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js is missing.

findings.title: Queue interception silently drops pull-request comment commands
findings.detail: GitHub sends pull-request conversation comments as issue_comment events too. This branch intercepts them, but the queue queries only issues, so the requested poll never processes them. A targeted `bun run -` probe sent the same signed owner command with issue.pull_request present. Output without queue membership: {"queued":false,"status":201,"runs":1,"polls":0}. With membership: {"queued":true,"status":200,"runs":0,"polls":1}. This removes existing webhook behavior in an explicitly out-of-scope area.
findings.suggestion: Restrict queue interception to issue comments without issue.pull_request, preserving the existing webhook path for pull-request comments.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner posts /limitless fix the PR on a pull request in a configured queue repository. The webhook acknowledges a poll request, but no run ever starts.

findings.title: Identity lookup failures disable the factory-author exclusion
findings.detail: Catching an identity error and substituting null makes bot null, so factory-authored slash commands pass the author exclusion. A targeted `bun run -` polling probe, with lifecycle reconciliation stubbed, supplied an unedited command from factory[bot] included in trusted logins. Output with successful identity lookup: {"failIdentity":false,"factoryAuthoredRuns":0}; with lookup failure: {"failIdentity":true,"factoryAuthoredRuns":1}. This violates the invariant that factory-authored commands never run.
findings.suggestion: When the posting identity cannot be determined, leave comments retryable instead of processing slash commands without the factory-author check.
findings.failure_scenario: The issue query succeeds, but the subsequent App identity refresh fails. A trusted factory bot's unmarked /limitless comment is then admitted and permanently recorded.

output.summary: Found a durability gap when resuming completed in-place jobs after deployment. Targeted tests: 34 passed; worker and pipeline tests could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Replay completed in-place results before applying execution compatibility checks
findings.detail: The evidence replay still depends on executor.canResume(), which rejects even completed jobs when their release SHA, environment, or daemon port differs. Resume then clears the handle without observing the stored failure. A deployment between execution and the evidence checkpoint can therefore permanently lose an observation. Targeted command: bun -e 'import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; import {isDeepStrictEqual} from "node:util"; const source=readFileSync("src/gates/lan.ts","utf8"); const body=source.slice(source.indexOf("(h, env, daemonPort) => {"),source.indexOf("\n      : undefined,")); const js=new Bun.Transpiler({loader:"ts"}).transformSync(`const probe = ${body};`); const workers={releaseSha:"new-release",job:()=>({in_place:1,state:"done",result:"durable failed GateRun",request:JSON.stringify({releaseSha:"old-release",env:{},daemonPort:1234})})}; const canResume=Function("workers","isDeepStrictEqual",`${js}; return probe;`)(workers,isDeepStrictEqual); console.log(JSON.stringify({completedJobWithStoredResult:true,canResumeAfterDeploy:canResume({id:"job"},{},1234)}));' Output: {"completedJobWithStoredResult":true,"canResumeAfterDeploy":false}.
findings.suggestion: Replay a completed job's stored result through the evidence checkpoint before discarding its handle. Apply release and environment compatibility checks when deciding whether an execution can continue, and add a real engine restart test with a changed release SHA.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place gate fails and persists its result; the daemon stops before inserting observations. A new release resumes the same run and SHA, rejects the old handle, and executes gates again. If they pass, the original failure has no observation row.

All 34 classifier/store tests passed, including Homebrew SQLite migration checks. Pipeline and worker tests could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.
