findings.title: Avoid scanning and resolving ownership for every historical run each poll
findings.detail: Every poll now loads all persisted runs, including their complete prompts, and calls linkedIssues for each, issuing one recursive ownership query per run. This happens synchronously before any GitHub await, even when there are no candidates or the runs belong to unrelated repositories. A direct Store probe with 2,000 unrelated runs materialized 400 MB of prompt text and performed 2,000 ownership lookups in approximately 68 ms. Both allocation and synchronous work grow without bound as run history accumulates, undermining the preceding daemon-stall fix.
findings.suggestion: Seed comparisons from a batched, repository-scoped decision projection, resolving effective ownership in SQL and avoiding loading irrelevant historical prompts. Preserve detection of newly published runs.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation accumulates thousands of runs with large issue or review prompts while polling a small queue. Every poll reads all that history and performs thousands of synchronous SQL queries, causing growing event-loop pauses and memory pressure even with an empty queue.

output.summary: No concrete defects found in the diff or surrounding queue logic. Direct Store probes passed for metadata stability, decision changes, and case-insensitive lookup. Targeted queue tests, lint, and typecheck could not complete because required dependencies and tools are missing from the checkout.

Reviewed the full diff, recovery classifications, CAS replay, persistence methods, and tests; found no concrete introduced defects. Migration smoke check and diff whitespace check passed. Targeted tests could not run: `bun test test/lease-store.test.ts test/claim-ref.test.ts` failed during initialization because the environment resolves an incompatible Zod lacking `prefault`. Behavioral test results remain unverified.

Reviewed the diff and recovery paths. Found a release-replay race that discards the journal on a malformed tip. Targeted suites could not start because the installed Zod lacks prefault; an isolated probe reproduced the defect.

findings.title: Classify the moved tip before discarding the release intent
findings.detail: Every moved replay unconditionally marks ownership lost and clears the intent, even when result.tip.record is malformed. This violates the recovery requirement to retain the intent on malformed observations. A moved result alone does not establish a successor generation or different owner. An isolated probe using the real SQLite lease methods reproduced output: {"result":"superseded","row":{"repo":"owner/project","ref":"refs/limitless/claims/12","runId":"run-a","confirmed":{"generation":1,"tip":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","state":"lost"},"intent":null}}. The targeted command `bun test test/lease-store.test.ts test/claim-ref.test.ts` could not execute tests: `TypeError: floors.prefault is not a function`.
findings.suggestion: Classify result.tip using the same rules as the initial read. Keep malformed or otherwise unclassifiable observations pending, and clear the journal only when supersession is established. Add a replay-race test where the competing tip is malformed.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery reads the confirmed held tip and starts replaying a journaled final release. Before updateRefs arrives, another writer installs a malformed claim commit. ClaimClient returns moved with that malformed tip. Recovery clears the final status and checkpoint intent and marks confirmed ownership lost, whereas observing the same malformed tip before replay would preserve both.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding land, classification, and restart paths. Found a restart-dependent misclassification. Diff whitespace checks passed. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout lacks the entities package.

findings.title: Include resumed observations when recording slow regressions
findings.detail: A resumed gate gets a new stage ID, while its existing observation retains the original stage ID: reinsertion for the same execution handle does nothing because of the unique constraint. Filtering observations by the current stage therefore excludes the resumed primary failure. The selector subsequently cannot set slow_regression, so a successful slow-regression re-check is finalized as flaky instead of load.
findings.suggestion: Find observations by the durable execution identity across stage restarts. Add a restart test that interrupts after observation insertion but before the slow-regression selector runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A LAN post-merge primary execution fails slowly. The daemon stops after inserting its observation but before persisting gate-result. On restart, the same completed handle resumes under a new stage ID. Its re-check passes, but the retained observation has slow_regression=0 and class=flaky.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and execution/finalization paths. Found a restart classification defect. Targeted tests in failure-class, failure-observations, pipeline-gates and land-queue could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Match resumed observations by execution identity, not current stage ID
findings.detail: A resumed gates stage receives a new stage ID. If the primary LAN result was observed before interruption, reattaching its durable handle attempts the same observation insert, which ON CONFLICT ignores; the existing row retains its original stage_id. This filter then excludes that row, so the slow-regression selector never records slow_regression on it. A passing re-check consequently finalizes as flaky instead of load.
findings.suggestion: Locate the primary observation using its durable execution identity across stage restarts. Add a restart test between observation insertion and the gate-result save, followed by a passing slow-regression re-check.
findings.failure_scenario: A primary LAN post-merge execution fails slowly. The daemon stops after observation insertion but before gate-result is saved. Resume reattaches the completed handle under a new stage ID, and the slow-regression re-check passes. The observation ends with slow_regression=0 and class=flaky rather than slow_regression=1 and class=load.

output.summary: Found two lease lifecycle defects using isolated dependency-injected probes. The supplied tests could not start because the available Zod dependency lacks prefault.

findings.title: Renew confirmed leases restored from persistence
findings.detail: The renewal loop visits only the in-memory handles map, which starts empty and is populated only by successful writes through operate. Held leases restored from SQLite, including acquisitions confirmed during recovery, never enter this map. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/lease-review-probe.ts"` produced `recovered confirmed held after renewal tick: { reads: 0, writes: 0, samples: 0, state: "held" }` despite active returning true.
findings.suggestion: Populate renewal candidates from recovered confirmed held rows, or derive them from current persisted ownership on each tick.
findings.failure_scenario: Restart with a confirmed held lease, start the manager with active returning true, and perform no explicit acquire or update. Every renewal tick skips the lease until it expires.

findings.title: Reconcile pending intents before refusing another run
findings.detail: The cross-run guard returns refused before reconcileLeaseIntent runs whenever the row has an intent. This violates the required reconciliation-first behavior and reports unresolved ownership as live. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/lease-review-probe.ts"` produced `different run with pending acquisition: { kind: "refused", reason: "live" }` with zero reads. A failed acquisition that could now be dropped therefore continues blocking another run through this entry point.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile pending intents before the cross-run ownership guard, return wait while reconciliation remains pending, then re-read the row and evaluate confirmed ownership.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A leaves a never-confirmed acquisition intent after an uncertain write. Once GitHub becomes readable, run B calls acquire. Instead of resolving A's intent and potentially acquiring the ref, the manager repeatedly refuses B without reading GitHub.

output.summary: Found three lease lifecycle defects using focused probes against the real manager and journal reconciliation with mocked dependencies. The probes failed all three assertions. The supplied suite could not load because the installed Zod lacks prefault. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Released ownership incorrectly triggers supersession
findings.detail: The supersedes check includes confirmed released rows. After another coordinator advances and releases the same logical run, acquisition returns superseded and changes the old released row to lost instead of acquiring the next generation. Probe command: bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts". Output: 'released reacquire: superseded'; Expected: "held", Received: "superseded".
findings.suggestion: Restrict the ownership-loss check to confirmed held ownership and allow released same-run tips through the generation-increment acquisition path.
findings.failure_scenario: Coordinator A releases generation 1. Coordinator B acquires and releases generation 2 for the same run. A subsequently tries to acquire generation 3 and is permanently rejected as superseded.

findings.title: Renewal loop omits recovered confirmed leases
findings.detail: The loop enumerates only the in-memory handles map, populated exclusively by writes applied through operate. Existing confirmed held rows and acquisitions confirmed by journal reconciliation never enter that map. Probe command: bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts". Output: 'restored lease renewal writes: 0'; Expected: 1, Received: 0, despite active returning true.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate confirmed held rows for renewal, or register their handles during recovery and successful reconciliation without manufacturing an anchor.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager restarts with an active confirmed held lease, or its first acquisition is confirmed asynchronously by reconciliation. start() never renews that lease, allowing it to expire.

findings.title: Cross-run refusal bypasses pending-intent reconciliation
findings.detail: An intent belonging to another run causes an immediate refused result before reconcile executes. This violates the requirement to reconcile pending intents before each operation and prevents a failed first acquisition from being forgotten promptly. Probe command: bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts". Output: 'cross-run reconcile: refused'; Expected: "held", Received: "refused". The prior intent remained unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile pending intents before applying the cross-run ownership guard. Return wait while unresolved; after a dropped never-confirmed acquisition, forget the row and continue acquisition.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A leaves an unconfirmed first-acquisition intent, but GitHub subsequently confirms the ref is absent. Run B acquires before a renewal tick; it is refused without reconciliation even though A's intent can be dropped and B can safely acquire generation 1.

output.summary: Found a spec-authoring conflict that can remove browser checks before verification. Existing spec-criteria tests passed (23 tests); a focused browser-marker assertion failed. The six changed test files could not load because dependencies were missing or incompatible. Diff whitespace checks passed.

findings.title: Update the criterion validator to allow marked preview checks
findings.detail: The prompt now permits browser checks, but outOfRunCriteria still flags phrases such as 'in a browser' and 'visually', regardless of browser:true. The spec stage consequently sends 'Invalid acceptance criteria' feedback asking the author to replace legitimate preview checks with repository commands/tests or move them out of scope. Reproduction: bun -e 'import { outOfRunCriteria } from "./src/pipeline/spec-criteria.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const criterion = { id: "AC-1", criterion: "The preview layout works at both viewports", how_to_verify: "Open the UI preview in a browser and visually inspect both viewport sizes", browser: true }; const spec = { summary: "UI", assumptions: [], requirements: [], acceptance_criteria: [criterion], out_of_scope: [], blocking_questions: [] }; assert.deepEqual(outOfRunCriteria(spec), [], "A marked UI preview check must not trigger the outside-the-run rewrite");'. Output: 'AssertionError: A marked UI preview check must not trigger the outside-the-run rewrite'; actual contains AC-1, expected [].
findings.suggestion: Make criterion validation recognize marked preview checks and update the retry feedback accordingly. Add a focused test proving a valid marked browser criterion does not trigger the outside-the-run rewrite, while genuinely external requirements remain flagged.
findings.failure_scenario: A spec author returns browser:true with how_to_verify 'Open the UI preview in a browser and visually inspect both viewport sizes'. The engine rejects it for a rewrite and instructs the author to replace or remove the browser verification requirement.

output.summary: Reviewed browser markers, prompt generation, verdict conversion, infrastructure handling, and resume context. No concrete defects found. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies are missing or incompatible (`entities` missing; installed Zod lacks `.overwrite()`).
Reviewed publication, recovery, command reservation and tests. Found a privacy failure in error diagnostics. The targeted test file could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing.

findings.title: Use fixed diagnostics for publication failures
findings.detail: The new question-publication path forwards identity, recovery and POST exceptions to logFailure, which logs String(error) with credential redaction only. Configured private strings can therefore escape into diagnostics, violating requirement 2. An injected lifecycle reproduction confirmed this. Exact isolated check: `bun -e 'const s=await Bun.file("src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts").text(); const logs=[]; const code=s.slice(s.indexOf("  const logFailure ="),s.indexOf("  const openQuestions =")).replaceAll(": Run", "").replaceAll(": string", "").replaceAll(": number", "").replaceAll(": unknown", ""); const f=Function("signal","exhausted","log","redactCredentials",code+"return logFailure;")({aborted:false},Symbol(),x=>logs.push(x),x=>x); f({id:"run1"},"owner/repo",7,Error("private-host.example")); console.log(logs[0]); if(logs[0].includes("private-host.example")) throw Error("configured private text reached diagnostics");'`. Output included `Issue lifecycle owner/repo#7 run run1: Error: private-host.example` and `error: configured private text reached diagnostics`.
findings.suggestion: Log a fixed publication-failure code instead of the exception. Add a test injecting an identity or gh failure containing a configured private string and assert that diagnostics contain only the fixed code.
findings.failure_scenario: A waiting run has a pending question publication. Identity lookup or gh rejects with an error containing a configured private hostname that is not a registered credential. The hostname is written verbatim to lifecycle logs.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, surrounding lifecycle code, and recovery tests. An injected-fake probe confirmed that inspection failure closes an uncertain POST checkpoint without recovery. The targeted command `bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts` could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js is missing; direct lifecycle imports also encountered missing entities.

findings.title: Recover uncertain POSTs before suppressing their checkpoints
findings.detail: The body-inspection catch marks the effect done before attempting marker recovery, even when pending.page records an uncertain prior POST. If GitHub accepted that POST and private-string inspection subsequently fails or newly blocks its body, reconciliation permanently closes the checkpoint without discovering the accepted comment. This violates the explicit requirement to recover uncertain POSTs before closing their checkpoints.
findings.suggestion: Separate recovery-envelope validation from outgoing-body inspection. For uncertain effects, recover using the independently generated marker and checkpointed identity before closing the checkpoint; suppress any subsequent POST when body inspection fails.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question comment but its response is lost, leaving page=1. Before the next poll, private-strings inspection becomes unavailable or the question becomes configured private text. Reconciliation saves state=done and page=0 without fetching comments or recording the accepted comment ID.

output.summary: Found three reproducible defects using isolated Store and CLI checks. The new conflict-round suite could not start because local dependencies are missing and inherited Zod is incompatible. One existing Store test passed; diff whitespace checks passed. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Resolve conflict rounds to their owner when landing
findings.detail: The new conflict run becomes the newest run for the PR, so LandQueue.request selects it when landing by PR URL or number. Its baseBranch is the PR head branch. Consequently, landing fetches that branch as the base, skips incorporating the actual target branch, and reads gate configuration from PR-controlled content. Running `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-conflict-contract.test.ts"` reproduced: `Expected: "main"; Received: "limitless/owner-feature"`.
findings.suggestion: Normalize round runs to their owning run before creating a land entry, preserving the original target branch and trusted gate configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory PR targeting main completes a conflict round. After approving the resolution, the operator lands by PR URL. The entry uses the feature branch as both base and head.

findings.title: Refresh stale observations before permanently skipping land triggers
findings.detail: Any cached snapshot suppresses a live lookup, and startConflictTrigger also prefers cached data over the supplied observation. A stale draft snapshot can therefore permanently skip a valid land-conflict trigger. Polling does not recover it when mergeability remains CONFLICTING. Running `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-conflict-contract.test.ts"` produced `state: "skipped", reason: "PR is draft"`, `live reads: 0`, `next poll's feed: []`, and `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0`.
findings.suggestion: Refresh eligibility for land triggers before terminally skipping them, and ensure the transaction uses the validated fresh observation rather than overriding it with cached data.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller observes a conflicting draft PR. The PR becomes ready between polls, and landing discovers a conflict. The cached draft flag skips the trigger; subsequent polling emits no new conflict transition.

findings.title: Order mixed round kinds chronologically
findings.detail: Review and conflict rounds now have independent numbering, but reviewRounds still orders only by round number. The CLI selects the last delivered entry as the default reviewed SHA, so an older review round can outrank a newly delivered conflict resolution. Running `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-conflict-contract.test.ts"` exercised the actual CLI: it submitted `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222` instead of the newer resolution head `3333333333333333333333333333333333333333`, exiting with `409: head moved: approving an older delivered head`.
findings.suggestion: Return rounds in durable chronological order, or explicitly select the newest delivered head for CLI approval independently of per-kind round numbering.
findings.failure_scenario: Review rounds 1 and 2 deliver successfully, followed by conflict round 1. Running `limitless review <run> --approve` without --sha attempts to approve review round 2's obsolete head.

output.summary: Found a lost-trigger defect and duplicate-comment retries. Three focused tests passed. Integration tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing local dependencies, incompatible parent-directory Zod, and temp-directory permissions. No repository files changed.

findings.title: Refresh stale snapshots before discarding land triggers
findings.detail: Any cached PR snapshot suppresses a fresh lookup, even when its head predates the durable land trigger. startConflictTrigger then permanently marks the trigger skipped as 'PR head moved'. Reproduction: `bun "$TMPDIR/conflict-review-probes.ts"` produced `{"lookups":0,"rounds":0,"trigger":{"state":"skipped","reason":"PR head moved"}}` and failed with `AssertionError: an eligible land trigger must not be discarded because the poller cache has an older head` (`0 !== 1`). The conflict remains unresolved unless another independent trigger arrives.
findings.suggestion: Refresh snapshots that disagree with the trigger's head before consuming the trigger. Preserve pending state when current eligibility cannot be established, and ensure startConflictTrigger does not override a fresh observation with stale cached data.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR advances from A to B and B is approved before the next poll. Landing B encounters a conflict while github_prs still contains A. Its durable trigger is discarded without checking GitHub.

findings.title: Check the comment marker on every POST retry
findings.detail: The marker lookup occurs outside the retry wrapper used by gh. If GitHub creates the comment but its response is lost, withGitHubRetry repeats the POST without checking the marker, creating duplicate resolution comments. A fake sender exercising that wrapper via `bun "$TMPDIR/conflict-comment-retry-probe.ts"` produced `{"attempts":2,"comments":2}` and failed with `AssertionError: a resolution comment must not be duplicated by an uncertain POST retry` (`2 !== 1`).
findings.suggestion: Place the marker lookup and conditional POST inside one retry operation, so every attempt checks whether an earlier uncertain POST succeeded.
findings.failure_scenario: The first comment POST succeeds remotely, but gh reports a transient unexpected EOF. The automatic retry posts the same comment again.

output.summary: Found three defects using isolated probes; all three produced assertion failures. Existing targeted suites could not load because of incompatible Zod and missing MCP dependencies. Typecheck lacked Bun types, and Biome was unavailable. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Restore local setup before resuming a pending retry
findings.detail: After restart, the gates stage runs checkoutCommitted(), deleting dependencies and build output. This cached-result return skips the initial suite and its setup, while the pending retry's persisted request has setup: []. The retry consequently runs without its prerequisites. An isolated real-command probe passed without interruption but failed after restart. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/review-executor-probe.test.ts". Output: resumed retry contained "ok":false,"output":"missing-dependency"; assertion reported "Expected: true, Received: false".
findings.suggestion: Restore the required setup and scratch environment before replaying local retries, or replay the full local suite while preserving first-attempt evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup installs node_modules, the initial check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts after persisting the regression-retry handle. Resume deletes node_modules, skips setup, and incorrectly blocks the run.

findings.title: Persist and recover the landing execution handle
findings.detail: Landing passes neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback to executeGate(), so its handle is discarded through the default no-op callback. This daemon gate path cannot reattach after restart and violates the requested durability contract. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/review-land-durability-probe.test.ts". Output: "state writes before landing attach: []" followed by "Expected to contain: durable-lease, Received: []".
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing handle, keyed by land entry and checked commit, before attaching; recover it when resuming checks.
findings.failure_scenario: A landing execution starts and the daemon restarts while awaiting its result. The resumed queue has no execution identity and calls start again instead of attach.

findings.title: Forward events from injected executors
findings.detail: executeGate() awaits only execution.result and never consumes execution.events. Gate callbacks work solely because the default local executor receives hooks outside the Executor interface. An injected executor emitting valid check events produces no live gate events or landing log entries. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/review-executor-probe.test.ts". Output: "observed gate events: 0"; assertion expected the emitted check but received [].
findings.suggestion: Consume execution.events in the common execution path and forward check events to gate callbacks, avoiding duplicate callbacks from the local executor.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor yields a completed-check event and resolves its GateRun. The stage verdict updates, but its gate callback never runs and the landing command log remains empty.

output.summary: Found two executor durability defects using isolated probes. Targeted repository tests were blocked by incompatible Zod and missing MCP dependencies; lint/typecheck were blocked by missing tooling/types. git diff --check passed. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Restore setup prerequisites when replaying local retries
findings.detail: Resume calls checkoutCommitted, which removes ignored dependencies, then this cached-result return skips the initial execution and its setup. The pending retry handle contains setup: [], so local attach cannot recreate those dependencies. Probe command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-restart-probe.ts". Output: "initial output: transient", "resumed retry output: missing dependency", "resumed retry exit code: 2", followed by AssertionError: retry must still have setup dependencies after restart.
findings.suggestion: Ensure replaying a local retry restores its setup prerequisites in the fresh checkout and scratch, while preserving the handle and first-attempt evidence. Add restart coverage with real setup-dependent checks.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup creates node_modules/ready; a check fails transiently; the regression-retry handle is persisted; the daemon restarts. Resume removes node_modules, reuses the cached initial result, and runs the retry without setup, producing a false blocking failure.

findings.title: Persist landing execution handles before attachment
findings.detail: This executeGate call supplies neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback, so it uses the no-op persistence default. Landing never records execution identity and cannot attach to it after restart, violating the requested handle lifecycle. Probe command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-land-handle-probe.ts". Output: "store writes before attach: 0", followed by AssertionError: landing must checkpoint the handle before attachment.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the handle against the landing attempt before attachment, restore it on resume, and clear it after consumption. Add a landing restart test that verifies attach is called without another start.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while landing checks are pending. The resumed queue has no saved handle and calls start again instead of attaching to the existing execution.

output.summary: Found a reproducible Codex editor startup regression. Portable sandbox tests passed (15 passed, 9 skipped). Real Seatbelt probes were unavailable inside this sandbox; remaining tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies. The checkout is unchanged.

findings.title: Credential files make the Codex editor probe fail
findings.detail: Preserving the editor's credential deny list sends regular files such as .npmrc and .netrc through readConfinement into canaryRoots. That selector accepts writable files, then sandboxProbe attempts mkdtemp inside them, gets ENOTDIR and returns 'probe inconclusive'. Codex editors therefore refuse to start on affected installations. Reproduction command: HOME="$review_home" TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/review-credential-file.test.ts". With an enforcing fake CLI and the real canaryRoots selector, output was {"withoutNpmrc":true,"withNpmrc":{"ok":false,"path":"fake-codex","version":"codex-cli 0.160.0","reason":"probe inconclusive","exitCode":null}}, followed by 'Expected: true; Received: false'.
findings.suggestion: Create canary directories only under directories. Keep denied credential files covered by the direct read probes, and add a regression test using the production selector with a stand-in .npmrc.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's home contains a writable regular ~/.npmrc or ~/.netrc, or sandbox.deny_read names another writable regular file. An edit-mode Codex invocation fails confinement verification before any sandbox command runs.

output.summary: Found a credential-read gap and a Linux compatibility regression. Sandbox tests passed with a temporary home (15 passed, 9 skipped). Real Seatbelt probes were unavailable; broader tests, typecheck and lint were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies. No repository files changed.

findings.title: The Cargo allowance exposes registry credentials
findings.detail: Allowing the entire Cargo home overrides the home-wide deny for .cargo/credentials and .cargo/credentials.toml. Neither file has a specific deny, so candidate tests and install scripts can still read and exfiltrate registry tokens. A temporary stand-in check, `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-read-policy.ts" cargo`, printed `Cargo credential has an overriding read allowance: true` and failed with `AssertionError: Gate must deny Cargo registry credentials`.
findings.suggestion: Allow only the Cargo toolchain and cache paths gates need, excluding both credential-file locations. Add a regression probe using stand-in Cargo credentials.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner has a registry token in ~/.cargo/credentials.toml, and a malicious gate script reads that absolute path. The later .cargo read allowance permits it.

findings.title: Accept GNU ls directory-denial results
findings.detail: READ_PROBE now uses ls for directories, but this check requires exit status 1. GNU ls returns 2 when denied access to a directory, and its `cannot open directory '<path>': Permission denied` diagnostic also fails deniedRead's filename parser. Consequently, an enforcing Linux sandbox is rejected. An injected-runner check, `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-read-policy.ts" ls`, produced `{"lsExit":1,"ok":true,"reason":null}` followed by `{"lsExit":2,"ok":false,"reason":"probe inconclusive"}` and failed its assertion.
findings.suggestion: Handle both GNU and BSD directory-denial statuses and diagnostics while retaining exact-path verification, or use a portable probe with consistent diagnostics.
findings.failure_scenario: A Linux Codex editor has an existing ~/.ssh directory. Its sandbox correctly denies directory reads, but GNU ls returns status 2; verification reports inconclusive and prevents the editor from starting.

output.summary: Found three durability gaps. Isolated local execution checks passed; two resume probes failed. Targeted suites could not reach assertions because installed Zod lacks overwrite() and the MCP SDK is missing. The worktree remained unchanged.

findings.title: Resume persisted retries instead of discarding their handles
findings.detail: The purpose whitelist excludes baseline, regression, and timeout retries. After restart, their persisted handles are discarded and new work starts; cancelGateExecution cannot cancel work owned by the previous process. The new tests explicitly expect this duplication. Probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-resume.ts"` produced `{"starts":1,"attaches":["duplicate"]}` and `AssertionError: a resumed retry must attach its durable handle rather than start duplicate work` (`1 !== 0`).
findings.suggestion: Persist the retry phase and preceding results so resume can attach to the recorded retry. Keep any required local setup replay specific to the local executor.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after persisting a retry handle but before receiving its result. Resume starts another execution instead of attaching to the existing one.

findings.title: Checkpoint the result before deleting its execution identity
findings.detail: The gate-result save removes the handle before the caller receives or persists the GateRun. A restart in this interval leaves neither the handle nor its result, so even an initial execution starts again. Probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-result-checkpoint.ts"` produced `durable state before caller received result: {"round":0}`, `start calls after resume: 2`, and `AssertionError: resume must retain the execution identity or its durable result until the caller consumes it` (`2 !== 1`).
findings.suggestion: Persist the result alongside the execution checkpoint, or retain the handle until the caller durably records consumption.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after gate-result commits but before baseline assignment or the gates-stage checkpoint. Resume starts duplicate work despite the completed execution.

findings.title: Persist and restore landing execution handles
findings.detail: Landing calls executeGate without a stored handle or persistence callback, so it uses the default no-op persistence function. Its handle is never saved before awaiting execution, and a restarted checking entry always calls start again. This leaves a required daemon gate path outside the durable executor contract.
findings.suggestion: Persist the handle with the landing entry, restore it when resuming checking, and clear it only after recording the result.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while landing checks are running. The resumed entry has no execution identity and starts another suite instead of attaching.

output.summary: Found three durability gaps in executor integration. Three isolated probes passed; four restart assertions failed. Repository suites could not load because available Zod lacks overwrite() and an MCP SDK module is missing. Diff checks passed; repository files were unchanged.

findings.title: Retry executions discard their persisted identity on restart
findings.detail: The purpose allowlist excludes baseline-retry, regression-retry and timeout even when the stored stage, round and SHA match. Restart therefore forgets the execution and calls start again. cancelGateExecution cannot cancel the previous execution after restart because it only consults an in-memory map. The dependency-isolated command `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-executor.test.ts" --test-name-pattern 'restart reattaches persisted'` produced `3 fail`: each expected attaches=["previous-execution"], starts=[], but received attaches=["new-execution"], starts=["new-execution"]. The new repository tests explicitly expect this replay, contrary to the requested executor restart contract.
findings.suggestion: Persist the retry substep and prerequisite results so durable executors reattach to pending retries. Keep replaying setup as a local-executor behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: Restart after a durable injected executor starts a baseline retry, regression retry or timeout rerun but before its result is consumed. The resumed run starts replacement work and loses the original execution.

findings.title: Landing checks never persist their execution handle
findings.detail: The landing call supplies neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback to executeGate. Its default persistence callback does nothing, so landing attaches and awaits work without ever recording its identity. A resumed checking entry calls start again. Routing landing through executeGate therefore does not satisfy the requirement that callers persist handles before awaiting executions.
findings.suggestion: Persist a handle scoped to the land entry and checked commit before attaching, and load it when resuming that entry.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a landing executor is running checks. The land entry survives, but its execution handle does not, so the queue cannot reattach and starts another execution.

findings.title: Handle removal is checkpointed before the result is durable
findings.detail: The wrapper clears and saves gateExecution before returning the GateRun to its caller. At that checkpoint, neither the result nor the caller's completed substep has been persisted. A crash immediately afterward loses both the execution identity and its result. The isolated command `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-executor.test.ts" --test-name-pattern 'after gate-result'` produced `1 fail`: expected starts=1 and attaches=["1","1"], received starts=2 and attaches=["1","2"].
findings.suggestion: Retain the handle until the caller durably records consumption, or persist the result and next substep atomically with handle removal.
findings.failure_scenario: An initial gate execution finishes, the gate-result checkpoint saves the cleared handle, and the daemon exits before the stage records its result. Resume starts another execution instead of recovering the completed one.

output.summary: Found a reproducible Codex editor launch regression. Sandbox checks produced 16 passes and 12 skips; two focused regression tests failed. Scratch/harness tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies. Real Seatbelt checks were unavailable inside this sandbox.

findings.title: Existing credential files prevent Codex editors from launching
findings.detail: Retaining the editor's denyRead list passes credential files into canaryRoots(), which accepts writable regular files as roots. The subsequent temp(root, ...) attempts to create a directory inside .netrc or .npmrc, throws ENOTDIR, and returns 'probe inconclusive' before invoking codex sandbox. runCodex consequently refuses the editor. Reproduction: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/review-codex-file-deny.test.ts" produced two failures: 'Expected: > 0', 'Received: 0' sandbox calls, with reason 'probe inconclusive'. Removing the stand-in credential file lets sandbox verification proceed.
findings.suggestion: Create negative write canaries only inside directories. Verify denied credential files through the existing read probes, and add coverage using writable .netrc and .npmrc stand-ins with the production canary selection.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner has a writable ~/.netrc, ~/.npmrc, Cargo credentials file, or another configured denied credential file. Every uncached Codex editor probe aborts during canary creation and the editor never starts.

output.summary: Found an incomplete security boundary for relocated factory data. Sandbox tests: 16 passed, 12 skipped because nested Seatbelt is unavailable. Other targeted tests could not load due to installed Zod incompatibilities already present on base; lint and typecheck were blocked by missing local dependencies.

findings.title: Deny relocated factory data outside the home directory
findings.detail: The gate's broad deny covers only home. With the supported LIMITLESS_HOME pointing outside home, or ~/.limitless symlinked there, other runs' checkouts and artifacts remain readable through Seatbelt's `(allow default)`. Neither configureReadPolicy nor this rule includes the factory data root. This leaves the explicitly requested isolation incomplete. Targeted command: `bun -e 'import {homeReadPolicy,readPolicyScope} from "./src/harness/read-policy.ts"; const p=readPolicyScope.run({home:process.env.TMPDIR,environment:{}},()=>homeReadPolicy(["/Volumes/factory/work/current"],true)); console.log("other run denied:",p.denyRead.some(p=>"/Volumes/factory/work/other/secret".startsWith(p+"/")));'` Output: `other run denied: false`.
findings.suggestion: Carry the configured factory data root into the shared policy and deny its lexical and canonical paths for gates, with the existing exceptions for this run's checkout, scratch and Git paths. Add coverage for relocated and symlinked data directories.
findings.failure_scenario: Set LIMITLESS_HOME=/Volumes/factory, or symlink ~/.limitless to that location. A malicious gate in /Volumes/factory/work/current can read /Volumes/factory/work/other and /Volumes/factory/runs/other by absolute path.

output.summary: Confirmed an output-buffering regression against the base commit. Sandbox tests: 34 passed, 15 skipped. Preview integration checks were blocked by loopback EPERM and unavailable nested Seatbelt; lint/typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies.

findings.title: Bound unterminated preview output before line framing
findings.detail: The new serve callbacks use runProcess's lineSplitter, whose pending buffer grows until a newline arrives. tailLimit bounds the retained output tail, but not this buffer. Previously, serve output was collected directly from chunks and stayed bounded. An untrusted preview can now exhaust the factory daemon's memory. A targeted probe using real subprocess output and mocked networking failed with `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/preview-output-review.test.ts"`: `Expected: < 8000000; Received: 17172595` retained heap bytes after a 16 MB unterminated line. The same probe passed against the base implementation, retaining 1,054,797 bytes.
findings.suggestion: Bound incomplete-line buffering for preview output, including the startup-marker parser, while preserving the confinement handshake and bounded diagnostics.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview serve process continuously writes stdout or stderr without newline characters. The parent retains the entire stream despite tailLimit: 4000, eventually exhausting daemon memory and interrupting other runs.

output.summary: Found two reproduced reliability regressions. Four focused sandbox tests passed. Preview integration tests were blocked by loopback EPERM; nested Seatbelt and dependency-based lint/typechecks were unavailable. Worktree unchanged.

findings.title: Handle rejection from abort-triggered teardown
findings.detail: stop() now rejects on ProcessTerminationError, but onAbort still calls void stop() without a rejection handler. If shutdown inspection fails before the preview owner awaits stop(), this becomes an unhandled rejection and can terminate the daemon. A temporary reproduction mocked port allocation/readiness and injected a process-inspection failure. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/preview-abort-review.test.ts". Output: "Unhandled error between tests" and "Invocation termination could not be confirmed: injected process inspection failure". The same reproduction against the base produced no unhandled error.
findings.suggestion: Attach a rejection handler in onAbort while preserving the rejected stopping promise for the owner and retaining the process-scope termination failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A running preview is cancelled, process inspection fails during teardown, and verification cleanup delays the owner's call to preview.stop().

findings.title: Bound pending output before line framing
findings.detail: The previous chunk collector retained only 4,000 characters. The new line callbacks use runProcess's lineSplitter, which retains an entire unterminated line; tailLimit does not bound that buffer. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/preview-output-review.test.ts". After 16 MiB of output without newlines, the bounded-retention assertion failed: "Expected: < 8388608; Received: 17964707". Against the base, it passed with 1,190,116 bytes of heap growth.
findings.suggestion: Bound the pending line buffers used by confined previews, or provide bounded chunk collection while retaining startup-marker detection.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview server continuously writes output without newline characters, including carriage-return progress output. The daemon retains the stream indefinitely and can exhaust its heap.

output.summary: Found a report privacy regression using an isolated source-level check. Targeted MCP tests could not start because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing.

findings.title: Line-level filtering exposes uncatalogued private verifier prose
findings.detail: The narrower filtering exposes private observations that the catalogue does not recognize. collectVerification calls collect(verify?.notes) without privateProse=true, so ordinary-language holdout observations without quoted literals or identifiers are not protected. Unstructured verifier diagnostics have the same gap. An isolated check using the actual catalogue functions, with schema validation and store I/O stubbed, reproduced a regression. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/mcp-redaction-review.ts". Output: base: "[withheld: holdout text]"; head: "[withheld: holdout result or quotation; 1 line]\nVerification notes: Blank input retained stale rows." The check failed with "AssertionError: Private verifier notes leaked in report".
findings.suggestion: Catalogue private observations from verifier notes and unstructured diagnostics before filtering reports line by line, while retaining explicit exemptions for public generic status messages. Add an integration regression test for these prose-only observations.
findings.failure_scenario: A holdout uses the quoted word uppercase, lastVerify.notes contains the private observation "Blank input retained stale rows.", and the report quotes those notes outside its holdout section. Another report line contains percent-encoded uppercase. Previously the report was withheld; now only the encoded-word line is withheld and the private observation is returned.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, surrounding privacy logic, paging, and tests; found no concrete defects. git diff --check passed. Targeted MCP tests could not run because dependencies are missing, including @modelcontextprotocol/sdk.

Found two reproducible defects in merge handling. Notifier and review-schema checks passed (65 tests). MCP, land-queue and HTTP suites were blocked by missing SDK dependencies; lint/typecheck were blocked by local tooling permissions and missing Bun types. Checkout unchanged.

findings.title: Preserve cancellation across the metadata lookup
findings.detail: The new await creates a cancellation window. cancel() returns true and records cancelled, but aborting the lookup is swallowed by catch(() => null), after which landed() unconditionally overwrites the entry. Targeted command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-land-cancel.ts"` failed with output `state after cancel: cancelled`, `state after metadata lookup: landed`, and `AssertionError: actual 'landed', expected 'cancelled'`.
findings.suggestion: Re-read the entry after the lookup and conditionally finalize it, preserving terminal queue states while recording confirmed merge evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: The GitHub merge succeeds; its metadata lookup remains pending; the user cancels the land; the lookup rejects on abort; the cancelled entry becomes landed.

findings.title: Complete metadata in the parent merge feed event
findings.detail: When the post-merge lookup fails or lacks metadata, this update emits the parent's run.merged event with null fields. Later reconciliation fills the Run columns only; the feed event remains incorrect permanently, leaving the requested accuracy issue unresolved. Targeted command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-merge-feed.ts"` failed: `parent run metadata: {"mergedBy":"owner","mergedAt":1791892800000}` versus `parent run.merged metadata: {"mergedBy":null,"mergedAt":null}`.
findings.suggestion: Ensure metadata completion also corrects the existing merge feed payload without emitting duplicate merge events, and assert its fields in the delayed-observation test.
findings.failure_scenario: A review-round land succeeds with a null metadata observation. The next poll records the merger and timestamp, but the parent's run.merged feed item still contains null for both fields.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding paths; 80 targeted tests passed. Missing MCP SDK dependencies blocked four test files; missing tooling/types blocked lint and typecheck. A controlled probe reproduced a cancellation regression.

findings.title: Preserve cancellation after the merge metadata lookup
findings.detail: The new await introduces a cancellation window. Its catch swallows the abort, then landed() unconditionally overwrites the cancelled entry and emits land.landed. Reproduction command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/merge-metadata-cancel.test.ts"`. Output: `state after aborted metadata fetch: landed`, followed by `Expected: "cancelled"` and `Received: "landed"`.
findings.suggestion: Propagate cancellation after the lookup and condition the final transition on the entry still being in the expected active state.
findings.failure_scenario: A merge succeeds, the subsequent metadata request remains pending, and the user cancels the land. cancel() returns true and aborts the request, but the catch converts that abort to null and the entry changes from cancelled to landed.

output.summary: Found two landing regressions with failing focused probes. All 62 GitHub notifier tests passed. Four other test files, lint, and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies or sandbox restrictions. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Publish landing notifications after the outer transaction commits
findings.detail: The new outer transaction suppresses publishFeed(): both landFeed() and resolveMergedRun() attempt publication while db.inTransaction is true, and nothing flushes after commit. When awaitCi() observes an already-merged PR, there is no subsequent metadata update to flush these items. Feed subscribers miss the landing until another write; long polls wait until timeout. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-landing-probe.ts" feed. Output: persisted: ["land.landed","run.merged"]; notifications: [{"kind":"run","feed":null,"inTransaction":true}]; AssertionError: landing must publish its committed run.merged feed item.
findings.suggestion: Move the atomic landing operation into a Store transaction that buffers notifications and publishes them after the outermost commit.
findings.failure_scenario: CI observation returns MERGED with complete metadata, landing records its transaction, and no unrelated store write follows. Feed subscribers receive neither land.landed nor run.merged.

findings.title: Preserve merge recording for failed and cancelled runs
findings.detail: Replacing updateRun({merged:true}) with resolveMergedRun() silently stops recording merges for failed or cancelled runs: that helper only handles succeeded, resolved, and needs_human statuses. Land requests do not exclude failed or cancelled runs with delivered PRs. The queue now reports landed while the run remains unmerged, loses merge metadata, and continues blocking dependents. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-landing-probe.ts" failed-run. Output: {"entry":"landed","status":"failed","merged":false,"mergedBy":null}; AssertionError: a confirmed queue merge must mark the run merged.
findings.suggestion: Record confirmed merge fields independently of run status, preserving failed or cancelled status and terminal evidence where appropriate.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed or cancelled run retains a delivered PR and is landed using an approved SHA. GitHub confirms the merge, but its run remains merged:false.

output.summary: Found three reproducible regressions. Eighty existing targeted tests passed; four temporary regression checks failed. Broader integration checks were blocked by missing MCP SDK and incompatible Zod dependencies. Repository files were unchanged.

findings.title: Publish landing notifications after the outer transaction commits
findings.detail: The new outer transaction suppresses every nested publishFeed() call because Store skips publication while db.inTransaction is true. Nothing flushes after this transaction commits. Consequently, run.merged and land.landed are persisted without notifying subscribers. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/review-512.test.ts". Output: 'landing publishes its committed merge and land feed items' failed with Expected to contain: "run.merged"; Received: [].
findings.suggestion: Record landing through a Store transaction helper that buffers notifications and publishes them after the outermost commit.
findings.failure_scenario: A resumed queue entry observes an already merged PR and calls landed(). Feed subscribers receive neither merge nor landing notification until an unrelated Store operation flushes the feed.

findings.title: Preserve merge evidence for failed and cancelled runs
findings.detail: Replacing unconditional updateRun({ merged: true }) with resolveMergedRun() loses merge recording for statuses that resolver refuses, including failed and cancelled. LandQueue.request() does not exclude these statuses. The entry becomes landed while the run remains merged:false, and subsequent metadata enrichment does nothing. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/review-512.test.ts". Both failed-run and cancelled-run checks produced Expected: true; Received: false.
findings.suggestion: Record the confirmed merge flag and metadata for every status the queue accepts, preserving terminal status and evidence where resolution is inappropriate.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed or cancelled run retains an open PR, which is explicitly approved and landed. Its land entry says landed, but its run and feed never record the confirmed merge.

findings.title: Encode consumer provenance before forwarding to older daemons
findings.detail: The parsed MCP input retains consumer and forwards it to the daemon. The base release's strict ReviewVerdictSchema rejects that unknown field, so a newer CLI cannot submit a named MCP approval to the previous daemon. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/review-512.test.ts". Validation against the actual base schema returned 'Unrecognized key(s) in object: consumer', followed by Expected: true; Received: false.
findings.suggestion: Translate consumer into the existing reviewer field at the MCP boundary and omit consumer from the HTTP payload, accounting for the previous reviewer length limit.
findings.failure_scenario: The updated limitless mcp CLI connects to a daemon running the base release and calls limitless_review with consumer:"agent-a". The daemon returns HTTP 400 instead of recording the approval.

output.summary: The patch probe passed added-file redaction and public-neighbor preservation. A separate probe confirmed a remaining credential leak through report diffs. Targeted repository tests could not start because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing.

findings.title: Cover report diffs or record the required follow-up
findings.detail: The new filter protects diff.text, but persisted reports still receive literal privacy filtering. A fenced unified diff containing +alpha and +beta exposes both halves of registered credential alpha\nbeta through reports[].text. The request explicitly requires covering other diff-rendering paths or listing them as follow-ups; neither was done. A dependency-free probe executing the actual getChange function with injected collaborators and real privacy functions confirmed this. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-report-path.ts". Output: "actual getChange diff leaks: false false", "actual getChange report leaks: true true", then "AssertionError: getChange report exposes both registered credential lines".
findings.suggestion: Apply prefix-aware credential redaction to report diff blocks before paging, or explicitly document this concrete leak as a follow-up as permitted by the request.
findings.failure_scenario: Register alpha\nbeta and persist report.md containing a fenced diff with consecutive +alpha and +beta lines. limitless_get_change returns both credential halves in reports[].text.

output.summary: The basic multiline case passes an isolated check, but two privacy leaks remain. Targeted repository tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies/tooling. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Truncated hunk annotations still expose credential text
findings.detail: Git truncates the function annotation in a hunk header, but this scan matches only complete credential components. A long component therefore leaks its prefix. An isolated harness using the exact helper and patch renderer, with a real Git diff, reproduced this. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-multiline.ts" header. Output included `@@ -7,6 +7,6 @@ header-secret-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `AssertionError: truncated credential prefix survives in hunk annotation`. This pre-existing leak remains unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Strip function annotations from hunk headers, or handle their truncation conservatively. Add a regression with a credential component longer than Git's annotation limit.
findings.failure_scenario: Register a credential whose first line exceeds 80 characters and whose second line is indented. Change an indented line several lines below it. Git quotes a truncated first credential line in the hunk header, and the change view returns it.

findings.title: Unsafe decoding leaves adjacent credential lines visible
findings.detail: When normalizedLayers returns null, the raw fallback loses decoded forms needed to recognize a multiline credential. The ordinary privacy filter withholds the undecodable line, but the remaining credential line survives. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-multiline.ts" unsafe. The exact helper/renderer harness returned `[withheld: private text; 1 line]\n+unsafe-beta-secret\n+public after` and `AssertionError: second credential line survives unsafe decoding of first line`. This pre-existing leak remains unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Fail closed for the affected hunk when decoding cannot settle, or retain sufficient decoded spans to withhold every contributing credential line. Add coverage for this decoding-limit case.
findings.failure_scenario: [redacted diagnostic]

output.summary: Found a reproducible routing-policy regression involving setup variants. Prompt tests passed using the available Zod v4 entry point. Normal targeted tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Keep setup variants separate when selecting routing evidence
findings.detail: Adding setup creates distinct configurations that can both satisfy policy.ts's standard-single-system filter for the same target. selectEvidence pools both arms, but generatePolicy takes only the first arm's summary while calculating costs and completeCases from both. Each case then has 2k trials, so completeCases rejects every case and policy generation reports insufficient evidence. Probe: `bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod4.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup-policy.test.ts"` used existing policy fixtures with 40 passing cases per arm. Output: `summaryTrials: 40, costDenominator: 80, pairedCases: 0, state: "insufficient evidence"`; assertion failed with `Expected: 40; Received: 0`. The preload selects the installed Zod v4 entry point without changing application code.
findings.suggestion: Select exactly one compatible system configuration per target for routing evidence, and use that system's trials consistently for summaries, costs and paired comparisons. Add coverage for standard systems with and without setup in one eval.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed review eval contains two standard single systems using the same model and implementer-report setting, one with setup:true and one without setup. Generating routing policy mixes their trials and loses all complete paired cases.

findings.title: Restore committed source after gate setup
findings.detail: The reviewer starts without discarding changes made by setup. Production gates and prepareImplement restore the committed tree afterward. Install hooks or generators can therefore repair or alter the defect before review probes execute, while the prompt still describes the original committed diff. The isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/setup-tree-probe.ts"` ran real setup with fake confinement and failed its preservation assertion: output was `{"setupOk":true,"sourceAfterSetup":"repaired","status":"M target.ts"}`.
findings.suggestion: Restore tracked source after successful setup using the existing discardChanges path, preserving installed ignored dependencies. Add a fake-harness test that verifies the reviewer sees committed source after setup modifies it.
findings.failure_scenario: A base setup command invokes an install hook or generator that overwrites a tracked file containing a gold defect. The readonly reviewer probes the overwritten file and incorrectly concludes that the committed defect does not reproduce.

findings.title: Keep setup variants distinct when selecting policy evidence

output.summary: Found two reproduced retry defects. All 32 focused retry-file tests passed. Broader tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies. The worktree was unchanged.

findings.title: Pass exact file paths instead of Bun substring filters
findings.detail: Bun interprets `test/a.test.ts` as a substring filter, so the generated retry also executes `test/a.test.ts.other.test.ts`. Those extra files are excluded from the file-count and duration calculation that authorizes skipping the gate slot. Reproduction command: `LIMITLESS_REVIEW_ROOT="$PWD" bun test /private/tmp/lr-NBt80d/claude-501/review-targeted.w3OUVy/retry.test.ts`. Output included `(pass) UNSELECTED_FILE`, `Ran 2 tests across 2 files`, and `error: expect(received).not.toContain(expected)`.
findings.suggestion: Prefix every substituted relative path with `./` so Bun selects exact files, and cover overlapping filenames with a real-runner test.
findings.failure_scenario: The report lists only test/a.test.ts, but other test paths contain that substring. The supposedly bounded retry runs those additional files without accounting for their count or duration.

findings.title: Preserve process isolation in targeted retries
findings.detail: The full check uses `--parallel`, which isolates test files in separate processes; the targeted command drops it. Files can consequently share module or environment state and produce a new failure that immediately confirms a regression. Reproduction command: `LIMITLESS_REVIEW_ROOT="$PWD" bun test /private/tmp/lr-NBt80d/claude-501/review-targeted.w3OUVy/retry.test.ts`. Two initial file failures cleared on retry, but shared environment state caused an isolation failure. Output showed `"verdict":"regressed"`, `"fullExitCode":0`, and `Expected: "flaky" / Received: "regressed"`.
findings.suggestion: Retain the full check's `--parallel` isolation and worker configuration in retry_files.
findings.failure_scenario: Two files fail transiently under the full parallel check. Their targeted retry runs in one process, where one file's environment mutation breaks the other. The factory confirms a regression and skips the full rerun, although the full check passes.

output.summary: Reviewed retry execution, configuration trust, classification and JUnit parsing. All 32 retry-file tests passed. Feedback/executor tests could not load because local dependencies were missing or incompatible. A real Bun probe reproduced an incorrect file-selection bug.

findings.title: Pass explicit paths so Bun retries only the selected files
findings.detail: Bun treats arguments without a leading './' as substring filters. The generated command therefore runs additional matching files, exceeding the file-count and duration bounds used to bypass the gate slot. With a passing a.test.ts and failing extra.test.ts, the exact command `bun test 'a.test.ts'` exited 1 with `(fail) unselected fails` and `Ran 2 tests across 2 files.` The command `bun test './a.test.ts'` exited 0 with `Ran 1 test across 1 file.`
findings.suggestion: Prefix every selected relative path with './' before shell quoting. Add a real Bun regression test with overlapping filenames that verifies only the selected file executes.
findings.failure_scenario: JUnit identifies a.test.ts as the only failing file and records a short duration. The targeted retry also executes extra.test.ts and any other matching paths, potentially running expensive tests outside the gate slot or confirming an unrelated failure.

output.summary: Reviewed the permitted pairing/heartbeat split and found two security defects through focused temporary regression checks. Repository tests and typecheck were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies; sandbox restrictions prevented loopback TLS testing. No repository files changed.

findings.title: Bind pairing confirmation to the TLS identities
findings.detail: The worker displays the coordinator-supplied random code without binding it to either certificate. A TLS-terminating relay can forward pairing and claim requests, preserve matching codes on both displays, capture the approved token, and cause the worker to pin the relay's certificate. The simulated-transport regression command `bun test "$TMPDIR/worker-protocol-review.test.ts"` printed `codes_match=true; worker_pinned_attacker=true; attacker_has_approved_token=true` and failed with `error: expect(received).toBeNull()` because the intercepted token authenticated successfully.
findings.suggestion: Derive and independently verify the confirmation code from both certificate fingerprints and the pairing transcript, or require an independently verified coordinator fingerprint before pairing.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the first pairing connection, terminates TLS, and relays requests to the real coordinator. The owner compares identical codes and approves, granting the attacker usable worker credentials.

findings.title: Protect the persisted TLS key when the listener is disabled
findings.detail: Returning before certificate initialization also skips registering the TLS key's read denial. After a restart with workers.listen unset, the existing key remains on disk but is absent from editor sandbox deny lists. Mode 0600 does not protect it from agents running as the same user. The regression command `bun test "$TMPDIR/worker-protocol-review.test.ts"` printed `listener_disabled=true; persisted_tls_key_read_denied=false` and failed with `Expected: true` / `Received: false` when checking the generated editor read policy.
findings.suggestion: Register protection for persisted worker secrets before agents start, independently of whether the worker listener is enabled, and retain it for the daemon's lifetime.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner enables workers, pairs machines, then disables the listener and restarts. An untrusted editor can read worker-tls/key.pem and steal the coordinator identity that existing workers have pinned.

output.summary: Reviewed the permitted pairing/heartbeat split and found two security defects. Focused probes confirmed both. Targeted tests could not load because of missing/incompatible dependencies; real loopback TLS testing was blocked by the sandbox's listen restriction. Diff checks passed; checkout unchanged.

findings.title: Bind pairing approval to the authenticated certificates
findings.detail: The first request accepts any TLS certificate, then trusts its fingerprint. The displayed code is a random server value that a relay can forward unchanged. The worker certificate fingerprint is merely stored; claiming the token requires no proof of its private key. A relay can therefore pass the owner's code comparison, receive the approved token, and leave the worker pinned to the relay. A transport-level relay probe (`bun "$TMPDIR/worker-pair-relay-probe.ts"`) produced: `Genuine owner/worker codes match: true`, `Worker pinned attacker certificate: true`, and `Relay obtained an approved bearer token: true`.
findings.suggestion: Cryptographically bind the compared code to both certificate identities and require proof of the worker's private key before releasing its token, or require an independently verified coordinator fingerprint.
findings.failure_scenario: An active network attacker intercepts initial pairing, terminates TLS with its own certificate, and relays the real coordinator's pairing responses. The owner approves the matching code, and the attacker obtains the worker token.

findings.title: Protect persisted worker credentials independently of process lifetime
findings.detail: Read protection is registered only in the process opening each file and disappears on release. The built-in editor deny list does not cover these paths. Consequently, a daemon started with the worker listener disabled exposes an existing coordinator key to editors; a daemon sharing a worker's home also lacks that separate worker process's token protections. The policy probe (`bun "$TMPDIR/worker-read-policy-probe.ts"`) reported `denied:true` for the key, token and fingerprint while registrations were held, then `denied:false` for all three after release. Mode 0600 does not protect against agents running as the same user.
findings.suggestion: Register stable worker credential paths during factory confinement initialization, including custom data directories, regardless of whether the listener or worker loop is active. Add coverage for fresh processes and disabled listeners.
findings.failure_scenario: Pair a worker or enable the coordinator listener once, then start a normal daemon using the same data directory without that component active. An editor can read the persisted token or TLS private key.

output.summary: Reviewed the permitted pairing-and-heartbeat split. Focused store checks passed, but certificate generation produced unusable TLS material on macOS. The targeted suite could not start because dependencies were missing or incompatible; loopback binding was also unavailable.

findings.title: Generate EC keys with named-curve encoding on macOS
findings.detail: macOS system LibreSSL 3.3.6 defaults to explicit EC parameters, which Bun rejects with ERR_OSSL_EC_DECODE_ERROR. Consequently, enabling workers.listen prevents the daemon from starting. A temporary probe calls certificate() and asserts that createSecureContext accepts its output. Command: `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/worker-review-tls-probe.ts"`. Output: `AssertionError: Got unwanted exception: certificate() must generate TLS material Bun can load; Actual message: "error:0f000080:elliptic curve routines:OPENSSL_internal:DECODE_ERROR"`. An independent probe adding named-curve encoding successfully created the TLS context.
findings.suggestion: Add `-pkeyopt ec_param_enc:named_curve` to certificate generation and cover compatibility with macOS system LibreSSL.
findings.failure_scenario: On macOS with /usr/bin/openssl first on PATH and no existing worker certificate, configure workers.listen and start the daemon. Certificate generation succeeds, but Bun.serve rejects the generated key and startup fails.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff as the explicitly permitted pairing-and-heartbeats slice. Found a reproducible TLS initialization failure that permanently blocks subsequent startup. Targeted tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing/incompatible dependencies; loopback TLS testing was blocked by sandbox port restrictions. The worktree remains unchanged.

findings.title: Failed certificate generation permanently blocks startup
findings.detail: The function publishes an empty key.pem before invoking OpenSSL, but its catch only releases read protection. A generation failure leaves partial material that every subsequent attempt rejects. With workers.listen enabled, this also prevents the entire coordinator daemon from starting. Injecting an OpenSSL command that exits 1 reproduced this; retrying with working OpenSSL returned "Incomplete worker TLS material". Minimal restart-state reproduction: `bun -e 'import {mkdtempSync,writeFileSync,rmSync} from "node:fs"; import {tmpdir} from "node:os"; import {join} from "node:path"; import {certificate} from "./src/workers/tls.ts"; const dir=mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),"worker-cert-restart-")); writeFileSync(join(dir,"key.pem"),""); try { for(let i=1;i<=2;i++) { try { (await certificate(dir)).release(); } catch(e) { console.log(`attempt ${i}: ${e.message}`); } } } finally { rmSync(dir,{recursive:true,force:true}); }'` Output: `attempt 1: Incomplete worker TLS material\nattempt 2: Incomplete worker TLS material`.
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate TLS material in protected staging files, publish only completed material, and clean up failed initialization without replacing an established identity. Add a failed-generation-and-restart regression test.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenSSL fails, times out, or the process stops after key.pem is created but before cert.pem is completed. Every later daemon startup with the worker listener enabled fails until someone manually repairs the files.

output.summary: Found two defects in worker cleanup and retry evidence handling. Focused probes reproduced both. Targeted repository tests could not load because dependencies are missing or incompatible; Biome was unavailable. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Preserve the process-termination safety boundary for worker jobs
findings.detail: Worker gates run without a processScope. Consequently, runProcess cannot latch a terminationError, scratch cleanup proceeds after unconfirmed shutdown, and the catch at line 234 swallows the error so the worker can accept more jobs. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-lifecycle.ts". Output: Worker-style unscoped gate cleanup: {"error":"Invocation termination could not be confirmed: injected process inspection failure","hasProcessScope":false,"scratchPreserved":false}. The pipeline deliberately preserves these directories and blocks further commands in this condition.
findings.suggestion: Give worker jobs a process scope, propagate termination failures, preserve their checkout and scratch, and stop accepting work when descendant shutdown cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate leaves a surviving descendant, or process inspection fails during cleanup. The worker removes its directories and starts subsequent work while the previous writer may still be running.

findings.title: Retain failing check evidence across infrastructure retries
findings.detail: The executor returns only the final attempt's GateRun, ignoring failed checks already accepted into job.events. A worker can report a genuine check failure, disconnect, and have another worker's successful retry classified as a clean pass without firstAttempt evidence. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-lifecycle.ts". Output: Reported failure then infrastructure retry: {"verdict":"pass","blocking":false,"firstAttempt":null,"storedEvents":2}. This violates the requirement that infrastructure retries never turn a failing check into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Track check results by attempt and retain previously reported failures in the final result and classification, including when execution falls back locally.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts a failing check event and disconnects before posting its final result. Worker B retries the same job and passes; the coordinator reports a clean pass and loses the failure from its gate verdict.

output.summary: Found two reproduced defects affecting gate verdicts and worker safety. Targeted repository tests could not load because dependencies are missing or incompatible. Isolated regression checks failed as described below; diff whitespace checks passed.

findings.title: Preserve distinct check identities through privacy filtering
findings.detail: Sanitizing the validated GateRun can replace distinct check names with the same placeholder. compareGates then matches both against the first baseline check, allowing a new regression to become nonblocking. Reproduction command: REVIEW_REPO_ROOT="$PWD" bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-private-identities.ts". Output: `Stored names: ["[withheld: private text]","[withheld: private text]"]`; local verdicts were `still_failing, regressed`, but LAN verdicts were `still_failing, still_failing`, both nonblocking. The assertion failed: `A new regression must remain blocking after privacy filtering`.
findings.suggestion: Use stable, collision-free check identities for comparison, or reject results whose identities collide after privacy filtering. Keep identifying data separate from redacted display text.
findings.failure_scenario: The private-string policy contains example.internal. Checks named example.internal-lint and example.internal-tests have baseline outcomes fail/pass and candidate outcomes fail/fail. Both stored names collapse to one placeholder, hiding the tests regression.

findings.title: Stop worker execution when process termination cannot be confirmed
findings.detail: Worker jobs run without a processScope. Consequently, a ProcessTerminationError cannot latch the existing cleanup guard: this catch reports an ordinary infrastructure failure, finally deletes the checkout and scratch, and the worker accepts another job. Reproduction command: REVIEW_REPO_ROOT="$PWD" bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-termination.ts". Injecting process-inspection failure produced `{"secondJobCompleted":true,"processScopePresent":false,"failedJobScratchExists":false,"failedJobCheckoutExists":false}` and failed the assertion `Worker must stop accepting jobs after an unconfirmed process termination`.
findings.suggestion: Run jobs within the process lifecycle scope, preserve directories when termination is unconfirmed, and stop accepting work on ProcessTerminationError.
findings.failure_scenario: Process inspection fails during gate shutdown, leaving descendant termination unconfirmed. The worker removes the failed job's directories and executes another job while descendants may still be running.

findings.title: Keep the smoke probe outside agent-writable scratch
findings.detail: The reader can overwrite probe.mjs because scratch is writable. Matching the requested command therefore does not prove bun test ran: replacing the script with a print of its embedded success marker produces a pass. An isolated reproduction using the actual probe and evidence functions, run with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-586-probe.ts"`, printed `Smoke result with invalid test and replaced probe: {"status":"pass"}` and failed with `AssertionError: smoke must reject a probe that never executes bun test` (`'pass' !== 'fail'`).
findings.suggestion: Place the trusted runner in the read-only cwd, keep the test fixture in scratch, and add a regression covering attempted probe replacement.
