output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding sandbox code. Lint and 14 focused tests passed using temporary dependency mappings. Broader checks encountered missing dependencies and sandbox restrictions; nested Seatbelt checks were unavailable.

findings.title: Use a supervisor compatible with Claude’s process restrictions
findings.detail: The bundled runProcess performs cleanup even after a successful child exit. That cleanup calls darwinCallerAncestors and enumerates other user processes. Claude’s macOS sandbox allows process-info only for targets in the same sandbox, so inspecting the unsandboxed Claude ancestor fails and runProcess rejects with ProcessTerminationError before emitting the success marker. Consequently, the new smoke check can fail despite Bun successfully running its assertion. The fake-harness tests execute this supervisor outside Claude’s sandbox and miss this incompatibility.
findings.suggestion: Use a bounded supervisor that manages only its owned Bun child without inspecting outside processes, and exercise that supervisor in the real sandbox regression check.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the new Claude Bun smoke check on macOS. The one-assertion test passes, but cleanup attempts to inspect an ancestor outside the Bash sandbox and rejects, causing smoke verification to fail.

output.summary: Outcome writes are guarded, but two isolated probes reproduced merge and push commands issued after claim loss. Repository tests, lint, and typecheck were blocked by missing SDK, Biome, and Bun type dependencies. The worktree was unchanged.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge and push helpers
findings.detail: The ownership checks precede asynchronous helpers that still await preflight work before issuing commands. mergePullRequest awaits its PR lookup; pushExistingBranch (called at line 522) awaits git lookups. Reclaiming during those waits still allows the old worker to merge or push. The check after mergePullRequest returns only prevents subsequent writes. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/land-claim-boundaries.test.ts". Both assertions expecting no commands failed: output included `merge commands after reclaim: [["gh","pr","merge",...]]` and `push commands after reclaim: [["git","push",...]]`, ending with `0 pass`, `2 fail`. This leaves a pre-existing race required by this request unresolved.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership validator into both helpers and check it after preflight awaits, immediately before each mutating command, including retry attempts. Add deferred tests at these internal boundaries.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker passes the queue's ownership check, then pauses during mergePullRequest's PR lookup or pushExistingBranch's remote lookup. Another owner reclaims the entry. Releasing the lookup before the next heartbeat still issues the merge or push.

output.summary: Outcome writes are guarded, but workers can still push or merge after losing ownership. An isolated probe confirmed both races. Repository tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies or sandbox restrictions.

findings.title: Ownership checks precede further awaits inside push and merge helpers
findings.detail:
The ownership transaction finishes before mergePullRequest awaits its fresh `gh pr view`; that helper then issues `gh pr merge` without checking ownership again. Likewise, pushApproved checks ownership before pushExistingBranch awaits commit resolution, transport preparation, ls-remote and merge-base, then pushes unchecked. Reclaiming during those awaits still permits the old worker's command before its next heartbeat. The new tests defer helper completion rather than these internal preparation steps. A source-isolated probe executing the current queue and helper method bodies with deferred command mocks confirmed both paths. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/land-claim-boundary-probe.ts"`. Output: `merge commands issued after reclaim: 1
push commands issued after reclaim: 1
AssertionError: A worker that lost its claim must issue no merge or push
2 !== 0`.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the push and merge helpers and check it after their preparation awaits, immediately before each remote mutation, including retries. Add deferred preparation tests for both helpers.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker passes its ownership check, then awaits the merge helper's PR lookup or the push helper's ancestry check. Another worker reclaims the entry. Releasing the awaited response before the heartbeat causes the old worker to issue a merge or push despite losing its claim.

output.summary: Found an incomplete push-ownership guard and a recovery cleanup regression, both reproduced with source-extracted functions and fake dependencies. Repository tests could not start because entities is missing; lint and typecheck were also blocked by missing Biome and Bun types.

findings.title: Recheck ownership before every push attempt
findings.detail: The guard runs once before remoteSh, whose withGitHubRetry loop can await a failed push and backoff, then push again without checking ownership. The requested stale-worker protection therefore remains incomplete. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/claim-review-repro.ts" push. The source-extracted reproduction printed `push attempted after reclaim: true` and `{"guards":1,"pushes":2,"owned":false}`, then failed with `AssertionError: stale worker must not retry a push after reclaim` and `2 !== 1`.
findings.suggestion: Carry the guard to the actual push execution boundary and invoke it immediately before every attempt, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The first push fails transiently with HTTP 502, another worker reclaims the entry, and the retry runs before the old worker's next heartbeat. The old worker still issues a push.

findings.title: Clean up the previous attempt on merged recovery
findings.detail: Attempt-specific paths change the early MERGED recovery branch: it now discards the newly claimed attempt's nonexistent path, leaving the crashed attempt's checkout and Git registration behind. Cleanup of older attempts exists only in checkout(), which this branch bypasses. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/land-cleanup-review-repro.ts". The source-extracted reproduction printed `worktrees remaining after merged recovery: ["land-1-1"]`, then failed with `AssertionError: merged recovery must clean up the crashed attempt checkout`.
findings.suggestion: Reuse ownership-guarded cleanup of previous attempts, including legacy paths, before returning from merged recovery.
findings.failure_scenario: Attempt 1 crashes after GitHub merges but before cleanup. Attempt 2 observes MERGED and removes land-1-2, leaving land-1-1 permanently because the entry is now terminal.

output.summary: Found an unclosed claim-loss race in push retries. A temporary fake-transport probe reproduced it. Repository tests could not start because entities is missing; lint and typecheck were blocked by missing Biome and Bun types. Worktree unchanged.

findings.title: Validate ownership on every push retry
findings.detail: The new guard runs once before remoteSh, which internally retries through withGitHubRetry. If ownership changes while the first push is pending or during backoff, another push runs before the heartbeat aborts the signal. This leaves the original request's prohibition on stale-worker pushes unmet. The fake-transport probe command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/claim-push-probe.ts"` failed with output: `push attempt 1: owns claim = true`; `push attempt 2: owns claim = false`; `{"guards":1,"pushes":2,"owned":false}`; `ASSERTION FAILED: stale worker retried push after claim loss`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the ownership guard to every actual push attempt, after preparatory awaits, and add a regression test that reclaims ownership between a transient failure and its retry.
findings.failure_scenario: A push fails transiently with HTTP 502, another owner reclaims the entry, and the retry occurs before the old worker's next heartbeat. The old worker can still publish its commit.

output.summary: Found missing UI visibility, a reproduced digest regression, and an unsupported restriction on fork PRs. Interpreted the requested open-PR support as including forks. Passed 64 existing tests; queue/CI tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies/tooling. No repository files changed.

findings.title: Keep blocked unowned lands in the digest
findings.detail: The new land entries emit feed items with runId=null, but the digest deletes every such item. Operators therefore receive no digest notification when a manual land blocks. Reproduction command: `env TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-iFsgXE/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-iFsgXE/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-iFsgXE/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-iFsgXE/claude-501/manual-land-digest.test.ts`. Output: Expected: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 1"; Received: "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0".
findings.suggestion: Reconcile unowned land items against current land entries by PR URL or entry ID instead of requiring a run.
findings.failure_scenario: A manual PR's checks fail, producing a blocked land and a land.blocked feed item with no runId; limitless digest reports zero blocked lands.

findings.title: Expose unowned land entries in the UI
findings.detail: The requested UI visibility is absent. Dashboard renders only live.runs, the UI never fetches /api/land, and these entries deliberately create no run. Consequently an unowned land is invisible in every state, including blocked.
findings.suggestion: Add UI rendering backed by land entries, including state, PR link, failure reason and an indication that no run owns the entry.
findings.failure_scenario: Queue a manual PR, then open the UI: no row represents its queued, checking, blocked or landed state.

findings.title: Support open fork PRs on configured repositories
findings.detail: This unconditional rejection excludes PRs opened from forks even when their destination repository is configured and the caller approves the exact current SHA. The request permits open PRs on configured repositories and does not exclude forks; the added refusal test codifies that unsupported restriction.
findings.suggestion: Resolve and validate the PR's head repository, then fetch and push through that repository while preserving the approval lease and exact-head merge checks.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targets a configured repository from a contributor's fork; limitless land with its full current SHA immediately throws "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, approval flow, persistence, restart paths, and UI integration. Seven store tests passed, and a direct probe confirmed unowned entries queue and emit feed events. Queue, migration, CI-classifier, typecheck, and lint checks were blocked by missing dependencies or sandbox restrictions.

findings.title: Unowned land entries are invisible in the UI
findings.detail: The request explicitly requires these entries to appear in the UI. This path creates an entry without a run, but the UI only renders runs: ui/store.ts never fetches /api/land, and Dashboard.tsx renders live.runs. No UI component consumes LandEntry or displays land feed events. Consequently, queued, blocked, and completed manual lands have no visible UI entry.
findings.suggestion: Add UI state and rendering for land entries independently of runs, including their state, refusal reason, PR link, and lack of an owning run.
findings.failure_scenario: Queue a hand-made PR through limitless land with its full SHA, then open the dashboard. The entry appears in land list and the feed but remains absent from the UI, including when its confined checks fail.

output.summary: Confirmed a crash-recovery gap with a real subprocess reproduction. Existing targeted tests: 27 passed; three startup/resume tests could not run because the MCP SDK dependency is missing. Repository files were unchanged.

findings.title: Resume discovery before declaring invocation cleanup complete
findings.detail: Recovery kills only recorded members and then deletes the journal without rescanning the invocation. A descendant forked between the last inspection and SIGSTOP is therefore lost if the daemon crashes before the next sweep. Confirmed with `bun "$TMPDIR/cleanup-fork-window.ts"`: output was `{"nextStepExitCode":0,"stdout":"next-step","pendingRecords":0,"lateDescendantStillAlive":true}`, followed by `error: ASSERTION FAILED: next step ran while an invocation descendant survived recovery`. That survivor can continue writing while the resumed run proceeds.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation context to resume discovery and freeze sweeps, and retain the cleanup record until the complete invocation is confirmed stopped. Add a crash test with a descendant forked after inspection and before freezing.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked process forks after its identity is recorded but before SIGSTOP. The cleanup supervisor dies after freezing that parent, before rescanning. Recovery kills the recorded parent, clears the journal, and starts the next command while the unrecorded child remains running.

output.summary: Eight cleanup tests and 19 proc tests passed. A targeted crash reproduction exposed a surviving descendant after recovery reported success. Missing dependencies blocked integration and hardening tests; environment/dependency errors blocked lint and typecheck.

findings.title: Finish the ownership sweep before declaring recovery complete
findings.detail: Recovery kills only recorded members and then deletes the invocation record. A member can fork after the live ownership snapshot but before SIGSTOP; crashing before the next scan leaves that descendant unrecorded. Recovery then permits another command while the previous writer survives. Targeted command `bun "$TMPDIR/cleanup-late-fork.ts"` exited 1 with output: `late descendant recorded: false\nnext command: 0 next-step pending: 0 late descendant alive: true\nAssertionError: unrecorded descendant must be dead before the next step runs`.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation metadata to resume the freeze/rescan cleanup, identity-check and record newly discovered members, and clear the record only after confirming shutdown. Add a crash regression covering a fork between the snapshot and SIGSTOP.
findings.failure_scenario: An invocation forks a detached child after the cleanup snapshot. The supervisor freezes the recorded parent and crashes before rescanning. Recovery kills the parent, clears all records, and starts the next command while the detached child remains able to write to the checkout.

output.summary: Reviewed the workflow, helper, and test setup. The marker test passes; Linux timeout tests skipped because GNU timeout is unavailable. A monitor-focused reproduction exposed incomplete child cleanup. Lint and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies.

findings.title: Timeout cleanup leaves detached descendants running
findings.detail: Both TERM and final KILL target only the timeout process group. The suite's runProcess implementation routinely launches children with detached: true, so these descendants escape both signals when their test worker is killed. The monitor-focused command `python3 "$TMPDIR/ci-detached-repro.py"`, with only sandbox-denied ps stubbed, printed `detached child alive after TERM and final process-group KILL: True` and failed with `AssertionError: timeout cleanup leaves a detached child alive`. This misses the requested child-cleanup behavior.
findings.suggestion: Track and terminate descendants across process groups, and extend the timeout regression test with a detached child.
findings.failure_scenario: A hanging test has a subprocess started through runProcess or spawn with detached: true. The deadline kills the test worker's group, but the detached subprocess remains running.

output.summary: Reviewed the workflow, timeout helper, and test setup. The marker test passed; Linux timeout tests skipped because this host is macOS without GNU timeout. A focused cleanup reproduction exposed surviving detached children. Sandbox restrictions blocked real ps and lint; typecheck lacked Bun type definitions.

findings.title: Timeout cleanup misses detached test subprocesses
findings.detail: Both the TERM handler and final KILL target only the timeout's process group. However, src/util/proc.ts launches subprocesses with detached: true, placing them outside that group. Killing Bun prevents its normal descendant cleanup, leaving those subprocesses running. A focused reproduction exercised --monitor and the identical final group kill, with ps stubbed because the sandbox denies it. Command: python3 "$TMPDIR/ci-detached-review.py". Output: "monitor printed tree: True", "detached child alive after TERM and final group KILL: True", followed by "AssertionError: CI cleanup leaves a detached subprocess running". The full GNU timeout wrapper could not run on this host.
findings.suggestion: Extend cleanup to descendants in separate process groups, using the pre-termination process snapshot to retain their identities. Add a regression fixture that starts a detached child and verifies it stops.
findings.failure_scenario: A test hangs while awaiting a subprocess launched through sh/runProcess. At the deadline, the wrapper kills the test runner's process group, but the detached subprocess remains alive and can retain resources and inherited output descriptors.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and feedback/publication paths. Found a reproducible gap for coloured gate logs. Passed 26 targeted cases using temporary bundles and available dependency versions; normal test execution was blocked by missing dependencies, and pipeline tests remain unverified.

findings.title: Include coloured terminal logs in the large-text warning
findings.detail: The reviewable filter rejects ANSI escape bytes, excluding ordinary captured gate output from headTextSizes even though it remains in headTextPaths and receives no binary blocker. The size rule consequently treats it as zero bytes and emits no warning. A temporary real-git fixture containing a 126,000-byte coloured log reproduced this. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-bundle/review-probe.js". Output: {"headTextPaths":["gate-output.txt"],"headTextSizes":{},"findings":[]}.
findings.suggestion: Include valid text containing ANSI formatting in size classification, and add a real-git regression covering a large coloured gate log.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer commits gate-output.txt containing '\x1b[32mPASS\x1b[0m\n'.repeat(9000). Despite exceeding 100 KiB, the audit emits no scratch-output warning and subsequent feedback omits it.

output.summary: 366 tests passed, with 2 sandbox-related skips. Lint and typecheck passed using cached dependencies. A separate probe reproduced incorrect filename attribution.

findings.title: Match zero blob IDs instead of treating them as wildcards
findings.detail: For an addition, the zero source ID matches any raw entry. If an earlier modified file shares the addition's destination blob, raw.find selects that file and the refusal names the wrong cause. Command: `bun --tsconfig-override "$TMPDIR/review635-deps/tsconfig.json" "$TMPDIR/review635-deps/diagnosis-probe.ts"`. Output: `Error: Published commit d18179ac603990880d59e296e946eb160f96a83e: a-fixture.txt exceeds the private text decoding limit; publication blocked`, followed by `error: Expected refusal to identify z-scratch.txt, the only patch that introduces undecodable content`.
findings.suggestion: Require zero IDs to match the corresponding raw zero IDs, or obtain the filename from the patch header. Add a regression with identical destination blobs.
findings.failure_scenario: An existing a-fixture.txt contains undecodable text outside the changed lines. A commit changes only its final clean line and adds z-scratch.txt with identical final contents. Only the scratch addition introduces undecodable patch content, but the refusal incorrectly names a-fixture.txt.

output.summary: Audit redaction and filename checks passed targeted testing: 173 passed, 2 sandbox-related skips, using cached dependency preloads. A production-path probe confirmed that base64 credentials still pass publication checks. Lint and typecheck could not complete because local dependencies are missing. The checkout is unchanged.

findings.title: Include registered credentials in production publication checks
findings.detail: Publication matching checks only the supplied entries. Production callers in the pipeline and land queue supply loadPrivateStrings(), which excludes registered credentials; credentials are combined only for filename diagnostics. Consequently, the requested base64 credential protection remains absent from published content. The new unit test hides this gap by manually adding registered credentials. A real staged-content probe, run with `NODE_PATH="$TMPDIR/review-deps.J9e8Ql" bun "$TMPDIR/review-publication.ts"`, failed with `AssertionError: Missing expected rejection.`
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials at production publication boundaries and add a regression through checkPrivatePublication with an empty private-entry list.
findings.failure_scenario: Register synthetic-review-credential, stage report.txt containing its base64 encoding, and call checkPrivatePublication(cwd, [], { staged: true }). The check succeeds, allowing publication of the encoded credential.

output.summary: Found an unfixed credential-publication gap. Direct decoder probes passed with explicit entries. Targeted suites, lint and typecheck could not run because dependencies are missing. No files changed.

findings.title: Include registered credentials in production publication checks
findings.detail: The delivery engine's privateEntries() and land queue's publication() supply only loadPrivateStrings() results. This function never adds registered credentials, so base64-encoded credentials still pass publication checks. The new test manually adds credentials to entries, masking the production gap. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {mock} from "bun:test"; mock.module("entities",()=>({decodeHTML:(s:string)=>s})); const {checkPublicationText}=await import("./src/gates/publication.ts"); const {registerCredential}=await import("./src/util/proc.ts"); registerCredential("probe","synthetic-secret-642"); checkPublicationText(Buffer.from("synthetic-secret-642").toString("base64"),"PR body",[]); console.log("ACCEPTED");' Output: ACCEPTED. The missing HTML dependency is stubbed as identity; this input contains no HTML references.
findings.suggestion: Ensure production publication checks include registered credentials, and add a regression that uses the production entry construction rather than manually inserting the credential.
findings.failure_scenario: With no private-string entries configured, register synthetic-secret-642 and publish its base64 representation in a PR body or changed file. Publication succeeds and exposes the recoverable credential.

output.summary: Found two eval aggregation defects. All 19 provider-workload tests pass; direct probes reproduce both defects. CLI/HTTP checks were blocked by incompatible Zod and missing MCP dependencies; lint/typecheck were blocked by missing Biome and Bun typings. No repository files changed.

findings.title: Do not attribute an entire review panel to its first model
findings.detail: The eval runner combines finder and verifier usage into trial totals, potentially across providers. This fallback assigns all those tokens and costs to details.provider and t.model_id, falsely inflating the first model's workload and omitting other participants. Probe command: `bun "$TMPDIR/provider-stats-review.ts" panel`. Output: `[{"provider":"alpha","models":[{"modelId":"alpha/m1","costUsd":2,"invocations":1}]}]`, followed by `AssertionError: mixed-panel total must not all be attributed to the first model`.
findings.suggestion: Use stored per-call evidence where available. When panel totals cannot be split reliably, expose them as unattributed or unavailable rather than assigning them to the first model.
findings.failure_scenario: A review panel uses alpha/m1 and beta/m2, each costing $1. The trial stores their combined $2 cost and identifies alpha/m1 as its starting target. Statistics charge all $2 to alpha/m1 and show no beta workload.

findings.title: Preserve known cache metrics for single-round evals
findings.detail: Any nonempty rounds array forces cache-read, cache-write and derived input tokens to null, even when a single-round trial stores the exact cache split. Implementation evals record rounds even for one call. These nulls also make the provider's aggregate metrics unknown. Probe command: `bun "$TMPDIR/provider-stats-review.ts" cache`. Output: `{"inputTokens":null,"cacheReadTokens":null,"cacheWriteTokens":null}`, followed by `AssertionError: single-round eval must retain its stored cache-read tokens` (`null !== 2`).
findings.suggestion: Use the trial's stored cache split when there is exactly one round; retain unknown values only where the split cannot be determined.
findings.failure_scenario: A one-round implementation trial stores tokensIn=10, cacheReadTokens=2 and cacheWriteTokens=1. Statistics report all three input/cache metrics as null instead of input=7, cache-read=2 and cache-write=1.

output.summary: Found two reproducible eval aggregation defects. All 19 workload tests pass. CLI/HTTP checks were blocked by incompatible Zod and missing SDK dependencies; lint/typecheck were blocked by missing Biome and Bun types. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Aggregate persisted review samples as individual invocations
findings.detail: Review trials can contain multiple provider calls in details.samples, including each call's status, usage and duration. This branch collapses them into one trial, producing incorrect invocation counts, successful share and timing statistics. Targeted command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/provider-stats-review.ts". Output: Two persisted review calls (one ok, one error): {"expected":{"invocations":2,"successfulShare":0.5,"p50WallTimeMs":200,"wallTimeMs":400},"actual":{"invocations":1,"successfulShare":0,"p50WallTimeMs":300,"wallTimeMs":300}}
findings.suggestion: Expand available details.samples into individual work records using their stored results and durations, without also counting the aggregate trial.
findings.failure_scenario: A two-sample review stores one successful 100 ms call and one failed 300 ms call. Statistics report one failed invocation lasting 300 ms instead of two calls with 50% success and 400 ms total.

findings.title: Preserve known cache-token totals for implementation evals
findings.detail: Whenever rounds exist, both cache splits are unconditionally discarded, although the eval runner persists accumulated cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens on the trial. Even a single-round trial therefore reports unknown measurements that are available. These nulls also propagate into provider totals. Targeted command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/provider-stats-review.ts". Output: Single round with persisted cache split: {"expected":{"inputTokens":10,"cacheReadTokens":2,"cacheWriteTokens":1},"actual":{"inputTokens":null,"cacheReadTokens":null,"cacheWriteTokens":null}}
findings.suggestion: Use persisted trial cache splits wherever attribution is unambiguous, including single-round trials and totals whose rounds all use the same provider/model.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation eval records one round with 13 prompt tokens and trial cache totals of 2 read and 1 written. The endpoint returns null for input and cached tokens instead of 10, 2 and 1.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and rerun compatibility paths. Isolated probes found two regressions; the ordinary Bun/header case passed. Repository tests, lint, and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies. Checkout remains unchanged.

findings.title: Preserve exact-field redaction for short credentials
findings.detail: Publication now redacts padded context instead of the extracted field. Credentials shorter than eight characters are redacted only on exact matches, so previously protected field values leak into signatures, ci_failures, and feed keys. Isolated check command: CI_REVIEW_ROOT="$PWD" bun test "$TMPDIR/ci682-review.test.ts". Output: {"previous":"[redacted]","current":"hunter2"}; assertion failed with Expected: "[redacted]", Received: "hunter2".
findings.suggestion: Retain padded redaction for crossing credentials, then apply exact-field redaction before constructing the signature.
findings.failure_scenario: Register credential "hunter2" and classify "Image: hunter2\nerror: broken". The previous implementation redacts the image; this implementation stores it verbatim in the signature.

findings.title: Budget the excerpt after redaction to retain the failure
findings.detail: The tail budget counts raw characters, but replacing eight-character credentials with "[redacted]" expands it. The final slice then removes the selected failing test and stack. Isolated check command: CI_REVIEW_ROOT="$PWD" bun test "$TMPDIR/ci682-review.test.ts". Output selected line "(fail) actual failure", excerpt length 2000, ending "] [redacted] [redacted] [redacted] [redacted] [redacted] [re"; the assertion that the excerpt contains the selected line failed.
findings.suggestion: Apply the final budget to redacted content while preserving the selected failure line and trimming surrounding context.
findings.failure_scenario:
Register "s3cr3t42" and classify "error: assertion
" followed by "s3cr3t42 " repeated 300 times, then "
 at test.ts:1
(fail) actual failure". The signature is correct, but its failure line and location disappear from the excerpt.

output.summary: Basic parsing probes passed, but two focused assertions exposed regressions. Targeted suites could not load without entities; typechecking lacked Bun types, and lint encountered a sandbox temp-directory error. No files were modified.

findings.title: Preserve exact-field redaction for short credentials
findings.detail: The padded publication input includes surrounding log text, so credentials shorter than eight characters no longer satisfy redactCredentials' exact-match rule. Previously, an image field equal to a registered credential was redacted; it now enters the persisted image and signature verbatim. Command: bun -e 'import {strict as assert} from "node:assert"; import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("REVIEW_SHORT_TOKEN", "abc123"); assert.equal(ciSignature("test", "Image: abc123\n(fail) actual", "").image, "[redacted]");' Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: actual 'abc123', expected '[redacted]'.
findings.suggestion: Preserve exact-field credential matching alongside context-aware redaction, and add a short-credential regression test.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered six-character credential exactly matches an Image field. The new helper returns that credential unchanged, and recordCiFailure stores it in runner_image and signature.

findings.title: Apply the tail budget after redaction
findings.detail:
The Bun tail budget counts raw characters, but replacing eight-character credentials with '[redacted]' expands the tail. The final prefix truncation then discards the selected failure line and stack. Command: bun -e 'import {strict as assert} from "node:assert"; import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("REVIEW_TOKEN", "abcdefgh"); const r = ciSignature("test", "context
context
error: assertion failed
" + "abcdefgh".repeat(300) + "
 at test.ts:1:1
(fail) actual failure", ""); assert.equal(r.excerpt.includes(r.line), true);' Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true.
findings.suggestion: Trim the redacted tail to the remaining budget from its beginning, preserving the selected failure line and nearest stack context.
findings.failure_scenario: A long Bun assertion block contains repeated eight-character registered credentials before the stack and failing test name. Redaction expands the retained tail beyond 2,000 characters, removing both diagnostics from the excerpt.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding worker, harness and coordinator code. Isolated execution probes reproduced three defects. Integration tests and typecheck could not initialize because required dependencies and Bun types are unavailable or incompatible. The checkout is unchanged.

findings.title: Redact credentials in result object keys
findings.detail: The sanitizer uses redactGateData, which leaves general JSON object keys untouched. Neither harness redacts its returned structured result, so worker credentials used as structured property names reach the coordinator. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-agent-jobs-probe.ts" secret. Output: "result contains registered credential as object key: true", followed by "AssertionError: credentials must be removed before posting results". The probe executes the current runAgent implementation with the real runner and fake harness, substituting checkout and transport.
findings.suggestion: Apply credential redaction that covers both keys and values before transmitting results, while retaining terminal normalization and path replacement.
findings.failure_scenario: A harness returns structured: { [registeredWorkerCredential]: "value" }. The result POST contains the literal credential as a property name.

findings.title: Bound event batches by serialized size
findings.detail: Batching considers only count and time, but the coordinator limits event bodies to 1 MiB. Both real harnesses permit 20,000-character tool results, so supported events can produce rejected batches. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-agent-jobs-probe.ts" oversized. Output: "event batch bytes: 3992291; listener limit: 1048576; result posts: 0", followed by an assertion failure.
findings.suggestion: Flush before serialized UTF-8 bytes exceed the listener limit, alongside the existing count and time limits, and handle individually oversized events explicitly.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent emits 200 tool results containing 20 KB each within one batching window. The coordinator returns 413 and the worker aborts the session instead of reporting its result.

findings.title: Report event rejection before abandoning the lease
findings.detail: A rejected event POST aborts the job controller, causing the catch block's !jobSignal.aborted guard to skip POST failure. For rejections such as 400 or 413, the coordinator still holds the job as leased; it receives no failure reason and cannot retry until lease expiry. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-agent-jobs-probe.ts" rejection. Output: "controller aborted: true; failure posts after rejected events: 0", followed by "AssertionError: event rejection must report failure while the lease is still held".
findings.suggestion: Track event rejection separately from cancellation. Stop the harness, then report sanitized failure using a live reporting signal when the rejection leaves the lease held.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects an event batch with 413 while heartbeats otherwise succeed. The worker removes the job locally without notifying failure, leaving coordinator capacity occupied until expiry.

output.summary: Found two defects in event reporting, reproduced with temporary probes using the real worker loop and mocked Git/transport. Targeted repository tests could not load because dependencies were missing or incompatible. No repository files were changed.

findings.title: Retries silently discard events when sequence numbers restart
findings.detail: Every lease starts seq at 0, but failAgentJob requeues the same job ID and agentJobEvents deduplicates by (job_id, seq). A retry therefore receives successful acknowledgements while its events are discarded in favor of the previous attempt's events. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-seq-probe.ts"` produced `{"sent":[{"attempt":1,"seq":0},{"attempt":2,"seq":0}],"persistedBatches":1,"persistedEvents":200,"hasSecondAttempt":false}` and failed with `AssertionError: retry worker events must not be discarded as duplicates`.
findings.suggestion: Provide the next unused sequence number in the lease reply, or namespace event batches by attempt while preserving retry idempotence.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts batch 0 and then fails. Worker B leases the requeued job and posts its own batch 0; the coordinator acknowledges it but retains only worker A's batch.

findings.title: Rejected event batches skip the failure report
findings.detail: The rejected post aborts the job controller, so the catch block's `if (!jobSignal.aborted)` skips POST failure. The checkout disappears, but the coordinator retains a leased job until expiry and loses the rejection reason. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-probe.ts"` with an injected HTTP 413 produced `{"eventCalls":1,"harnessAborted":true,"failureCalls":0,"checkoutCount":0}` and failed with `AssertionError: a rejected event batch must post failure`.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish event rejection from external cancellation and report the sanitized failure using a bounded signal that remains usable after aborting the harness.
findings.failure_scenario: A tool-output batch exceeds the coordinator's 1 MiB event-body limit. The coordinator returns 413, the worker aborts the harness, and no failure notification is sent.

output.summary: Reviewed restart, reconciliation, adoption and reporting paths. Confirmed one restart regression with an isolated probe using real Git; the probe passes against the base. Targeted repository tests could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. Diff checks passed; no repository files changed.

findings.title: Persist the transition to local fallback before running it
findings.detail: A done job with failed confinement falls back locally while its durable agentJob handle still references that done result. If the local session edits files and the coordinator restarts before implementation-ready, reconciliation adopts the same result again. workerPublication.adopt rejects the dirty worktree, ending the run NeedsHuman. An isolated probe executing the actual executor and publication hook with real Git reproduced this: `bun run "$TMPDIR/s6-fallback-probe.ts"` failed with `AssertionError: A restart during local fallback must resume local work, rather than re-adopt a consumed worker result` and `1 !== 2`. The resumed outcome was `NeedsHumanError: ... Coordinator HEAD or worktree changed during worker session`. Running the probe against the base produced two local calls and resumed successfully.
findings.suggestion: Persist a transition that prevents replaying the consumed done job before starting local fallback. Add a restart test after that fallback has written local changes.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker reports confinement.ok=false with sha equal to parentSha; the coordinator falls back locally; that session writes a file; a deploy interrupts it before implementation-ready. Resume replays the worker adoption check and incorrectly ends NeedsHuman despite no unreported push.

output.summary: Reviewed restart, reconciliation, adoption and reporting paths. 94 targeted tests passed using cached dependencies; socket restrictions blocked integration checks. Confirmed a worker shutdown regression.

findings.title: Preserve worker shutdown cancellation for late reports
findings.detail: The timeout-only signal also ignores the worker's global shutdown signal. If the coordinator remains unavailable after a push, stopping the worker leaves result reporting retrying until the attempt deadline. runWorker's finally block awaits that task, so shutdown can hang for many minutes. An isolated runWorker reproduction with Git/publication stubbed and transport held open confirmed this: `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-worker-shutdown.test.ts"` failed with `result signal aborted after worker shutdown: false`, `Expected: true`, `Received: false`.
findings.suggestion: Combine `combined` with the attempt-deadline timeout for published results. Exclude the per-job controller so fencing and job cancellation still cannot abort reporting.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker successfully pushes, the coordinator becomes unreachable before accepting its report, and the owner sends SIGINT or SIGTERM. The worker waits for the remaining attempt deadline instead of shutting down.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding routing, refusal, result validation, fallback, and shutdown paths; found no actionable defects. Diff whitespace checks passed. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies are absent (missing entities); typecheck was blocked by missing Bun types.

Reviewed the diff and surrounding eligibility, cancellation, fallback, publication, and result-validation paths; found no concrete defects. Diff whitespace checks passed. Targeted tests could not start because dependencies were missing (`entities`); typechecking was blocked by missing Bun type definitions.

Reviewed the diff, surrounding runner code and tests. Found missing CLI wiring for production complexity. Full targeted tests and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies; Biome was blocked by temporary-file permissions.

findings.title: Wire production run lookup into the CLI
findings.detail: The CLI never supplies lookupRun, and PR bodies do not publish triage complexity. Consequently, every CLI-generated case receives medium even when its production run record is available, missing the requirement to preserve complexity when it can be found. An isolated CLI-wiring probe run with `bun "$TMPDIR/replay-metadata-probe.ts"` printed `Available run r1 complexity: small; CLI generated complexity: medium` and failed with `AssertionError: 'medium' !== 'small'`.
findings.suggestion: Connect an injectable reader for the configured daemon or local run store to the CLI's lookupRun dependency, retaining the documented fallback when the record is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: A merged factory PR references a locally available run whose triage complexity is small. Running the documented generator stores medium instead.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, Git history, and surrounding eval/report code. Found a broken default invocation and production-metadata defects. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies are missing; typechecking was blocked by missing Bun types. A focused metadata probe reproduced an assertion failure.

findings.title: Allow generation when the default dataset does not exist
findings.detail: The generator unconditionally reads evals/implement/cases.json, but neither that file nor its directory exists in this checkout. Consequently, the documented invocation fails before fetching or validating any PR. A direct read confirmed ENOENT. The tests hide this by always creating a populated dataset first.
findings.suggestion: Initialize an empty in-memory envelope when the dataset is absent, then validate and publish it after accepting the first case.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the documented generator command from a fresh checkout with dependencies installed: reading the default case path throws ENOENT before any PR is processed.

findings.title: Connect the CLI to production run records
findings.detail: The CLI supplies only cache access and never supplies lookupRun. PR bodies do not contain triage complexity, so every case generated through the requested command receives medium, even when its report names a locally available run with a known complexity. Providing an injection point only to programmatic callers leaves the CLI requirement unimplemented.
findings.suggestion: Wire an injectable run-record lookup into the CLI using the existing local store or daemon API, retaining the documented fallback when records are unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a PR whose footer names an available production run with complexity small: the generated case records medium and 'lookup not configured'.

findings.title: Preserve large production cases instead of rejecting them
findings.detail: replayProduction can return the valid production complexity large, but ImplementCaseSchema accepts only trivial, small, and medium. Passing the metadata directly into that schema rejects the PR before validation. The new test explicitly expects this rejection, although the request imposes no such exclusion and seeks harder production tasks.
findings.suggestion: Extend implement-case complexity support to preserve valid production values, and test that a large case satisfying both validation checks is accepted.
findings.failure_scenario: A merged PR has qualifying hidden tests and lookupRun returns complexity large; generation excludes it with a schema error without running either validation.

findings.title: Recognize successful discreet factory reports
findings.detail: renderReport emits 'Every gate below passed.' or 'Checks below have no blocking regressions.' for successful discreet reports. This parser recognizes only branded success introductions, incorrectly recording needs_human:unknown. A focused probe executing the extracted function failed with command `bun "$TMPDIR/replay-review-probe.ts"`: output `needs_human:unknown` followed by `AssertionError: Successful discreet factory report must record needs_human:false`.
findings.suggestion: Recognize both discreet success introductions alongside their branded equivalents.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a merged factory PR published with discreet enabled and a successful report: its production outcome is stored as unknown despite explicit success evidence.

output.summary: Found two validation defects using real Git fixtures. Targeted repository tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Validate the recorded base rather than a different tree
findings.detail: Base validation removes evals/ through snapshot mode, while head validation uses the original commit. This can accept a hidden test that already passes at the recorded base, violating the required exclusion rule. A probe using the production pushSnapshot helper confirmed this. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/replay-validation-probe.ts". Output: {"realBase":0,"snapshotBase":1,"realHead":0}; AssertionError: A valid replay must fail at its recorded base.
findings.suggestion: Check the hidden command against the actual pinned base after setup. Separately verify that the runner representation of both revisions preserves the validation result.
findings.failure_scenario: The base contains evals/value.json. A PR adds a test reading that unchanged file and changes unrelated implementation code. The test passes at both original commits but fails in the stripped base snapshot, so the generator incorrectly accepts it.

findings.title: Match the runner's cleanup before validating hidden tests
findings.detail: Validation runs hidden tests immediately after setup. gradeImplement instead resets and runs git clean -fdq after gates, removing untracked setup outputs before injecting hidden files. Consequently, validation can accept cases whose reference implementation fails grading. The new fixture itself uses an untracked ready file and exercises this mismatch. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/replay-setup-probe.ts". Output: {"generatorHead":0,"graderHead":1}; AssertionError: Reference validation must agree with the runner hidden-test preparation.
findings.suggestion: Share the runner's hidden-test preparation lifecycle with validation, and test that the reference implementation of an accepted case actually passes grading.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup creates an untracked ready file, and hidden tests require both the correct answer and that file. Generator validation passes at head, but grading the same reference code deletes ready and fails the hidden test.

output.summary: Found two replay-validation defects using extracted production functions and real-git fixtures. Repository tests, lint and typecheck could not complete because entities, Biome and Bun type definitions are missing. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Forced snapshots exclude the factory PRs this generator targets
findings.detail: Every generated case forces snapshot mode, removing evals/ before running baseline gates. Limitless's own tests require that directory, as docs/EVALS.md explicitly documents. Consequently, recent factory PRs are excluded before hidden-test validation even when they satisfy the requested base/head checks. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/replay-review-probe.ts"`, using extracted generator/preparation functions and a real-git fixture, reported `excluded: runner preparation: snapshot mode removed evals/ and baseline check reads-evals fails`, while independently checking the original pins produced `base exit=1, head exit=0`.
findings.suggestion: Provide a replay preparation path compatible with the factory repository's required eval fixtures while preserving contamination protections; avoid unconditionally selecting the unsupported snapshot representation.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a replay from a Limitless PR whose base has the normal test suite reading evals/ datasets. Its hidden tests fail at base and pass at head, but snapshot preparation rejects it.

findings.title: Validate hidden commands with the grader's environment
findings.detail: Validation runs hidden tests through runGates, which supplies gateEnv() and forces CI=1. Actual grading in gradeImplement runs the same command through runConfined with agentEnv(), which does not force CI. Validation can therefore publish cases whose reference implementation fails during evaluation. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/replay-review-probe.ts"` produced `base:"fail", head:"pass", reason:"accepted"` for a CI-sensitive hidden test, followed by `same reference solution with grader environment: exit=1`, with `Expected: "1"; Received: undefined`.
findings.suggestion: Share hidden-command execution between generation and grading so both use the same environment, confinement and result classification.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon runs without CI set, and a changed test expects CI=1 or otherwise changes behavior under CI. Generator validation accepts the case, but the identical reference solution fails its hidden tests during grading.

output.summary: Found two result-handling defects using real Git and normal-executor probes. Targeted tests had 530 passes; socket-dependent checks were blocked by sandbox restrictions. No repository files changed.

findings.title: Return failure when confinement fails despite exit code zero
findings.detail: The response uses exitCode without checking result.ok. A confinement diagnostic can make the normal executor return ok=false with exitCode=0, so the wrapper exits successfully and AgentTestSession emits gate-pass while its output says FAIL. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-agent-gate.ts"` produced `normal-executor-confinement {"status":0,"reportedFailure":true}`.
findings.suggestion: Return a nonzero status whenever result.ok is false, preserving an existing nonzero exit code. Add coverage for confinementError=true with exitCode=0.
findings.failure_scenario: The trusted test command catches a child sandbox error and exits zero. The executor classifies the gate as a confinement failure, but the implement session receives success.

findings.title: Preserve timeout failures for reuse on the same tree
findings.detail: completed() excludes timed-out results, so these factory executions are never recorded or reused. The gates stage reruns the same suite and loses the original failure and attempt history, contrary to the requested failure reuse. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-agent-gate.ts"` with a normal-executor timeout and then committing the unchanged snapshot produced `normal-executor-timeout {"status":1,"recorded":false,"reuse":null}`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the normal timeout retry policy during the requested factory run, then persist and reuse the resulting timeout failure and retry history. Continue rejecting interrupted or untrustworthy executions.
findings.failure_scenario: An implement-session factory test reaches its configured timeout. The implementer finishes without further edits, with unchanged gate configuration and environment. The gates stage executes the full suite again instead of carrying over the timeout result.

output.summary: Found three defects in snapshotting and failure handling. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies were missing or incompatible; focused real-Git and executor probes confirmed the findings. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Conflict-resolution snapshots can differ from the round commit
findings.detail: Starting from HEAD loses ignored files already tracked by the incoming merge parent. completeMerge explicitly preserves those paths, so the factory tests a different tree and cannot reuse the result. A real-Git probe using the unchanged snapshotTree body and actual completeMerge confirmed this. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/probe-snapshot-merge.ts". Output: "snapshot contains generated.txt: false\nround contains generated.txt: true\nASSERTION FAILED: snapshot tree must equal round commit tree".
findings.suggestion: Share merge-aware staging rules with completeMerge, preserving incoming tracked paths without changing the session index.
findings.failure_scenario: A local conflict-resolution session merges a base that tracks generated.txt, while HEAD's .gitignore excludes it. The snapshot omits generated.txt; the eventual merge commit includes it.

findings.title: Timed-out factory executions are discarded instead of reused
findings.detail: completed(result) rejects every timeout, so a timed-out test gate leaves no durable failure record. The same final tree therefore runs the suite again during gates, losing the original failure and retry history. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/probe-agent-gate.ts". Output: "timed-out factory gate command status: 1\ndurable timeout records: 0\nsame-tree timeout lookup: null".
findings.suggestion: Persist completed timeout failures with their classification and bounded retry history, then reuse them for the matching tree. Keep cancellation distinct from a gate timeout.
findings.failure_scenario: The implementer's factory gate times out, then the session finishes without changing files. Gates reruns the same suite; a later pass can replace the timeout with a clean result.

findings.title: A failed gate can return success to the session
findings.detail: The returned status uses the raw exitCode even when the executor classified the result as a confinement failure. Such a result can have ok=false and exitCode=0, making the wrapper print FAIL but exit successfully. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/probe-agent-gate.ts". A real shell check through the local executor with injected confinement produced: "real shell diagnostic marked FAIL: true\nreal shell diagnostic command status: 0".
findings.suggestion: Return a nonzero status whenever result.ok is false, preserving meaningful nonzero exit codes where available.
findings.failure_scenario: A test command emits a confinement-failure diagnostic but its shell exits 0, for example after handling a failed nested sandbox command. The factory rejects the gate, but the implementer's command reports success.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding lifecycle code. Four dependency-isolated probes reproduced defects using temporary fixtures, including real gate subprocesses. The repository test command could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Clean interrupted gate edits before running the local fallback
findings.detail: After confirming shutdown, this path reruns the request against the worktree left by the failed executor. Unlike LAN execution, an in-place attempt can already have modified tracked files or left partial build artifacts. The fallback therefore checks different inputs from the committed SHA, potentially producing incorrect gate evidence or baseline cache entries. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-dirty.ts". Output: {"cleanPassed":true,"fallbackPassed":false,"source":"dirty"}, followed by AssertionError: Fallback must start from the committed clean input, not interrupted gate edits.
findings.suggestion: After confirming process shutdown, restore committed inputs and restart the appropriate full gate attempt, including required setup.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor modifies a tracked source file and then crashes while the daemon remains attached. The daemon observes the failed job and reruns its checks against the modified file.

findings.title: Preserve setup scratch across executor retry jobs
findings.detail: Each job calls executeGate independently, so runLocalGates creates and removes separate command scratch for each attempt. The daemon's surrounding commandScope cannot extend into the executor. Meanwhile, freshCheckoutFor returns false for in-place execution, causing retries to omit setup. Dependencies installed into scratch HOME during setup are consequently missing during retries. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-scratch.ts". Output: {"localRetryPassed":true,"inplaceRetryPassed":false}, followed by AssertionError: Executor retry must retain setup scratch as in-process retries do.
findings.suggestion: Preserve owned scratch across the gate and its retry sequence, or explicitly rebuild the required setup before retrying in new scratch.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup creates $HOME/prepared, the first check fails transiently, and its retry requires that setup artifact. The in-process retry passes; the executor retry fails because its HOME is new.

findings.title: Resume targeted retries instead of cancelling them
findings.detail: The purpose allowlist excludes baseline-retry-targeted, regression-retry-targeted, full retries, and timeout reruns. Even a matching, currently leased in-place retry is cancelled and its worktree reset. The engine also re-enters through the initial purpose, so retry progress is replayed rather than resumed. This leaves an explicitly required gate purpose without restart survival. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-retry.ts". Output: {"resumed":null,"cancelled":1,"cleanups":1}, followed by AssertionError: Matching targeted retry must reattach to its existing job.
findings.suggestion: Persist the retry phase and preceding evidence, then resume the recorded purpose and handle without replaying the initial gate.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a targeted retry is leased on the same release, stage, round, SHA, and environment. The resumed engine cancels that healthy job and starts the gate sequence again.

findings.title: Honor the local executor option alongside LAN execution
findings.detail: The lan branch ignores the inplace option. Its lanExecutor uses localExecutor directly for repositories outside workers.repos, so those local gates remain daemon-owned even with executor.enabled=true and a live executor. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-lan.ts". Output: {"executorEnabled":true,"liveExecutor":true,"repo":"org/local","handleKind":"local"}, followed by AssertionError: Local gates must use the enabled executor when LAN is enabled for other repos.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local delegation through the enabled in-place executor while retaining LAN dispatch for configured repositories.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure gates.executor="lan", workers.repos=["org/remote"], and executor.enabled=true. Gates for org/local run inside the daemon and are lost on restart.

output.summary: Found four reproducible defects. In an exact-HEAD scratch copy, `bun test test/review-inplace-regressions.test.ts` produced the four assertion failures detailed below. The 84 existing executor tests and changed-file lint passed. Worker tests encountered unavailable-port errors; typecheck was blocked by missing evals/review/trace-experiment.json. The repository was unchanged.

findings.title: Crash fallback can approve modified source
findings.detail: After confirming that executor processes stopped, fallback reruns the request without restoring the committed checkout. An interrupted gate's edits therefore become inputs to the replacement check. The regression command reported `LIVE CRASH FALLBACK: {"ok":true,"output":"dirty","job":"done"}` and failed with `Expected: false; Received: true`: the committed source would fail this check.
findings.suggestion: After confirmed shutdown, restart the interrupted stage from its recorded commit and rerun required setup before accepting replacement results.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate modifies a tracked source file, then the executor crashes while the daemon remains attached. The replacement check passes against that modified file and records a passing result for the unchanged commit SHA.

findings.title: Separate jobs discard scratch needed by retries
findings.detail: Each executeGate call creates and removes its own scratch, while in-place retries skip setup because freshCheckoutFor returns false. The daemon's commandScope cannot preserve scratch in the executor process. The regression command produced `local:true,inplace:false` and `setup-ready: No such file or directory`, failing with `Expected: true; Received: false`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve executor-owned scratch across the stage's initial check and retries, or reconstruct the required setup before retrying.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup creates a prerequisite under HOME or a scratch-backed cache. A check fails once and is retried without setup. Local execution succeeds, but in-place execution retries with empty scratch and fails.

findings.title: Matching targeted retries are cancelled on resume
findings.detail: The purpose whitelist excludes baseline-retry-targeted and regression-retry-targeted, so even a matching, actively leased in-place retry is discarded. The regression command reported `TARGETED RESUME: {"oldState":"cancelled"}` and failed because the expected saved handle was replaced by undefined. This leaves the requested targeted-retry restart coverage unimplemented.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry-stage state to resume matching retry jobs, and preserve them when entering recovery instead of treating them as initial-job mismatches.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts during a targeted retry with unchanged stage, round, purpose, SHA, environment and release. Recovery cancels the surviving job and repeats gate work.

findings.title: PID existence does not establish executor freshness
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID birth identity; no heartbeat or freshness timestamp is recorded or checked. The regression command stopped its own executor subprocess and advanced the coordinator clock beyond times.fresh. It reported `STALLED EXECUTOR STILL AVAILABLE: true` and failed `toBeUndefined()`. A stale leased executor can also leave waitStopped polling indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Add a responsiveness/freshness signal distinct from process identity, apply the required freshness timers, and retain confirmed-stop protection before fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor remains alive with a stalled event loop. The daemon continues selecting it beyond the freshness window, and expired leased jobs cannot complete fallback while waitStopped treats the stalled owner as available.

output.summary: Found a private-key isolation defect. Isolated JWT, caching, and repository-selection checks passed. Targeted repository tests could not load because dependencies were missing. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Protect the configured App key from agent reads
findings.detail: The configuration accepts key paths outside configDir, but never adds the key to the read-deny policy or registers it with protectPrivateFile. Agents run as the same user, so mode 0600 does not prevent them from reading such a key. The generated-key probe `bun "$TMPDIR/github-key-policy-probe.ts"` produced `{"configAccepted":true,"keyDeniedToAgent":false}` and failed with `AssertionError: Configured GitHub App key must be denied to agents`.
findings.suggestion: Protect the configured key in its lexical and canonical locations using the shared private-file/read-policy mechanism. Add regression coverage for an external key and a symlink target.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure private_key_path as an absolute path outside configDir that an agent can read, such as a file within its checkout. Startup accepts the mode-0600 key, and the agent can read the private key and mint App credentials despite its dummy GH_TOKEN.

output.summary: Found two security defects in key confinement and identity selection. Focused JWT, caching, refresh, redaction, and failure probes passed. Targeted tests, lint, and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies and tooling.

findings.title: Protect the configured private key from agent reads
findings.detail: Absolute key paths are accepted, but the key is never added to the shared read-deny policy. That policy protects the config directory, so a key elsewhere remains readable by editors running as the same user; mode 0600 provides no isolation from them. A focused probe printed `{"keyProtectedFromEditors":false}`. Command: `bun -e 'import {configureReadPolicy, homeReadPolicy, readPolicyScope} from "./src/harness/read-policy.ts"; const home=process.cwd(); readPolicyScope.run({...configureReadPolicy(undefined,home+"/config"),home,environment:{}},()=>console.log(homeReadPolicy([]).denyRead.some(p=>(home+"/app.pem").startsWith(p))));'` Output: `false`.
findings.suggestion: Add the configured and canonical key paths to the shared private-file protection used by agents and gates, including symlink targets.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure a valid 0600 key outside the config directory, or symlink a key inside that directory to an external file. An editor can read the private key and authenticate independently as the App.

findings.title: Do not interpret argument values as repository flags
findings.detail: The flag search scans every argument without respecting which arguments are values. In the merge command, a PR body equal to `--repo` overrides the actual PR URL and selects `--match-head-commit` as the repository. The provider then returns the owner identity, silently bypassing the configured App. Command: `bun -e 'import { githubRepo } from "./src/integrations/github-identity.ts"; console.log(githubRepo(["pr", "merge", "https://github.com/o/r/pull/1", "--body", "--repo", "--match-head-commit", "a".repeat(40)]));'` Output: `--match-head-commit`.
findings.suggestion: Pass the repository explicitly from callers that know it, or parse flags while skipping their values. Add a regression case with flag-shaped PR text.
findings.failure_scenario: An App-configured repository enters automatic delivery with its PR body set to `--repo`. The merge subprocess receives the owner's environment instead of the installation token.

output.summary: Reviewed identity routing, credential handling, and login comparisons. Focused probes passed JWT, caching, and token-injection checks but reproduced two defects. The targeted test suite could not start because dependencies were missing; isolated probes used locally available dependencies.

findings.title: Apply the signing key checks during startup
findings.detail: Startup uses statSync, which follows symlinks, whereas signingKey opens with O_NOFOLLOW. Consequently, configuration loads successfully with a key that every App-authenticated call rejects. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/github-app-review-key-probe.ts"` printed `startup config: accepted symlink`, followed by `first GitHub call: GitHub App private key <scratch>/link.pem: symlink refused`, and failed with `AssertionError: Missing expected exception: startup must refuse a key the signing provider cannot use`.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the signing key's descriptor-based validation during startup so unusable keys refuse configuration immediately.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure private_key_path as a symlink to an owner-readable 0600 PEM file. Startup succeeds, but all GitHub operations for listed repositories fail.

findings.title: Let successful App authentication satisfy doctor
findings.detail: The App identity check never reconciles the preceding unconditional owner `gh auth status` failure. An installation covering every configured repository therefore still fails doctor without an owner login, despite valid App authentication. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/github-app-review-doctor-probe.ts"` produced `{"id":"gh","status":"fail","message":"not authenticated or no repo access","fix":"gh auth login"}` alongside `{"id":"github-identity","status":"ok","message":"factory[bot]: token exchange ok; installation repositories: o/r"}`, then failed with `AssertionError: working App-only setup must not require owner gh login`.
findings.suggestion: Require owner authentication for repositories using the owner identity; use successful App authentication for App-only configurations.
findings.failure_scenario: All configured repositories use the App, token exchange and installation coverage succeed, and no owner gh login exists. Doctor incorrectly fails and init's authentication preflight also refuses.

output.summary: Reviewed identity routing, approvals, caching, redaction and configuration. Lint passed and 353 targeted tests passed using installed dependencies. Four checks were environment-blocked; typechecking could not complete because an eval JSON file is missing.

findings.title: Reject unsupported key paths during startup
findings.detail: Startup uses statSync, which follows symlinks, while signingKey opens with O_NOFOLLOW and always rejects them. Consequently, configuration loads successfully but every App-authenticated operation fails. The targeted probe `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun --cwd "$TMPDIR/review-fixture" --preserve-symlinks --preserve-symlinks-main ./review-key.ts` exited 1 with `Startup configuration accepted symlink`, followed by `GitHub App private key .../key-link.pem: symlink refused`.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the provider's file-validation logic during startup so unsupported paths and unreadable files are rejected immediately with a clear reason.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure private_key_path as a symlink to an otherwise valid owner-owned 0600 RSA key. The daemon accepts the configuration, but all GitHub calls for listed repositories fail.

output.summary: Structured parser probes passed, but an isolated engine probe reproduced authentication failures consuming rounds. Targeted tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies/tooling.

findings.title: Propagate verifier authentication exhaustion instead of consuming a round
findings.detail: When concurrent review requests changes, this branch suppresses the verifier's authentication-related NoCapacityError. oneRound returns false, so buildLoop increments both round counters. This leaves the new authentication handling incomplete for verification. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-auth-round.ts"`, an isolated probe executing the extracted engine functions, produced `Verification failure ignored after review requested changes: Error: No model available for verify after: authentication failed: login rejected`, then `round: 3 roundsOnImplementer: 2` and `AssertionError: Authentication exhaustion must not consume an implementation round (3 !== 2)`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve a structured authentication cause on routing exhaustion and propagate it through concurrent verification error handling. Add an integration test combining review rejection with verifier authentication exhaustion.
findings.failure_scenario: A standard/deep run receives a request_changes review while every eligible verifier fails authentication. The engine advances the round and can hit the implementation-round limit instead of immediately entering needs_human with the authentication reason.

output.summary: Reviewed classification, coordinator fallback, LAN fallback, round accounting, and provider health. Focused harness and health probes passed; no concrete defects found. Five targeted test suites could not start because dependencies were missing or incompatible, including Zod lacking z.json.

Reviewed lifecycle persistence, re-approval, and integration wiring. In a scratch copy, 199 existing targeted tests and changed-file lint passed; adversarial probes exposed three defects. Typechecking was blocked by the pre-existing missing evals/review/trace-experiment.json file. The checkout was unchanged.

findings.title: Persist lifecycle notifications before polling can lose them
findings.detail: Notifications are constructed only from the status observed during reconciliation. A needs_human or failed status that becomes resolved before its comment is checkpointed disappears permanently. An earlier comment failure also prevents later notifications from being recorded. Scratch command `bun test test/review-884.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'failure notification'` failed with `Expected: true; Received: false` after rejecting the started comment, resolving the failed run, and polling again. Sampling also skips the start-label effect for runs failing before their first poll: `bun test test/review-884.test.ts` reported `Expected to contain: "labels[]=limitless:in-progress"; Received: [ "labels[]=limitless:failed" ]`.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle events and their reasons durably when transitions occur, then let polling deliver pending effects independently of the current status and earlier write failures.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails; the first lifecycle poll cannot post its started comment. The owner resolves the run before the next poll. Only the started comment is retried, and the failure notification is never posted.

findings.title: Use timeline order for re-approval within the same second
findings.detail: The strict timestamp comparison rejects a trusted priority application appearing after the failure-label event when both have the same timestamp. GitHub timestamps have second precision, while the requirement explicitly calls for event order and actor. Scratch command `bun test test/review-884.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'needs_human|ordinary|ordered'` failed the ordered-event probe: expected `{eligible:true, priority:1}`, received `{eligible:false, reason:"factory status requires priority re-approval after failure"}`.
findings.suggestion: Compare ordered timeline positions for failure-label and trusted priority applications, accounting consistently for the existing finished-run approval check.
findings.failure_scenario: The failure label and a subsequent trusted priority-label application occur within one second. The issue remains ineligible until another priority application is made.

findings.title: Decouple lifecycle updates from issue-queue enablement
findings.detail: Lifecycle management requires queue trust configuration and repository membership, and its poller starts only when the issue queue is enabled. Consequently, ordinary CLI, MCP, and webhook issue runs outside that configuration receive no lifecycle labels, despite the requirement covering every start path. Disabling the queue also strands labels on existing runs. Scratch command `bun test test/review-884.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'needs_human|ordinary|ordered'` failed the ordinary-run probe with `Expected: true; Received: false` for the in-progress label.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and apply it to issue-linked runs from all required start paths.
findings.failure_scenario: With github.queue disabled, an owner starts an issue-linked run through a supported entry point. No in-progress, needs-you, or failed label is ever reconciled.

output.summary: Found lost lifecycle comments, a re-approval bypass, and lifecycle updates incorrectly restricted to queue-enabled repositories. Isolated probes using the real store and reconciler produced 1 pass and 5 assertion failures. Repository tests could not load because entities is missing; typechecking was blocked by missing Bun types. No repository files were changed.

findings.title: Persist lifecycle events before their status can disappear
findings.detail: Comments are derived from the current status, and pending checkpoints are created only immediately before posting. If a run reaches needs_human or failed and is resolved before the next poll, its reason comment is permanently lost. This also happens after a restart between applying the failure label and recording the comment. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.test.ts". Both probes failed with "Expected: true; Received: false" and produced only the started comment. These probes used the real Store and reconciler with configuration/publication helpers stubbed.
findings.suggestion: Durably record each required event and its reason when the status changes, then let polling deliver those recorded effects independently of the current status.
findings.failure_scenario: Apply the failed label, stop before comment processing, resolve the run, and restart. The failure comment is never posted.

findings.title: Preserve re-approval protection for CLI and MCP issue links
findings.detail: Resolving a failed CLI/MCP run makes its desired label set none, deleting limitless:failed. However, latestIssueRun only finds issue source references, so a run linked through Closes #7 provides no local re-approval barrier. The queue can immediately select the issue using its original priority application. A rejected failure-label write exposes the same gap after in-progress is removed. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.test.ts". Both probes printed labels ["priority:1"] and {"eligible":true,"priority":1}, failing with "Expected: false; Received: true".
findings.suggestion: Reuse the existing eligibility guard with terminal history covering every linkedIssues start path, so protection survives resolution and failed GitHub writes.
findings.failure_scenario: A CLI run containing Closes #7 fails, receives limitless:failed, and is manually resolved without another priority application. The next reconciliation removes failed and the queue picks it again.

findings.title: Run lifecycle updates independently of queue admission configuration
findings.detail: lifecycleManaged requires nonempty queue trust and membership in githubQueue.repos, and the reconciler is only scheduled by startIssueQueue. Consequently, CLI/MCP and label/comment-triggered runs outside that allowlist never receive the required lifecycle labels and comments. The request explicitly covers every start path and does not make queue admission configuration a prerequisite. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.test.ts". The disabled-queue CLI probe printed "disabled-queue labels: [] comments: 0" and failed with "Expected to contain: limitless:in-progress; Received: []".
findings.suggestion: Schedule lifecycle delivery independently of issue selection and apply it to issue-linked runs regardless of queue admission settings, retaining discreet comment suppression.
