findings.failure_scenario: Start a CLI run with Closes #7 in a GitHub repository without github.queue configuration. No lifecycle updates are delivered.

output.summary: Found four defects using isolated probes against the real store and lifecycle code, with fake GitHub responses and dependency stubs. Repository tests and typecheck could not load because entities, the MCP SDK, and Bun types are missing. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Failed-label write errors allow CLI-linked issues to be picked again
findings.detail: The label loop removes in-progress before adding failed. If that addition fails, the queue proceeds with neither status label. For CLI/MCP runs linked through Closes directives, latestIssueRun returns null because it only searches issue source references, so admission accepts the issue without re-approval. Probe `bun run "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts" repick` returned `{"labels":[],"result":{"eligible":true,"priority":1}}` and failed with `AssertionError: failed CLI-linked issue must not be re-picked without re-approval during label-write failure`.
findings.suggestion: Include all linked-run failures in the existing admission evidence and prevent pending failed-label delivery from enabling admission. Preserve the single claim check.
findings.failure_scenario: A CLI run containing Closes #7 fails. Removing in-progress succeeds, adding failed returns HTTP 503, and the subsequent queue query sees the original trusted priority label.

findings.title: Failure and needs-human comments omit the required reason
findings.detail: Both comments always use fixed text, even when the reason is safe to publish. This misses the explicit requirement to comment with the reason; the new tests instead assert its omission. Probe `bun run "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts" reason` posted only `failed: see https://factory.example.com/runs/...` and failed with `AssertionError: failure comment must include its safe reason`.
findings.suggestion: Persist the event's reason, redact credentials, sanitize and check the complete body, and use fixed fallback text only when publication is blocked.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails with the public reason Gate typecheck failed. Issue watchers receive a generic failure link without that reason.

findings.title: Private-text rejection permanently drops the fallback comment
findings.detail: When the publication check rejects a body, the effect is marked done without posting anything. The request requires a fixed safe message instead. Probe `bun run "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts" fallback` returned `{"comments":[],"labels":["limitless:needs-you"],"checkpoint":"done"}` and failed with `AssertionError: private-text rejection must post a fixed safe fallback`.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint and deliver a checked fixed fallback that omits blocked values. Apply this behavior during initial observation and pending-body revalidation.
findings.failure_scenario: The configured UI hostname appears in private-strings.txt. Every lifecycle body containing that URL is permanently suppressed, including needs-human notifications.

findings.title: Transitions between polls have no durable lifecycle checkpoint
findings.detail: Effects are created from the current run snapshot only during polling. A needs-human transition followed by resolution before the next poll disappears without a recorded event or comment. Probe `bun run "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts" transition` returned status resolved, only the started comment, and a null needs-human checkpoint; it failed with `AssertionError: needs-human transition must survive resolution before the next poll`.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle events durably when run transitions occur, then let polling deliver those pending events independently of the current status.
findings.failure_scenario: A run enters needs_human and the owner resolves it in the UI within the polling interval. The next poll sees only resolved and never posts the required needs-human comment.

output.summary: Reviewed lifecycle persistence, polling, eligibility, and publication. Isolated probes reproduced four defects. `bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts test/github-notifier.test.ts test/land-queue.test.ts` could not load because dependency `entities` is missing. Repository files were unchanged.

findings.title: Persist lifecycle transitions when run state changes
findings.detail: Effects are recorded only when polling observes the current status. Store.updateRun and resolveRun do not enqueue lifecycle effects, so intermediate transitions disappear permanently. The dependency-stubbed probe `bun "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts"` returned `"check":"needs_human transition between polls is retained","passed":false`; only the started comment remained.
findings.suggestion: Durably enqueue lifecycle events alongside the corresponding run-state transaction, then let polling deliver those recorded events.
findings.failure_scenario: After one poll, a run reaches needs_human and is resolved before the next poll or daemon restart. Its needs-you comment and lifecycle event are never recorded or delivered.

findings.title: Decouple lifecycle delivery from queue admission
findings.detail: Lifecycle handling requires the repository to remain in an enabled githubQueue, and its only scheduler is startIssueQueue. Consequently CLI, MCP, and webhook runs outside that configuration receive no lifecycle labels. Disabling admission also abandons already-managed runs. `bun "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts"` returned `"check":"disabling admission does not abandon an active run","passed":false`, with labels still `["limitless:in-progress"]` after failure.
findings.suggestion: Schedule lifecycle reconciliation independently of automatic issue admission and continue delivering outstanding effects for existing runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A run receives in-progress, queue admission is disabled, and the run subsequently fails. Its in-progress label remains indefinitely and no failure comment appears.

findings.title: Publish sanitized needs-human and failure reasons
findings.detail: Both messages always contain fixed text and a UI link; run.error is never included, even when entirely public. This omits the explicitly requested reason. `bun "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts"` returned `"check":"ordinary failure reason is published","passed":false`; the posted message was `Limitless run run-1 failed: see https://example.com/runs/run-1.`
findings.suggestion: Include the recorded reason after credential redaction and private-string checking, using fixed fallback text when publication is blocked.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails with the public reason `gate lint failed`. Issue watchers receive no explanation of the failure.

findings.title: Post a safe fallback instead of discarding blocked comments
findings.detail: Publication-check failures mark the comment done without posting anything; the delivery-time check repeats this behavior. The request requires a fixed public fallback. `bun "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts"` returned `"check":"private UI link uses fixed public fallback","passed":false`, with `"comments":[]` and the failed effect marked `"state":"done"`.
findings.suggestion: Check and persist a fixed fallback body that omits blocked values, then deliver it through the normal checkpointed comment path.
findings.failure_scenario: cfg.uiUrl contains a configured private string. Every lifecycle comment is permanently suppressed, including failure and needs-you notifications.

output.summary: Reviewed allowance handling, CI path matching, verify-change repairs, and delivery paths. No concrete defects found. Allowance parsing checks and git diff --check passed. Targeted regression tests could not load because dependencies are absent (`entities` missing).

Reviewed audit matching, allowance propagation, publication paths, restarts, and verify-change handling. No concrete defects found. Allowance probes and diff checks passed. Six targeted test suites could not start because dependencies are absent (`Cannot find package 'entities'`).
Found a production restart gap using a focused probe against the real scheduler. Diff checks passed. The targeted restart tests could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Keep incomplete rollback eligible for startup recovery
findings.detail: Persisting status needs_human before rollback prevents automatic recovery: Scheduler.start() only requeues running and waiting_input runs, and dispatches only queued runs. A restart after this save therefore never reaches rollbackRejectedMerge. The new tests hide this by invoking executeRun directly. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/post-merge-rejection-recovery-probe.ts"`, using the real Scheduler with an interrupted rejection fixture, produced `{"status":"needs_human","pendingRebaseSha":"base","engineResumeCalls":0}` and `AssertionError: Restart must resume the recorded rejection to finish rollback` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.suggestion: Persist the rejection while retaining a recoverable status until rollback completes, or explicitly recover unfinished rejection checkpoints at startup. Test recovery through Scheduler.start().
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after the rejection checkpoint is saved, either before reset or immediately after reset. Startup skips the terminal run, leaving rollback or checkpoint cleanup unfinished; a restart before reset also leaves the rejected merge checked out.

output.summary: Found a restart recovery defect and reproduced it with an isolated scheduler probe. Diff whitespace checks passed. Delivery tests were blocked by missing entities; lint hit a sandbox temp-write error, and typecheck lacked Bun types.

findings.title: Keep unfinished rollback eligible for restart recovery
findings.detail: This write marks the run needs_human before rollback completes, but Scheduler.start() only recovers running and waiting_input runs. A daemon restart therefore never invokes rollbackRejectedMerge for this checkpoint. The new tests conceal this by calling executeRun directly. Probe command: bun run "$TMPDIR/rejection-recovery-probe.ts". Output: {"status":"needs_human","rollbackCheckpointPending":true,"executions":0}, followed by AssertionError: daemon restart must resume the recorded rejection to finish rollback (0 !== 1). The same probe with status running executes recovery once.
findings.suggestion: Persist the rejection while retaining a recoverable status until rollback completes, or explicitly recover unfinished rejection checkpoints in the scheduler. Exercise restart through scheduler startup.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after rejection persistence or immediately after git reset. On startup, the terminal run is skipped, leaving rollback cleanup and persisted pending-merge state unfinished.

output.summary: Confirmed transaction rollback, persistence across reopening, deduplication, and final claim refusals with scratch probes. Reproduced two command-filter defects. Repository tests, lint, and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies, tools, and Bun types.

findings.title: Defer commands when factory identity cannot be resolved
findings.detail: Catching identity errors as null disables the factory-author exclusion while still processing slash commands. This violates the factory-author and retryability invariants. With the real queue and store, `bun "$TMPDIR/comment-command-probe.ts" identity` output `{"mode":"identity","runs":1,"processed":1,"logs":[]}`, followed by `AssertionError: Factory-authored commands must not run when identity lookup fails` (`1 !== 0`). Only lifecycle delivery was stubbed.
findings.suggestion: Leave commands retryable when identity resolution fails, or use independently verified factory-author information before processing them.
findings.failure_scenario: The App bot is included in trusted logins, its unedited slash command is newer than the boundary, and identity resolution fails after the issue query succeeds. The bot's command creates a run and is permanently recorded.

findings.title: Do not reject owner commands merely quoting factory markers
findings.detail: The substring check silently rejects legitimate requests containing marker examples, even when written by a trusted human. `bun "$TMPDIR/comment-command-probe.ts" marker` output `{"mode":"marker","runs":0,"processed":0,"logs":[]}`, followed by `AssertionError: Trusted unedited commands containing marker text must run` (`0 !== 1`). The otherwise identical ordinary-command probe created one run.
findings.suggestion: Identify actual factory comments using author information or recorded comment IDs; avoid treating marker text anywhere in a request as proof of factory authorship.
findings.failure_scenario: After the enable boundary, the owner posts `/limitless Fix the <!-- limitless-lifecycle:... --> marker parser` on an open issue. The unedited command is skipped forever without a refusal or diagnostic.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and reproduced three failures using real integration code and SQLite with fake GitHub responses. Supplied tests could not start because dependency resolution failed. Assumed out-of-scope PR comments should retain existing webhook behavior. Reproduction command: bun --tsconfig-override "$TMPDIR/review-deps-Ln1mZq/tsconfig.json" "$TMPDIR/review-deps-Ln1mZq/comment-probes.ts". No repository files changed.

findings.title: PR comment commands are swallowed by the queue hint branch
findings.detail: GitHub also sends issue_comment events for pull requests. This branch intercepts them, but the queue queries only issues, so those commands disappear. The reproduction command in the summary returned: {"queueStatus":200,"queueRunCount":0,"hints":1,"nonQueueStatus":201}, followed by assertion failure `200 !== 201`.
findings.suggestion: Restrict the queue hint branch to issue comments without issue.pull_request, preserving the existing PR comment path.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner posts /limitless fix this PR on a pull request in a configured queue repository. The webhook records it as ignored and triggers a poll that cannot find the PR.

findings.title: Marker substring filtering silently rejects valid owner commands
findings.detail: Containing marker text does not establish that the factory posted a comment. A trusted owner may legitimately discuss that text in a request. The reproduction command in the summary returned: {"control":{"runs":1,"processed":true},"actual":{"runs":0,"processed":false}}, followed by assertion failure `0 !== 1`.
findings.suggestion: Identify factory comments through posting identity or recorded comment IDs rather than rejecting marker text anywhere in a request.
findings.failure_scenario: An unedited, post-boundary owner comment says `/limitless fix the parser for ` followed by a quoted <!-- limitless-lifecycle:... --> marker. Every poll silently skips this otherwise valid command.

findings.title: Identity lookup failure disables factory-author exclusion
findings.detail: Catching identity errors as null makes bot null, so author.toLowerCase() === bot cannot exclude the factory. Slash commands still execute and are permanently recorded. The reproduction command in the summary returned {"runs":1,"processed":true}, followed by assertion failure `1 !== 0` for a factory-authored comment.
findings.suggestion: Keep commands retryable when the factory identity cannot be established, or retain independently verified bot identity for the exclusion check.
findings.failure_scenario: The trusted list includes the App bot, a successful GraphQL response contains its slash command, and the subsequent identity lookup fails, such as during token refresh. The factory starts a run from its own comment despite the explicit exclusion invariant.

output.summary: Found two attribution/finalization defects. All 34 classifier and persistence tests passed, including Homebrew SQLite compatibility. Pipeline tests, lint, and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies or tools.

findings.title: Record the gates stage's round for initial verification
findings.detail: Initial verify-change checks run through oneRound(ctx, -1), while ctx.state.round remains 0. Observations therefore receive round 0, and completion with round -1 skips them. They remain unfinalized despite the stage completing; terminal handling can later misclassify regressions as unclassified/interrupted. Targeted command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-d0a-observations.ts"` produced `initial verification completion: [{"round":0,"history":null,"class":null}]`.
findings.suggestion: Capture the active stage's round when inserting observations and add coverage through initial verify-change execution.
findings.failure_scenario: A verify-change run's initial round -1 executes a failing check. Its observation is stored under round 0 and excluded from its completion transaction.

findings.title: Recognize credential-bearing LAN jobs that complete locally
findings.detail: WorkerStore.keepLocal marks credential-bearing jobs failed with worker=null but sets neither failure_reason nor setup_fallback. After local completion, this function returns unknown attribution, causing observations to lose coordinator location, OS, and captured load. Null location also prevents setup promotion. Targeted command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-d0a-observations.ts"` produced `local LAN completion: {"location":null,"remote":false,"loadCaptured":true}`. The probe stubbed only unused HTML-decoding and Git dependencies.
findings.suggestion: Persist an explicit local-completion marker and use it consistently for execution attribution, including the keepLocal path.
findings.failure_scenario: A LAN gate request contains a registered credential, executes locally through keepLocal, and fails. Its observation incorrectly records unknown location and OS with null load.

output.summary: Reviewed persistence, replay, classification and migration compatibility. Found three defects with focused failing probes. 34 targeted tests passed; pipeline/worker tests and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies.

findings.title: Record durable results before rejecting incompatible handles
findings.detail: Observation happens only after executeGate returns, but resumeGateExecution can first reject and clear a completed in-place handle when its release, environment or port differs. Its stored failed result is then never observed. A focused probe using the real resume path and a completed job from an older release failed: `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-resume.test.ts"` produced `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0`.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint an unrecorded completed durable result before invalidating its handle or starting another execution, independently of whether that handle remains eligible for reuse.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place gate finishes with a failure, the daemon stops before the evidence insert, and deployment changes the release SHA. Resume rejects the old handle, clears it and reruns without recording the original failure.

findings.title: Require valid provenance before classifying a resumed pass
findings.detail: The earlier-stage branch treats any successful result as retry_passed without validating execution provenance. The engine's confirm callback only withholds reusable gate evidence when trackedClean is false; it still completes with passing comparisons. Consequently, earlier failures become flaky, or load for timeouts, even when the resumed check passed by modifying tracked files. `bun test "$TMPDIR/failure-observation-review.test.ts"` failed the invalid-provenance probe with `Expected: not "flaky"`.
findings.suggestion: Carry execution provenance into observation finalization and require a validated pass on the recorded SHA and unchanged tracked tree before assigning retry_passed.
findings.failure_scenario: A failure is observed, the daemon restarts before stage completion, and the next initial execution edits tracked files before passing. The earlier observation is permanently finalized as flaky despite invalid provenance.

findings.title: Preserve timeout rerun history when rerun setup fails
findings.detail: When a timeout triggers the stage rerun and that rerun fails during setup, compareGates emits only the setup failure and synthetic not_run checks. Finalization excludes not_run, finds no comparison for the observed timeout and assigns no_retry, losing the attempted stage rerun. `bun test "$TMPDIR/failure-observation-review.test.ts"` produced `Expected: "rerun_failed"; Received: "no_retry"`.
findings.suggestion: Pass the stage's timeout-rerun outcome into finalization independently of executed-check comparisons, while continuing to exclude synthetic checks from observation inserts.
findings.failure_scenario: The initial test check times out; the timeout rerun's dependency setup fails before tests execute. The initial timeout is finalized with history no_retry instead of rerun_failed.

output.summary: No concrete defects found. Reviewed recovery, rollback ordering, reconciliation, and release following. Passed 76 isolated deploy/restart tests and eight install/recovery scenarios. Unmodified targeted tests were blocked by missing entities and incompatible Zod dependencies; real executor subprocess tests remain unverified.

Found two reproducible defects. 78 focused tests passed with client-port resolution stubbed. Unmodified broader checks were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies. No repository files were changed.

findings.title: Reject timed-out executor control commands
findings.detail: The control helper checks only exitCode for disable, enable and bootstrap, although sh can return timedOut=true with exitCode=0. Unlike inspection, these paths treat an unconfirmed operation as successful. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-executor-probe.ts" rollback` produced: {"error":"Error: deploy gate failed; staying on previous\nError: gate failed","rollbackCheckedOutPrevious":true,"loaded":false,"disabled":false,"intentRetained":true}. The fake disable returned exit zero with timedOut=true, and rollback still restored the previous checkout.
findings.suggestion: Reject timedOut results for every executor mutation. Add coverage proving an unconfirmed disable prevents checkout restoration and an unconfirmed bootstrap prevents successful reconciliation.
findings.failure_scenario: During rollback, executor bootout succeeds but disable times out with exitCode=0. The helper authorizes restoring older code without confirming persistent disable, allowing launchd to reload the executor against that older release.

findings.title: Redact inspection diagnostics before exposing them
findings.detail: Unknown inspection results embed raw launchctl stdout and stderr in reason, which status logs directly without redaction. Launchctl output can contain environment credentials. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-executor-probe.ts" status` produced: {"registeredRedactionWorks":true,"logs":["custom.executor: unknown: launchctl print gui/501/custom.executor failed (timed out, exit 0): environment = { REVIEW_TOKEN => synthetic-review-registered-credential }","release: ","health: ok"]}. The registered credential therefore reaches output despite being recognized by redactCredentials.
findings.suggestion: Apply redactCredentials when constructing inspection failure reasons, including caught errors, before returning or logging them.
findings.failure_scenario: A launchctl print operation times out after emitting environment data containing a registered credential; limitless service status prints that credential verbatim.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding admission logic. Isolated publication checks passed, but a repository-identity probe reproduced a compatibility regression. Targeted tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies or temporary-directory permissions.

findings.title: Preserve existing repository registrations when canonicalizing queue names
findings.detail: Lowercased queue names now reach Factory.createRun, but resolveRepo and Store.getRepoBySlug still use case-sensitive lookup. An existing mixed-case registration is missed, creating a duplicate repository with the current global merge policy. This can change a previously PR-only repository to automatic merging. Offline command `bun "$TMPDIR/issue-queue-repo-identity.ts"`, using the actual Store and source-extracted resolver with an injected GitHub response, produced `{"beforeReusesRepo":true,"afterReusesRepo":false,"beforeMergePolicy":"pr","afterMergePolicy":"auto","repos":["Owner/Project","owner/project"],"githubLookups":1}` and failed with `AssertionError: Canonicalized queue admission must reuse the registered repository`.
findings.suggestion: Resolve canonical queue names to existing registrations case-insensitively before creating runs, preserving their IDs and settings. Add a regression covering an existing mixed-case registration.
findings.failure_scenario: The database contains Owner/Project with mergePolicy=pr, the queue config names Owner/Project, and the current global merge policy is auto. After this change, queue admission creates owner/project with mergePolicy=auto instead of reusing the existing repository.

output.summary: No actionable defects found. Five isolated queue/Store regression probes passed with lifecycle reconciliation stubbed. Repository tests, lint, typecheck and benchmark were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies. Worktree unchanged.

Found a release-recovery race that deletes an unresolved intent. With temporary dependency isolation, 198 existing tests passed and two regression probes failed. Normal tests, lint, typecheck, and the Homebrew subprocess check were blocked by missing or incompatible dependencies.

findings.title: Classify the moved tip before discarding the release intent
findings.detail: Every moved replay result marks confirmed ownership lost and clears the intent, even when result.tip.record is malformed or contains no evidence of supersession. This bypasses the classification used for the initial read and violates the requirement to preserve unresolved intents under uncertainty. The temporary regression command `bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/lease-review-preload.ts" "$TMPDIR/lease-review-race.test.ts"` failed both cases with `Expected: "pending"; Received: "superseded"`; the resulting row had `confirmed.state: "lost"` and `intent: null`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the recovery classification to result.tip. Preserve the intent for malformed or otherwise unclassifiable tips; mark ownership lost only when the tip establishes supersession. Add coverage for these races.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery reads the confirmed tip and starts replaying a release. Before updateRefs arrives, another writer installs a malformed record, or a different record with the same generation, holder, and run. The CAS correctly rejects the release, but recovery deletes its final status and checkpoint intent instead of retaining it for reconciliation.

output.summary: Found a recovery invariant violation, reproduced with two failing assertions. Migration smoke check passed. Repository tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by incompatible or missing dependencies and temp-directory permissions.

findings.title: Classify the moved tip before discarding ownership and intent
findings.detail: Every `moved` replay result unconditionally marks ownership lost and clears the journal. ClaimClient can return `moved` with a malformed record or the same generation, holder and run; neither establishes supersession. This contradicts the initial-read classification and the requirement to retain malformed pending intents. Regression command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-recovery-review.test.ts"` (dependency-isolated recovery probe). Both cases failed with `Expected: "pending"`, `Received: "superseded"`; output showed confirmed state `lost` and intent `null`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same record classification to `result.tip` as to the initial read. Preserve the intent for malformed or otherwise unclassifiable tips; mark lost only when supersession is established.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery reads the confirmed tip and starts replaying a release. Before updateRefs arrives, another commit containing a malformed claim replaces that tip. CAS fails and ClaimClient returns `moved`; recovery deletes the final release intent instead of retaining it for later reconciliation.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding execution paths. An actual land executor probe reproduced incorrect persisted retry history. Also passed 42 bundled classifier/store tests; normal targeted suites could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Do not record a retry for an unretried land timeout
findings.detail: The comparison unconditionally sets firstAttempt, even when retries.has(r) is false. For a primary timeout, observationHistory consequently records rerun_failed although only one execution ran. This persists false retry evidence for downstream failure analysis. Targeted command `bun test ./probes/land-executor.test.js`, run from `$TMPDIR/d0b-review.ondiLh`, failed with `Expected: "no_retry"; Received: "rerun_failed"`; its assertion that exactly one execution ran passed.
findings.suggestion: Set firstAttempt only when a retry actually ran, and extend the existing ineligible land timeout test to assert history is no_retry.
findings.failure_scenario: A primary land check times out. Targeted retry eligibility rejects it, leaving the retries map empty, but finalization saves history=rerun_failed.

output.summary: Found two classification defects with isolated mocked-executor/SQLite probes. The targeted suite could not load because dependencies are missing (`entities`). Diff whitespace checks passed; the checkout is unchanged.

findings.title: Preserve slow-regression evidence across durable gate replay
findings.detail: A resumed gates stage gets a new stage ID, while replaying the same durable handle preserves the existing observation through ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. This stage-ID filter therefore excludes that observation, so the selector never stores slow_regression=1. The isolated probe using real runGateExecution and FailureObservations, with this selection/update logic, failed. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/d0b-review-probe.ts"`. Output: `{"resumedStage":2,"observationStage":1,"selectedHandles":[],"slow_regression":0,"class":"flaky","history":"retry_passed"}` followed by `AssertionError: a passing slow-regression retry must remain load after restart`.
findings.suggestion: Select observations by the durable execution identity, including run, round, SHA and purpose, rather than requiring the current stage ID. Add a restart test immediately after observation insertion.
findings.failure_scenario: A LAN post-merge primary failure is observed, the daemon restarts before the gate-result checkpoint, and the resumed slow-regression re-check passes. The observation is finalized as flaky instead of load.

findings.title: Carry retry confinement failures into the land comparison verdict
findings.detail: The synthesized comparison always uses regressed, even when the retry has a confinement error. The shared classifier detects confinement from the primary observation or the comparison verdict; consequently this path records regression and loses D0a's confinement precedence. The isolated finalizer probe failed. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/d0b-land-classification-probe.ts"`. Output: `{"class":"regression","history":"retry_failed","primaryConfinement":0,"retryConfinement":true}` followed by `AssertionError: land retry confinement must retain classifier precedence`.
findings.suggestion: Derive the comparison verdict from the effective result, using confinement_error when confinementFailed returns true, as retryRegressions does.
findings.failure_scenario: A land primary test fails normally, then its targeted retry cannot run because confinement fails. The entry blocks, but its finalized observation incorrectly reports a code regression.

output.summary: Found two ownership/reconciliation defects, reproduced by three failing probes. All 34 submitted tests passed with temporary dependency shims. Normal tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by incompatible or missing dependencies. The checkout was unchanged.

findings.title: Reconcile pending intents before refusing another run
findings.detail: This guard returns refused before reconciliation whenever another run has an intent, including an acquisition that never obtained ownership. Once GitHub becomes readable, run B still cannot reconcile and forget A's failed acquisition. This violates invariants 8 and 9. A temporary regression probe run with `bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/lease-review-preload.ts" "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts"` failed with `Expected: "held"; Received: "refused"`.
findings.suggestion: After rejecting obsolete handles, reconcile the intent first and return wait if unresolved. Then reload the row and apply the cross-run ownership guard.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A's first acquisition fails to send and returns unconfirmed because the subsequent read fails. GitHub becomes readable and the ref remains absent. Run B calls acquire before the renewal loop reconciles A's intent; it receives refused instead of acquiring generation 1.

findings.title: Exclude released and lost history from the superseded guard
findings.detail: The superseded check treats every confirmed row as current ownership, including released and lost rows. Once a higher generation appears, repeated acquisitions keep returning superseded, preventing subsequent handoffs or adoption. Two probes using `bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/lease-review-preload.ts" "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts"` failed with `Expected: "held"; Received: "superseded"`: adoption of an expired successor and acquisition after a later same-run release.
findings.suggestion: Apply the ownership-loss guard to currently held confirmed ownership. Let released/lost history proceed through the released-tip and takeover decision rules.
findings.failure_scenario: The local row confirms a released generation 1. Another member acquires and releases generation 2 for the same run. Local acquire should obtain generation 3 and inherit the checkpoint, but instead marks the historical row lost and returns superseded indefinitely. Likewise, a lost generation 1 cannot adopt an expired generation 2 with takeover enabled.

output.summary: Found three defects through four failing isolated probes using the actual lease-store methods and in-memory SQLite. The repository suite could not start because available Zod lacks prefault; lint and typecheck were unavailable due to sandbox/temp and missing dependency errors. The checkout was not modified.

findings.title: Enroll reconciliation-confirmed acquisitions in the renewal loop
findings.detail: The loop only renews entries in handles, but handles is populated exclusively by directly applied writes. An acquisition confirmed by reconcileLeaseIntent or startup recovery remains absent forever, so active is never called and the lease expires without renewal. Command: LEASE_REVIEW_ROOT="$PWD" bun test --cwd "$TMPDIR" "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.js". Both reconciliation and recovery probes failed with: "Expected number of calls: 1", "Received number of calls: 0".
findings.suggestion: Populate the renewal registry when reconciliation or recovery confirms held ownership, without manufacturing a fresh anchor.
findings.failure_scenario: An acquisition reaches GitHub but returns unconfirmed. A later tick confirms its intent and clears it, yet subsequent ticks never renew that active generation. The same happens when startup recovery confirms the acquisition.

findings.title: Reconcile pending intents before refusing another run
findings.detail: The cross-run guard returns refused before reconciliation whenever an intent exists. A never-confirmed acquisition whose ref is now readable and absent therefore blocks another run instead of being dropped and forgotten. Unresolved intents also incorrectly return refused rather than wait. Command: LEASE_REVIEW_ROOT="$PWD" bun test --cwd "$TMPDIR" "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.js". The dropped-intent probe failed with: "Expected: \"held\"", "Received: \"refused\"".
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the intent first, return wait while unresolved, then re-read the row and enforce the cross-run ownership guard.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A leaves an unconfirmed first-acquisition intent and ends. GitHub becomes readable with the ref absent. Run B calls acquire before a loop tick and is refused without any reconciliation request.

findings.title: Keep retry-local ownership separate from confirmed ownership
findings.detail: Assigning mine to confirmed lets the superseded check use a tentative acquisition generation instead of durable confirmed ownership. This violates the requirement that superseded never derive from a pending acquisition. Command: LEASE_REVIEW_ROOT="$PWD" bun test --cwd "$TMPDIR" "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.js". With the SQLite row absent, the retry probe failed with: "Expected: \"refused\"", "Received: \"superseded\"".
findings.suggestion: Use mine only to retry same-holder contention. Base loss and superseded classification exclusively on the row's confirmed ownership.
findings.failure_scenario: A first acquisition gets moved to a same-holder generation-1 record with different fields. Before its retry read, another holder advances to generation 2. The manager returns superseded although it never confirmed any generation.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, verification ordering, infrastructure classification, and resume paths. Found one browser-availability defect, reproduced with a fake-stream probe. Focused repository tests could not initialize because entities is missing and the resolved Zod version is incompatible.

findings.title: Require successful browser setup before recording availability
findings.detail: The absence of a browser_unavailable warning does not prove successful setup. browserMcp constructs configuration before the CLI initializes MCP; a subsequent startup failure produces no such warning. ClaudeStreamParser ignores failed mcp_servers statuses in initialization records. Consequently, a genuine infrastructure block becomes unclear and triggers implementation feedback rounds. A fake-stream probe exercising the existing parser and this classification expression reproduced this. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/browser-startup-review.ts". Output: {"mcpStatus":"failed","structuredResultRetained":true,"warningCodes":[],"browserContext":"available"}, followed by "FAIL: failed MCP startup counted as successful browser setup"; exit 1.
findings.suggestion: Record an engine-owned successful browser-setup outcome for the invocation and require it before setting available. Preserve unavailable or unknown handling when MCP initialization fails or success cannot be confirmed, and add a fake initialization-failure regression test.
findings.failure_scenario: The preview is ready and browser configuration succeeds, but Playwright MCP fails to initialize. Claude continues without browser tools and returns a marked criterion blocked by the environment. No browser_unavailable warning exists, so the engine incorrectly converts the row to unclear and sends it through implementation rounds.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, verdict ordering, and resume handling. Found a reproducible conflict in browser-criterion authoring. All 23 existing spec-criteria tests passed; browser and pipeline tests could not load because dependencies were missing or incompatible.

findings.title: Allow marked preview checks through the spec validation guard
findings.detail: The prompt now permits browser checks, but outOfRunCriteria still flags “in a browser”, “visually”, and “screenshot” regardless of browser:true. engine.ts then labels these valid criteria invalid and instructs the author to replace them with commands/tests or move them out of scope. This guarantees an unnecessary spec invocation for common browser-check wording and can remove the visual acceptance check before verification. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { expect } from "bun:test"; import { outOfRunCriteria } from "./src/pipeline/spec-criteria.ts"; expect(outOfRunCriteria({ acceptance_criteria: [{ id: "AC-1", browser: true, how_to_verify: "Inspect the UI preview visually" }] } as never)).toEqual([]);'. Output: error: expect(received).toEqual(expected); Expected: []; Received: [{ id: "AC-1", browser: true, how_to_verify: "Inspect the UI preview visually" }].
findings.suggestion: Update the out-of-run guard and rewrite feedback to permit browser verification for marked preview checks while retaining checks for genuinely external requirements. Add focused coverage for this authoring path.
findings.failure_scenario: The spec author returns browser:true with how_to_verify containing “Inspect the UI preview visually”. The engine rejects that permitted verification method and requests a replacement criterion.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, surrounding lifecycle code, privacy checks and command dispatch. Two isolated reconciler probes failed. Repository tests, lint and typecheck were blocked by missing dependencies/tools. The probes used mocked storage/external dependencies and an HTML-decoder stub for ASCII inputs. No repository files changed.

findings.title: Recover uncertain POSTs before suppressing their bodies
findings.detail: A failed body inspection marks the checkpoint done before marker recovery, even when page > 0 records an uncertain prior POST. This violates requirement 4 and loses acknowledgement of an already-visible comment. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/q4-review.test.ts"` failed with `Expected: 42; Received: null`; the probe recorded no GitHub recovery calls and a done checkpoint with commentId null.
findings.suggestion: Recover uncertain effects using the independently generated marker and checkpointed author before closing them. Apply outgoing-body suppression when deciding whether to issue another POST.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question comment but its response is lost. Before restart, its text is added to private-strings.txt. Reconciliation suppresses the stored body and closes the checkpoint without finding the accepted comment.

findings.title: Use fixed diagnostics for delivery and recovery failures
findings.detail: Inspection failures use fixed codes, but delivery/recovery failures still pass raw exceptions to the inherited logger, which checks registered credentials only. Configured private strings therefore escape through diagnostics, contrary to requirement 2. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/q4-review.test.ts"` failed with `Expected to not contain: "private-error-text"; Received: "Issue lifecycle owner/repo#7 run run-1: Error: private-error-text"`.
findings.suggestion: Emit fixed failure codes for publication-related identity, delivery and recovery errors without including exception text.
findings.failure_scenario: A question publication's identity lookup fails with a GitHub App key-path error containing a configured private string. The logger includes that private path verbatim. The same exposure is reproduced by an injected recovery exception.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and traced publication, recovery, and command reservation. An isolated probe confirmed a diagnostic privacy leak. Repository tests, lint, and typecheck could not run successfully because required dependencies and tools are missing or incompatible.

findings.title: Use fixed diagnostic codes for publication failures
findings.detail: Question-delivery failures still pass exception text to logFailure, which only performs literal credential redaction. Configured private strings and percent-encoded credentials can therefore leak through identity or GitHub errors despite being withheld from the question. This violates requirement 2. An isolated probe using the actual reconciler and inspection code, with unrelated import shims, ran `bun "$TMPDIR/q4-review-probe.ts" "$PWD"` and printed `withheld body: true` followed by `encoded credential leaked in diagnostic: true`.
findings.suggestion: Log fixed codes for identity, delivery, and recovery failures instead of exception text. Add coverage where those failures contain configured private strings and encoded credentials.
findings.failure_scenario: A question contains a registered credential in percent-encoded form and is correctly withheld. The awaited identity lookup rejects with an error containing that encoded value. The catch logs the encoded credential verbatim. An identity error naming a configured private key path similarly bypasses private-string protection.

output.summary: Found two reproducible defects in trigger consumption and comment retries. The land-store test passed; conflict-round and migration tests could not load because installed Zod lacks .overwrite(). No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Stale cached snapshots permanently discard valid conflict triggers
findings.detail: The saved GitHub snapshot overrides the supplied observation, even when it describes an older head. processConflictTriggers also uses any saved snapshot without refreshing it. Consequently, a land conflict at the current head can be permanently marked skipped because polling still holds the previous head. Reproduction: `bun "$TMPDIR/conflict-review-probes/stale-snapshot.ts"` output `state: "skipped", reason: "PR head moved"`, followed by `AssertionError: current-head land trigger must create a round` and `0 !== 1`.
findings.suggestion: Refresh observations that disagree with the trigger's head, honor the fresh observation, and retain the trigger pending until its eligibility can be established.
findings.failure_scenario: Polling saved head A; a review round pushes head B; landing B encounters a base conflict before the next poll. The durable trigger for B is consumed against snapshot A and discarded without starting a resolution.

findings.title: Comment retries bypass the duplicate-comment check
findings.detail: The marker lookup occurs outside the retry wrapper used by gh. If GitHub accepts the comment but its response is lost, withGitHubRetry repeats the POST without checking the marker again. This violates the single-comment requirement. A focused reproduction using the actual retry helper, `bun "$TMPDIR/conflict-review-probes/comment-retry.ts"`, output `posted comments: 2` followed by `AssertionError: an accepted post with a lost response must not duplicate the comment` and `2 !== 1`.
findings.suggestion: Put the marker lookup and conditional post together inside each retry attempt, using the underlying runner to avoid nested retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The first conflict-summary comment is stored by GitHub, but gh reports a retryable HTTP 502 or timeout. The automatic retry posts an identical second comment.

output.summary: Reviewed trigger persistence, eligibility, merge preparation, and delivery. Found two correctness defects. Two isolated store checks reproduced stale-observation failures. The integration test could not load because the installed Zod lacks overwrite(); that dependency issue predates this diff.

findings.title: Do not replace current PR observations with cached eligibility
findings.detail: startConflictTrigger replaces its supplied observation with saved poller data, while processConflictTriggers also skips refreshing any PR with a saved snapshot. Consequently, stale eligibility can start rounds for draft/closed PRs or permanently discard valid land triggers. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/conflict-store-review.test.ts". Output: "round created for draft: true" and "trigger after fresh ready observation: [{ state: 'skipped', reason: 'PR is draft' }]"; both assertions failed (0 pass, 2 fail).
findings.suggestion: Refresh PR eligibility for startup and land triggers, use the current observation, and retain pending triggers when eligibility cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller saved a conflicting draft PR. The operator marks it ready and requests landing before another poll. Landing detects conflicts, but the consumer uses the cached draft status and permanently skips the trigger. Subsequent polling sees unchanged CONFLICTING mergeability and emits no replacement trigger.

findings.title: Resolve against the PR's current base branch
findings.detail: Conflict preparation fetches the owning run's original baseBranch. Neither the trigger observation nor delivery validates the PR's current target branch. After a PR is retargeted, a poller conflict therefore merges the wrong branch, or finishes successfully without doing anything when the old base is already an ancestor of the head.
findings.suggestion: Observe and persist the PR's current base identity, merge that base, and validate it before delivery; alternatively, explicitly refuse retargeted PRs.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory PR originally targeting main is retargeted to release and becomes conflicting. main is already contained in the PR head. The poller starts a round, but preparation fetches main and takes the ancestor-to-done path, leaving the actual release conflict unresolved.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and restart, retry, cancellation, and landing paths. Direct probes confirmed lost executor events and retries failing after setup-output cleanup. Targeted tests could not reach assertions because the installed Zod lacks .overwrite(), used by unchanged code. No files were modified.

findings.title: Resumed local retries skip setup after deleting its output
findings.detail: On restart, checkoutCommitted removes dependencies and generated files with git clean -ffdxq. runGateExecution then returns the persisted initial result without rerunning setup, and the pending regression retry contains setup: []. Checks consequently run without their dependencies or build output. A direct local-executor probe produced {"retryBeforeCheckoutCleanup":true,"retryAfterRestartCleanup":false}. The new restart tests use fake results, which cannot expose this filesystem dependency.
findings.suggestion: Restore the setup prerequisites before replaying a local retry after restart, or safely replay the full initial attempt while preserving retry accounting and evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup installs dependencies or generates build output; a check fails transiently; the daemon restarts after persisting the regression-retry handle. Resume deletes the setup output, skips the cached initial execution, and reruns only the check, producing a persistent failure.

findings.title: Persist landing execution handles before attaching
findings.detail: Landing calls executeGate without either a stored handle or a persistence callback. The default callback is a no-op, so the execution handle is never durable. After restart, the queue starts another execution instead of attaching to the one already started. This leaves a daemon gate path outside the requested durability contract.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing check handle against its landing attempt and checked commit, load it on resume, and clear it after consuming the result.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a landing executor is running. The landing entry remains checking, but its handle is lost; the resumed queue calls start again and cannot recover or cancel the original execution.

findings.title: Consume execution events through the shared executor path
findings.detail: executeGate awaits execution.result without reading execution.events. Injected executors receive no GateHooks, so their check events never reach pipeline events or landing logs. The default local implementation masks this by invoking hooks directly. A direct bun -e probe with an executor yielding one successful check event returned {"result":"pass","observedCheckEvents":0,"expected":1}.
findings.suggestion: Consume and dispatch execution events alongside the result through the shared path, with appropriate redaction, and avoid duplicate local notifications.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits check progress through Execution.events and resolves a successful GateRun. The stage completes, but onResult is never called, gate progress is absent, and landing command logs remain empty.

output.summary: Found three defects in restart handling, landing durability, and event forwarding. Two isolated reproductions failed assertions. The requested targeted suites could not load because installed dependencies lack Zod .overwrite() and the MCP SDK module. The worktree was not modified.

findings.title: Restore setup state before resuming a local retry
findings.detail: A resumed gates stage calls checkoutCommitted(), which removes dependencies and build output. This cached-result return then skips the initial execution, including setup, while retryRegressions runs with setup: []. The retry therefore runs in a different environment and can falsely block a valid change. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-resume.ts"` produced `[{"restart":false,"verdict":"flaky","output":""},{"restart":true,"verdict":"regressed","output":"missing-build"}]`, followed by `AssertionError: restart must preserve retry outcome`.
findings.suggestion: Restore the prerequisite setup environment when replaying local retries after restart, while preserving recorded attempts and reattaching pending executions.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup generates build files or installs dependencies; a check fails transiently; the daemon restarts after saving the initial result but before completing its regression retry. Cleanup deletes setup output, the initial result is reused, and the check-only retry fails because its prerequisites are missing.

findings.title: Persist and resume landing execution handles
findings.detail: The landing caller supplies neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback to executeGate(), so the callback defaults to a no-op. The handle is never durable before attach/result, and a restarted landing attempt always calls start again. This leaves the explicitly requested landing path outside the durable executor lifecycle.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle before attaching, reload it on resume, and clear it only after consuming the result. Associate it with the exact checked commit.
findings.failure_scenario: A landing executor starts work and the daemon restarts before its result is recorded. The resumed queue has no handle to attach to and starts another execution instead.

findings.title: Forward executor events to daemon gate observers
findings.detail: executeGate() never consumes execution.events. Gate hooks reach only the internally constructed local executor; an injected executor has no hooks parameter and can report progress only through its event stream. Consequently its check events never reach pipeline events or landing logs. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-events.ts"` produced `{"streamed":0,"delivered":0}` followed by `AssertionError: executor check events must reach gate hooks` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.suggestion: Consume the execution event stream alongside the result and forward check/status events to the appropriate observers, without duplicating local callbacks.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits a completed-check event and returns a successful GateRun. The stage consumes the result, but no gate event or landing check output is recorded.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding gate/editor confinement code; found no concrete introduced defects. Sandbox tests with a temporary HOME: 15 passed, 9 skipped. Real Seatbelt probes were unavailable inside this sandbox. Other targeted tests were blocked by incompatible Zod APIs and a missing MCP dependency, limiting validation.

Found two gaps in gate read confinement. Two focused policy tests passed. Broader tests were blocked by sandbox permissions and missing/incompatible dependencies; real Seatbelt probes skipped because nested Seatbelt is unavailable. Policy reproduction command: bun -e 'import {tmpdir} from "node:os"; import {join} from "node:path"; import {homeReadPolicy,readPolicyScope} from "./src/harness/read-policy.ts"; readPolicyScope.run({home:tmpdir()},()=>{const p=homeReadPolicy([],true); console.log(p.allowRead?.includes(join(tmpdir(),".cargo")),p.denyRead.includes(join(tmpdir(),".cargo/credentials.toml")),p.denyRead.some(d=>"/srv/limitless/runs/other/private".startsWith(d+"/")));});' Output: true false false.

findings.title: Cargo's toolchain allowance exposes its credential files
findings.detail: The gate allowlist grants recursive reads of CARGO_HOME, including credentials and credentials.toml, where Cargo stores registry tokens. Neither file is denied. The generated Seatbelt profile allows the Cargo directory after denying home, so malicious tests or dependency scripts can still read and exfiltrate these credentials. The reproduction in the summary confirms Cargo is allowed and credentials.toml has no specific denial.
findings.suggestion: Allow only the Cargo toolchain/cache directories gates need, excluding credential files, and add a stand-in credential read probe.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner has logged into a registry with Cargo, creating ~/.cargo/credentials.toml; a gate script reads that absolute path and sends its token over HTTPS.

findings.title: Deny the factory data directory when it is outside home
findings.detail: The broad deny covers only the OS home directory. loadConfig supports LIMITLESS_HOME elsewhere, but passes only configDir into configureReadPolicy, leaving the factory data root unprotected except for registered database files. With LIMITLESS_HOME=/srv/limitless, the default-allow profile permits reads of other runs' checkouts, artifacts and other private factory files. The reproduction in the summary confirms an unrelated run under that root matches no denial. This misses the explicit requirement to exclude other runs and factory data.
findings.suggestion: Include the configured factory data root among the broad denied roots, with the same narrow checkout, scratch and Git exceptions used for home.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation sets LIMITLESS_HOME=/srv/limitless while the owner's home is elsewhere. Candidate code running as a gate reads /srv/limitless/runs/other/private or another run's checkout.

output.summary: Found three durability gaps in the executor seam. Direct probes confirmed start→persist→attach ordering, but also confirmed that resumed retries discard their handles. Targeted tests could not execute because the installed Zod lacks .overwrite(), used by unchanged schema code. No files were modified.

findings.title: Resume pending retries through their saved executor handle
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial and rebase handles are eligible for attachment. A restart during baseline-retry, regression-retry or timeout instead discards the saved handle and starts another suite. cancelGateExecution only finds executions in the current process's WeakMap, so it cannot cancel the previous process's execution. A direct probe with a saved regression-retry handle produced ["save:discard","start:new","save:gate-started","attach:new","save:gate-result"], with no attachment or cancellation of the old execution. This violates the requested restart contract; the new tests explicitly assert this incorrect behavior.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough attempt state to resume the pending retry and attach its saved handle. Keep the local executor's setup replay behavior inside the local implementation.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an injected durable executor is running a regression retry. Resume abandons that job and starts a new initial suite, leaving the original job running and ignoring its result.

findings.title: Retain execution identity until its result is durably consumed
findings.detail: The finally block saves a state with gateExecution removed before returning the GateRun to the caller. At that point neither the baseline nor the stage comparison/checkpoint contains this result. A crash after this save loses both the execution identity and its result, so resume calls start again even for an initial execution. Persisting the handle before attach does not close this later durability gap.
findings.suggestion: Persist the completed result alongside its execution identity, or clear the handle atomically with the caller's durable result checkpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: An initial gate execution finishes, gate-result saves the cleared handle, and the daemon exits before lastGates/completedChecks is saved. Restart starts another execution instead of attaching the completed one.

findings.title: Persist and restore handles for landing checks
findings.detail: The landing call supplies neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback to executeGate. Its default persistence callback does nothing, so the handle is never saved before attachment or result consumption. A resumed checking entry always starts another execution. This leaves one required daemon gate path outside the durable executor contract.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the landing execution handle and its commit identity, restore it when resuming checking, and clear it when the result is durably recorded.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after a landing executor starts work but before checks finish. The queue resumes the checking entry without its previous handle and starts duplicate work.

output.summary: Found three durability gaps in execution resume handling. A targeted probe reproduced duplicate execution after a restart. The requested test files could not load because the installed Zod lacks number().overwrite(), used by unchanged code.

findings.title: Handle is cleared before the result is durably consumed
findings.detail: The helper clears and saves gateExecution before returning the GateRun. The caller has not yet persisted the baseline or gate comparison, so a crash here loses both the execution identity and its result. The targeted command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-resume.ts"` reproduced this boundary: `Durable state before caller stores returned result: {"round":0}`, followed by `Starts after restart at that boundary: 2 attached IDs: 1,2` and `Expected restart to reuse execution 1; started 2 executions`.
findings.suggestion: Keep the handle until the caller checkpoints the consumed result, or persist the result alongside the handle before clearing it.
findings.failure_scenario: An execution finishes, gate-result saves the cleared handle, and the daemon stops before the caller saves the baseline or completed gate stage. Resume starts the same work again.

findings.title: Resume discards execution handles for every retry
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial and rebase handles can be reattached. A pending timeout, baseline-retry or regression-retry handle is discarded when the stage resumes from its initial execution. cancelGateExecution only consults an in-memory map, so after a daemon restart it neither cancels nor attaches to that existing execution. This violates the requested restart contract for gate retries; the new tests explicitly expect replacement starts.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the stage's retry phase and preceding results so resume can attach to the pending retry. Preserve local setup replay through executor-specific handling rather than discarding durable identities for all executors.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an injected executor is running a regression retry. Resume forgets that handle and starts fresh initial and retry executions while the original execution remains unobserved.

findings.title: Landing checks never persist their execution handle
findings.detail: The landing queue calls executeGate without a stored handle or persistence callback. Its default persistence callback does nothing, so attach and result consumption proceed without recording the execution identity anywhere. Restarting a checking entry therefore always starts another execution, leaving this daemon gate path outside the required durability mechanism.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle before attach, reload it when resuming the checking entry, and clear it together with the durable check outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after a landing executor starts checks but before the entry advances to waiting_ci. The resumed entry calls start again instead of attaching to the previously started work.

output.summary: Reviewed policy construction and gate/editor wiring. Sandbox checks: 16 passed, 12 skipped because nested Seatbelt is unavailable. Scratch tests could not load because installed Zod lacks prefault. Found one remaining read-boundary gap.

findings.title: Deny the factory data root when it resides outside home
findings.detail: The gate policy denies only home and specific credential/database paths. With LIMITLESS_HOME outside home, or ~/.limitless symlinked outside home, the default allow rule therefore permits reading other runs' checkouts, logs and factory files. This misses the explicit requirement to exclude factory data except this run's allowances. Targeted command: bun -e 'import {tmpdir} from "node:os"; import {homeReadPolicy,readPolicyScope} from "./src/harness/read-policy.ts"; readPolicyScope.run({home:tmpdir(),environment:{}},()=>console.log(homeReadPolicy(["/opt/factory/runs/current","/opt/scratch"],true).denyRead.some(p=>"/opt/factory/runs/other/private.txt".startsWith(p+"/"))));' Output: false.
findings.suggestion: Include canonical factory data and worktree roots in the shared gate read policy, then grant only the current checkout, scratch and required Git/toolchain paths.
findings.failure_scenario: Set LIMITLESS_HOME=/opt/factory, or symlink ~/.limitless to an external volume. A malicious gate reads /opt/factory/runs/other/worktree files or other private factory artifacts by absolute path.

output.summary: Reviewed policy construction, caller coverage, path resolution, overlap checks, and launch preflights; found no confirmed defects. Targeted checks: 32 tests passed, 12 skipped. findings.title: Metadata lookup can overwrite a concurrent cancellation
findings.detail: The new awaited lookup catches cancellation as null and then calls landed unconditionally. cancel() can mark the entry cancelled during this await, but landed() overwrites it. An isolated bun -e check mocking mergePullRequest as successful and rejecting the held client lookup after q.cancel(1) printed exactly: "after cancel: cancelled\nafter metadata lookup abort: landed".
findings.suggestion: Recheck the abort signal and current entry state after the metadata lookup before changing queue state. Preserve confirmed merge evidence separately if necessary.
findings.failure_scenario: The merge succeeds, the metadata lookup remains pending, and the user cancels the land entry. Aborting the lookup causes the cancelled entry to become landed and emits land.landed.

findings.title: Metadata backfill leaves the reported merge-feed disagreement intact
findings.detail: Backfill updates runs only; the existing run.merged feed item retains null fields because its trigger fires only on the initial merged transition. An isolated bun -e Store/reconcileMergedRuns check produced runMergedBy:"actor" while the feed still contained mergedBy:null and mergedAt:null. With polling disabled, the new reconciliation branch also never calls the available client, so a failed initial metadata lookup leaves even the run fields empty permanently.
findings.suggestion: Provide a bounded recovery path for missing merge metadata, including polling-disabled installations, and ensure the existing merge-feed record reflects recovered metadata without emitting duplicate merge events.
findings.failure_scenario: The post-merge metadata request fails or returns incomplete metadata. The queue emits run.merged with null fields. A later saved MERGED observation fills the run row but leaves the feed wrong; without polling, neither is repaired.

output.summary: Found a merge-metadata recovery defect affecting the requested feed accuracy. All 62 notifier tests passed. MCP, CLI HTTP, and land-queue suites could not load because installed MCP SDK modules are missing.

findings.title: Missing merge observations leave permanently incomplete feed entries
findings.detail:
If the new post-merge lookup fails or returns incomplete metadata, landed() immediately marks both runs merged with null fields. Later reconciliation can fill the run row from a saved snapshot, but resolveMergedRun only updates metadata; the feed trigger fires only when merged changes from false to true. Consequently run.merged permanently retains null fields, leaving the specific feed disagreement in the request unresolved. With polling disabled, reconciliation also skips fetching these already-merged runs, so even the parent row can remain incomplete permanently. Reproduction command: bun --eval 'import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { reconcileMergedRuns } from "./src/integrations/github-notifier.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const repo=s.upsertRepo({slug:"test/repo",kind:"github",url:"unused",localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); const r=s.createRun(repo,{repo:repo.slug,prompt:"fix"}); const url="https://github.com/test/repo/pull/1"; s.updateRun(r.id,{status:"succeeded",prUrl:url,merged:true}); s.saveGithubPr({url,repo:repo.slug,runId:r.id,delivered:1,nodeId:"PR_1",data:JSON.stringify({url,state:"MERGED",mergedBy:{login:"owner"},mergedAt:"2026-10-13T12:00:00Z"})}); await reconcileMergedRuns(s,async()=>null); console.log(JSON.stringify({run:{mergedBy:s.getRun(r.id)?.mergedBy,mergedAt:s.getRun(r.id)?.mergedAt},feed:s.readFeed().items.filter(i=>i.kind==="run.merged").map(i=>i.data)})); s.close();'
Output: {"run":{"mergedBy":"owner","mergedAt":1791892800000},"feed":[{"prUrl":"https://github.com/test/repo/pull/1","mergedBy":null,"mergedAt":null,"status":"succeeded"}]}
findings.suggestion: Provide durable recovery for an incomplete merge observation, including when polling is disabled, and ensure the feed exposes the recovered metadata. Add a test that checks feed values after recovery rather than only event counts.
findings.failure_scenario: A review-round merge succeeds, but its follow-up GitHub lookup fails transiently. The queue emits parent and round run.merged entries with null metadata. A later complete MERGED snapshot repairs the run rows while both feed entries retain null values.

findings.title: Publish landing feed items after the outer transaction commits
findings.detail: The new outer database transaction encloses every publication attempt. Store.publishFeed returns while db.inTransaction is true, and landed never flushes it after commit. On the already-merged observation path, run.merged and land.landed remain unpublished until an unrelated store operation occurs. Targeted command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501/merge-review.test.ts`. Output: `known merge publishes its feed items after commit`: Expected to contain "run.merged"; Received: [].
findings.suggestion: Use a store transaction wrapper that queues publications and flushes them after the outermost commit.
findings.failure_scenario: awaitCi observes an already-merged PR, landed commits the queue and run updates, and no subsequent store mutation occurs. SSE subscribers receive neither landing feed item, and feed long polls wait until timeout.

findings.title: Make metadata enrichment observable to feed consumers
findings.detail: Metadata enrichment changes an existing feed row without advancing its ID. A consumer that read the initial null metadata and advanced its cursor can never receive the corrected fields through subsequent feed reads. Targeted command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501/merge-review.test.ts`. Output: `consumer learns merge metadata after consuming initial merge`: Expected: true; Received: false. The stored row contained the metadata, but reading after its original ID returned [].
findings.suggestion: Ensure metadata completion is observable through the cursor-based feed, or publish the original merge item after metadata retrieval completes.
findings.failure_scenario: A polling agent reads run.merged while the optional GitHub metadata lookup is pending. The lookup succeeds and fills mergedBy and mergedAt, but the agent's subsequent reads start after that item and retain the original null values.

findings.title: Preserve merge recording for failed or cancelled runs
findings.detail: Replacing updateRun({merged:true}) with resolveMergedRun silently drops confirmed merges for failed and cancelled runs: that helper only updates succeeded, resolved, or needs_human runs. LandQueue.request has no corresponding status restriction and permits an explicit current SHA. The entry therefore becomes landed while its run remains unmerged. Targeted command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-aKvD59/claude-501/merge-review.test.ts`. Output: `landing a failed run records its confirmed merge`: Expected: true; Received: false; the preceding assertion confirmed entry.state was "landed".
findings.suggestion: Record confirmed merge fields for these terminal statuses while preserving their existing status and evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed run retains its PR and branch and is landed using an explicit current SHA. GitHub confirms the merge, but the queue records landed while run.merged remains false and no run.merged feed item is created.

findings.title: Landing no longer records merges for failed or cancelled runs
findings.detail: The previous landed() unconditionally set merged=true. Its replacement calls resolveMergedRun(), which only updates succeeded, resolved, or needs_human runs. Neither request() nor context() excludes failed or cancelled runs with a delivered PR. The queue therefore records landed while the run remains unmerged, and subsequent metadata enrichment also refuses it. Targeted command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const p=s.upsertRepo({slug:"a/b",kind:"github",url:"unused",localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); for(const status of ["failed","cancelled"]){const r=s.createRun(p,{repo:p.slug,prompt:"fix"}); s.updateRun(r.id,{status,prUrl:"https://github.com/a/b/pull/1"}); console.log(status,s.resolveMergedRun(r.id,null,null,{confirmedAt:123}),s.getRun(r.id)?.merged);} s.close();' Output: failed false false; cancelled false false.
findings.suggestion: Record confirmed merges for these statuses while preserving their terminal status and evidence, and add coverage through the queue.
findings.failure_scenario: A run delivers a PR and subsequently fails or is cancelled. Its approved PR is successfully landed through the queue; the entry becomes landed, but run.merged stays false and no run.merged event is emitted.

findings.title: A transient metadata failure permanently strands null merge fields
findings.detail: landed() marks both runs merged before this single optional lookup. If the lookup fails, times out, or still returns OPEN, reconciliation only consults saved snapshots for these runs. githubTracked() excludes merged runs, so polling will not obtain a newer snapshot either. This remains broken after restart, especially with polling disabled. Targeted command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; import {reconcileMergedRuns} from "./src/integrations/github-notifier.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const p=s.upsertRepo({slug:"a/b",kind:"github",url:"unused",localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); const r=s.createRun(p,{repo:p.slug,prompt:"fix"}); s.updateRun(r.id,{status:"succeeded",prUrl:"https://github.com/a/b/pull/1",merged:true}); let calls=0; await reconcileMergedRuns(s,async()=>{calls++;return null;}); console.log(JSON.stringify({tracked:s.githubTracked().length,calls,mergedBy:s.getRun(r.id)?.mergedBy})); s.close();' Output: {"tracked":0,"calls":0,"mergedBy":null}.
findings.suggestion: Provide a bounded, durable reconciliation path for missing merge metadata without repeating the merge operation.
findings.failure_scenario: The squash merge succeeds, but the immediate metadata request encounters a transient GitHub failure. Both parent and round retain null mergedBy and mergedAt indefinitely despite GitHub subsequently having complete metadata.

findings.title: Reject finder replay across different setup configurations
findings.detail: Setup runs even when the trial replays stored finders, but validateReplay checks only finder prompts, targets, lenses and vendors—not setup. Consequently, a setup:true trial can silently reuse findings produced without dependencies installed, despite its distinct cache identity. A focused probe using the real replay functions with schema parsing stubbed reproduced this: `bun run "$TMPDIR/replay-setup-probe.ts"` printed `Accepted setup:true replay from source without setup` and failed with `AssertionError: setup:true must not reuse finder results produced without setup`.
