output.summary: Found two reproducible retry defects. All 32 retry-files tests passed; executor and feedback tests could not load because of dependency errors. The worktree remains unchanged.

findings.title: Preserve process isolation during targeted retries
findings.detail: The full check uses --parallel, which isolates test files in separate processes, but retry_files omits it. Multiple files therefore share globals and module mocks during confirmation. I reproduced this with two files that each capture globalThis.__reviewSeen, set it true, and assert the captured value is undefined. Command `bun test --parallel=2` returned `2 pass, 0 fail`; command `bun test a.test.ts b.test.ts` returned `1 pass, 1 fail` with `Received: true`. A targeted failure immediately confirms a regression without a full rerun, so this execution-mode change can falsely block a flaky change.
findings.suggestion: Keep the full check's process-isolation setting in the targeted retry command, with bounded parallelism.
findings.failure_scenario: Two files fail transiently in the isolated full check. On retry their transient failures disappear, but their globals or module mocks interfere because the targeted command runs both in one process. The factory reports a confirmed regression although a full retry would pass.

findings.title: Pass exact file paths instead of Bun substring filters
findings.detail: Ordinary relative filenames are quoted but lack a ./ prefix. Bun interprets these arguments as substring filters, so they can select additional files. With test/a.test.ts and nested/test/a.test.ts present, command `bun test test/a.test.ts` reported `2 pass` and `Ran 2 tests across 2 files`; `bun test ./test/a.test.ts` reported `1 pass` and `Ran 1 test across 1 file`. The slot exemption counts and times only the reported files, so the actual retry can exceed both bounds and failures in additional files can incorrectly confirm the original regression.
findings.suggestion: Normalize filenames to explicit checkout-relative paths beginning with ./ before quoting and substituting them.
findings.failure_scenario: The report lists one short failing file, test/a.test.ts, while many other test paths contain that suffix. The retry bypasses the gate slot based on one file but executes all matching files, including potentially slow or independently flaky tests.

findings.title: Prefix every retry file with ./ to prevent Bun substring matching
findings.detail: Ordinary relative filenames are passed as Bun test filters rather than exact paths. In a temporary fixture containing test/a.test.ts and nested/test/a.test.ts, the exact command `bun test test/a.test.ts` reported `Ran 2 tests across 2 files.` Both `selected` and `unselected` executed. The command `bun test ./test/a.test.ts` reported `Ran 1 test across 1 file.` Consequently, a retry can execute files outside its selected list, including expensive files excluded from the duration and file-count bounds used to bypass the gate slot.
findings.suggestion: Prefix all validated relative file arguments with ./ before shell quoting. Add a real Bun regression test with duplicate path suffixes that verifies only the selected file executes.
findings.failure_scenario: The report selects test/a.test.ts with a duration below 60 seconds, while nested/test/a.test.ts also exists. The generated targeted command runs both files without acquiring the full gate slot, despite budgeting for only one.

output.summary: Reviewed the permitted pairing/heartbeat first slice and found four defects. Focused probes confirmed plaintext credential storage, missing sandbox denials and failed TLS recovery. Targeted tests could not initialize because of missing @simplewebauthn/server and incompatible Zod; loopback TLS testing was blocked by a listener bind failure.

findings.title: Pairing codes do not prevent a TLS relay from stealing worker access
findings.detail: The initial request accepts any coordinator certificate, and the displayed code is simply returned by that server. A TLS intermediary can forward pairing and claim requests to the real coordinator, preserving the code the owner compares while learning both the claim secret and issued token. The worker then pins the intermediary's certificate. The supplied worker fingerprint is stored but never used to require proof of possession, so it does not prevent this attack.
findings.suggestion: Bind the out-of-band verification code to the authenticated pairing transcript and both certificate fingerprints, and require worker proof of possession before issuing credentials.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the first pairing connection and relays it to the coordinator. Both displays show the same code, the owner approves, and the attacker obtains a valid worker token.

findings.title: Persisted worker secrets are protected only by process-local registrations
findings.detail: The TLS key is registered only while the listener is enabled. Worker token protection is registered only inside the separate pairing or worker process, and pairing releases it on return. The daemon's editor sandbox credential list does not include these persisted paths. Thus disabling the listener exposes its existing key to editors; running a daemon on a paired worker machine likewise leaves its worker credentials readable. Probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/worker-review-probe.ts"` printed `editor policy denies saved worker token: false` and `editor policy denies saved TLS key: false` after creating representative files and constructing the editor read policy.
findings.suggestion: Register all persisted worker credential paths during daemon sandbox initialization, regardless of listener state or whether another worker process is running, and retain those denials for the daemon lifetime.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable the worker listener once, then restart with workers.listen unset and launch an editor. Its sandbox permits reading the saved coordinator TLS key. A daemon sharing a paired worker's data directory similarly permits reading the worker token.

findings.title: Heartbeat fields bypass credential redaction before persistence
findings.detail: Heartbeat capabilities are serialized directly into SQLite. Sanitizing list responses later does not remove secrets already persisted, and the worker also sends its capability strings without redaction. Probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/worker-review-probe.ts"` registered a synthetic credential, submitted it as osVersion, and printed `stored plaintext credential: true`.
findings.suggestion: Redact secret-bearing capability strings before transmission and persistence. Reject identity/version fields containing protected text if redaction would interfere with matching.
findings.failure_scenario: An authenticated heartbeat contains a registered credential in osVersion, releaseSha or bunVersion. The coordinator stores the credential verbatim in workers.capabilities.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation permanently blocks subsequent startup
findings.detail: Certificate creation publishes an empty key.pem before awaiting openssl. If generation fails or the process exits before cert.pem is written, every subsequent attempt throws `Incomplete worker TLS material`. Because listener startup is awaited by startDaemon, this also prevents the coordinator daemon from starting. Probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/worker-review-probe.ts"` simulated the interrupted state and printed `restart after interrupted TLS creation: Error: Incomplete worker TLS material`.
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate TLS material in protected staging files, publish it with a recoverable checkpoint, and clean up incomplete first-generation material without replacing an established identity.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops during its first openssl invocation after key.pem is created. Restarting with workers.listen configured fails repeatedly until someone manually repairs or deletes the TLS files.

output.summary: Reviewed the permitted pairing/heartbeat slice and confirmed two defects with focused probes. Targeted tests could not initialize because dependencies were missing or incompatible; lint and typecheck were also blocked by missing Biome and Bun types. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate generation prevents subsequent startup
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the final key file before invoking OpenSSL, but failure leaves that file behind. Every subsequent attempt rejects the incomplete material, even after the original failure is resolved. With workers enabled, this prevents the entire daemon from starting. Reproduction command: `bun -e 'import { mkdtempSync, rmSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; import { certificate } from "./src/workers/tls.ts"; const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "worker-cert-review-")); const saved = process.env.PATH; try { process.env.PATH = dir; try { await certificate(dir); } catch { console.log("first attempt: openssl unavailable"); } process.env.PATH = saved; try { const tls = await certificate(dir); tls.release(); console.log("retry: recovered"); } catch (e) { console.log("retry:", e.message); } } finally { process.env.PATH = saved; rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); }'`. Output: `first attempt: openssl unavailable\nretry: Incomplete worker TLS material`.
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate TLS material in protected temporary files, then publish it with a recoverable initialization protocol. Preserve existing valid certificates.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenSSL fails or the process stops after the empty key file is created but before the certificate is written. Restarting cannot recover without manual file removal.

findings.title: Heartbeat capabilities bypass redaction before persistence
findings.detail: Heartbeat string fields are stored verbatim. Sanitizing list responses later does not protect the database or backups, and a heartbeat can even persist its registered bearer token in plaintext despite the hash-only storage requirement. Reproduction command: `bun -e 'import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; import { WorkerStore } from "./src/db/workers.ts"; const store = new Store(":memory:"); const w = new WorkerStore(store, "release"); w.pairingKey = "synthetic-key"; const p = w.pair("review-runner", "a".repeat(64), "b".repeat(64)); w.approve(p.code); const claim = w.claim(p.secret); if (!("token" in claim)) throw new Error("No token"); const row = w.authenticate(claim.token); if (!row) throw new Error("Not authenticated"); w.heartbeat(row, { releaseSha: claim.token, bunVersion: Bun.version, os: "darwin", osVersion: "test", cpuCount: 1, ramBytes: 1, freeSlots: 1, onAC: true, idleSeconds: 0, jobs: [] }); console.log("plaintext bearer token persisted:", w.worker("review-runner")?.capabilities?.includes(claim.token)); store.close();'`. Output: `plaintext bearer token persisted: true`.
findings.suggestion: Apply credential and private-string filtering before persisting capabilities, rejecting sensitive identity/version fields where redaction would invalidate their meaning.
findings.failure_scenario: An authenticated worker submits a schema-valid heartbeat containing a registered credential in releaseSha, bunVersion, or osVersion. The coordinator writes that credential into workers.capabilities.

output.summary: Reviewed the permitted pairing/heartbeat split and confirmed two defects with targeted probes. The requested test files could not load because @simplewebauthn/server is missing and the available Zod lacks overwrite(). No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Redact heartbeat metadata before persisting it
findings.detail: heartbeat() stores untrusted capabilities verbatim. Redaction in list() only protects presentation; registered credentials remain in SQLite and its backups. Probe command: bun -e 'import { Database } from "bun:sqlite"; import { WorkerStore } from "./src/db/workers.ts"; import { registerCredential } from "./src/util/proc.ts"; const db = new Database(":memory:"); db.exec(await Bun.file("src/db/migrations/20261015T145911-workers.sql").text()); const workers = new WorkerStore({db}, "release"); workers.pairingKey = "key"; const p = workers.pair("runner", "a".repeat(64), "b".repeat(64)); workers.approve(p.code); const secret = "fixture-credential-12345"; registerCredential("PROBE_SECRET", secret); workers.heartbeat(workers.worker("runner"), {releaseSha:"release", bunVersion:Bun.version, os:"darwin", osVersion:secret, cpuCount:1,ramBytes:1,freeSlots:1,onAC:true,idleSeconds:0,jobs:[]}); console.log("Stored credential in plaintext:", db.query("SELECT capabilities FROM workers").get().capabilities.includes(secret));' Output: Stored credential in plaintext: true
findings.suggestion: Apply credential and private-string filtering before storing capabilities, while preserving validated fields needed for availability checks.
findings.failure_scenario: An authenticated worker submits a registered credential in osVersion or another string field. The coordinator permanently stores the plaintext credential.

findings.title: Recover from interrupted initial certificate generation
findings.detail: The function publishes an empty key.pem before invoking openssl and leaves it behind when generation fails. Every subsequent call refuses this partial state, so a transient first-start failure permanently blocks the configured daemon listener or worker pairing. Probe command: bun -e 'import {mkdtempSync,writeFileSync,rmSync,existsSync} from "node:fs"; import {tmpdir} from "node:os"; import {join} from "node:path"; import {certificate} from "./src/workers/tls.ts"; const root=mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),"worker-cert-probe-")); const original=process.env.PATH; try {writeFileSync(join(root,"openssl"),"#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n",{mode:0o700}); process.env.PATH=root; try {await certificate(join(root,"tls"));} catch {console.log("First generation failed");} process.env.PATH=original; console.log("Partial key retained:",existsSync(join(root,"tls/key.pem"))); try {const cert=await certificate(join(root,"tls")); cert.release(); console.log("Retry succeeded");} catch(e) {console.log("Retry:",e.message);} } finally {process.env.PATH=original; rmSync(root,{recursive:true,force:true});}' Output: First generation failed; Partial key retained: true; Retry: Incomplete worker TLS material
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate TLS material in a protected staging location, then publish it with a recoverable initialization protocol. Preserve existing established identities.
findings.failure_scenario: openssl fails or the process stops after the empty key is created but before the certificate is written. Restarting continues to fail until someone manually removes the partial material.

output.summary: Reviewed lease transitions, cancellation, restart handling, result validation, and worker execution. Focused probes confirmed two defects. Targeted tests could not load because @simplewebauthn/server is missing and the available Zod version lacks required methods.

findings.title: Reject or normalize reordered check results
findings.detail: validRun accepts checks in any order, but retryFailures assigns returned checks to their original attempts by array index. A focused `bun -e` probe invoking validRun and retryRegressions printed `reordered result accepted: true`, followed by `[{"name":"A","verdict":"flaky","blocking":false,"resultName":"B"},{"name":"B","verdict":"regressed","blocking":true,"resultName":"A"}]`. The coordinator therefore accepts remote data that assigns another check's passing evidence to a failing check.
findings.suggestion: Require results to follow requested check order, or normalize them into that order before storing and consuming them.
findings.failure_scenario: Request checks A and B, then receive retry results ordered B/pass, A/fail. Both pass validation, and the retry consumer marks A flaky using B's result.

findings.title: Publish the worker cache only after initialization completes
findings.detail: Initialization creates the final cache directory before writing HEAD and running git init. If interrupted during those steps, subsequent jobs see an existing directory and permanently skip initialization. A targeted `bun -` worker-loop probe supplied a valid git bundle and a cache containing only objects/, representing an interrupted first initialization. It printed `{"failures":2,"leases":3,"cacheStillIncomplete":true}`: successive jobs failed without repairing the cache.
findings.suggestion: Initialize in a temporary sibling directory and atomically rename it into place, following the coordinator cache implementation.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker stops after creating the cache's objects directory but before writing HEAD. After restarting, every job for that repository fails during Git discovery and falls back to other workers or local execution until the cache is manually removed.

output.summary: Reviewed lease transitions, worker execution, validation and restart handling. An injected-request probe confirmed unbounded bundle retries while heartbeats renew the job. Targeted suites could not load because of missing/incompatible dependencies; sandbox restrictions prevented listener probes.

findings.title: Bound bundle retries so failed transfers reach fallback
findings.detail: Connection errors and 5xx responses retry forever while the heartbeat loop continues renewing this job. Consequently, persistent bundle-transfer failures never exhaust the lease or reach another worker/local fallback. This also interacts with the listener's 60-second idle timeout: bundle generation allows 300 seconds but sends no response until finished, so sufficiently slow bundles repeatedly lose their connections. An injected-request probe observed 20 bundle failures, 19 heartbeats reporting the held job, and zero infrastructure-failure reports.
findings.suggestion: Give bundle transfer a bounded overall deadline and report infrastructure failure when exhausted. Configure the bundle route's server timeout to accommodate its generation deadline.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker leases a job and keeps successfully heartbeating, but every bundle request loses its connection—for example, bundle generation consistently exceeds the listener's 60-second idle timeout. The job remains leased indefinitely and the run never falls back locally.

findings.title: Protect the smoke runner from agent modification
findings.detail: The runner and assertion file are placed in agent-writable scratch, but success trusts only the runner's printed marker. An agent can read the marker from probe.ts, replace probe.mjs with console.log(marker), and execute the exact requested command. A targeted `bun -` reproducer using the extracted bunVerifierCheck function and a fake harness did this and printed `Replaced runner; no bun test executed: {"status":"pass"}`. Thus the regression check can pass without exercising bun test.
findings.suggestion: Put the runner in the read-only checkout and independently verify that the scratch test retains its expected contents. Add a fake-harness case that replaces the runner or test and must fail.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude modifies the writable probe to print the expected success marker before executing the requested command; smoke reports pass although no assertion ran.

output.summary: Found two reproducible sanitization gaps. Targeted unit and pipeline tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. An isolated execution of the sanitizer confirmed that file URLs, home-relative links, and absolute paths in link labels remain unchanged. No files were modified.

findings.title: Normalize local link destinations before matching roots
findings.detail: Only literal absolute paths match the configured roots. The isolated sanitizer probe returned `[source](file:///Users/example/.limitless/work/run/src/main.ts)` and `[source](~/.limitless/work/run/src/main.ts)` unchanged. The former still publishes the username; the latter is the home-relative form explicitly described in the request. Once the username is private-listed, the file URL blocks delivery instead of becoming a usable relative link.
findings.suggestion: Recognize local file URLs and home-relative representations, normalize them to local paths, then apply the existing directory-boundary checks.
findings.failure_scenario: With worktree `/Users/example/.limitless/work/run`, a report contains `[source](file:///Users/example/.limitless/work/run/src/main.ts)` or `[source](~/.limitless/work/run/src/main.ts)`.

findings.title: Sanitize local paths in labels even when the destination is relative
findings.detail: The regular expression consumes an entire Markdown link, but the callback only examines its destination. If that destination is already relative, it returns the complete original match, shielding any absolute path in the label from the bare-path replacement. The isolated probe returned `[/Users/example/.limitless/work/run/src/main.ts](src/main.ts)` unchanged. This still exposes the username or blocks publication after private-listing.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize local paths in link labels independently while preserving ordinary relative and external destinations.
findings.failure_scenario: A report uses `[/Users/example/.limitless/work/run/src/main.ts](src/main.ts)` with the corresponding absolute worktree configured.

findings.title: Local paths in link labels bypass sanitization

An absolute local path in the label survives when the destination is relative or external. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/publication-582-review/probe.ts" labels`. findings.title: Common local link spellings remain unchanged
findings.detail: Only literal absolute prefixes match. Both the tilde form explicitly shown in the request and file URLs bypass rewriting. Commands: `bun "$TMPDIR/publication-582-review/probe.ts" tilde` and `bun "$TMPDIR/publication-582-review/probe.ts" uri`. Both produced `AssertionError`: `[source](~/.limitless/work/run/src/a.ts)` and `[source](file:///Users/example/.limitless/work/run/src/a.ts)` remained unchanged instead of becoming `[src/a.ts](src/a.ts)`. File URLs retain the public username leak.

findings.title: Parent segments misclassify paths outside the worktree
findings.detail: Containment is checked before resolving `..`. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/publication-582-review/probe.ts" outside`. Output: `AssertionError`, actual `[../../runs/log.txt](../../runs/log.txt)`, expected `<data>/runs/log.txt`. The target is a factory log outside the worktree, but publication creates a broken repository link instead of the required plain placeholder.

findings.title: Rewriting an image turns it into a text link
findings.detail: The matcher consumes the optional image `!`, but reconstruction drops it. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/publication-582-review/probe.ts" image`. Output: `AssertionError`, actual `[plot.png](plot.png)`, expected `![plot.png](plot.png)`. Published report images consequently stop rendering.

findings.failure_scenario: A report embeds `![plot](/Users/example/.limitless/work/run/plot.png)`.

output.summary: Outcome writes are guarded, but publication commands, CI writes, and worktree cleanup still have ownership gaps. A focused CI reproduction failed as described below. Requested regression tests could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing; importing the queue also requires the missing entities package. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Ownership checks precede asynchronous publication preparation
findings.detail: The ownership check before mergePullRequest does not protect the actual merge command. That helper awaits `gh pr view` before issuing `gh pr merge`, and its retry loop can issue further commands without checking ownership. Similarly, pushApproved checks ownership before calling pushExistingBranch, but that helper awaits rev-parse, transport preparation, ls-remote, and merge-base before pushing. Reclaiming during these awaits still lets the old worker merge or push before its next heartbeat. Checking ownership after the helper returns only protects the outcome write.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the publication helpers and invoke it immediately before each mutating command, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: Defer mergePullRequest's preliminary `gh pr view` response, reclaim the entry with a new owner, then release the OPEN response before the heartbeat. The old worker issues `gh pr merge`. The equivalent race exists during pushExistingBranch's remote lookup.

findings.title: CI inspection still writes after its ownership callback becomes false
findings.detail: Passing `current` into ciDecision does not guard every write inside it. inspectCi awaits default-branch checks, emits main-red events and calls setSetting before checking current(). Other paths record failures after awaited job inspection, and requestRerun writes its result after awaiting the request without rechecking ownership. Targeted command: `bun -e 'import {ciDecision} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; let owner=true,writes=0; const sha="a".repeat(40); const store={getRepoBySlug:()=>({defaultBranch:"main"}),getSetting:()=>({}),setSetting:()=>{writes++},ciFailures:()=>[]}; await ciDecision(store,{repo:"test/repo",url:"https://github.com/test/repo/pull/1"},{headRefOid:sha,ci:"FAILURE",failing:[]},async(_,p)=>{if(p.includes("check-runs")){owner=false;return {status:200,body:{total_count:0,check_runs:[]}}}return {status:200,body:{sha}}},false,()=>owner,()=>owner,"land",sha); console.log({owner,writes}); if(writes) throw Error("Lost worker wrote CI state");'`. Output: `{ owner: false, writes: 1 }`, followed by `error: Lost worker wrote CI state` (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Guard CI writes after asynchronous reads and rerun responses, with ownership validation in the same transaction as each write.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker loses its claim while awaiting default-branch check results during CI inspection. Releasing those results still updates persisted CI state, despite the ownership callback returning false.

findings.title: Lost workers unconditionally delete the shared land checkout
findings.detail: LandClaimLost unwinds through the unconditional finally block, which calls discard. Every claim for an entry uses the same `land-${entry.id}` path. If the new owner has recreated that checkout while the old worker awaited a response, the old worker removes the new owner's worktree and recursively deletes its files. The new database guards therefore still allow a stale worker to disrupt its replacement.
findings.suggestion: Give each claim a separate worktree path, or coordinate cleanup so an old claim cannot remove a replacement claim's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner A awaits CI or merge results; owner B reclaims the entry and creates its checkout. A's response arrives, assertClaim throws, and A's finally block deletes B's active checkout.

output.summary: Found two remaining stale-worker races using temporary fixtures with fake commands and responses. The targeted queue suite could not start because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing; direct helper imports also encountered missing entities.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside publication helpers before issuing commands
findings.detail: The ownership check precedes mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits a PR lookup before issuing gh pr merge and can await reconciliation or retries. Reclaim during those awaits still permits the stale worker to merge before line 715 detects ownership loss. pushExistingBranch similarly awaits several commands before pushing. A temporary fixture executing the extracted queue merge method and actual merge helper reproduced this. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/land-claim-boundary.ts". Output: worker result: claim lost; commands after reclaim: [ "gh pr merge" ]; FAIL: stale worker issued gh pr merge after reclaim during preflight view.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the publication helpers and invoke it after preflight awaits and before each merge or push attempt, including retries. Add regression tests that defer an internal preflight response.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker enters mergePullRequest's gh pr view; another owner reclaims the entry; the lookup returns OPEN before the next heartbeat. The old worker issues gh pr merge despite having lost ownership.

findings.title: Ownership callbacks do not fence CI inspection writes
findings.detail: Passing current into ciDecision does not guard every write inside inspectCi. For example, after awaiting PR check data, it calls recordCiFailure before checking current. requestRerun also writes its returned outcome without rechecking ownership. A temporary fixture invoking the actual ciDecision with a deferred check response reproduced a write after ownership loss. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/land-ci-claim-boundary.ts". Output: decision: { complete: true, state: "pending" }; writes after reclaim: [ "recordCiFailure" ]; FAIL: land CI inspection wrote after losing its claim.
findings.suggestion: Fence CI inspection mutations and returned rerun outcomes with claim validation in the same transaction as each write. Add a deferred CI-inspection regression test covering ownership loss.
findings.failure_scenario: A land worker awaits REST check details during failed-CI inspection. Another owner reclaims the land entry, then the REST response arrives. The old worker persists CI failure data despite current returning false.

output.summary: Found a reproducible ownership gap in push retries. The supplied targeted tests could not reach assertions because the checkout lacks the entities package. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Recheck claim ownership on every push retry
findings.detail: The guard runs once before remoteSh, but remoteSh uses withGitHubRetry to issue subsequent pushes after asynchronous failures and backoff. Losing the claim during the first attempt therefore still permits another push before the heartbeat aborts the signal. A temporary test exercised the actual pushExistingBranch and retry helper with mocked git execution. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/claim-retry.test.ts". Output: {"pushes":2,"guards":1,"owned":false}; assertion failed with Expected: 1, Received: 2. This leaves a pre-existing race unaddressed by the requested fix.
findings.suggestion: Run the ownership guard inside the retry callback before each push attempt, and propagate guard refusal without retrying it. Add a regression test that reclaims ownership during a transient push failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The initial push passes the guard, then returns HTTP 502 after another owner reclaims the entry. The retry delay expires before the next heartbeat, and the stale worker issues a second push without validating ownership.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and claim-loss paths. Confirmed a push retry bypasses ownership validation. Targeted repository tests could not start because the entities dependency is missing.

findings.title: Recheck claim ownership before each push retry
findings.detail: The guard runs once before remoteSh, but remoteSh's withGitHubRetry callback can issue subsequent pushes without invoking it again. A reclaim during a transient failure or backoff therefore permits another push before the heartbeat aborts the worker. An isolated probe extracted the current push/retry functions and injected transport responses. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/land-push-claim-review.ts"`. Output: `{"guardCalls":1,"pushAttemptOwnedStates":[true,false]}` followed by `error: push was retried after claim loss without rechecking guard` (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Invoke the ownership guard inside the retry callback immediately before every push attempt, and propagate guard refusal without retrying.
findings.failure_scenario: The initial push returns HTTP 502 without updating the remote. Another owner reclaims the entry during the five-second retry delay. Before the old worker's ten-second heartbeat, the retry pushes successfully because the remote still matches the approved SHA.

findings.title: Unowned PRs reject the existing PR-number syntax

findings.title: Fork PRs are categorically rejected despite the requested acceptance rule
findings.detail: An open PR targeting a configured GitHub repository satisfies the request even when its head belongs to a fork. This unconditional rejection adds an exclusion absent from the requirements and prevents those hand-made PRs from receiving confined land checks.

output.summary: Found a reproduced cleanup recovery gap and a cancellation race. All 19 proc tests and 8 cleanup tests passed. Three integration tests were blocked by missing dependencies; an isolated engine check was also blocked by an incompatible installed Zod version.

findings.title: Recovery clears ownership without discovering remaining descendants
findings.detail: Recovery kills only recorded members and then deletes the invocation record. A member can fork after the discovery snapshot but before SIGSTOP; if the daemon crashes there, that descendant is never recorded or recovered. A targeted reproduction using real processes and an inspection hook to arrange this ordering confirmed it. Command: REVIEW_REPO="$PWD" bun "$TMPDIR/review-cleanup-race.ts". Output: "recorded before crash: [71833] owned: [71833,71848]", "next command: 0 next-step-ran", "unrecorded descendant alive: true pending records: 0". The command exited 1.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation discovery metadata to recover additional marked descendants, and complete discovery and termination before clearing the record or allowing another command.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked parent forks after a cleanup snapshot. Cleanup records and freezes the parent, then the daemon dies before its next discovery pass. Recovery kills the parent, clears its record, and starts the next command while the unrecorded child remains alive.

findings.title: Recovery failure ignores cancellation and shutdown
findings.detail: The new recovery await runs outside executeScopedRun's cancellation handling. Its catch unconditionally writes failed and replaces the error, even if the scheduler cancelled the run or aborted it for daemon shutdown during recovery. This loses the cancellation reason and, on shutdown, makes a run terminal instead of re-queuing it as the existing engine path does.
findings.suggestion: Honor the abort signal and current persisted cancellation state after recovery fails, preserving the existing cancellation and shutdown re-queue behavior while retaining pending cleanup records.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery awaits birth inspection or termination confirmation. The scheduler aborts the run for shutdown or user cancellation. Inspection then fails or confirmation times out; executeRun marks the run failed instead of queued or cancelled.

output.summary: Found a reproduced recovery escape and a Linux identity issue across reboots. Existing focused checks: 27 passed; three integration tests could not run because an SDK dependency is missing. Repository files were unchanged.

findings.title: Recovery clears ownership without finishing descendant discovery
findings.detail: Recovery kills only persisted members and deletes the invocation record without repeating discovery. A member can fork after the original census but before SIGSTOP; a crash before the next sweep leaves that child unrecorded. Recovery then allows the next command while the child survives. Reproduced by extending the existing crash test with that fork: `bun test "$TMPDIR/cleanup-fork-review.test.ts" -t 'a fresh process recovers'` failed at `expect(await processBirth(extraPid)).toBeNull()`, with `Received: "1793423946:866293"`. The resumed command had already written its sentinel.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough invocation discovery context to finish the freeze/rescan/kill cleanup after restart. Clear the record only after confirming the invocation has no remaining descendants.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked descendant forks between discovery and its first SIGSTOP. The daemon crashes after that stop, before rescanning. Recovery kills the recorded parent, clears the record, and starts the next command while the unrecorded child keeps running.

findings.title: Persisted Linux identities need a boot identifier
findings.detail: On Linux, processBirth returns only /proc/<pid>/stat starttime, measured in ticks since boot. Persisted records survive a reboot, but that identity does not distinguish boots. An unrelated process in a subsequent boot can have the same PID and starttime, pass this comparison, and receive SIGKILL.
findings.suggestion: Include the Linux boot ID in persisted process identities and treat records from a previous boot as absent without signalling their PIDs.
findings.failure_scenario: The machine reboots with a pending cleanup record. A process in the new boot receives the recorded PID and starts at the same boot-relative tick. Daemon startup recovery kills that unrelated process.

output.summary: Reviewed the workflow, wrapper, and test markers. The targeted marker test passed; two Linux timeout tests skipped on macOS. GNU timeout was unavailable, and sandbox restrictions blocked process-tree inspection during an additional probe.

findings.title: Process-group cleanup leaves detached test subprocesses running
findings.detail: Both cleanup signals target only timeout's process group. The suite's runProcess helper (src/util/proc.ts:541) starts subprocesses with detached: true, giving them separate process groups. If a test hangs awaiting one of those commands, terminating Bun prevents its normal cleanup, while this wrapper's TERM and KILL miss the detached command and its descendants. The new cleanup test covers only children that remain in the original group.
findings.suggestion: Track and stop descendant processes across process-group boundaries, and extend the timeout test with a detached, TERM-ignoring child.
findings.failure_scenario: A test starts a hanging command through sh/runProcess. At the CI deadline, the wrapper kills the test runner's group, but the command's separate process group survives the wrapper's exit.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding process code. The marker test passed; two Linux-only tests skipped on macOS, where GNU timeout is unavailable. A probe using a temporary foreground-timeout shim confirmed that detached children survive cleanup.

findings.title: Timeout cleanup leaves detached test subprocesses running
findings.detail: Both cleanup signals target only timeout's process group. The repository's runProcess helper starts every subprocess with detached: true, placing it outside that group. Killing Bun therefore leaves those subprocesses alive without their normal cleanup owner. A targeted wrapper probe using a temporary foreground-timeout shim printed: "Wrapper exit: 137", "Printed tree: True", "Detached child survived: True". Native GNU timeout could not be tested on this macOS host.
findings.suggestion: Track and stop descendants outside the wrapper's process group as well, and extend the Linux cleanup test with a detached child representative of runProcess.
findings.failure_scenario: A test hangs while awaiting a subprocess started through sh/runProcess. At 20 minutes, the wrapper kills Bun and its own group, but the detached subprocess continues running on the CI runner.

Audit probes passed for percent-encoded and base64 credentials. Publication still accepts base64-encoded registered credentials. Targeted test files could not load because the checkout lacks entities; isolated base64 probes used an identity HTML-decoder mock.

findings.title: Registered credentials never reach publication matching
findings.detail: Publication checks still match only caller-supplied private entries. Production callers in pipeline/engine.ts and land/queue.ts supply loadPrivateStrings results, without registeredCredentials(). Consequently, the new base64 decoder never sees registered credentials when checking published bodies, titles or content. The added publication test manually includes credentials, masking this production gap. Isolated probe command: bun -e 'import { mock } from "bun:test"; mock.module("entities",()=>({decodeHTML:(text:string)=>text})); const { checkPublicationText } = await import("./src/gates/publication.ts"); const { registerCredential } = await import("./src/util/proc.ts"); const value="synthetic-review-credential"; registerCredential("review-probe",value); const encoded=Buffer.from(value).toString("base64"); try { checkPublicationText(encoded,"PR body",[]); console.log("FAIL: publication accepted a base64-encoded registered credential"); process.exitCode=1; } catch(e) { console.log("blocked",String(e)); }'. Output: FAIL: publication accepted a base64-encoded registered credential (exit 1). The HTML mock does not affect this base64-only input.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials at the publication enforcement boundary, and test a production-style caller that supplies only private entries.
findings.failure_scenario: Register a credential absent from private-strings.txt, then place its base64 encoding in a report body. Literal credential redaction leaves the encoding intact, and publication checking permits it.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and publication/audit callers. Direct matcher probes confirmed a decoding gap. Targeted tests could not start because dependencies, including entities, are absent.

findings.title: Base64 matching stops before decoding nested escapes
findings.detail: base64Match returns decoded text only when it already contains a literal protected value. Consequently, normalizedLayers never receives percent-encoded values inside base64, despite supporting successive decoding. A targeted assertion failed: `bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { privateMatches } from "./src/gates/private.ts"; assert.equal(privateMatches(Buffer.from("%73ynthetic-credential").toString("base64"), [{value:"synthetic-credential",entry:1}]).length, 1);'` produces `AssertionError: 0 !== 1`. The same percent-encoded value without the base64 wrapper matches successfully.
findings.suggestion: Check eligible base64 candidates through bounded subsequent decoding before deciding whether they contain a protected value, while retaining the exclusion of unrelated runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A private entry or registered credential is percent-encoded and then base64-encoded into a filename or published content. The matcher returns no hit, so audit filename/detail sanitization and publication checks allow the recoverable value through. Double base64 encoding similarly bypasses detection.

output.summary: Found three eval aggregation defects. All 19 workload tests passed. CLI and HTTP checks were blocked by unavailable/incompatible dependencies (Zod prefault and MCP SDK). Seeded checks reproduced incorrect attribution, success share, and cache metrics. No files changed.

findings.title: Combined panel usage is attributed entirely to the primary provider
findings.detail: Review panel trials store combined finder/verifier usage and cost, but this fallback assigns everything to details.provider and t.model_id. The verifier provider disappears from the statistics, and invocation counts undercount actual calls. Targeted command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; import {computeProviderStatistics} from "./src/db/stats.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const r=s.createEvalRun({role:"review",models:["finder-a"],k:1,maxUsd:10},[]); s.recordEvalTrial({evalRunId:r.id,effort:null,caseId:"case",modelId:"finder-a",trial:0,cacheKey:"key",harness:"fake",status:"ok",output:null,pass:true,score:1,details:{provider:"provider-a",invocationStatus:"ok",verifiers:[{modelId:"verifier-b",effort:"default",candidates:["c"]}],cacheReadTokens:0,cacheWriteTokens:0},tokensIn:300,tokensOut:30,costUsd:3,costEquivUsd:3,durationMs:100,createdAt:1}); console.log(JSON.stringify(computeProviderStatistics(s,0,1).map(x=>({provider:x.provider,models:x.eval?.models.map(m=>({model:m.modelId,cost:m.costUsd,tokens:m.tokensIn,invocations:m.invocations}))})))); s.close();' Output: [{"provider":"provider-a","models":[{"model":"finder-a","cost":3,"tokens":300,"invocations":1}]}]. This matches the writer's combined-result behavior in src/pipeline/review.ts.
findings.suggestion: Use stored per-call evidence where available. Represent inseparable combined usage as unattributed rather than assigning it to the primary provider/model.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel calls a finder on provider A and a verifier on provider B. Both calls' spend is reported under A, and B receives no workload.

findings.title: Eval grading failures are counted as provider invocation failures
findings.detail: The aggregator uses EvalRound.status as the invocation outcome. However, runner.ts:1208–1212 overwrites an originally successful round status when implementation grading errors or times out. Consequently successfulShare describes grading outcomes rather than provider success. Targeted command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; import {computeProviderStatistics} from "./src/db/stats.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const run=s.createEvalRun({role:"implement",models:["m"],k:1,maxUsd:10},[]); s.recordEvalTrial({evalRunId:run.id,effort:null,caseId:"case",modelId:"m",trial:0,cacheKey:"key",harness:"fake",status:"error",output:null,pass:false,score:0,details:{provider:"p",invocationStatus:"ok",cacheReadTokens:20,cacheWriteTokens:10,rounds:[{round:0,provider:"p",modelId:"m",effort:"default",status:"timeout",pass:false,reason:"timeout",tokensIn:100,tokensOut:5,costUsd:1,costEquivUsd:1,durationMs:100}]},tokensIn:100,tokensOut:5,costUsd:1,costEquivUsd:1,durationMs:100,createdAt:1}); const t=computeProviderStatistics(s,0,1)[0]?.eval?.totals; console.log(JSON.stringify({storedInvocationStatus:"ok",storedCacheRead:20,storedCacheWrite:10,reported:t})); s.close();' Output included storedInvocationStatus:"ok" but reported.successfulShare:0, cacheReadTokens:null, cacheWriteTokens:null, inputTokens:null.
findings.suggestion: Derive provider success from invocation status evidence, keeping grading outcomes separate. Where historical round outcomes cannot be recovered, expose the uncertainty.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation call returns ok, then its grading command times out. A single successful provider call is reported with a successful share of zero.

findings.title: Recorded cache splits are discarded for implementation evals
findings.detail: Every trial with rounds receives null cache-read, cache-write and uncached-input metrics. Implementation trials have rounds even for one call, while their details retain aggregate cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens. The targeted command in the preceding finding stored 100 input tokens, 20 cache-read tokens and 10 cache-write tokens for one round, but returned null for all three split metrics. These measurements are available and exactly attributable in this case.
findings.suggestion: Preserve trial cache splits when attribution is exact, including single-round trials, and use available aggregate splits for provider totals when all rounds share that provider.
findings.failure_scenario: A one-round implementation eval records cache-read 20 and cache-write 10. The endpoint and CLI report both as unknown, failing to provide the requested cached-token statistics.

output.summary: Reviewed aggregation, CLI/HTTP wiring and eval persistence. All 19 workload tests passed; focused probes exposed two incorrect results. CLI/HTTP verification was limited by incompatible Zod and a missing MCP dependency. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Preserve known cache measurements for single-round evals
findings.detail: Any trial containing rounds unconditionally loses its cache measurements, even when its single round has fully attributable cache totals in details.cacheReadTokens and details.cacheWriteTokens. This also makes inputTokens unknown. Targeted command: `bun "$TMPDIR/provider-statistics-probe.ts" cache`. The probe seeded one round with stored cache reads of 2 and writes of 1. Output: `{ storedCacheReadTokens: 2, reportedCacheReadTokens: null }`, followed by `AssertionError: null !== 2`.
findings.suggestion: Use persisted trial cache totals when attribution is unambiguous, including single-round trials; retain unknown values only where the stored records cannot establish the split.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed single-round implementation eval records 10 input tokens including 2 cache-read and 1 cache-write tokens. Statistics report all three input/cache measurements as null instead of 7, 2 and 1.

findings.title: Do not treat implementation grading failures as provider failures
findings.detail: Round status is not exclusively the invocation status. In src/evals/runner.ts, successful provider results have roundEvidence.status overwritten with error or timeout when implementation grading fails. Passing that status into summarize lowers the provider's successful share despite a successful invocation. Targeted command: `bun "$TMPDIR/provider-statistics-probe.ts" status`. A single-round record matching this persistence path produced `{ invocationStatus: "ok", reportedSuccessfulShare: 0 }`, followed by `AssertionError: 0 !== 1`.
findings.suggestion: Derive provider success from invocation outcomes, using details.invocationStatus where applicable. Do not substitute grading outcomes for unavailable invocation evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: The implementation harness returns ok, then hidden-test grading times out. The stored invocationStatus remains ok while the round status becomes timeout; provider statistics report a successful share of zero.

findings.title: Avoid assigning an entire panel's workload to its primary model
findings.detail: Review eval trial totals combine finder and verifier results across models and providers. The fallback record assigns all those tokens and costs to details.provider and t.model_id, ignoring the other participants. The runner's sendTo path and combined() confirm that these are combined totals. Targeted command: `bun "$TMPDIR/provider-statistics-probe.ts" panel`. A seeded panel trial with primary provider alpha and a beta-model verifier produced only `[{"provider":"alpha","costUsd":0.5,"models":["m"]}]`. Thus beta's work disappears and alpha receives the combined spend.
findings.suggestion: Use attributable stored invocation evidence where available. Where panel totals cannot be split, expose that attribution limitation explicitly rather than reporting the combined workload as belonging to one provider/model.
findings.failure_scenario: A review panel uses an alpha finder and a beta verifier. Both calls contribute to the trial's stored cost and tokens, but the endpoint reports the entire workload under alpha and its finder model.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and rerun compatibility paths. Direct probes verified failure selection and excerpt boundaries but exposed a credential-redaction regression. Targeted test files could not start because the entities dependency is missing.

findings.title: Preserve exact-match redaction for short failure lines
findings.detail: Publication now passes surrounding log context to redactCredentials. Credentials shorter than eight characters are redacted only when the entire input equals the credential, so a credential exactly matching the selected line is no longer removed. Previously bounded received that line alone. The raw credential now enters persisted signatures and fix triggers. Reproduction: bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("REVIEW_PASSWORD", "error:x"); console.log(ciSignature("test", "header\nerror:x\nstack", "failure").line);' outputs error:x; expected [redacted]. An assertion against [redacted] also failed.
findings.suggestion: Retain exact-value credential matching for the selected logical line and image while preserving contextual redaction for credentials crossing publication boundaries. Add a regression test for a short credential matching the complete failure line.
findings.failure_scenario: Register the seven-character credential error:x, then inspect a log containing header\nerror:x\nstack. The signature line and serialized signature retain the credential.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and rerun compatibility paths. Direct checks passed for normal Bun failures, runner-header exclusion, fallback and timeout selection. Two excerpt boundary checks failed. Targeted test files could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Reserve the failing line after redaction expands the excerpt
findings.detail:
The tail budget counts source characters, but redaction can expand eight-character credentials into ten-character markers. The final prefix truncation then discards the chosen failing test name. Reproduction: bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("REVIEW_TOKEN", "abcdefgh"); const r=ciSignature("test", "context
error: assertion failed
"+"abcdefgh".repeat(300)+"
(fail) actual failing test", ""); console.log(r.excerpt.length, r.excerpt.includes(r.line)); if (!r.excerpt.includes(r.line)) throw new Error("excerpt omitted the chosen failure line");'. Output: 2000 false, followed by 'error: excerpt omitted the chosen failure line'.
findings.suggestion: Allocate the excerpt budget after redaction and preserve the chosen failure line explicitly, trimming intermediate context first.
findings.failure_scenario: A long Bun assertion block contains repeated registered eight-character credentials before its trailing (fail) line. Redaction expands the retained tail beyond its budget, so the excerpt omits the failing test name.

findings.title: Trim indentation before bounding the failure-line excerpt
findings.detail: Signature selection accepts arbitrary leading whitespace and trims it, but the excerpt takes the first 500 raw characters of that line. Reproduction: bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; const r=ciSignature("test", "header\n"+" ".repeat(600)+"(fail) actual failure\nstack", ""); console.log(JSON.stringify({line:r.line,containsFailure:r.excerpt.includes("(fail) actual failure")})); if (!r.excerpt.includes("(fail) actual failure")) throw new Error("excerpt omitted the chosen failure line");'. Output: {"line":"(fail) actual failure","containsFailure":false}, followed by 'error: excerpt omitted the chosen failure line'.
findings.suggestion: Skip leading whitespace when extracting the selected failure line into the excerpt.
findings.failure_scenario: A failure-shaped line has more than 500 characters of indentation. Its signature is correct, but its excerpt contains whitespace and surrounding lines without the failure diagnostic.

output.summary: Found three event-reporting defects using source-extracted worker probes and SQLite checks. Targeted tests could not start because installed dependencies lack the MCP SDK, entities, and Zod prefault support. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Retry attempts silently lose events by restarting sequence numbers
findings.detail: Every attempt starts seq at zero, but agent_job_events retains previous attempts and deduplicates on (job_id, seq). After requeueing onto another worker, new batches collide with old batches and receive successful responses without being stored. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/worker-review-probe.ts". The SQLite probe output was {"label":"retry","rows":[{"seq":0,"events":"failed attempt"}]} after inserting a successful retry's batch at sequence zero.
findings.suggestion: Provide a durable sequence cursor in the lease or namespace event batches by attempt while preserving request-retry idempotency.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A posts batches and then fails or loses its lease. Worker B leases the same job and restarts its event sequence at zero; the coordinator silently discards its overlapping batches.

findings.title: Rejected event batches abort without reporting job failure
findings.detail: The rejection handler aborts the job controller. The catch at line 533 then skips POST failure because jobSignal is aborted. The coordinator retains the leased job until expiry, losing the actual failure reason and delaying reassignment. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/worker-review-probe.ts". The source-extracted runner with a rejected batch produced {"label":"rejected","aborted":true,"calls":["events"],"batchBytes":5420}; no failure request occurred.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish reporting failures from cancellation and send a bounded failure notification with a signal independent of the aborted harness.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects an events batch with HTTP 400 or 413 while the worker still holds the lease. The harness stops, but the worker never reports the failure.

findings.title: Event batching can exceed the coordinator's body limit
findings.detail: Batches are bounded only by event count and time, while the events endpoint limits bodies to 1 MiB. Both harnesses permit 20,000-character tool results, so valid bursts can exceed that limit before reaching 200 events. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/worker-review-probe.ts". A source-extracted runner emitting 100 such results produced {"label":"large","aborted":true,"calls":["events"],"batchBytes":2006110}, exceeding the server's 1048576-byte limit.
findings.suggestion: Also bound batches by serialized UTF-8 size and define handling for an individual oversized event.
findings.failure_scenario: A harness emits 100 tool results containing 20,000 ASCII characters each within one flush interval. The worker sends a roughly 2 MB batch, which the coordinator rejects, aborting the session.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding worker, harness, and coordinator code. Found three failure-path defects. Targeted tests could not load because @simplewebauthn/server is missing and the installed Zod lacks prefault; a payload-size probe confirmed oversized batches.

findings.title: Report event rejection before discarding the job
findings.detail: A rejected event batch aborts the job controller. The runAgent catch then skips POST failure because jobSignal.aborted is true. The coordinator retains a leased job until expiry, losing the rejection reason and delaying retry. The added rejection test only checks that the job is not done, so it permits this state.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish event-delivery failure from coordinator cancellation and send a bounded failure notification using a signal that the event rejection did not abort.
findings.failure_scenario: POST events returns 400 or 413 while the coordinator still recognizes the lease. The harness stops and the checkout disappears, but the job remains leased with no failure report until lease expiry.

findings.title: Keep event batches within the listener's body limit
findings.detail: Batching limits event count and elapsed time but not serialized size. The coordinator rejects event bodies over 1 MiB. Claude tool results can each contain 20,000 characters; a probe with 60 such events produced 1,203,670 bytes, despite being below the 200-event threshold. Valid harness output can therefore abort an otherwise successful session.
findings.suggestion: Flush batches before their serialized byte size exceeds the listener limit, and define handling for an individual oversized event.
findings.failure_scenario: Sixty 20,000-character tool results arrive within 250 ms. They are posted together, exceed the coordinator's 1 MiB limit, and receive 413, aborting the session.

findings.title: Prevent new sessions from starting while heartbeat-fenced
findings.detail: The fencing interval aborts only jobs present when it runs. Lease acceptance and harness dispatch never check heartbeat freshness, so a worker whose last successful heartbeat is already older than one lease period can start another paid session and run until the next interval.
findings.suggestion: Check heartbeat freshness when accepting an agent lease and immediately before harness dispatch; keep agent execution fenced until a heartbeat succeeds.
findings.failure_scenario: Heartbeat responses are lost while lease and bundle requests remain reachable. After the fencing interval aborts existing sessions, another lease response arrives and starts a harness despite the stale heartbeat, spending quota for up to another heartbeat interval.

findings.title: Keep renewing the lease while a fenced worker reports its commit
findings.detail: The new signal keeps result retries alive after the fence aborts the controller, but heldJobs() excludes every aborted controller. Subsequent heartbeats therefore omit this job and stop renewing its lease. If reporting takes another lease period, the coordinator requeues the job and rejects its eventual report, leaving the pushed commit unreported. A probe using the actual heldJobs, heartbeat and sweep implementations confirmed this. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-fenced-lease.ts"`. Output: `After fence, heartbeat jobs: []`; at 60000 ms the job was `state: queued, attempt: 2, failure_reason: Lease expired`, despite an attempt deadline of 600000.
findings.suggestion: Track pending publication reports separately from execution cancellation and keep their jobs in heartbeat lease renewals until reporting finishes or the attempt deadline expires.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes during coordinator downtime and its fence fires. After restart, heartbeats succeed but result requests keep failing or stall for over 60 seconds. The job loses its lease while its independent result retry remains active; the accepted report cannot be recovered and the run can end NeedsHuman.

findings.title: Wire production complexity lookup into the CLI

findings.title: Recover orphaned hidden files after interrupted publication

Every subsequent invocation chooses that same next ID and rejects it at existsSync(hidden), preventing any further cases from being added without manual cleanup. The catch block cannot recover from process interruption.

findings.title: Wire production complexity lookup into the CLI
findings.detail: The documented CLI supplies only cache to generateReplayCases. findings.title: Handle CRLF separators around quoted requests
findings.detail:
Trailing separator removal strips only LF bytes. A CRLF blank separator before the next heading therefore leaves a standalone CR, which fails quoted-line validation. Reproduced with: bun -e 'import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; const source=readFileSync("scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts","utf8"); const chunk=source.slice(source.indexOf("export function replayRequest"),source.indexOf("export async function replayProduction")); const code=new Bun.Transpiler({loader:"ts"}).transformSync(chunk.replace("export function", "function")); const replayRequest=eval(code+"; replayRequest"); console.log(replayRequest("## Request

> Repair answer.

## Checks
"));' Output: error: Malformed quoted Request block (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Recognize CRLF section separators while preserving the request's original content.
findings.failure_scenario: A merged PR body uses CRLF line endings and contains a valid quoted Request followed by another section; the generator refuses it.
