findings.detail: Base validation uses synthetic snapshot history with evals removed, while head validation uses the actual commit and history. A failure caused by that transformation can qualify a case even when its hidden tests pass at the actual base. A real-git reproduction, `bun "$TMPDIR/replay-history-probe.ts"`, printed: `Actual base hidden assertion: pass`, `Generator snapshot-base assertion: fail`, `Actual head hidden assertion: pass`. The assertion checked whether the latest commit subject starts with release; the snapshot replaces it with Snapshot head.
findings.suggestion: Perform the required fail/pass validation against fresh detached worktrees at the actual base and head. Keep snapshot compatibility checking as a separate step.
findings.failure_scenario: A changed test inspects Git history or an evals file that exists at both original pins. It passes at both pins but fails against the transformed base, causing acceptance of a non-discriminating replay.

findings.title: Preserve large production complexities instead of excluding them
findings.detail: replayProduction returns the production complexity unchanged, but ImplementCaseSchema accepts only trivial, small and medium. A run triaged large therefore causes case parsing to fail before validation. This excludes precisely the harder production tasks requested here. The isolated probe `bun "$TMPDIR/replay-review-probe.ts"` printed `Known production complexity: large` and `Generator schema accepts it: false`.
findings.suggestion: Extend implement-case complexity support to represent the production triage values, including large, and retain that value in generated cases.
findings.failure_scenario: A qualifying PR has a run record with complexity large and the injected lookup finds it. Generation excludes the PR with a schema error regardless of its hidden-test results.

findings.title: Wire production run lookup into the documented CLI
findings.detail: The CLI supplies only cache, so lookupRun is always undefined in the user-facing generator. Even when the PR footer names a run available in the configured factory store, its triage complexity is never sought and is replaced with medium. Only programmatic tests exercise successful metadata lookup. The isolated probe `bun "$TMPDIR/replay-review-probe.ts"` reported `run r1: lookup not configured` and `Triage complexity: unknown (default medium)`.
findings.suggestion: Supply a read-only lookup against the configured factory run records, retaining the unknown fallback when the record genuinely cannot be found.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the documented command on the factory host for a PR whose local run record has complexity small. The generated case records medium despite the production value being available.

output.summary: Reviewed snapshot creation, gate execution, reuse, and evidence handling. An isolated executor probe confirmed a failed gate can return command success. Targeted tests could not initialize because entities is missing and the resolved Zod lacks required APIs. No files were modified.

findings.title: Return failure when gate classification rejects a zero exit
findings.detail: GateResult.ok can be false with exitCode 0: runOne rejects confinement-launch failures detected in output independently of process exit. This return expression nevertheless sends status 0 to the implementer. An isolated runAgentGate probe returned status 0 alongside text saying FAIL. Reproduction of the status calculation: bun --eval 'const source = await Bun.file("src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts").text(); const expression = source.match(/status: (.*),/)[1]; const status = new Function("result", `return ${expression}`)({ok:false, exitCode:0, confinementError:true}); console.log(`failed gate status=${status}`); if (status === 0) throw new Error("failed gate reported success");'. Output: failed gate status=0; error: failed gate reported success.
findings.suggestion: Ensure a rejected gate result always returns a nonzero status, while preserving usable nonzero process exit codes.
findings.failure_scenario: The trusted test command encounters an inner confinement-launch failure but catches it and exits 0. The gate executor correctly sets ok=false and confinementError=true, yet the wrapper exits successfully, misleading the implementer and any shell condition checking the command.

output.summary: Found two correctness issues in snapshot fidelity and repeated requests. Session/watchdog tests passed (45 tests). Integration tests could not load because entities is missing and installed Zod APIs are incompatible. No repository files changed.

findings.title: Snapshot merge resolutions with the round's inclusion rules
findings.detail: snapshotTree rebuilds from HEAD, omitting ignored files introduced by MERGE_HEAD. Resolution rounds use completeMerge, which explicitly preserves those files. Thus an unchanged resolution produces a different committed tree and runs the suite again. Real-git probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-798-merge.ts". Output: {"snapshotIncludesIgnored":false,"roundIncludesIgnored":true,"treesMatch":false}. The probe used snapshotTree's three Git operations with production stageAll and compared against production completeMerge.
findings.suggestion: Share the merge-aware staging rules with snapshot creation, using a temporary index while preserving the session index.
findings.failure_scenario: The merged base introduces a tracked file matching .gitignore, and another file conflicts. After resolving the conflict, the implementer requests the suite and makes no further edits. The snapshot omits the ignored file, while the round commit includes it.

findings.title: Reuse existing executions before handling another session request
findings.detail: runAgentGate computes the cache key but never looks up an existing execution before running the suite. Each wrapper invocation supplies a fresh request ID, so repeated commands on an unchanged tree rerun it. putAgentGate then overwrites the previous comparison. A failing execution followed by a passing request becomes a clean pass, losing the original failure and retry classification; verify substitution can consequently accept it as clean evidence.
findings.suggestion: Return the validated recorded execution for an existing key before executing again. Preserve prior failure provenance if explicit reruns are supported.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer runs bun test twice without changing files. The first execution fails, including its automatic retry; the second passes. The second execution replaces the failure record, and the gates stage reuses a clean pass.

output.summary: Reviewed lease, cancellation, restart and release compatibility paths. Isolated probes confirmed lease and retry-resume defects. The integration test could not load because dependencies, including entities, are missing.

findings.title: Enforce worktree exclusion inside the lease transaction
findings.detail: leaseInplace checks only the selected job's state. It can lease another job for a worktree whose previous job is still leased or has stopped=0. The daemon-side scan does not provide an atomic reservation: concurrent starts can both scan before either attaches and inserts its row. An isolated probe using the actual WorkerStore and SQLite, with peripheral dependencies mocked, ran `bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-probe.ts"` and printed `leased jobs for same worktree: job1 job2`, followed by `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: second executor must not lease the same worktree`.
findings.suggestion: Atomically exclude jobs whose canonical worktree already has an active or unconfirmed-stopped job when leasing, and reserve the worktree across start/checkpoint/enqueue.
findings.failure_scenario: Two starts for the same worktree overlap before their job rows are inserted; two executor processes then lease those rows and run checks concurrently in that worktree.

findings.title: Track executor freshness rather than only process existence
findings.detail: Executors have no heartbeat timestamp, and executor() treats a matching live PID as available indefinitely. A stalled executor therefore continues receiving jobs. For an existing leased job, sweep eventually fails the lease, but waitStopped keeps waiting indefinitely because the same PID still exists. The isolated probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-probe.ts"` printed `executor considered available after 24h without heartbeat: true`.
findings.suggestion: Add an executor freshness observation and apply the specified freshness timer. Refuse stale executors for new dispatch, and provide a bounded, explicit failure when shutdown cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor's event loop stalls while a gate runs. Its lease expires, but the daemon remains blocked in waitStopped instead of reaching a terminal outcome; new gates also select that executor.

findings.title: Resume surviving retry jobs as well as initial jobs
findings.detail: The purpose whitelist excludes baseline retries, regression retries and timeout reruns, even when the saved stage, round, purpose, SHA, environment and lease all match. Restarting during one of these jobs cancels it and restarts the stage's initial suite. The isolated probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-probe.ts"` returned `matching targeted retry resume: undefined` and `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: matching retry handle should reattach` for a matching regression-retry-targeted handle.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to resume at the recorded retry purpose, preserving the surviving job and its prerequisite outputs.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a targeted regression retry or full baseline retry is running under the executor. The resumed engine discards that valid job and repeats earlier gate work.

findings.title: Detect rollback without relying on a persistent release setting
findings.detail: Release-change detection relies entirely on executor.daemonRelease, which only this new daemon writes. The base release never updates that setting. After rollback to it, the setting still names the executor's release, so the executor keeps renewing and running jobs under a different daemon release. The older engine also cannot attach to an inplace handle and performs its existing worktree cleanup before encountering that unsupported handle.
findings.suggestion: Validate the currently running coordinator's release through a live identity or handshake that cannot remain valid across rollback to a daemon lacking this feature. Stop and confirm existing jobs before the older daemon can reuse their worktrees.
findings.failure_scenario: Release A starts an executor gate, then the daemon rolls back to the supplied base release B while the executor remains running. B leaves the release marker at A; the executor continues its gate while B resumes or cleans the same worktree.

output.summary: Traced enqueueing, leases, cancellation, confinement and restart handling. Found three defects. Two focused probes confirmed missing private-file protection and stopped-process availability. The targeted test command, `bun test test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts`, could not load because dependency `entities` is missing; integration behavior remains unverified.

findings.title: Register daemon private files in the executor's confinement policy
findings.detail: Private-file protections are process-local. Daemon startup registers the API token and worker credentials, but executor startup only opens the database and binds the read policy. With LIMITLESS_HOME outside the user's home, these files lose the daemon's explicit read denies and become readable by untrusted gates. A focused homeReadPolicy probe returned executorDeniesToken=false and daemonDeniesToken=true.
findings.suggestion: Share registration of the daemon's private files with executor startup, including custom data directories, before executing any gate.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure LIMITLESS_HOME=/data/limitless and enable the executor. A gate reads /data/limitless/api-token or worker private keys, which the in-process gate policy denies.

findings.title: Process existence does not establish executor freshness
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth identity; no heartbeat timestamp exists. An unresponsive executor remains available indefinitely. After a leased job expires, waitStopped also keeps trusting that live process and waits forever, preventing fallback and potentially cancellation. A real subprocess probe confirmed that a SIGSTOPped process still passes the identity comparison.
findings.suggestion: Track executor freshness separately from process identity. Reject stale executors for new jobs and reattachment, and provide a bounded, fail-closed path when a stale owner cannot confirm shutdown.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor becomes suspended or hangs during a check. Its lease expires, but the daemon waits indefinitely for stopped=1 because the executor's PID and birth still match.

findings.title: Retry jobs are persisted but never reattached
findings.detail: The resume allowlist accepts only baseline, initial and rebase. In-place targeted retries and timeout retries also receive durable handles and survive shutdown, but resume rejects those handles even when stage, round, purpose, SHA, environment and release match. The engine then cancels the surviving retry and repeats earlier gate work, leaving the requested retry restart coverage unimplemented.
findings.suggestion: Persist the retry continuation and evidence needed to resume each supported gate purpose, then reattach matching retry jobs instead of rejecting them through this allowlist.
findings.failure_scenario: Restart the daemon while a baseline-retry-targeted or regression-retry-targeted job is running. Resume cancels that job and starts the stage's initial gate execution again.

output.summary: Traced identity selection, token caching, approval checks, and credential confinement. Found an App-key exposure path. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies (entities and the MCP SDK) are missing; an isolated read-policy probe confirmed the confinement gap. No files changed.

findings.title: Protect the configured App key from agent reads
findings.detail: private_key_path accepts paths outside configDir, but readPolicy is still constructed with only configDir and the existing credential paths. The configured key is never added to denyRead. Agents run as the same OS user, so mode 0600 does not prevent them from reading it. An isolated configureReadPolicy/homeReadPolicy probe returned denied:false for an external App-key path. This exposes a credential capable of minting installation tokens.
findings.suggestion: Add the configured private-key path, including its resolved symlink target, to the shared credential read-deny policy. Test that an external key is denied to agents and gates.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure private_key_path to an owner-readable 0600 file outside configDir and the existing denied directories. A tool-enabled agent reads that file and obtains the App private key.

output.summary: Reviewed repository identity routing, approval handling, and secret protection. Standalone checks passed for JWT signing, caching, refresh, and redacted exchange failures. Found a private-key confinement gap. The targeted test files could not load because dependencies are missing; config imports also encountered an incompatible installed Zod API.

findings.title: Protect the configured App key from agent reads
findings.detail: The config accepts private_key_path outside the config directory, but never adds that file to readPolicy or protectPrivateFile. Existing confinement protects the config directory, not arbitrary App key paths. Mode 0600 does not protect against agents running as the same OS user. A temporary-fixture probe using configureReadPolicy and homeReadPolicy returned {"configuredKeyMode":"0600","keyInsideAllowedCheckout":true,"keyReadDenied":false}, confirming that an allowed checkout can contain a readable App key.
findings.suggestion: Register the configured key and its canonical path with the shared private-file protection before starting agents or gates, or refuse key locations outside protected paths. Add a confinement regression test for an external key path.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator configures an absolute private_key_path in an agent-readable location, such as an allowed checkout. Startup accepts its regular mode-0600 file, and an agent can read and exfiltrate the App private key.

output.summary: Reviewed identity selection, token caching, GitHub callers, approval handling, and key protection. Confirmed a startup-validation defect with an isolated probe. Repository tests could not load because dependencies were missing and the available Zod version was incompatible.

findings.title: Reject unusable key paths during startup
findings.detail: Startup uses statSync, which follows symlinks, while signingKey opens with O_NOFOLLOW and rejects them. Consequently, configuration and daemon startup accept a key path that makes every App-authenticated operation fail. Startup also omits the signer's ownership check. An isolated probe, with unrelated eval/review modules stubbed to bypass incompatible Zod APIs, confirmed the mismatch. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/github-app-startup-review.test.ts". Output: "(fail) startup refuses a key path the signer cannot use" and "Expected: true\nReceived: false"; the preceding assertion confirmed that signing rejects the same path with "symlink refused".
findings.suggestion: Reuse the signer's file validation during startup, including no-follow opening, ownership, regular-file, and readability checks, so unusable configurations refuse immediately.
findings.failure_scenario: Set private_key_path to a symlink pointing to a valid owner-owned 0600 RSA key. Startup succeeds, but the first GitHub operation fails with "symlink refused" and all configured App repositories remain unusable.

output.summary: Reviewed authentication routing, key validation, approval identity, and doctor behavior. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies are absent (missing entities). Isolated probes confirmed inconsistent startup and signing validation. No repository files were changed.

findings.title: Validate the key with the same rules at startup and signing
findings.detail: Startup uses statSync, which follows symlinks, but signingKey opens with O_NOFOLLOW and rejects them. Consequently, startup accepts a configuration that cannot perform any App-authenticated operation. Startup also omits the ownership check enforced by signingKey. An isolated loadConfig probe printed `Startup configuration accepted symlink: true`; invoking the actual provider with that path printed `GitHub App private key <scratch>/link.pem: symlink refused`. The probes mocked unrelated unavailable dependencies and made no network calls.
findings.suggestion: Share the secure file-opening and validation implementation between startup and signing so invalid paths, ownership, and permissions fail clearly before the daemon starts.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure private_key_path as a symlink to a valid owner-owned 0600 RSA key. The daemon starts successfully, but every GitHub operation for a listed repository fails with 'symlink refused'.

findings.title: Do not require owner authentication for an App-only installation
findings.detail: Doctor still unconditionally derives the gh check from `gh auth status` using the owner's environment. Even when App token exchange succeeds and the installation covers every configured repository, a machine without an owner's gh login receives a failed check and doctor exits 1. App-authenticated gh calls do not require that login because the provider supplies GH_TOKEN.
findings.suggestion: Evaluate authentication requirements using the configured repository identities. Require owner authentication for repositories using the owner identity, and use the App exchange result for App repositories.
findings.failure_scenario: All configured repositories use the App, SSH transport works, and App exchange and repository coverage checks succeed, but no owner OAuth login is stored in gh. Doctor reports 'not authenticated or no repo access' and fails despite working factory authentication.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding parser, worker fallback, routing, health, and round-checkpoint code. No concrete defects found. Targeted tests could not reach assertions because required dependencies were missing and the available Zod lacked z.json().

Traced parsing, LAN fallback, coordinator routing, and round accounting. Found an authentication-classification gap confirmed by a focused probe. Targeted tests could not start because dependencies were missing or incompatible. No files changed.

findings.title: Preserve authentication classification when the CLI stalls after rejection
findings.detail: The timeout returns precede authentication classification and omit failureClass. If Claude emits a structured authentication rejection but hangs before exiting, an idle timeout returns stuck. The LAN executor accepts that result instead of falling back locally, and Context.invoke returns it as a task failure; implementation then proceeds to gates and consumes a round. A focused runClaude probe feeding the captured fixture with idleTimedOut:true returned {"status":"stuck","error":"no output for 10s"}, with no failureClass.
findings.suggestion: After preserving explicit caller cancellation, prioritize a parsed authentication rejection over timeout/stall classification, or retain failureClass on those results. Add a regression test combining the captured rejection with an idle timeout.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude emits the authentication-failure stream, then hangs during shutdown until the idle watchdog fires. Its rejected session is recorded as a finished stuck implementation instead of triggering authentication fallback.

output.summary: Found four lifecycle and eligibility defects through code tracing and isolated probes. Targeted tests could not load because entities and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk are missing. No files were modified.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates incorrectly require an enabled issue queue
findings.detail: lifecycleManaged excludes every repository outside githubQueue.repos, and the reconciler only runs when the queue is enabled. CLI, MCP, label-triggered and comment-triggered runs therefore receive no lifecycle labels outside queue repositories, despite the requirement covering every start path.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission and manage all issue-linked runs in eligible repositories.
findings.failure_scenario: With githubQueue disabled, start a CLI run containing Closes #7. Neither its start nor its eventual failure updates the issue labels.

findings.title: Status transitions can disappear before their effects are recorded
findings.detail: Events are reconstructed from the current status rather than durably recorded when the transition occurs. A failure or needs_human transition followed by resolution between polls disappears. An earlier comment failure also breaks the loop before later events receive pending checkpoints. An isolated source probe using `bun -` produced `needs_human then resolved between polls: {"labels":[],"comments":["Limitless run r1 started: https://example.com/runs/r1"],"checkpoint":null}`. A second case with repeated start-comment failures likewise lost the failure comment after resolution.
findings.suggestion: Persist lifecycle event intents and their original reasons atomically with run transitions, then let polling deliver those durable intents.
findings.failure_scenario: The start comment keeps failing, the run fails, and the owner resolves it before GitHub recovers. The eventual retry posts only the start comment; no failure checkpoint or comment exists.

findings.title: A partial failure-label transition permits immediate re-pick
findings.detail: The transition deletes in-progress before adding failed. If that POST fails, the queue sees neither blocking label. For CLI/MCP Closes directives, latestIssueRun returns null because it only searches issue source references, so its local re-approval guard does not help. An isolated source probe using `bun -` returned `{"labels":["priority:1"],"eligibility":{"eligible":true,"priority":1},"logs":["Issue lifecycle owner/repo#7 run r1: Error: GitHub write failed"]}`.
findings.suggestion: Add the target status label before removing the old label, and make the shared latest-run re-approval check cover all linked-issue start paths.
findings.failure_scenario: A CLI run with Closes #7 fails. Deleting in-progress succeeds but adding failed is rejected. The same poll admits another run with the unchanged priority approval.

findings.title: Timestamp comparison rejects valid same-second re-approval
findings.detail: The new guard compares createdAt strictly rather than using labeled-event order. GitHub timestamps have second precision, so a trusted priority application later in the timeline can share the failure event's timestamp. An isolated policy probe using `bun -` with failure followed by trusted approval at the same timestamp returned `{"eligible":false,"reason":"factory status requires priority re-approval after failure"}`.
findings.suggestion: Use the ordered timeline to determine whether a trusted priority application follows the most recent failure-label application, including timestamp ties.
findings.failure_scenario: An automation applies failed and the trusted owner reapplies a priority label later in the same second. The issue remains ineligible despite the required re-approval.

output.summary: Found two lifecycle defects using isolated probes with fake dependencies. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities package. git diff --check passed.

findings.title: Lifecycle transitions disappear before polling checkpoints them
findings.detail: Events are derived from the current status rather than durably recorded when the transition occurs. A failed or needs_human run resolved before the next poll never receives its required reason comment. Pending label writes are also abandoned after the status changes: their checkpoints are never replayed. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/lifecycle-review-probe.ts"`, exercising the implementation with fake dependencies, printed `failure resolved between polls: {"labels":[],"comments":["<!-- limitless-lifecycle:run-a:started -->\nLimitless run run-a started: https://example.com/runs/run-a"]}` and `failed label rejected then resolved: {"labels":[],"failedLabelCheckpoint":"pending"}`, then failed its assertion.
findings.suggestion: Persist lifecycle event intent and publication text alongside the status transition, and reconcile outstanding effects independently of the current status.
findings.failure_scenario: Between two polls, a run reaches failed or needs_human and is then resolved. Alternatively, its failure-label write fails, and the run is resolved before the retry poll.

findings.title: A failed label write allows an unapproved repeat of a CLI-linked issue
findings.detail: The failure transition deletes in-progress before adding failed. If the latter write fails, the issue has neither blocking label. For CLI/MCP runs linked through Closes directives, latestIssueRun returns null because it only searches issue source references; the completed run also no longer claims the issue. Consequently, the same poll can select it using its original priority approval. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/lifecycle-review-probe.ts"` printed `CLI Closes run failed, failed-label write rejected, queue eligibility: {"labels":[],"decision":{"eligible":true,"priority":1}}` and failed its assertion.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the admission block until failure publication succeeds, and make the existing eligibility check recognize failed runs linked through Closes directives even when GitHub writes fail.
findings.failure_scenario: A CLI or MCP run containing Closes #7 fails. Removing in-progress succeeds, adding failed returns an error, and issue #7 retains its original trusted priority label. The queue immediately starts another run without fresh approval.

output.summary: Found four lifecycle and re-approval defects using temporary probes against extracted implementation code. The checkout is unchanged. Targeted repository tests could not load because dependencies are absent (Cannot find package 'entities'); git diff --check passed.

findings.title: Include sanitized reasons in failure and needs-human comments
findings.detail: Both comments always contain fixed UI-link text; run.error is never read. Ordinary public reasons are therefore omitted, contrary to both lifecycle requirements. Command `bun /private/tmp/lr-5yH32t/claude-501/lifecycle-review-probe.ts` produced `reason included: false` for error `Gate lint failed: missing semicolon`.
findings.suggestion: Include the recorded reason after credential redaction and publication checks, using fixed fallback text when publication is blocked.
findings.failure_scenario: A managed issue run fails with a safe, actionable error. Its GitHub comment says only that it failed and links to the UI.

findings.title: Post the required fallback instead of permanently suppressing blocked comments
findings.detail: Publication-check failures mark the comment done without posting anything. The delivery-time check repeats this behavior at line 249. Command `bun /private/tmp/lr-5yH32t/claude-501/lifecycle-review-probe.ts` produced `blocked body fallback posted: false checkpoint: done`. Subsequent polls cannot recover the missing notification.
findings.suggestion: Persist and deliver a safe fixed fallback when the original body is blocked, rather than acknowledging an unposted comment as done.
findings.failure_scenario: The UI URL or run identifier matches a private string. Labels change, but the lifecycle comment and required fallback are both permanently absent.

findings.title: Record lifecycle transitions when they happen
findings.detail: Effects are created only from the current run snapshot during polling. No durable effect is recorded by updateRun or resolveRun. A failure or needs-human transition followed by resolution before the next poll disappears entirely, including across a restart. Command `bun /private/tmp/lr-5yH32t/claude-501/lifecycle-review-probe.ts` produced `failure between polls reported: false`.
findings.suggestion: Durably record lifecycle events alongside state transitions, then let polling deliver the recorded effects.
findings.failure_scenario: After a poll, a run fails and the owner resolves it through the API before the next poll. The reconciler sees only resolved and never records or posts the failure notification.

findings.title: Allow re-approval when the retained failure label predates the latest run
findings.detail: Eligibility requires the failure-label timestamp itself to be at least the latest failed run's finishedAt, even when a trusted priority application occurred after both. A re-approved run can fail before its first lifecycle poll, leaving the previous failed label present; label reconciliation then skips reapplying it. Further priority applications cannot unblock that issue. Command `bun /private/tmp/lr-5yH32t/claude-501/eligibility-review-probe.ts` produced `trusted priority applied after both failure label and latest failed run: {"eligible":false,"reason":"priority re-approval required after the latest issue run"}`.
findings.suggestion: Accept trusted priority evidence after both the latest failure and the failure-label application, while preserving timeline ordering for equal timestamps.
findings.failure_scenario: A previously failed issue is re-approved and picked. The new run fails before the next poll, so GitHub retains the old failed-label event. The owner reapplies priority afterward, but admission still refuses indefinitely unless the failure label is manually cycled.

output.summary: Found four lifecycle requirement gaps. Isolated probes confirmed omitted reasons, queue-only coverage, and lost transitions between polls. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies are absent: Cannot find package 'entities'. No files were modified.

findings.title: Publish the sanitized failure or needs-human reason
findings.detail: Both comments always use fixed text and discard run.error, including entirely public reasons. The probe produced only 'failed: see https://example.com/runs/run-example.' for a run whose reason was 'Required configuration is missing'. This fails the explicit requirement to comment with the reason.
findings.suggestion: Include the reason after credential redaction and publication checking; use fixed text when publication is blocked.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails or reaches needs_human with a safe, actionable reason. Issue watchers receive no explanation.

findings.title: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue eligibility
findings.detail: lifecycleManaged requires trusted queue accounts and repository membership, and reconciliation is started only by startIssueQueue. Consequently CLI, MCP, label, and comment-triggered runs outside enabled queue repositories never receive lifecycle labels or durable comments. The request explicitly covers every start path without this repository restriction.
findings.suggestion: Schedule lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission and cover all issue-linked runs.
findings.failure_scenario: With github.queue disabled, an owner starts a CLI run containing Closes #7. Starting or failing that run produces no lifecycle labels or comments.

findings.title: Checkpoint lifecycle events when transitions occur
findings.detail: Events are recorded only from the current status during polling. No transition hook records an outbox entry. If needs_human or failed changes to resolved before the next poll, its comment is never recorded and cannot survive a restart. An isolated probe confirmed that running → needs_human → resolved between reconciliations leaves no comment:needs_human checkpoint.
findings.suggestion: Persist pending lifecycle events atomically with the relevant run transitions, then deliver them through polling.
findings.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human just after a poll. The owner resolves it through the UI before the next poll, or resolves it after a restart but before reconciliation. The required needs-you comment is permanently lost.

findings.title: Post a fixed fallback when publication checking blocks text
findings.detail: When checkBody throws, the effect is marked done without posting anything. The delivery-time check repeats this behavior. This permanently suppresses the notification instead of posting the fixed fallback required by the request; the added private-body test explicitly expects suppression.
findings.suggestion: Replace blocked text with a safe fixed notification and keep it pending until delivery succeeds.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured private string matches the UI hostname or run id in a comment. Labels change, but the issue never receives any notification, even after subsequent polls or restarts.

output.summary: Reviewed audit allowances, CI path matching, delivery and draft pushes, verification repairs, worker publication, and restart handling. No concrete defects found. Allowance parsing checks passed. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout lacks the `entities` dependency; integration behavior remains unverified.

Reviewed allowance parsing, audit classification, verify-change repairs, publication paths, restart handling, and worker release matching. No concrete defects found. git diff --check passed. Targeted tests could not run because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

Found a restart recovery defect: terminal status prevents unfinished rollback from resuming. The targeted restart suite could not load because the checkout lacks the entities package. An isolated scheduler probe confirmed the recovery gap.

findings.title: Keep rejected runs recoverable until rollback completes
findings.detail: This write marks the run needs_human before reset/clean finishes. Scheduler.start() only recovers running and waiting_input runs, so a daemon restart never invokes the new rollbackRejectedMerge resume path. The tests conceal this by explicitly calling executeRun on terminal runs. An isolated scheduler probe with a persisted needs_human rejection produced {"queries":[["queued","cancelled"],["running","waiting_input"]],"executed":0,"status":"needs_human"} and failed with `AssertionError: persisted rejection must resume to finish rollback` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.suggestion: Persist the rejection checkpoint while keeping the run recoverable, then set needs_human after rollback completes; alternatively, explicitly recover unfinished rejection checkpoints in the scheduler. Test recovery through scheduler startup.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after the rejection write but before reset, or immediately after reset before clean/state save. On startup the run remains terminal and is never scheduled, leaving the rejected merge or incomplete rollback state in the checkout indefinitely.

output.summary: Found a restart recovery defect: terminalizing the run prevents the scheduler from finishing rollback. The targeted test file could not load because the checkout is missing the entities package. An isolated scheduler probe confirmed terminal rejections are not recovered.

findings.title: Keep unfinished rejection rollback eligible for startup recovery
findings.detail: This checkpoint sets needs_human before rollback, but Scheduler.start only recovers running and waiting_input runs, and tick only executes queued runs. A daemon restart therefore never reaches rollbackRejectedMerge for this checkpoint. The new tests conceal this by explicitly calling executeRun on the terminal run. An isolated probe of Scheduler.start with a needs_human rejection returned {"recovered":0,"active":[],"status":"needs_human"}.
findings.suggestion: Persist the rejection while keeping unfinished cleanup eligible for recovery, or explicitly recover rejected runs with unfinished rollback at scheduler startup. Test through scheduler restart rather than directly invoking executeRun.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops immediately after rejection persistence or after reset but before clean/state save. On startup the run remains needs_human and is never scheduled, leaving the rejected merge or incomplete cleanup and stale head/state permanently in place.

output.summary: Found three command-processing defects using isolated probes of the changed processing code. The targeted suite could not load because dependencies are missing: bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts reported Cannot find module '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js'. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: An empty enable poll causes later commands to be discarded
findings.detail: A successful poll with no open issues stores no boundary. When an issue and command subsequently appear, that later poll establishes the boundary from their timestamps and permanently excludes the command. This moves initialization past the first successful poll and silently loses commands posted after polling was enabled. An isolated probe of the processing block, run with `bun "$TMPDIR/comment-review-probe.mjs"`, printed `empty initial poll, then new command: runs=0; expected=1`.
findings.suggestion: Establish a durable GitHub-time boundary on the first successful poll even when no open issues are returned, so later commands are eligible.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable the queue while the repository has no open issues. After its first successful poll, open an issue and post a trusted command before the next poll. That command never runs.

findings.title: Identity failures bypass the factory-author exclusion
findings.detail: Identity lookup errors become null, which makes bot null and disables the factory-author check while slash commands continue running. A factory bot included in the trusted list is therefore admitted during an identity API failure, violating the requirement that factory-authored comments never run. An isolated processing-block probe run with `bun "$TMPDIR/comment-review-probe.mjs"` printed `identity API failure, factory-authored command: runs=1; expected=0`.
findings.suggestion: Leave commands retryable when the posting identity cannot be established, or retain independently verified bot identity for the exclusion.
findings.failure_scenario: The trusted list contains factory[bot], an unedited factory-authored slash command is newer than the boundary, and identity lookup fails. The poll creates and records a run for that comment.

findings.title: Marker substrings silently reject legitimate trusted requests
findings.detail: Any occurrence of `<!-- limitless-` rejects a command, even when a trusted human includes that text as the subject of the requested change. The substring does not establish factory authorship and adds an undocumented eligibility restriction. An isolated processing-block probe run with `bun "$TMPDIR/comment-review-probe.mjs"` printed `trusted request containing marker text: runs=0; expected=1`.
findings.suggestion: Use verified authorship or durable posting provenance to identify factory comments rather than rejecting marker text anywhere in a request.
findings.failure_scenario: A trusted human posts `/limitless fix parsing of <!-- limitless-status -->` after the boundary. The unedited command is skipped on every poll.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, transaction handling, webhook routing, and queue lifecycle. Isolated probes reproduced two defects. The targeted test files could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, discord.js, and entities dependencies are missing.

findings.title: Identity lookup failure disables factory-author exclusion
findings.detail: Catching identity errors as null sets bot to null, so a trusted factory bot's slash command passes the author exclusion and creates a run. This violates the requirement that factory-authored commands never run. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/q1c-review-probe.ts". Output: factory slash command with identity error: runs=1, authors=["factory[bot]"]. The probe executes the queue code with fake GraphQL and mocked lifecycle delivery.
findings.suggestion: Leave commands retryable when the posting identity cannot be established, or obtain the factory bot login independently of token refresh.
findings.failure_scenario: An App bot appears in github.queue.trusted, its unedited /limitless command is newer than the boundary, and identity resolution fails after the GraphQL response succeeds.

findings.title: Marker substring rejects legitimate owner commands
findings.detail: The includes check rejects any request mentioning a factory marker, even when a trusted human wrote it. Such commands satisfy the specified command rules but are silently skipped forever. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/q1c-review-probe.ts". Output: owner request quoting a factory marker: runs=0, authors=[].
findings.suggestion: Recognize factory-generated comments by their validated framing and provenance rather than a substring anywhere in the request.
findings.failure_scenario: After enablement, the owner posts the unedited command '/limitless remove the obsolete <!-- limitless-status --> marker'. Every poll skips it.

output.summary: Reviewed checkpoints, replay, attribution, and classification. Classifier/store checks passed, including Homebrew SQLite. Pipeline/worker tests could not load because the entities dependency is missing. Found two durability/history defects.

findings.title: Replay completed in-place results before checking execution compatibility
findings.detail: Completed in-place jobs still pass through canResume, which requires the original release SHA, environment, and daemon port to match. After a deployment changes any of these, resume clears the handle without observing its stored result and starts another execution. A failure completed before the evidence checkpoint can therefore disappear when the new execution passes.
findings.suggestion: Replay and checkpoint a completed job's stored result independently of the compatibility checks required to continue live execution. Retain those checks for unfinished jobs.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place initial gates job completes with a failure; the daemon stops before observe runs. A new release resumes the run with a different build SHA. canResume rejects the completed job, its handle is cleared, and passing replacement gates leave no observation of the original failure.

findings.title: Preserve timeout re-run history when its setup fails
findings.detail: When the initial check times out and the timeout re-run fails during setup, compareGates emits a synthetic not_run comparison for that check. Finalization excludes that comparison and calls observationHistory(undefined), permanently recording no_retry instead of rerun_failed. A Store probe produced [{"class":"unclassified","history":"no_retry"}]. The direct command `bun -e 'import { observationHistory } from "./src/gates/failure-class.ts"; console.log(observationHistory(undefined));'` outputs `no_retry`.
findings.suggestion: Carry timeout re-run outcome evidence into finalization even when the re-run never reaches its checks, and record rerun_failed for the original timeout observation.
findings.failure_scenario: The baseline test passes, the initial post-change test times out, and the stage's timeout re-run fails its setup command. The stage completes with blocking comparisons, but the timeout observation incorrectly claims no retry occurred.

output.summary: Reviewed execution identity, evidence persistence, classification, promotion, and restart paths. 34 targeted tests passed, including Homebrew SQLite migration coverage. Pipeline tests could not load because the installed dependencies lack entities. Found a restart path that loses completed failure evidence.

findings.title: Replay completed in-place results before rejecting resume compatibility
findings.detail: Recording still depends on passing canResume before attaching the stored execution. The in-place executor requires the recorded release SHA, environment, and daemon port to match even when the job is already done. When these change during deployment, resume discards the handle and starts another execution without recording the completed result. This violates the required replay-before-reexecution durability guarantee.
findings.suggestion: Record an existing completed in-place result through the evidence checkpoint before applying compatibility checks for live execution or discarding its handle. Preserve its original execution identity and attribution.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place gates execution fails and persists its result in gate_jobs. The daemon crashes after executeGate returns but before observation insertion. A newer daemon resumes with a different buildSha; canResume returns false, the stored handle is cleared, and a fresh passing execution leaves no observation of the original failure.

output.summary: Reviewed deploy, installation recovery, and executor lifecycle changes. An isolated probe confirmed incomplete cleanup after an installation inspection failure. The four targeted test files could not start because installed dependencies lack zod.prefault and entities.

findings.title: Preserve recovery state when executor inspection fails after enable
findings.detail: This early throw bypasses executor cleanup after reconcileExecutor has already enabled the label. On a fresh installation there is no replacement journal or deploy intent, so the failed command leaves an enabled executor plist without durable recovery state. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-executor-probe.ts"` produced `Error: launchctl print gui/501/dev.limitless.executor failed (exit 1): Operation not permitted`, followed by `"enabled": true`, `"executorPlistExists": true`, `"intentExists": false`, and `"journalExists": false`. launchd can subsequently start this unit at login despite installation having failed.
findings.suggestion: Record durable recovery state before enabling a newly installed executor. On inspection failure, attempt to disable it and retain that state until shutdown and reconciliation are confirmed; do not bypass all executor cleanup here.
findings.failure_scenario: During the first executor installation, launchctl enable succeeds, but the subsequent launchctl print fails with a permission or transport error. Installation exits unsuccessfully while the executor plist remains enabled, with no journal or intent for the next invocation to recover.

output.summary: Found two executor shutdown gaps using isolated probes against the service code. The requested targeted tests could not reach assertions because installed dependencies lack zod.prefault and entities. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Failed plist inspection bypasses rollback shutdown
findings.detail: installedUnits silently skips nonzero plutil results, so unit() conflates inspection failure with no installed executor. Deploy then writes no intent and restores the previous checkout without shutting down the live executor. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-executor-probe.ts" plutil-failure. Output: {"mode":"plutil-failure","executorLoaded":true,"executorDisabled":false,"executorCommands":[],"checkouts":["git checkout -q --detach B","git checkout -q --detach A"],"intent":false}. The same ambiguity can make reconciliation return successfully without enabling an installed executor.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish failed inspection from confirmed absence. Refuse checkout changes and successful reconciliation when executor discovery is unconfirmed, and retain any existing intent.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor is installed and loaded, plutil returns a nonzero inspection error, and a deploy gate fails after checkout of the target release. Rollback checks out the previous release while the executor remains loaded and enabled.

findings.title: Daemon installation failure leaves the executor enabled
findings.detail: Installation replaces the daemon before reaching the executor. If daemon replacement fails, this catch restores only the daemon migration and throws; it never shuts down the existing executor. With checkout B and processes originally running A, restoration can start the daemon from B without confirming its health, while the executor remains loaded and can restart from B. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-executor-probe.ts" install-failure. Output after the simulated daemon bootstrap failure: {"mode":"install-failure","executorLoaded":true,"executorDisabled":false,"executorCommands":[],"checkouts":[],"intent":false}. This violates the requirement that failed installation leave no executor running on an unconfirmed release.
findings.suggestion: Ensure installation failure paths confirm executor shutdown and disablement when daemon replacement or health confirmation fails, retaining durable recovery state if shutdown cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: The release checkout has advanced from A to B, the daemon and executor still run A, and service install fails while bootstrapping or health-checking the replacement daemon before reaching the executor installation step.

output.summary: Found a mixed-case repository compatibility regression. Store probe confirmed lowercase lookup misses an existing mixed-case record. Targeted tests could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing; a resolveRepo probe was also blocked by missing entities.

findings.title: Preserve existing repository identity when canonicalizing queue keys
findings.detail: The lowercased repo now also becomes the repository passed to createRun. Existing persisted repository slugs are case-sensitive: getRepoBySlug and resolveRepo use exact equality. A queue previously configured as Owner/Repo therefore stops resolving its existing repository record and registers a second owner/repo record through gh. This loses the existing record's mergePolicy and repository profile. An in-memory Store probe printed `configured spelling: none canonical spelling: null`, confirming the lookup mismatch.
findings.suggestion: Resolve existing repository records case-insensitively before creating queue runs, or preserve their registered spelling for run creation while using canonical keys for snapshots and invalidations. Add a regression covering a persisted mixed-case repository with nondefault settings.
findings.failure_scenario: An existing installation has a registered Owner/Repo repository with mergePolicy none and queue repos ["Owner/Repo"]. After upgrading, queue admission passes owner/repo to resolveRepo, which misses the existing record and creates another with the global merge policy, potentially auto-merging work previously configured never to merge.

output.summary: Found a compatibility regression for existing mixed-case repository registrations. Targeted queue tests could not start because the MCP SDK dependency is missing; a resolver probe was also blocked by missing entities.

findings.title: Preserve existing repository identity when canonicalizing queue keys
findings.detail: The lowercase repo now flows into issueRunRequest and Factory.createRun. However, Store.getRepoBySlug and resolveRepo still use case-sensitive lookups. An existing Owner/Repo registration is therefore missed, and resolveRepo registers owner/repo separately using remote defaults and cfg.githubMerge, losing the existing defaultBranch and mergePolicy. Targeted command: bun -e 'import { Store } from "./src/db/store.ts"; const s = new Store(":memory:"); s.upsertRepo({slug:"Owner/Repo",kind:"github",url:null,localPath:null,defaultBranch:"release",mergePolicy:"none"}); console.log(s.getRepoBySlug("owner/repo")); s.close();' Output: null.
findings.suggestion: Resolve existing repository registrations case-insensitively before creating another registration, while retaining canonical queue keys. Add a regression covering an existing mixed-case registration with nondefault branch and merge policy.
findings.failure_scenario: Before upgrading, the queue and stored repository both use Owner/Repo with defaultBranch release and mergePolicy none. After upgrading, queue admission requests owner/repo, creating a second repository registration with the remote default branch and global merge policy.

output.summary: Found a reproducible recovery defect that discards a release intent on malformed data. The targeted suites could not load because the installed Zod lacks required APIs; an isolated probe using the real lease methods and claim client reproduced the defect. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Classify the moved tip before discarding a release intent
findings.detail: Every replay result of `moved` immediately marks confirmed ownership lost and clears the intent, without inspecting `result.tip.record`. The claim client also returns `moved` when the new tip is malformed. This violates the required malformed-data behavior and permanently discards the journaled final status and checkpoint. Isolated command `REVIEW_CHECKOUT="$PWD" bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review-race.test.ts"` failed with `Expected: "pending"; Received: "superseded"`; its printed row had confirmed state `lost` and `intent: null`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the recovery classification rules to the tip returned by `moved`. Preserve the intent and confirmed ownership when that record is malformed; mark lost only when a valid record establishes supersession.
findings.failure_scenario: A confirmed generation-1 holder has a pending release. Recovery reads its confirmed tip and starts replaying. Before updateRefs arrives, another writer changes the ref to a malformed claim commit. CAS refuses the release, and the client's follow-up read returns that malformed tip as `moved`. Recovery incorrectly clears the release intent and marks ownership lost.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, storage methods, claim client and recovery tests. An isolated probe confirmed intent loss during a release-replay race. The repository tests could not start because the available Zod dependency lacks required APIs.

findings.title: Preserve the intent when a replay encounters a malformed tip
findings.detail: Every `moved` replay result marks confirmed ownership lost and clears the intent without inspecting `result.tip`. ClaimClient also returns `moved` for a malformed competing tip, which invariant 3 requires retaining for retry. The isolated command `bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review-probe.test.ts"`, using the actual lease methods, ClaimClient and GitHub fake, failed with Expected: "pending", Received: "superseded"; the resulting row had confirmed.state "lost" and intent null.
findings.suggestion: Classify the returned tip using the same recovery rules as the initial read. Preserve the intent for malformed or otherwise unclassifiable records, and mark lost only when supersession is established.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery reads the confirmed held tip and starts replaying a journaled release. Before updateRefs arrives, the ref moves to a malformed commit. CAS correctly refuses the release, but recovery deletes its complete final-status and checkpoint intent and incorrectly marks ownership lost.

output.summary: Found a restart classification defect and confirmed the faulty selection with a dependency-free probe. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

findings.title: Preserve slow-regression evidence when resuming a durable execution
findings.detail: A restart creates a new stage ID, while reattaching the same durable execution preserves its original observation: the unique execution key makes the repeated insert a no-op. This filter therefore excludes the persisted row. The selector subsequently computes a slow regression but never records slow_regression=1; if its re-check passes, finalization classifies it as flaky instead of load. A dependency-free probe executing this exact selection returned {"persistedObservationStage":1,"resumedStage":2,"handlesSelectedForSlowFlag":[]}. Command: bun -e 'const source = await Bun.file("src/pipeline/engine.ts").text(); const start = source.indexOf("const observedHandles ="); const end = source.indexOf("ctx.checkCancelled();", start); const row = { run_id: "run", purpose: "rebase", sha: "head", stage_id: 1, handle_id: "durable-job" }; const ctx = { run: { id: "run" }, stageId: 2, store: { failureObservations: () => [row] } }; const handles = new Function("ctx", "sha", source.slice(start, end) + "return observedHandles;")(ctx, "head"); console.log(JSON.stringify({ persistedObservationStage: row.stage_id, resumedStage: ctx.stageId, handlesSelectedForSlowFlag: handles }));'
findings.suggestion: Select observations using the persisted execution identity across resumed stages. Add a restart test interrupted after observation insertion and before the slow-regression selector, then verify a passing re-check finalizes as load.
findings.failure_scenario: A durable LAN primary post-merge execution fails slowly and its observation is inserted. The daemon restarts before the selector runs. The execution is reattached under a new stage ID, and its slow-regression re-check passes.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and traced land ownership, retries, confirmation and restart paths. Found a restart classification defect. Both targeted test commands could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. No files were modified.

findings.title: Include replayed observations when recording slow regressions
findings.detail: A restart creates a new gates stage ID. When the persisted primary execution is reattached, observation insertion conflicts with its existing execution identity and preserves the original stage_id. This filter consequently excludes that observation, so the selector never records slow_regression on it. If the re-check passes, finalization records retry_passed but classifies the failure as flaky instead of load.
findings.suggestion: Select observations by the persisted execution identity rather than requiring the current stage ID. Add restart coverage between primary observation insertion and the slow-regression selector.
findings.failure_scenario: A LAN post-merge primary execution fails slowly. Terminate at the gate-result save after observation insertion, then resume the persisted handle in a new gates stage. The re-check passes, but the original observation retains slow_regression=0 and finalizes as flaky.

output.summary: Found three ownership and recovery defects using isolated regression probes with the real manager and reconciliation code. No repository files changed. The supplied test suite could not start because the available Zod dependency lacks prefault.

findings.title: Released ownership incorrectly blocks later reacquisition
findings.detail: The supersession check includes confirmed released rows. After another member acquires and releases a later generation, the original member permanently returns superseded instead of acquiring the released tip. It also marks its already-released generation lost and can emit a false onLost callback. Regression command: bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts". Output: "released ownership must not prevent reacquiring a later released tip" failed: Expected "held", Received "superseded".
findings.suggestion: Apply ownership-loss checks to confirmed held ownership; let released rows reach the released-tip acquisition decision.
findings.failure_scenario: Member A acquires and releases generation 1. Member B acquires the same run at generation 2 and releases it. A attempts to acquire the same run again and receives superseded rather than generation 3.

findings.title: Renewal omits leases confirmed through reconciliation
findings.detail: The renewal loop only visits the handles map, which is populated exclusively by directly applied writes. An unconfirmed acquisition subsequently confirmed by reconciliation never enters that map, so even an active lease receives no renewals. Recovery at manager construction has the same omission. Regression command: bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts". Output: "renewal writes after reconciled acquisition: 0"; assertion failed with Expected > 1, Received 1.
findings.suggestion: Register handles when reconciliation confirms held ownership and initialize renewal tracking for recovered confirmed held rows, without manufacturing an anchor.
findings.failure_scenario: An acquisition applies remotely but returns unconfirmed. A loop tick reconciles it to confirmed held. Subsequent ticks have active(h) returning true, but never renew this generation, allowing it to expire.

findings.title: Cross-run rejection bypasses pending-intent reconciliation
findings.detail: A different run is refused before the pending intent is reconciled. This prevents an acquisition known not to have applied from being dropped and forgotten by the next operation, and returns refused instead of wait when the intent remains unresolved. Regression command: bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts". Output: "next run reconciles a never-confirmed acquisition before refusing" failed: Expected "held", Received "refused".
findings.suggestion: Reconcile pending intents before the cross-run ownership check, return wait for unresolved intents, then re-read the row before deciding whether to refuse.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A's first acquisition returns unconfirmed with no confirmed ownership. GitHub subsequently reports the ref absent. Run B attempts acquisition before a loop tick; it is refused without reading GitHub, leaving A's disposable intent blocking B.

output.summary: Found two lease recovery and renewal defects using isolated probes. The targeted command `bun test test/leases.test.ts` could not load because the installed Zod lacks `prefault`, used by existing settings code.

findings.title: Reconcile pending intents before rejecting another run
findings.detail: The cross-run guard returns before reconciliation whenever the previous run has an intent. This violates the requirement to reconcile pending intents before every operation, and returns `refused` where unresolved intents require `wait`. Probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/lease-review-probe.ts"` produced `cross-run pending` with result `{"kind":"refused","reason":"live"}`, reads:0, writes:0, and the original intent unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile first, return wait if pending, then re-read the row and apply the cross-run ownership guard.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A's first acquisition leaves an unconfirmed intent but never creates the ref. A ends, and run B attempts acquisition before a renewal tick. Although reading the absent ref would drop and forget A's intent, B is refused without any read. Repeated acquisitions remain blocked until another path reconciles A.

findings.title: Include reconciled and recovered ownership in renewal
findings.detail: The renewal loop only visits the in-memory handles map, populated exclusively by direct applied writes in operate(). Recovery and reconcile() can confirm held ownership without registering a handle, so those leases never reach active() or renew. Probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/lease-review-probe.ts"` recovered an acquisition to confirmed held, then ran a tick; output showed reads:1, writes:0, active:0.
findings.suggestion: Register generation-bound handles when reconciliation confirms held ownership, and initialize renewal tracking for persisted confirmed held rows. Keep their anchors unavailable until a valid write establishes one.
findings.failure_scenario: An acquisition reaches GitHub but its response is lost. Recovery after restart, or reconciliation on a subsequent loop tick, confirms that acquisition. Even with active() configured to return true, subsequent ticks never renew the lease, allowing it to expire without detecting or reporting loss.

output.summary: Reviewed browser markers, prompt generation, verdict normalization and resume paths. Found one infrastructure-classification defect, confirmed with an isolated fake-stream parser probe. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies were missing or incompatible.

findings.title: Require positive browser setup evidence before converting blocks
findings.detail: The engine records browser availability solely from the absence of browser_unavailable. That warning covers configuration rejection, but not subsequent MCP startup failures. ClaudeStreamParser ignores failed MCP server status in its init event while accepting a successful structured verifier result. A fake-stream probe with playwright status failed produced only an init event and was consequently classified available. Marked environmental blocks then become unclear, lose covering-test requests, and enter implementation feedback instead of bounded environment-block handling.
findings.suggestion: Record successful browser setup explicitly for the invocation and preserve infrastructure-block handling when MCP initialization fails or setup success is unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview is ready and browserMcp constructs its configuration, but the Playwright MCP process fails during initialization. The verifier returns a marked criterion as environmentally blocked. No browser_unavailable warning exists, so the engine incorrectly converts it to unclear and requests another implementation round.

output.summary: Found two browser-verification defects. Existing spec-criteria tests passed; a targeted browser-marker probe reproduced incorrect rejection. Six changed test files could not load because dependencies were missing or incompatible (`entities` and Zod `.overwrite()`). No files were modified.

findings.title: The spec retry path rejects newly permitted browser checks
findings.detail: The prompt now permits visual preview criteria, but outOfRunCriteria still flags `visually`, `screenshots`, and `in a browser`, regardless of the browser marker. engine.ts then tells the author to replace these criteria with repository commands and tests and move external concerns out of scope. This can remove the browser checks this change requires. Reproduction command: `bun -e 'import {outOfRunCriteria} from "./src/pipeline/spec-criteria.ts"; const rows = outOfRunCriteria({acceptance_criteria:[{id:"AC-1", criterion:"Preview layout fits", how_to_verify:"Visually inspect the UI preview", browser:true}]}); console.log("flagged browser checks:", rows.map(row => row.id)); if (rows.length) throw new Error("A local preview check is incorrectly classified as out-of-run");'`. Output: `flagged browser checks: [ "AC-1" ]`, followed by `error: A local preview check is incorrectly classified as out-of-run` (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Update the out-of-run classifier and rewrite feedback to permit marked local-preview checks while preserving checks for genuinely external requirements. Add a focused spec-authoring regression test.
findings.failure_scenario: A spec author returns browser:true with how_to_verify `Visually inspect the UI preview`. The engine incorrectly requests a rewrite that can replace the visual check with a non-browser test.

findings.title: Absence of a warning does not prove successful browser setup
findings.detail: Every preview-backed invocation without a browser_unavailable event is classified as available. browserMcp only validates files and constructs a server configuration; it does not start the MCP server or confirm its handshake. Failures when the CLI subsequently launches that server do not emit browser_unavailable through this path. A verifier can therefore correctly report an infrastructure block, yet the engine converts it to unclear, suppresses the environment retry, and sends product-change feedback despite lacking the required successful browser-setup record.
findings.suggestion: Record an engine-owned browser setup outcome for the same invocation and require positive success before conversion. Preserve unknown or failed startup outcomes as infrastructure limitations.
findings.failure_scenario: The preview is ready and browser configuration validation succeeds, but the MCP child fails to start or complete its handshake. The CLI still returns structured verification output with a marked row blocked because browser tools are unavailable. The engine records available and converts that row to unclear.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and lifecycle recovery paths. An isolated production-code probe confirmed one recovery defect. The targeted test file could not start because dependencies, including the MCP SDK and entities, are missing.

findings.title: Recover uncertain POSTs before suppressing their checkpoints
findings.detail: Body inspection runs before marker recovery. If inspection now fails, this catch marks an uncertain POST done without checking whether GitHub accepted it, violating the required recovery-before-close behavior. An isolated `bun -` probe with injected dependencies printed `recoveryGETs:0` and a done checkpoint with page reset to zero, followed by `FAIL: uncertain POST closed without marker recovery`.
findings.suggestion: For checkpoints with a recovery page, independently generate the expected marker and recover using the checkpointed author before closing the effect. Apply outgoing-body inspection before any new POST.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question POST, but its response is lost, leaving page=1. Before restart, its question text becomes a configured private string. Reconciliation suppresses the stored body and closes the checkpoint without recovering the accepted comment ID.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff, surrounding lifecycle and dispatch code, and ran isolated probes. Found privacy revalidation and oversized-publication defects. The targeted test file could not start because dependencies are absent: Cannot find module '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js'. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Reinspect original fields when delivering pending publications
findings.detail: Pending effects skip field inspection and recheck only their transformed body. If credentials are registered after checkpoint creation, checkBody redacts the newly recognized credential but publishes the surrounding field, bypassing whole-field withholding. An isolated `bun -` probe checkpointed a question, registered its embedded credential, then delivered it. Output contained `Question 1: private context: [redacted] end context`, with no withholding diagnostic.
findings.suggestion: Revalidate complete original questions and selected reasons against current protections before delivering pending effects. Withhold the entire matching field or durably suppress publication while preserving uncertain-POST recovery.
findings.failure_scenario: A question publication is checkpointed during a budget pause. Before delivery, configuration reload registers a credential present in that question. The next poll publishes the surrounding sensitive context instead of withholding the entire question.

findings.title: Bound publication bodies to GitHub's comment limit
findings.detail: Questions and reasons are appended without a size bound. A long field or combined question set exceeding GitHub's 65,536-character comment limit can never publish, yet remains pending and repeats recovery and POST attempts each poll. An isolated `bun -` probe using a fake gh that enforces this limit returned `{"postAttempts":2,"state":"pending","published":false}` after two polls with a 66,000-character question.
findings.suggestion: Inspect complete original fields first, then bound the outgoing body while preserving its envelope, question IDs and UI instructions. Use a fixed UI fallback when necessary.
findings.failure_scenario: A waiting run has one 66,000-character question, several questions whose combined body exceeds the limit, or an oversized needs-human reason. GitHub rejects every publication with HTTP 422 and no useful comment appears.

Reviewed trigger persistence, eligibility, merge preparation and delivery. Two targeted probes reproduced defects. The conflict-round suite could not execute because the installed Zod lacks number().overwrite(), used by existing schema code.

findings.title: Stale cached observations permanently discard eligible triggers
findings.detail: The saved snapshot overrides the supplied observation, and processConflictTriggers also skips a fresh lookup whenever a snapshot exists. An outdated draft flag or head therefore permanently marks a valid landing trigger as skipped. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/conflict-review.ts". Output: {"rounds":0,"triggers":[{"state":"skipped","reason":"PR is draft"}]} despite supplying an OPEN, non-draft observation for the current head.
findings.suggestion: Validate landing triggers against a fresh observation, and prevent older cached data from overriding it. Keep triggers pending when freshness cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: The saved snapshot says the PR is draft. The PR becomes ready, and landing discovers a conflict before polling refreshes the snapshot. Its trigger is skipped permanently; refreshing the draft flag alone does not emit another pr.conflicting event.

findings.title: A lost comment response produces duplicate resolution comments
findings.detail: The marker check occurs outside the per-command withGitHubRetry wrapper. If GitHub accepts the comment but its response fails transiently, the wrapper posts it again without checking the marker. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/conflict-comment-retry.ts". Output: {"comments":2}, using the actual retry helper with an accepted first request followed by unexpected EOF.
findings.suggestion: Recheck the marker within each retry attempt before posting the comment.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub stores the resolution comment, but gh receives unexpected EOF. Its automatic retry creates a second identical comment, violating the one-comment requirement.

findings.title: Do not permanently consume triggers using stale PR snapshots
findings.detail: The saved github_prs snapshot overrides the supplied observation regardless of freshness. After a review push advances the head, a landing conflict can therefore be permanently marked skipped because the poller still holds the previous head. Conversely, cached isDraft=false overrides a newer draft observation. Isolated `bun -` store probes produced `[{"state":"skipped","reason":"PR head moved"}]` and `rounds: 0` for a valid newer head, and `{"currentObservationIsDraft":true,"roundStarted":true}` for a draft PR. processConflictTriggers also directly consumes cached snapshots without refreshing them.
findings.suggestion: Validate triggers against a current observation with head-version protection. Leave triggers pending when cached data is outdated instead of permanently skipping them.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round pushes head B while the saved poller snapshot still names A. The operator approves B, and landing encounters a conflict. The trigger for B is skipped using snapshot A; with polling disabled, nothing subsequently resolves the blocked entry.

findings.title: Resolve against the PR's current target branch
findings.detail: Conflict preparation always fetches the original owner's baseBranch. Neither the poller nor readPrHead requests the PR's current baseRefName, and delivery never verifies it. Retargeting an open PR therefore causes the round to merge the wrong branch and potentially report success while the actual conflict remains. An isolated `bun -` readPrHead probe supplied baseRefName='release' and returned `{"githubBase":"release","returnedBase":null}`.
findings.suggestion: Observe and persist the PR's current target branch, merge its pinned tip, and verify the target remains consistent before delivery.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory PR originally targets main and is later retargeted to release. The poller reports a conflict with release, but the round merges main. If main is already an ancestor, the run immediately succeeds without resolving anything; otherwise it can push unrelated main changes into the PR.
