Reviewed trigger persistence, round execution, delivery, and restart paths. Direct probes reproduced two defects. The targeted test suite could not initialize because the installed Zod lacks .overwrite(), used by unchanged code.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot permanently discards a valid landing trigger
findings.detail: The cached github_prs data overrides the supplied observation without checking freshness. processConflictTriggers likewise uses any cached snapshot instead of fetching the current PR. A valid landing trigger for head B is therefore marked skipped when the cache still names A. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"), u="https://github.com/test/repo/pull/1", h="b".repeat(40); const r=s.upsertRepo({slug:"test/repo",kind:"github",url:null,localPath:null,defaultBranch:"main",mergePolicy:"pr"}); const o=s.createRun(r,{repo:r.slug,prompt:"feature"}); s.updateRun(o.id,{status:"succeeded",baseSha:h,branch:"feature",prUrl:u}); s.saveGithubPr({url:u,nodeId:null,data:JSON.stringify({state:"OPEN",headRefOid:"a".repeat(40)})},false,[]); s.recordConflictTrigger(u,h,"land",Date.now()); s.startConflictTrigger(s.pendingConflictTriggers()[0].id,{state:"OPEN",headRefOid:h},Date.now()); console.log(s.db.query("SELECT state, reason FROM conflict_triggers").all()); s.close();' Output: [{ state: "skipped", reason: "PR head moved" }].
findings.suggestion: Refresh observations that predate or disagree with the trigger, and keep the trigger pending until a current observation confirms eligibility or refusal.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round pushes head B while the poller cache still contains A. Landing B encounters conflicts. Its durable trigger is consumed against A and permanently skipped, so that landing event never starts a resolution round.

findings.title: Comment retries bypass the duplicate-comment check
findings.detail: The marker lookup runs once, but gh wraps each individual command in withGitHubRetry. If GitHub accepts the comment and its response is lost, the wrapper repeats the POST without looking for the marker again. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {withGitHubRetry,githubRetry} from "./src/git/repos.ts"; import {CommandError} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; githubRetry.baseDelayMs=1; const comments=[]; if(!comments.length) await withGitHubRetry(async()=>{comments.push("marker"); if(comments.length===1) throw new CommandError("lost response",1,"","unexpected EOF",false);}); console.log({comments:comments.length});' Output: { comments: 2 }.
findings.suggestion: Make the marker lookup and conditional post one retry operation, using the raw runner inside it so every retry checks whether the previous post landed.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub creates the resolution comment, then gh reports an unexpected EOF or timeout. Automatic retry creates a second identical comment, violating the one-comment requirement.

findings.title: Stale snapshots permanently discard valid land-conflict triggers
findings.detail: The saved poller snapshot overrides the supplied observation, regardless of freshness. If the cache still names an earlier head, the valid trigger is permanently marked skipped as 'PR head moved'. processConflictTriggers also uses cached snapshots without refreshing them. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/conflict-review-probes.ts". Output: stale snapshot: [{"state":"skipped","reason":"PR head moved"}] rounds: 0.
findings.suggestion: Refresh observations that disagree with a land trigger before deciding eligibility, use the fresh observation, and retain the trigger as pending while its head cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round pushes head B while the poller snapshot still names A. Landing B encounters a base conflict. Its durable trigger for B is consumed against cached A and skipped; later polling cannot recover that trigger.

findings.title: Comment retries can publish duplicate resolution summaries
findings.detail: The marker check runs outside the retry wrapper. The gh wrapper retries only the comment POST, so a successful POST followed by a lost response creates another comment without checking whether the first landed. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/conflict-review-probes.ts". A fake successful side effect followed by CommandError(stderr='unexpected EOF') produced: comments after lost acknowledgement: 2.
findings.suggestion: Recheck the resolution marker before each retry after an uncertain comment outcome, rather than blindly retrying the POST.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub creates the resolution comment, but gh loses the response with a retryable connection error. withGitHubRetry repeats the POST and the PR receives two identical comments, violating the one-comment requirement.

output.summary:
Reviewed executor routing, persistence, cancellation and restart behavior. An isolated Bun fixture reproduced lost setup output on retry resume. Targeted gate tests could not run because the installed Zod lacks .overwrite(), used by existing schema code. No files were modified.

Found three executor lifecycle defects. Direct probes confirmed restart-dependent retry verdicts and dropped executor events. Targeted suites could not initialize because installed dependencies lack z.number().overwrite() and the MCP SDK module.

findings.title: Restore setup inputs before resuming a local retry
findings.detail: On restart, checkoutCommitted() removes generated files and dependencies. runGateExecution then returns the cached initial result without rerunning setup, while the pending regression retry's stored request has setup: []. The retry therefore runs without its required build inputs. An isolated Bun fixture using the actual helpers produced: "initial: transient exit 1", "simulated crash", "resumed retry: missing-build exit 2". Before this change, resuming reran the complete gate suite, including setup.
findings.suggestion: Make local retry recovery restore the prerequisite setup and build state before replaying checks. Add a restart test using real setup-generated inputs rather than only fake GateRun results.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup creates build-output; a check transiently fails and would pass on retry. The daemon restarts after persisting the retry handle. Resume deletes build-output, skips the cached initial execution and attaches the setup-free retry, which fails because build-output is missing.

findings.title: Persist landing execution handles before awaiting results
findings.detail: Landing calls executeGate without either a stored handle or a persistence callback. Its default persistence callback does nothing, so landing handles are never durable. After a restart during checks, the queue calls start again rather than attaching to the execution already started. This leaves the requested durability seam incomplete for one of the explicitly included daemon gate paths.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle with its checked commit, pass it back on resume, and clear it after consuming the result. Cover restart between start and result with an injected executor.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor starts landing checks and returns a handle. The daemon terminates before the result arrives. The resumed land entry has no handle and starts a second execution instead of attaching to the first.

findings.title: Resumed local retries skip setup after checkout cleanup
findings.detail: The cached initial result skips the full local execution on resume, but the gates stage first calls checkoutCommitted(), which deletes dependencies and build output. The pending retry has setup: [], so it runs without the environment its first attempt produced. A direct `bun -` stdin probe exercising runGateExecution and retryRegressions returned [{"restart":false,"verdict":"flaky","blocking":false},{"restart":true,"verdict":"regressed","blocking":true}] for identical gates.
findings.suggestion: Restore the setup environment before replaying a local retry, or replay the full local attempt sequence when restarting after checkout cleanup.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup creates build output or installs dependencies; the initial check fails transiently; the daemon restarts before the regression retry completes. Resume deletes those files, skips the cached initial execution, and runs the retry without setup, producing a false blocking regression.

findings.title: Landing executions have no durable handle
findings.detail: This executeGate call supplies neither a persistence callback nor a stored handle. Its handle is discarded, and a resumed landing entry always calls start again. This leaves landing checks outside the requested durable start/persist/attach lifecycle.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle before attachment and reuse it on resume, keyed to the checked base and head commits.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon terminates while landing checks are running. On restart, the queue starts another execution instead of attaching to the existing one; an injected remote executor's original execution becomes untracked.

findings.title: Executor events never reach gate observers
findings.detail: executeGate only awaits execution.result and never consumes execution.events. Notifications currently work only because the internally constructed local executor closes over hooks; injected executors receive no hooks and their event streams are ignored. A direct `bun -` stdin probe supplying a check event returned {"eventIteratorsConsumed":0,"onResultCalls":0}. Pipeline gate events and landing command logs therefore disappear for injected executors.
findings.suggestion: Consume execution.events while awaiting the result and forward check notifications to the existing observers, avoiding duplicate notifications from the local executor.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits completed checks through Execution.events and returns its GateRun. The verdict is recorded, but no live gate notifications or landing check output are recorded.

Traced persistence, retries, restart cleanup, landing and events. Found three defects. Targeted tests could not run assertions because installed dependencies lack Zod .overwrite() and the MCP SDK module. An isolated executor probe confirmed dropped events. No files modified.

findings.title: Restore setup before replaying a local retry after restart
findings.detail: Resume calls checkoutCommitted, which deletes dependencies and generated files, then runGateExecution returns the cached initial result. The pending regression retry contains setup: [], so local attach reruns checks without restoring their prerequisites. Command: `bun run -` with an inline temporary-repository fixture exercising runGateExecution, retryRegressions and checkoutCommitted. Output: `Resumed gate verdict: regressed blocking: true`, followed by `AssertionError: resume must restore setup before replaying a local retry` (actual `regressed`, expected `flaky`).
findings.suggestion: Make local retry resume restore its required setup and filesystem state before running checks, while retaining the recorded first-attempt evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup creates a required build file or installs dependencies; the initial check fails transiently; the daemon restarts with a pending regression retry. Checkout cleanup removes the prerequisite, cached initial execution skips setup, and the retry fails permanently.

findings.title: Persist and restore landing execution handles
findings.detail: The landing queue supplies neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback to executeGate. Its handle is discarded, and every resumed checking entry calls start again. This leaves landing outside the requested durable executor lifecycle.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the landing handle before attachment and reload it on resume, scoped to the exact landing attempt and checked commit.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after the landing executor starts but before checks finish. The resumed queue starts another execution instead of attaching to the recorded execution.

findings.title: Forward execution events to daemon hooks
findings.detail: executeGate awaits result without consuming execution.events. Logging works only through hooks captured by its internally constructed local executor; injected executors cannot receive those per-call hooks. Command: `bun run -` with an inline fake executor emitting one check event and an onResult counter. Output: `Observed gate callbacks: 0`, followed by `AssertionError: executor check events must reach the daemon gate hooks` (`0 !== 1`).
findings.suggestion: Consume execution.events through the shared execution path and forward check/status events to the appropriate daemon hooks without duplicating default local events.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits check events and returns a GateRun. The stage uses its result, but gate progress events disappear and landing logs contain no check output.

findings.title: Resumed local retries skip setup after worktree cleanup
findings.detail: On restart, the gates stage calls checkoutCommitted(), which removes generated files and dependencies. This early return then skips the completed initial execution, including its setup. The pending regression retry contains setup: [], so local attach replays checks without their prerequisites. Prepare baseline retries have the same problem when discardChanges removes setup output. Previously, restarting the stage reran setup and checks together.
findings.suggestion: Reconstruct the required setup and scratch environment before replaying a local retry, while retaining its original failure and retry budget. Add a restart test whose checks depend on setup-generated files.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup installs node_modules; an initial check fails transiently; the daemon restarts after saving the initial result or retry handle. checkoutCommitted deletes node_modules, the saved initial result skips installation, and the retry fails because dependencies are missing instead of passing.

findings.title: Landing executions never persist or resume their handles
findings.detail: The landing caller supplies neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback. executeGate therefore uses its no-op persistence default and attaches without recording the execution anywhere. Restarting a checking land entry calls start again. This leaves one required daemon gate path outside the durable executor contract.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle before attachment, reload it when resuming checking, and clear it after consuming the result. Preserve local replay behavior for legacy entries.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor starts landing checks and returns a handle. The daemon restarts before the result arrives. The resumed queue loses that handle and starts a second execution instead of attaching to the first.

findings.title: The shared execution path discards executor events
findings.detail: executeGate awaits result without consuming events. GateHooks reach only the internally constructed local executor; injected executors receive no hooks. Consequently their check events never reach pipeline gate events or landing logs. Confirmed with command: bun -e 'import {executeGate} from "./src/gates/executor.ts"; let seen=false; const e={kind:"lan",start:async()=>({kind:"lan",id:"1",startedAt:0}),attach:()=>({events:{async *[Symbol.asyncIterator](){seen=true;}},result:Promise.resolve({setupOk:true,setup:[],checks:[]}),cancel:async()=>{}})}; await executeGate({},new AbortController().signal,{},e); if(!seen) throw Error("execution.events was never consumed");' Output: error: execution.events was never consumed (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Consume execution.events alongside the result and forward events through the shared reporting path, avoiding duplicate reporting by the local executor.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits a check result through Execution.events and resolves its GateRun. The stage receives the verdict, but its gate event and landing command output are absent.

structured.summary: Traced persistence, retries, restart cleanup, landing and events. Found three defects. Targeted tests could not run assertions because installed dependencies lack Zod .overwrite() and the MCP SDK module. An isolated executor probe confirmed dropped events. No files modified.

findings.title: Resumed local retries skip setup after worktree cleanup
findings.detail: On restart, the gates stage calls checkoutCommitted(), which removes generated files and dependencies. This early return then skips the completed initial execution, including its setup. The pending regression retry contains setup: [], so local attach replays checks without their prerequisites. Prepare baseline retries have the same problem when discardChanges removes setup output. Previously, restarting the stage reran setup and checks together.
findings.suggestion: Reconstruct the required setup and scratch environment before replaying a local retry, while retaining its original failure and retry budget. Add a restart test whose checks depend on setup-generated files.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup installs node_modules; an initial check fails transiently; the daemon restarts after saving the initial result or retry handle. checkoutCommitted deletes node_modules, the saved initial result skips installation, and the retry fails because dependencies are missing instead of passing.

findings.title: Landing executions never persist or resume their handles
findings.detail: The landing caller supplies neither a stored handle nor a persistence callback. executeGate therefore uses its no-op persistence default and attaches without recording the execution anywhere. Restarting a checking land entry calls start again. This leaves one required daemon gate path outside the durable executor contract.
findings.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle before attachment, reload it when resuming checking, and clear it after consuming the result. Preserve local replay behavior for legacy entries.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor starts landing checks and returns a handle. The daemon restarts before the result arrives. The resumed queue loses that handle and starts a second execution instead of attaching to the first.

findings.title: The shared execution path discards executor events
findings.detail: executeGate awaits result without consuming events. GateHooks reach only the internally constructed local executor; injected executors receive no hooks. Consequently their check events never reach pipeline gate events or landing logs. Confirmed with command: bun -e 'import {executeGate} from "./src/gates/executor.ts"; let seen=false; const e={kind:"lan",start:async()=>({kind:"lan",id:"1",startedAt:0}),attach:()=>({events:{async *[Symbol.asyncIterator](){seen=true;}},result:Promise.resolve({setupOk:true,setup:[],checks:[]}),cancel:async()=>{}})}; await executeGate({},new AbortController().signal,{},e); if(!seen) throw Error("execution.events was never consumed");' Output: error: execution.events was never consumed (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Consume execution.events alongside the result and forward events through the shared reporting path, avoiding duplicate reporting by the local executor.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor emits a check result through Execution.events and resolves its GateRun. The stage receives the verdict, but its gate event and landing command output are absent.

output.summary:
Reviewed the diff and traced gate/editor policy construction. A targeted policy probe confirmed Cargo credentials remain allowed. Targeted tests were limited by sandbox read restrictions, unavailable nested Seatbelt, and missing/incompatible dependencies; these environment failures are not findings.

Checked policy wiring, profile generation and launch probes. Two focused policy tests passed. Broader tests were limited by sandbox permissions and incompatible/missing dependencies; real Seatbelt probes could not run. Found a credential exposure in the gate allowlist.

findings.title: Exclude Cargo credentials from the gate toolchain allowance
findings.detail: Allowing the entire CARGO_HOME makes credentials and credentials.toml readable to candidate tests and install scripts. Neither file appears in the credential denies, so the later Cargo allow overrides the home deny. A temporary-home policy probe returned {"allowed":true,"credentialDenied":false}. Adding either file to sandbox.deny_read instead prevents every gate from launching because the overlap check rejects its parent Cargo allowance. This leaves a standard credential store exposed despite the requested gate boundary.
findings.suggestion: Allow only the Cargo toolchain subdirectories gates need, keeping credentials and credentials.toml outside those allowances. Cover both the default and custom CARGO_HOME with a stand-in credential read probe.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner has authenticated with cargo login, creating $CARGO_HOME/credentials.toml. A malicious dependency install script reads that absolute path during a gate and sends the registry token over the unrestricted network.

findings.title: Exclude Cargo registry credentials from the toolchain allowance
findings.detail: Allowing the entire Cargo home overrides the home deny for both ~/.cargo/credentials and ~/.cargo/credentials.toml, which contain registry authentication tokens. Neither file has a specific deny. Adding them through sandbox.deny_read instead prevents every gate from launching because the overlap check rejects the Cargo allowance. Check: `bun -e 'import {tmpdir} from "node:os"; import {homeReadPolicy,readPolicyScope} from "./src/harness/read-policy.ts"; readPolicyScope.run({home:tmpdir()},()=>{const p=homeReadPolicy([],true); console.log(JSON.stringify({cargoAllowed:p.allowRead?.some(x=>x.endsWith("/.cargo")),cargoTokenDenied:p.denyRead.some(x=>/\/\.cargo\/credentials(?:\.toml)?$/.test(x))}));});'` returned `{"cargoAllowed":true,"cargoTokenDenied":false}`.
findings.suggestion: Narrow the Cargo allowance to the toolchain and cache paths gates need, leaving registry-token files outside it. Add coverage for both credential filenames and a custom CARGO_HOME.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner has used cargo login. Malicious dependency code or candidate tests read the owner's Cargo credentials by absolute path and exfiltrate the registry token over the unrestricted network.

Reviewed executor wiring, cancellation, and restart paths. Found three durability gaps; a direct probe confirmed pending retries start new work. Targeted tests could not load because the installed Zod lacks overwrite(), used by unchanged code.

Found two durability gaps in the executor seam. An isolated resume probe failed as described below. Four targeted test files could not load because installed dependencies lack Zod .overwrite() and an MCP SDK module. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Resume pending retries instead of discarding their handles
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial, and rebase executions can reattach. After a restart during a retry, the stage begins with its initial execution, discards the stored retry handle, and starts new work. cancelGateExecution cannot cancel the previous execution after process restart because its lookup is memory-only. The new tests explicitly expect this duplicate execution, contrary to the requested restart contract.
findings.suggestion: Persist retry progress and preceding results so resume can attach to the pending retry. Keep setup replay specific to local executions.
findings.failure_scenario: A fake LAN executor starts a regression retry and the daemon restarts before its result arrives. Resume forgets that handle and starts another suite while the original retry remains running.

findings.title: Persist execution handles for landing checks
findings.detail: Landing calls executeGate without stored or persist arguments, so its handle is never saved. A restart during landing checks therefore always calls start again. This leaves one daemon gate path without the requested durable execution identity.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the landing execution handle and associate it with the entry and checked SHA, then pass it back on resume.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after the landing executor starts a suite but before checking finishes. The reclaimed landing entry starts a second execution rather than attaching to the first.

findings.title: Checkpoint the result before clearing its execution handle
findings.detail: The gate-result checkpoint removes the handle without storing the returned GateRun. The caller has not yet persisted the baseline, comparison, or completed-stage checkpoint. A crash in that interval loses both the result and the identity needed to retrieve it, causing completed executor work to start again.
findings.suggestion: Persist the result together with execution identity, or clear the handle atomically with the caller's durable result checkpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: An initial gate execution finishes, gate-result saves the cleared handle, and the daemon exits before lastGates or completedChecks is saved. Resume calls start instead of recovering the completed execution.

findings.title: Resume pending retry executions instead of replacing them
findings.detail: The purpose whitelist prevents baseline-retry, regression-retry and timeout handles from ever being reattached. On restart, the engine discards their identities and starts replacement work; cancelGateExecution cannot cancel an execution owned by the previous process. This violates the requested restart contract. Isolated command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-YblQ82/claude-501/review-executor-resume.ts`. Output: `AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly deep-equal`, actual `["start:new", "attach:new"]`, expected `["attach:pending-retry"]`.
findings.suggestion: Persist the retry phase and its prerequisite results so resume can attach to the pending retry. Preserve setup replay specifically for local executions.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after persisting a remote retry handle but before receiving its result. Resume starts another execution and leaves the original execution unobserved.

findings.title: Persist landing gate handles before attaching
findings.detail: The landing queue calls executeGate without a stored handle or persistence callback. Consequently, executeGate uses its no-op persistence default and awaits the execution without recording its identity anywhere. Landing checks therefore bypass the durability contract provided for pipeline checks.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint the landing execution handle with its entry and checked SHA, then supply that handle when resuming the same checks.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while landing checks are running. The resumed queue has no execution identity and starts another suite instead of attaching to the existing execution.

findings.title: Bound pending lines before buffering preview output
findings.detail: The new line callbacks route serve output through runProcess's lineSplitter, which accumulates the entire pending line until a newline or process exit. tailLimit and collect's slice do not bound that buffer. Previously, serve output was truncated on every chunk. A targeted probe confirmed this: `bun -e 'import { runProcess } from "./src/util/proc.ts"; let longest = 0; const result = await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e","process.stdout.write(String.fromCharCode(120).repeat(8 * 1024 * 1024))"],cwd:process.cwd(),env:{...process.env},tailLimit:4000,onStdoutLine:line=>{longest=Math.max(longest,line.length)}}); console.log(JSON.stringify({exitCode:result.exitCode,retainedTail:result.stdout.length,longestBufferedLine:longest}));'` produced `{"exitCode":0,"retainedTail":4000,"longestBufferedLine":8388608}`.
findings.suggestion: Bound pending line buffers while preserving startup-token detection, or collect preview diagnostics through a bounded chunk callback. Add coverage for sustained output without newlines.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview server keeps serving successfully while continuously writing stdout or stderr without newlines. The factory daemon retains all that output throughout verification and can exhaust memory.

findings.title: Keep server output buffering bounded before splitting lines
findings.detail: Replacing chunk collection with onStdoutLine/onStderrLine introduces unbounded buffering: runProcess's lineSplitter retains everything until a newline, independently of tailLimit. A persistent server emitting newline-free output continually grows daemon memory and repeatedly scans the growing string. Previously, each chunk was immediately capped at 4,000 characters. In a temporary probe with port allocation and readiness mocked, serve='printf server-broken >&2; exec sleep 60' also produced 'Error: Preview readiness timed out at http://127.0.0.1:32123/health: ' with the diagnostic missing.
findings.suggestion: Bound incomplete-line buffering and collect timeout diagnostics from bounded raw chunks, while preserving the confinement startup handshake.
findings.failure_scenario: A preview server writes progress using carriage returns, or continuously writes stdout/stderr without newlines. Its incomplete line remains buffered for the server's lifetime despite tailLimit: 4_000, consuming increasing daemon memory; readiness failures also omit that output.

findings.detail: The new awaited metadata lookup opens a cancellation window. cancel() records cancelled and returns true, but the continuation calls landed() unconditionally, overwriting the terminal state. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-land-cancel.ts". Output: `cancel returned: true\nstate after cancel: cancelled\nstate after lookup: landed`.
findings.suggestion: After the lookup, check the abort signal and current entry state before updating runs or finishing the entry. Preserve cancellation and shutdown semantics.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub merges successfully; the metadata lookup remains pending; a user cancels the entry; the lookup resolves or rejects. The cancelled entry becomes landed.

findings.title: Metadata backfill leaves the requested run.merged feed fields null
findings.detail: The backfill updates the run row but leaves its existing run.merged feed item unchanged. This preserves the reported agent-facing defect when metadata arrives later. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-merge-feed.ts". Output: `run metadata: {"mergedBy":"owner","mergedAt":1791892800000}` followed by `run.merged data: {"prUrl":"https://github.com/test/repo/pull/1","mergedBy":null,"mergedAt":null,"status":"succeeded"}`.
findings.suggestion: Make recovered merge metadata visible in the feed through a defined correction mechanism, and assert the feed's metadata in the late-observation test.
findings.failure_scenario: The queue confirms a merge but its metadata lookup fails or returns incomplete data. A later saved MERGED observation fills the run fields, while agents reading run.merged still receive null actor and timestamp.

findings.title: Post-merge lookup overwrites a successful cancellation
findings.detail: The new awaited metadata lookup introduces a cancellation window. cancel() aborts the worker and records cancelled, but the lookup rejection is swallowed and landed() unconditionally replaces that state. Targeted command `bun run -` with an inline fixture mocking mergePullRequest as successful and deferring the metadata client produced: `cancel returned: true state: cancelled`, then `state after metadata lookup: landed`, followed by `error: Expected cancelled, received landed`.
findings.suggestion: Recheck cancellation and entry ownership after the lookup before changing queue state, or refuse cancellation once the merge has completed.

Found three merge-recording defects with targeted reproductions. All 62 notifier tests passed. Four other affected test files could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing. Repository files were unchanged; reproduction fixtures were created under TMPDIR.

findings.title: Feed consumers never receive late merge metadata
findings.detail: The queue publishes run.merged with null metadata before fetching it. This method then edits the existing feed row without advancing its ID. Consumers that read or acknowledge that item cannot discover the correction through subsequent feed reads. Reproduction: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-merge-metadata.ts"` printed `feed {"delivered":{"prUrl":"https://github.com/test/repo/pull/1","mergedBy":null,"mergedAt":null,"status":"succeeded"},"afterCursor":[]}` despite successfully filling the stored metadata.
findings.suggestion: Make completed metadata observable through the cursor-based feed, either before publishing the merge item or through a subsequent durable update item.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent consumes run.merged while the queue's metadata request is pending, advances its cursor, and continues polling after metadata arrives.

findings.title: Missing merge metadata cannot recover with polling disabled
findings.detail: After the queue marks a run merged, reconciliation only consults saved snapshots and always skips the supplied client. With polling disabled, a failed, interrupted, or temporarily stale post-merge metadata request therefore leaves null fields permanently. Reproduction: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-merge-metadata.ts"` supplied a client returning complete merge metadata but printed `recovery {"calls":0,"mergedBy":null,"mergedAt":null}`.
findings.suggestion: Persist pending metadata enrichment and allow bounded reconciliation through the existing client when no complete saved observation exists.
findings.failure_scenario: Polling is disabled and the daemon restarts after landed is checkpointed but before metadata is saved, or the single metadata request fails.

findings.title: Landing no longer records merges for failed or cancelled runs
findings.detail: Replacing unconditional updateRun({merged:true}) with resolveMergedRun silently drops merge recording for failed and cancelled statuses. Land requests do not reject these statuses, and terminal failed/cancelled rounds pass assertNoRoundInFlight. The entry becomes landed while its run remains unmerged. Reproduction: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-merge-metadata.ts"` printed `failedRun {"recorded":false,"merged":false}` for a confirmed merge on a failed run.
findings.suggestion: Record confirmed merge fields for failed and cancelled runs while preserving their existing terminal status and evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed or cancelled run retains a delivered PR branch, and an explicit approved SHA is successfully landed through the queue.

findings.title: Confirmed lands no longer mark failed or cancelled runs as merged
findings.detail: Replacing updateRun({merged:true}) with resolveMergedRun loses merge recording for failed and cancelled runs. The queue accepts these runs, but resolveMergedRun only updates succeeded, resolved, or needs_human runs. Subsequent fillMergedRunMetadata also refuses them because merged remains false. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/merge-review.test.ts"` failed `confirmed queue merge remains recorded for failed and cancelled runs`: `Expected: true; Received: false`.
findings.suggestion: Record the confirmed merge independently of run status, preserving failed/cancelled status and terminal evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A delivered run is failed or cancelled, its current PR head is approved, and the queue successfully lands it. The land entry becomes landed while the run remains merged:false and produces no run.merged item.

findings.title: Interrupted metadata reads have no restart recovery
findings.detail: The queue durably marks the entry landed and both runs merged before fetching metadata. If shutdown interrupts that fetch, the landed entry is never resumed. With polling disabled, reconciliation skips merged runs and only checks saved snapshots, so it never invokes the available GitHub client to recover the fields. A transient metadata-fetch failure has the same permanent result. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/merge-review.test.ts"` failed `restart without polling recovers interrupted merge metadata`: `Expected: "owner"; Received: null`, after reopening the store and reconciling three times with a successful client.
findings.suggestion: Persist unfinished metadata enrichment and resume it after restart, using a bounded recovery mechanism that also works with polling disabled.
findings.failure_scenario: Polling is disabled and the daemon stops after landed() commits but before mergeMetadata completes. After restart, mergedBy and mergedAt remain null indefinitely despite GitHub having both values.

findings.title: Metadata enrichment is invisible to consumers past the merge item
findings.detail: The successful queue path initially commits run.merged with null metadata, then rewrites that feed row in place. Feed reads and publications only return IDs greater than the consumer's cursor, so a consumer that handled the initial merge item never receives the corrected fields. Targeted command `bun test "$TMPDIR/merge-review.test.ts"` failed `feed consumer learns merge metadata filled after initial merge item`: `Expected: true; Received: false`; reading after the initial cursor returned no correction.
findings.suggestion: Ensure consumers receive populated merge metadata before advancing past the merge notification, or expose enrichment through a subsequent feed item they can consume.
findings.failure_scenario: An MCP consumer reads and acknowledges run.merged while the post-merge GitHub lookup is pending. The lookup succeeds and updates the old row, but subsequent limitless_feed calls never reveal the merger or merge time.

findings.failure_scenario: An MCP consumer reads and acknowledges run.merged while the post-merge GitHub lookup is pending. The lookup succeeds and updates the old row, but subsequent limitless_feed calls never reveal the merger or merge time.

Found two remaining credential leaks using real Git patches and the extracted parser. Integration tests could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing. No repository files were modified.

Found two remaining privacy gaps. Standalone probes reproduced both. Targeted MCP tests could not start because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing from this checkout.

findings.title: Blank context lines can disable credential scanning
findings.detail: With diff.suppressBlankEmpty=true, Git emits blank context lines without a space prefix. This parser flushes and sets inHunk=false at that line, ignoring subsequent additions until another hunk header. worktreeGit does not override this setting. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-patch-probe.ts"` with a real Git patch produced `suppressBlankEmpty hidden lines: []`, `both credential lines exposed: true`, and `blank context: whole-patch matches=0; per-line matches=0`.
findings.suggestion: Pin diff.suppressBlankEmpty=false when obtaining patches, or correctly parse unprefixed blank context lines. Add a regression with this Git configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable diff.suppressBlankEmpty=true and replace an ordinary line immediately after a blank context line with the two lines of a registered credential. Both credential lines remain visible in the returned patch.

findings.title: Truncated hunk annotations still expose credential text
findings.detail: The annotation scan searches for complete credential lines, but Git truncates function annotations to approximately 80 bytes. A longer credential line therefore survives this scan and the ordinary privacy filters. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-patch-probe.ts"` produced an annotation beginning `@@ -7,7 +7,7 @@ sensitive-alpha-...`, followed by `hidden lines: []`, `leaks annotation fragment: true`, and `annotation: whole-patch matches=0; per-line matches=0`.
findings.suggestion: Remove hunk function annotations from exposed patches, or redact annotations using matching rules that account for Git's truncation and whitespace handling. Test a credential line longer than the annotation limit.
findings.failure_scenario: Register a credential whose first line is `sensitive-alpha-` plus 180 characters and whose second line is numeric. Change a numeric line several lines below it. Git includes the truncated first credential line as the hunk annotation, exposing roughly 80 characters.

findings.title: Truncated hunk annotations still expose credential text
findings.detail: The annotation scan matches complete credential lines, but Git truncates function annotations to 80 bytes. A longer credential line therefore survives this scan and the final whole-patch privacy check. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-multiline.ts"` against a real Git-generated patch returned `hidden: []`, `literalPrivacyMatches: 0`, and `FAIL: truncated credential line survives in hunk annotation`.
findings.suggestion: Suppress hunk annotations or account for Git's truncation and trimming when checking them. Add a regression using a credential line longer than 80 bytes.
findings.failure_scenario: Register a two-line credential whose lines exceed 80 bytes. Keep it unchanged near the top of a file, then modify a later line outside its context range. Git quotes a truncated credential line after `@@`; getChange returns that fragment.

findings.title: Other diff renderers remain vulnerable without the requested follow-up
findings.detail: The request requires other diff-rendering outputs to receive equivalent protection or be listed as follow-ups. Review prompts still embed reviewDiff.patch and firstParentPatch without reconstructed-side filtering, and this change provides no follow-up listing. Ordinary credential redaction preserves both prefixed lines: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-diff-output.ts"` printed `+alpha-review-secret` and `+beta-review-secret`, then `FAIL: ordinary patch-output redaction preserves both credential lines`.
findings.suggestion: Reuse patch-aware filtering before embedding review patches, or explicitly document these review-prompt paths as follow-ups as permitted by the request.
findings.failure_scenario: A verify-change review embeds a patch containing an added multiline registered credential. The two added lines reach the model because their '+' prefixes prevent literal credential matching.

output.summary:
Reviewed setup execution, prompts, caching, grading and production validation. Found an order-dependent routing-policy regression. Targeted tests could not load because installed dependencies lack the required Zod API and MCP SDK; a focused policy probe reproduced the finding using the installed Zod v4 export. No files were modified.

Reviewed setup confinement, base pinning, prompts, caching, and policy consumers. A focused probe reproduced a policy-selection regression. Targeted tests could not load because installed Zod lacks overwrite and the MCP SDK is missing.

findings.title: Handle both setup variants when selecting routing evidence
findings.detail: Adding setup permits two standard single systems for the same target and implementerReport setting. Both pass policy.ts's evidence filter, but generatePolicy calls summarize(...)[0], silently choosing whichever system appears first in the trial rows. Thus trial ordering determines which arm supplies production routing metrics. A focused command using test/evals-policy-support.ts, generatePolicy, and mock.module("zod",()=>require("zod/v4")) created otherwise identical setup/non-setup arms with pass rates 1 and 0. Generating policy with the original and reversed trial arrays produced respectively [["false",0]] and [["true",1]].
findings.suggestion: Define which setup variant supplies routing evidence and apply that rule consistently in selectEvidence and generatePolicy, or reject ambiguous evidence explicitly. Add a regression test with both variants for one target and reversed trial ordering.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed eval contains standard single systems with and without setup for the same model. Their outcomes differ. Policy generation silently uses only the first arm, and reversing trial order changes the selected metrics.

findings.title: Keep setup variants separate when selecting policy evidence
findings.detail: Allowing setup variants introduces two valid standard/include systems for the same target, but selectEvidence in src/evals/policy.ts pools both systems' trials. generatePolicy then passes those pooled rows to completeCases, which rejects every case containing 2*k trials instead of k, leaving the target without complete paired evidence. Its summary also depends on which system appears first. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-setup-policy-probe.ts". With one completed case in each arm and schema initialization stubbed, output was {"selectedModels":1,"systems":["control","prepared"],"completeCases":0}, followed by AssertionError: 0 !== 1.
findings.suggestion: Update policy evidence selection to choose one setup configuration per target consistently, and test a run containing both standard setup variants.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed review eval contains standard/include systems for candidate-a both with and without setup, each completing the same cases. Policy generation pools the arms and reports no complete paired cases despite all trials completing.

Reviewed retry execution, configuration trust, classification and JUnit parsing. All 32 retry-file tests passed. Executor and feedback tests could not load because of missing or incompatible dependencies. A real Bun probe confirmed the file-selection defect below.

findings.title: Preserve process isolation in targeted retries
findings.detail: The full check uses Bun's --parallel mode, which isolates files in separate processes, but the targeted command runs files together in one process. This can introduce shared-global or module-cache failures that the full check does not have. Confirmed with two temporary test files that each assert a global is undefined and then set it: `bun test --parallel=2 a.test.ts b.test.ts` exited 0 with `2 pass, 0 fail`; `bun test a.test.ts b.test.ts` exited 1 with `1 pass, 1 fail` and `expect(received).toBeUndefined() / Received: true`. retryFailures treats this newly introduced failure as confirmation and skips the full rerun.
findings.suggestion: Include --parallel with the repository's worker setting in retry_files so targeted confirmation retains the full check's process isolation.
findings.failure_scenario: Two files fail transiently during the initial parallel check. Their next parallel run would pass, but they share globals or cached modules when run in one process. The targeted retry creates an additional failure and incorrectly confirms a regression without running the full check.

findings.title: Pass explicit file paths instead of Bun substring filters
findings.detail: Ordinary filenames are quoted but lack a leading './'. Bun interprets these arguments as substring filters, so the retry can execute additional files. In a temporary fixture, `bun test test/a.test.ts --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=report.xml` ran both `test/a.test.ts` and `nested/test/a.test.ts`, reporting `1 pass`, `1 fail`, and exit code 1. Using `./test/a.test.ts` reported `1 pass`, `0 fail`, and exit code 0. Extra files invalidate the slot-bypass size and duration calculation, and their failures can incorrectly confirm a regression without a full retry.
findings.suggestion: Prefix every selected relative path with './' before shell quoting, and add a regression test with overlapping file paths.
findings.failure_scenario: The report lists only test/a.test.ts with a short duration, while the repository also contains nested/test/a.test.ts. The targeted retry runs both files outside the gate slot despite calculating its bound from only the first file.

findings.detail: Ordinary filenames are quoted but lack a leading './'. Bun interprets these arguments as substring filters, so the retry can execute additional files. In a temporary fixture, `bun test test/a.test.ts --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=report.xml` ran both `test/a.test.ts` and `nested/test/a.test.ts`, reporting `1 pass`, `1 fail`, and exit code 1. Using `./test/a.test.ts` reported `1 pass`, `0 fail`, and exit code 0. Extra files invalidate the slot-bypass size and duration calculation, and their failures can incorrectly confirm a regression without a full retry.
findings.suggestion: Prefix every selected relative path with './' before shell quoting, and add a regression test with overlapping file paths.
findings.failure_scenario: The report lists only test/a.test.ts with a short duration, while the repository also contains nested/test/a.test.ts. The targeted retry runs both files outside the gate slot despite calculating its bound from only the first file.

Found two retry correctness defects with real Bun probes. All 32 JUnit/slot tests passed; gate-feedback and gate-executor tests could not load because installed dependencies lack required Zod and MCP SDK APIs.

findings.title: Prefix retry filenames with ./ so Bun selects exact files
findings.detail: Root-level filenames are passed as bare Bun filters. Bun interprets these as substring matches, so the targeted retry can execute unrelated files and incorrectly confirm a regression. A temporary-fixture reproduction through retryRegressions generated `bun test 'a.test.ts'`, which printed `1 pass`, `1 fail`, and `Ran 2 tests across 2 files`, producing `regressed blocking: true`. The configured full command, `bun test ./a.test.ts`, exited 0. The extra files also invalidate the file-count and duration bounds used to bypass the gate slot.
findings.suggestion: Prefix every relative retry path with ./ before shell quoting, and add a regression test with root-level and nested files sharing a basename.
findings.failure_scenario: The configured check runs only ./a.test.ts. Its initial intermittent failure reports a.test.ts, which passes on retry, but nested/a.test.ts has an unrelated persistent failure. The generated targeted command runs both files and blocks the change without running the successful full check.

findings.title: Preserve process isolation in targeted retries
findings.detail: The full check uses --parallel, which isolates test files in separate processes, but the targeted command omits it. With two files that assert an environment variable is unset and then set it, `bun test --parallel=2 a.test.ts b.test.ts` produced `2 pass, 0 fail`; `bun test a.test.ts b.test.ts` produced `1 pass, 1 fail` with `Expected: undefined, Received: "set"`. A targeted failure therefore need not reproduce the original failure, yet retryFailures immediately treats it as confirmation.
findings.suggestion: Keep --parallel and the repository's worker setting in the targeted retry command.
findings.failure_scenario: Two files fail transiently in the isolated full suite. Their targeted rerun shares process state and fails deterministically from cross-file interference. The factory confirms a regression without the full rerun; on baseline this can incorrectly establish a failing baseline.

findings.title: Pass explicit file paths rather than Bun substring filters
findings.detail: Only names beginning with '-' receive a './' prefix. Bun interprets other relative arguments as substring filters. In a temporary fixture containing test/a.test.ts and other/test/a.test.ts, `bun test test/a.test.ts` reported `Ran 2 tests across 2 files`; `bun test ./test/a.test.ts` reported `Ran 1 test across 1 file`. The retry can execute files outside the parsed failure list, invalidating both failure confirmation and the count/duration calculation used to bypass the gate slot.
findings.suggestion: Normalize the selected files to explicit './' paths before shell quoting and substitution.
findings.failure_scenario: The report lists one short failing file, test/a.test.ts, while additional files have paths containing that suffix. The supposedly bounded unslotted retry runs all matching files, potentially including long suites or failures unrelated to the original failing file.

output.summary:
Reviewed the diff and surrounding code, treating this as the explicitly permitted listener/pairing/heartbeat split. Found three defects. Local probes confirmed credential-policy and certificate-recovery failures. Targeted tests were blocked by missing/incompatible dependencies; the loopback reproduction was blocked by the sandbox's listener restriction. No repository files were modified.

Reviewed the permitted pairing/heartbeat first slice. Found pairing interception, incomplete credential confinement, and TLS restart recovery defects. Small probes confirmed the protocol and policy failures. Targeted tests could not start because dependencies were missing/incompatible; sandbox restrictions prevented loopback listener checks.

findings.title: Pairing code comparison does not prevent coordinator impersonation
findings.detail: The first request accepts any TLS certificate, and the worker subsequently pins that certificate. The comparison code is random coordinator-provided data, rather than a value bound to the TLS identities. An intermediary can relay the genuine pairing response and claim requests unchanged: both screens show the same code, but the intermediary obtains the issued token and the worker saves the intermediary's fingerprint. The submitted worker certificate fingerprint is never used to prove possession or protect token delivery. A loopback reproduction could not run because the sandbox refused the listener bind.
findings.suggestion: Authenticate the initial coordinator fingerprint out of band, or use a pairing protocol whose compared code cryptographically binds the participants and protects token issuance against a relay.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the initial pairing connection, terminates TLS, and forwards pairing traffic to the real coordinator. The owner compares identical codes and approves; the attacker captures a valid worker token.

findings.title: Persisted worker credentials lack protection in other daemon processes
findings.detail: Credential protection exists only in the current process's reference-counted private-path registry. Pairing releases those registrations while leaving the files on disk, and a separately running factory never registers the worker token or fingerprint. The built-in editor deny list does not cover the data directory. Similarly, restarting with the worker listener disabled leaves its persisted TLS key unregistered. Mode 0600 does not stop agents running as the same user. Probe command: bun -e 'import{mkdtempSync,rmSync}from"node:fs";import{tmpdir}from"node:os";import{privateFile}from"./src/workers/tls.ts";import{homeReadPolicy,readPolicyScope}from"./src/harness/read-policy.ts";const h=mkdtempSync(tmpdir()+"/deny-review-"),p=h+"/token";try{privateFile(p,"test-token").release();console.log("persisted token denied:",readPolicyScope.run({home:h,environment:{}},()=>homeReadPolicy([])).denyRead.includes(p))}finally{rmSync(h,{recursive:true,force:true})}'. Output: persisted token denied: false.
findings.suggestion: Register persistent worker secret paths whenever factory read policy is initialized, independently of whether pairing, the worker loop, or the listener runs in that process.
findings.failure_scenario: Pair a machine that also runs a factory daemon, then let an editor read its data-directory worker token. That daemon's sandbox policy contains no deny for the file, allowing worker impersonation.

findings.title: Failed certificate initialization permanently blocks subsequent starts
findings.detail: Initialization publishes an empty key.pem before running openssl. If generation fails or the process stops before cert.pem is written, every subsequent attempt throws 'Incomplete worker TLS material', even after the original failure is resolved. Probe command: bun -e 'import{mkdtempSync,mkdirSync,writeFileSync,chmodSync,rmSync}from"node:fs";import{tmpdir}from"node:os";import{certificate}from"./src/workers/tls.ts";const d=mkdtempSync(tmpdir()+"/cert-review-"),p=process.env.PATH;mkdirSync(d+"/bin");writeFileSync(d+"/bin/openssl","#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n");chmodSync(d+"/bin/openssl",448);try{process.env.PATH=d+"/bin";try{await certificate(d+"/tls")}catch{}process.env.PATH=p;try{await certificate(d+"/tls")}catch(e){console.log(e.message)}}finally{process.env.PATH=p;rmSync(d,{recursive:true,force:true})}'. Output: Incomplete worker TLS material.
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate TLS material in a private staging location, publish it only when complete, and provide recovery for interrupted initial generation without replacing an established identity.
findings.failure_scenario: The first listener startup encounters a temporary openssl failure or is interrupted during generation. Subsequent daemon starts fail until someone manually removes the partial TLS files.

findings.title: Pairing codes do not authenticate the TLS endpoints
findings.detail: The first request accepts any certificate, then pins that certificate without binding it to the owner-approved code. An interceptor can terminate TLS and relay pairing and claims to the real coordinator. Both screens show the same code, but the interceptor receives the secret and issued token. The supplied worker fingerprint is never used to prove possession. A mocked transport relay confirmed: `relay obtained approved worker token: true` and `worker pinned relay certificate: true`.
findings.suggestion: Bind approval to authenticated endpoint identities, using a fingerprint comparison or a pairing protocol that prevents a relay from obtaining the issued token.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's initial pairing connection and forwards application requests to the coordinator. The owner approves the matching code; the attacker obtains an authenticated worker token.

findings.title: Persisted worker credentials lose sandbox protection
findings.detail: Protection depends on process-local registrations. Disabling the listener skips registration of its existing TLS key, and a daemon never registers the token written by a separate worker CLI process. These paths are absent from the built-in credential deny list. An editor-policy probe returned false for both `persisted TLS key denied in editor policy` and `paired worker token denied in daemon editor policy`. Mode 0600 does not isolate agents running as the same user.
findings.suggestion: Register persistent worker credential paths in every factory process before starting agents, independently of listener enablement or whether that process created the files.
findings.failure_scenario: Pair a worker on a machine that also runs the daemon, or restart a coordinator with its worker listener disabled. A tool-enabled editor can read the persisted worker token or TLS key.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation prevents subsequent startup
findings.detail: Certificate creation publishes an empty final key file before invoking OpenSSL. A crash or command failure before the certificate is written leaves only that key. Every later attempt throws `Incomplete worker TLS material`, preventing coordinator startup while the listener is enabled. A temporary-directory probe reproduced that result.
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate material in temporary files and provide recovery for interrupted initial publication without replacing an established identity.
findings.failure_scenario: The process exits after creating key.pem but before OpenSSL writes cert.pem. Restarting the daemon repeatedly fails until someone manually removes the partial material.

Output: Incomplete worker TLS material.

output.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding code, treating this as the explicitly permitted listener/pairing/heartbeat split. Found three defects. Targeted tests were blocked by missing/incompatible dependencies; the loopback reproduction was blocked by the sandbox's listener restriction. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Pairing code comparison does not prevent coordinator impersonation
findings.detail: The first request accepts any TLS certificate, and the worker subsequently pins that certificate. The comparison code is random coordinator-provided data, rather than a value bound to the TLS identities. An intermediary can relay the genuine pairing response and claim requests unchanged: both screens show the same code, but the intermediary obtains the issued token and the worker saves the intermediary's fingerprint. The submitted worker certificate fingerprint is never used to prove possession or protect token delivery. A loopback reproduction could not run because the sandbox refused the listener bind.
findings.suggestion: Authenticate the initial coordinator fingerprint out of band, or use a pairing protocol whose compared code cryptographically binds the participants and protects token issuance against a relay.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the initial pairing connection, terminates TLS, and forwards pairing traffic to the real coordinator. The owner compares identical codes and approves; the attacker captures a valid worker token.

findings.title: Persisted worker credentials lack protection in other daemon processes

Mode 0600 does not stop agents running as the same user. Reviewed the permitted pairing/heartbeat slice and reproduced two TLS startup defects. Pairing also permits token theft by an active relay. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies were missing or incompatible; the loopback relay probe was blocked by sandbox port restrictions.

Reviewed the diff and surrounding confinement code, treating the documented pairing/heartbeat split as authorized. Found three defects. Focused state probes confirmed credential protection loss and persistent certificate initialization failure. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies were missing/incompatible; the sandbox also refused loopback listening. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Pairing code comparison does not prevent token theft by a relay
findings.detail: The initial TLS connection accepts any certificate. A relay can forward the pairing request to the real coordinator and return its code unchanged, so the owner's code comparison succeeds. The relay receives the pairing secret and can claim the approved token. Subsequent pinning authenticates the relay's certificate. The supplied worker certificate fingerprint is stored but never requires proof of private-key possession.
findings.suggestion: Bind pairing approval to an authenticated cryptographic exchange, or require out-of-band verification of the coordinator fingerprint before transmitting the pairing secret.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the first pairing connection, terminates TLS, and proxies the pairing and claim requests. After the owner approves the matching code, the attacker obtains a valid worker token.

findings.title: Generated EC key prevents worker listener startup on macOS
findings.detail: With macOS /usr/bin/openssl (LibreSSL 3.3.6), the generated TLS material is rejected by Bun. A temporary fixture invoking startWorkerListener with a fresh home, run with `bun "$TMPDIR/worker-tls-startup-probe.ts"`, exited 1 with `ERR_OSSL_EC_DECODE_ERROR: error:0f000080:elliptic curve routines:OPENSSL_internal:DECODE_ERROR`. This occurs during TLS decoding, before socket binding.
findings.suggestion: Generate key material in a format supported by Bun with the system OpenSSL on macOS, and exercise listener startup using that generated material.
findings.failure_scenario: On the tested macOS host with Bun 1.4.3 and system LibreSSL, enabling workers.listen in a fresh data directory makes daemon startup fail.

findings.title: Failed certificate generation permanently blocks subsequent startup
findings.detail: Generation creates key.pem before invoking OpenSSL, but failure leaves that file behind. The next attempt rejects the partial files instead of recovering. A temporary probe ran certificate with OpenSSL unavailable, restored PATH, and retried. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/worker-tls-retry-probe.ts"`. Output: `first generation: failed` followed by `retry: Incomplete worker TLS material`.
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate new TLS material in temporary files, then publish it with a recoverable initialization scheme. Clean up failed unpublished generation without replacing established certificates.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenSSL fails, times out, or the process stops after key.pem is created but before cert.pem is written. Every later daemon start or pairing attempt fails until the owner manually removes the partial material.

findings.title: Pairing permits a relay attacker to obtain the approved token
findings.detail: The initial request accepts any TLS certificate, then trusts the code and fingerprint returned over that connection. An intermediary can forward pairing and claim requests to the real coordinator, preserving the code that the owner compares, while reading the pairing secret and issued token. The submitted worker fingerprint is stored but never requires proof of possession. A focused store probe confirmed that possession of the forwarded secret alone obtains a valid token.
findings.suggestion: Bind approval to the actual TLS endpoints using a locally derived verification code, or authenticate the coordinator fingerprint through an independent channel before sending pairing requests. Require proof of possession if the worker certificate is intended to authenticate its identity.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the first pairing connection, presents its own certificate, and relays requests to the coordinator. The owner sees matching codes and approves; the attacker receives a valid worker token and the worker pins the attacker's certificate.

findings.title: Persisted worker secrets are not denied in other agent processes
findings.detail: Private-file protection is a process-local registration that pairing releases before exiting. A daemon running on the same machine never registers the worker token or worker key, and a disabled worker listener likewise leaves its persisted coordinator key unregistered. These paths are absent from the built-in credential deny list, so editor sandboxes can read them. The focused probe printed `PERSISTED TOKEN: editor policy denies token or ancestor: false`. Mode 0600 does not protect files from agents running as the same user.
findings.suggestion: Register persisted worker credential paths in the shared sandbox policy before agents start, independently of whether this process runs pairing, a worker loop, or the listener. Include configured data directories and canonical paths.
findings.failure_scenario: Pair a worker, let the pairing command exit, then start an editor through a daemon using the same data directory. Its sandbox permits reading the persisted worker token and impersonating that worker.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation permanently prevents startup
findings.detail: Initialization publishes an empty final key file before awaiting OpenSSL. If generation fails or the process stops before the certificate is written, subsequent starts reject the leftover material instead of recovering. With workers enabled, this exception also prevents the owner daemon from starting. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-workers-state-probe.ts"` against an empty key file produced `CERTIFICATE RESTART 1: Incomplete worker TLS material` and the same error on restart 2.
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate TLS material in a temporary location, then publish it with a recoverable initialization protocol. Distinguish incomplete first-time generation from previously established identity material.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after creating key.pem but before OpenSSL creates cert.pem. Every later daemon start fails until someone manually removes or repairs the files.

structured.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding confinement code, treating the documented pairing/heartbeat split as authorized. Found three defects. Focused state probes confirmed credential protection loss and persistent certificate initialization failure. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies were missing/incompatible; the sandbox also refused loopback listening. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Pairing permits a relay attacker to obtain the approved token
findings.detail: The initial request accepts any TLS certificate, then trusts the code and fingerprint returned over that connection. An intermediary can forward pairing and claim requests to the real coordinator, preserving the code that the owner compares, while reading the pairing secret and issued token. The submitted worker fingerprint is stored but never requires proof of possession. A focused store probe confirmed that possession of the forwarded secret alone obtains a valid token.
findings.suggestion: Bind approval to the actual TLS endpoints using a locally derived verification code, or authenticate the coordinator fingerprint through an independent channel before sending pairing requests. Require proof of possession if the worker certificate is intended to authenticate its identity.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the first pairing connection, presents its own certificate, and relays requests to the coordinator. The owner sees matching codes and approves; the attacker receives a valid worker token and the worker pins the attacker's certificate.

findings.title: Persisted worker secrets are not denied in other agent processes
findings.detail: Private-file protection is a process-local registration that pairing releases before exiting. A daemon running on the same machine never registers the worker token or worker key, and a disabled worker listener likewise leaves its persisted coordinator key unregistered. These paths are absent from the built-in credential deny list, so editor sandboxes can read them. The focused probe printed `PERSISTED TOKEN: editor policy denies token or ancestor: false`. Mode 0600 does not protect files from agents running as the same user.

findings.failure_scenario: Pair a worker, let the pairing command exit, then start an editor through a daemon using the same data directory. Its sandbox permits reading the persisted worker token and impersonating that worker.

findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation permanently prevents startup
findings.detail: Initialization publishes an empty final key file before awaiting OpenSSL. If generation fails or the process stops before the certificate is written, subsequent starts reject the leftover material instead of recovering. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-workers-state-probe.ts"` against an empty key file produced `CERTIFICATE RESTART 1: Incomplete worker TLS material` and the same error on restart 2.
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate TLS material in a temporary location, then publish it with a recoverable initialization protocol. Distinguish incomplete first-time generation from previously established identity material.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after creating key.pem but before OpenSSL creates cert.pem. Every later daemon start fails until someone manually removes or repairs the files.

findings.title: Failed certificate generation permanently blocks subsequent startup
findings.detail:
The final key path is created before OpenSSL runs, but failure only releases its read protection. An OpenSSL failure or interruption leaves an empty key without a certificate; subsequent calls always throw "Incomplete worker TLS material". On the coordinator this prevents the entire daemon from starting, including its owner API. Reproduced with command: bun -e 'import {certificate} from "./src/workers/tls.ts"; import {mkdtempSync,writeFileSync,rmSync} from "node:fs"; import {tmpdir} from "node:os"; const h=mkdtempSync(`${tmpdir()}/cert-review-`), p=process.env.PATH; try {writeFileSync(`${h}/openssl`,"#!/bin/sh
exit 1
",{mode:448});process.env.PATH=h;await certificate(h).catch(()=>console.log("generation failed"));process.env.PATH=p;await certificate(h).then(c=>{c.release();console.log("retry succeeded")}).catch(e=>console.log(e.message));}finally{process.env.PATH=p;rmSync(h,{recursive:true,force:true})}'. Output: "generation failed
Incomplete worker TLS material".
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate TLS material in temporary paths, publish it only when complete, and provide recovery for interrupted initial generation without replacing an established certificate.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable workers.listen, then have OpenSSL fail or terminate during the first certificate generation. Restore OpenSSL and restart: the retained partial material prevents all subsequent daemon starts until manually removed.

findings.title: Failed certificate generation permanently blocks subsequent startup
findings.detail: The function publishes an empty key.pem before invoking openssl, but its catch block leaves that file behind. After a transient generation failure, subsequent calls fail with "Incomplete worker TLS material" without retrying generation. Because startDaemon awaits the worker listener, this also prevents the configured coordinator daemon from starting. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {spyOn} from "bun:test"; import {mkdtempSync,rmSync} from "node:fs"; import {tmpdir} from "node:os"; import {join} from "node:path"; import * as proc from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {certificate} from "./src/workers/tls.ts"; const dir=mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),"cert-review-")); const spy=spyOn(proc,"sh").mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error("transient openssl failure")); try {await certificate(dir).catch(e=>console.log(e.message)); spy.mockRestore(); await certificate(dir).then(c=>c.release()).catch(e=>console.log(e.message));} finally {spy.mockRestore();rmSync(dir,{recursive:true,force:true});}' Output: "transient openssl failure\nIncomplete worker TLS material".

Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {certificate} from "./src/workers/tls.ts"; import {mkdtempSync,writeFileSync,rmSync} from "node:fs"; import {tmpdir} from "node:os"; import {join} from "node:path"; const dir=mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),"review-workers-")); try {writeFileSync(join(dir,"key.pem"), "", {mode:0o600}); for(let i=0;i<2;i++){try {await certificate(dir)} catch(e){console.log(`attempt ${i+1}: ${e.message}`)}}} finally {rmSync(dir,{recursive:true,force:true})}' Output: "attempt 1: Incomplete worker TLS material" and "attempt 2: Incomplete worker TLS material".
findings.suggestion: Generate and validate TLS material in temporary files, then publish it with a recoverable initialization protocol. Recover interrupted initialization without replacing an established certificate.
findings.failure_scenario: On the first start with workers.listen enabled, OpenSSL fails or the daemon is interrupted after key.pem is created but before cert.pem is written. Restarting the daemon repeatedly fails.

findings.title: Heartbeat data bypasses redaction before persistence
findings.detail: Heartbeat strings are stored verbatim, although they are untrusted and can contain registered credentials. Sanitizing list() later does not remove plaintext secrets from SQLite. A valid heartbeat with osVersion equal to the authenticated worker token persists that token, contradicting the hash-only token storage requirement. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {Database} from "bun:sqlite"; import {WorkerStore} from "./src/db/workers.ts"; const db=new Database(":memory:"); db.exec(await Bun.file("src/db/migrations/20261015T145911-workers.sql").text()); const w=new WorkerStore({db},"sha"); w.pairingKey="test-key"; const p=w.pair("runner","a".repeat(64),"b".repeat(64)); w.approve(p.code); const {token}=w.claim(p.secret); const worker=w.authenticate(token); w.heartbeat(worker,{releaseSha:"sha",bunVersion:Bun.version,os:"darwin",osVersion:token,cpuCount:1,ramBytes:1,freeSlots:1,onAC:true,idleSeconds:0,jobs:[]}); console.log("plaintext token persisted:", w.worker("runner").capabilities.includes(token)); db.close();' Output: "plaintext token persisted: true".
findings.suggestion: Redact credential-bearing worker metadata before writing it to SQLite. Reject metadata whose sanitization would invalidate fields needed for matching or availability.
findings.failure_scenario: An approved worker submits its bearer token, or another registered credential, in a schema-valid heartbeat string. The coordinator retains the plaintext credential in workers.capabilities and database backups.
