Found two reproducible defects in result ordering and worker cleanup. Temporary targeted probes failed for both. The existing worker and executor suites could not load because of a missing MCP dependency and an incompatible Zod API. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Reject final results that contradict streamed failures
findings.detail: Final results are validated independently of stored check events. A worker can stream a failing check, then submit the same check as passing; both requests receive HTTP 200 and the passing result becomes authoritative. This violates the requirement that failing checks never become passes. Targeted command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-results.ts". Output included: events 200 {"ok":true}; result 200 {"ok":true}; Stored check after streamed failure: true. The probe exercised the actual request handler with transport and output privacy isolated.
findings.suggestion: Validate the final GateRun against check events from the current lease attempt. Treat contradictory outcomes as an infrastructure failure, retaining the original evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: An authenticated worker posts a requested check with ok=false and exitCode=1, then posts a structurally valid final result for the requested SHA with that check changed to ok=true and exitCode=0. The coordinator records a passing job.

findings.title: Preserve requested check order before accepting results
findings.detail: validRun accepts any permutation of the requested checks, but retryFailures associates returned checks with originals by array index. An accepted reordered LAN result therefore assigns outcomes to the wrong checks. Targeted command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-results.ts". Output: Reordered retry accepted: true; Retry attribution: [{"name":"x","resultName":"y","blocking":false},{"name":"y","resultName":"x","blocking":true}]. Check x actually failed its retry but was marked nonblocking using y's passing result.
findings.suggestion: Require results to match requested check order, or normalize validated results into that order before storing and returning them.
findings.failure_scenario: Checks x and y both regress. Their LAN retry returns valid results in order [y passing, x failing]. Validation accepts them, and retryRegressions marks x flaky and y regressed using the opposite checks' evidence.

findings.title: Preserve requested check order when accepting results
findings.detail: validRun accepts any permutation of the requested checks, but retryFailures pairs returned checks with original failures by array index. An accepted reversed response therefore attaches results and firstAttempt evidence to the wrong checks; regression retries can mark the wrong check flaky. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/worker-review.test.ts". The targeted assertion expected [["a","a"],["b","b"]] for [result name, firstAttempt name], but received [["b","a"],["a","b"]].
findings.suggestion: Require results in requested order, or normalize validated results into that order before completion and downstream retry processing.
findings.failure_scenario: Checks a and b both fail initially. A LAN retry returns valid results ordered b then a. Validation accepts them, and positional retry processing associates b's result with a's original failure and vice versa.

findings.title: Prevent gate-created directory permissions from terminating the worker
findings.detail: A gate can leave an unreadable directory inside its writable checkout. git worktree remove then fails, its error is swallowed, and rmSync throws from finally. That rejects the job task, whose rejection handler aborts the entire worker and its other jobs. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/worker-review.test.ts". A real Git worktree containing blocked/nested with blocked chmod 000 reproduced the cleanup failure: "ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty".
findings.suggestion: Use cleanup that safely restores directory traversal permissions without following symlinks, and isolate cleanup failures so they cannot abort unrelated jobs.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate runs `mkdir -p blocked/nested; chmod 000 blocked` and finishes. Cleanup fails after result submission, the worker exits, and any concurrently running jobs are aborted.

Found two reproduced security defects in worker checkout and repository opt-in enforcement. Targeted tests could not load because the MCP SDK is missing and the installed Zod lacks .overwrite(); isolated probes ran successfully.

findings.title: Accepted result ordering corrupts retry assignments
findings.detail: validRun accepts checks in any order, but retryFailures assigns returned checks to original failures by array index. A reordered worker response therefore associates results with the wrong checks. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-boundaries.ts". Output: "reversed result accepted: true" and "retry original -> result: A -> B:false, B -> A:true".
findings.suggestion: Validate checks against the requested order, or normalize validated results into that order before returning them.
findings.failure_scenario: Checks A and B both initially fail. The retry response lists B failing followed by A passing. Validation accepts it, and the retry code assigns A's passing result to B's original failure.

findings.title: Infrastructure retries erase observed check failures
findings.detail: complete stores only the latest attempt's GateRun, ignoring failed check events already recorded for the job. LAN attachment returns that result unchanged, so an infrastructure retry can turn an observed failure into a clean pass, contrary to the request. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-worker-boundaries.ts". Output: "after failed streamed A and infrastructure retry: [{\"name\":\"A\",\"ok\":true,\"firstAttempt\":null},{\"name\":\"B\",\"ok\":true,\"firstAttempt\":null}]".
findings.suggestion: Preserve validated failures across infrastructure attempts and local fallback, and apply the existing retry classification instead of returning a clean passing result.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing check, then disconnects before posting its final result. Another worker or the local fallback passes that check. The final result contains no firstAttempt evidence and can be treated or cached as a clean pass.

findings.title: Worker checkout can execute filters outside confinement
findings.detail: addDetachedWorktree performs checkout while the hardened wrapper discovers filter settings from the bare cache. A global includeIf matching the new worktree's Git directory activates additional filters during checkout, so those filters escape suppression and execute before confinementScope starts. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-filter.ts". Output: unconfined filter executed: true.
findings.suggestion: Create the worktree with --no-checkout, record its trusted Git paths, then perform the checkout through worktreeGit from the new worktree, as createWorktree already does.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker has a conditional Git configuration defining a smudge filter for linked worktrees, and the supplied commit selects that filter through .gitattributes. Checkout executes the filter with unrestricted worker privileges, including access to its token.

findings.title: Removing repository opt-in does not stop persisted jobs from leaving
findings.detail: The repository allowlist is checked only when starting a new job. Persisted queued jobs remain leasable after a restart with the repository removed from workers.repos; neither reattachment nor the lease and bundle routes check the current policy. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-optin.ts". Output: removed opt-in still leased: true.
findings.suggestion: Enforce the current repository allowlist at lease and bundle delivery, and cancel or route persisted jobs locally when their repository is no longer opted in.
findings.failure_scenario: A private repository has a queued LAN job when the daemon stops. The owner removes it from workers.repos and restarts. A paired worker can still lease that job and download its source bundle.

structured.summary: Found two reproduced security defects in worker checkout and repository opt-in enforcement. Targeted tests could not load because the MCP SDK is missing and the installed Zod lacks .overwrite(); isolated probes ran successfully.

findings.title: Worker checkout can execute filters outside confinement
findings.detail: addDetachedWorktree performs checkout while the hardened wrapper discovers filter settings from the bare cache. A global includeIf matching the new worktree's Git directory activates additional filters during checkout, so those filters escape suppression and execute before confinementScope starts. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-filter.ts". Output: unconfined filter executed: true.
findings.suggestion: Create the worktree with --no-checkout, record its trusted Git paths, then perform the checkout through worktreeGit from the new worktree, as createWorktree already does.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker has a conditional Git configuration defining a smudge filter for linked worktrees, and the supplied commit selects that filter through .gitattributes. Checkout executes the filter with unrestricted worker privileges, including access to its token.

findings.title: Removing repository opt-in does not stop persisted jobs from leaving
findings.detail: The repository allowlist is checked only when starting a new job. Persisted queued jobs remain leasable after a restart with the repository removed from workers.repos; neither reattachment nor the lease and bundle routes check the current policy. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-optin.ts". Output: removed opt-in still leased: true.
findings.suggestion: Enforce the current repository allowlist at lease and bundle delivery, and cancel or route persisted jobs locally when their repository is no longer opted in.
findings.failure_scenario: A private repository has a queued LAN job when the daemon stops. The owner removes it from workers.repos and restarts. A paired worker can still lease that job and download its source bundle.

Publication boundaries use the shared sanitizer, but isolated checks confirmed two ways local paths survive. The targeted test command `bun test test/publication-text.test.ts` could not run because the checkout lacks the `entities` dependency. Reproduction command: bun -e 'const s = await Bun.file("src/gates/publication.ts").text(); const js = new Bun.Transpiler({loader:"ts"}).transformSync(s.slice(s.indexOf("export function sanitizePublication"), s.indexOf("/** Check both")).replace("export function", "function")); const f = new Function(js + "; return sanitizePublication")(); for (const x of ["[test](~/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts)", "[test](file:///Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts)", "[/Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts)"]) console.log(f(x, "/Users/example/.limitless/work/run", "/Users/example/.limitless"));'

findings.title: Recognize local paths expressed with tilde or file URLs
findings.detail: Only literal absolute prefixes match. The reproduction command in the summary printed: FAIL tilde link: expected "[test/a.ts](test/a.ts)", got "[test](~/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts)"; FAIL file URI: expected "[test/a.ts](test/a.ts)", got "[test](file:///Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts)". The tilde form appears in the original request; file URLs retain the username and either publish it or block delivery once it is private-listed.
findings.suggestion: Normalize supported local-path representations before classifying them, including home-relative paths and file URLs.
findings.failure_scenario: A report links to ~/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts or file:///Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts while the recorded worktree is /Users/example/.limitless/work/run.

findings.title: Sanitize absolute paths in link labels
findings.detail: The regex consumes an entire Markdown link, then returns it unchanged when its destination needs no rewrite. Absolute paths in its label therefore escape the bare-path replacement. The reproduction command in the summary printed: FAIL absolute label: expected "[test/a.ts](test/a.ts)", got "[/Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts)". This retains the username in published text or causes the privacy check to block delivery.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize local paths in link labels independently of whether the destination changes.
findings.failure_scenario: The report contains [/Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts).

findings.title: Normalize parent segments before choosing the replacement
findings.detail: Lexical prefix matching treats paths that escape the worktree as repository files. The reproduction command in the summary printed: FAIL parent traversal: expected "<data>/runs/log.txt", got "[../../runs/log.txt](../../runs/log.txt)". This produces a broken repository link instead of the required plain-text data-directory placeholder.
findings.suggestion: Normalize dot segments before checking directory containment and deriving the replacement.
findings.failure_scenario: With worktree /Users/example/.limitless/work/run, the report links to /Users/example/.limitless/work/run/../../runs/log.txt.

findings.title: Avoid sanitizing the previously published PR body
findings.detail: Applying publicationText to pr.body + text rewrites existing published content, despite that being explicitly out of scope. An older report's worktree links fall outside the current round's worktree but inside the data directory, so appending a round converts those historical links into plain <data> paths and discards their labels.
findings.suggestion: Append the sanitized new section to the existing body without sanitizing the existing body again.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round appends to a PR whose existing body contains links into the original run's worktree.

findings.title: Home-relative and file URL links bypass sanitization
findings.detail: The sanitizer only recognizes literal absolute directory prefixes. The reproduction command in the summary outputs `[test](~/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts)` and `[test](file:///Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts)` unchanged. The home-relative form is explicitly shown in the request; file URLs also retain the username. Without a matching private-string entry these publish unchanged; with one, file URL reports remain blocked.
findings.suggestion: Recognize home-relative paths and local file URLs before applying directory-boundary checks, and test both worktree and data-directory destinations.
findings.failure_scenario: A report links to a worktree file using `~/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts` or `file:///Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts`.

findings.title: An unchanged link destination shields local paths in its label
findings.detail: The regex consumes an entire Markdown link, then returns it unchanged when its destination needs no rewrite. Bare local paths inside its label therefore never reach the path matcher. The reproduction command in the summary outputs `[/Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts)` unchanged, exposing the username or blocking delivery once it is private-listed.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize local paths in link labels independently of destination rewriting, while preserving ordinary destinations.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer uses an absolute worktree path as the visible label of a repo-relative link.

The tilde form appears in the original request; file URLs retain the username and either publish it or block delivery once it is private-listed.
findings.suggestion: Normalize supported local-path representations before classifying them, including home-relative paths and file URLs.
findings.failure_scenario: A report links to ~/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts or file:///Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts while the recorded worktree is /Users/example/.limitless/work/run.

findings.title: Sanitize absolute paths in link labels
findings.detail: The regex consumes an entire Markdown link, then returns it unchanged when its destination needs no rewrite. Absolute paths in its label therefore escape the bare-path replacement. The reproduction command in the summary printed: FAIL absolute label: expected "[test/a.ts](test/a.ts)", got "[/Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts)". This retains the username in published text or causes the privacy check to block delivery.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize local paths in link labels independently of whether the destination changes.
findings.failure_scenario: The report contains [/Users/example/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts).

findings.title: Normalize parent segments before choosing the replacement
findings.detail: Lexical prefix matching treats paths that escape the worktree as repository files. The reproduction command in the summary printed: FAIL parent traversal: expected "<data>/runs/log.txt", got "[../../runs/log.txt](../../runs/log.txt)". This produces a broken repository link instead of the required plain-text data-directory placeholder.
findings.suggestion: Normalize dot segments before checking directory containment and deriving the replacement.
findings.failure_scenario: With worktree /Users/example/.limitless/work/run, the report links to /Users/example/.limitless/work/run/../../runs/log.txt.

findings.title: Avoid sanitizing the previously published PR body
findings.detail: Applying publicationText to pr.body + text rewrites existing published content, despite that being explicitly out of scope. An older report's worktree links fall outside the current round's worktree but inside the data directory, so appending a round converts those historical links into plain <data> paths and discards their labels.
findings.suggestion: Append the sanitized new section to the existing body without sanitizing the existing body again.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round appends to a PR whose existing body contains links into the original run's worktree.

findings.title: Sanitize local paths inside otherwise unchanged links
findings.detail: The regex consumes the entire Markdown link, but the callback checks only its destination. If that destination is relative, an absolute path in the label is returned unchanged and never reaches the bare-path matcher. The probe printed: FAIL: local path remains: [/factory/data/work/run/src/main.ts](src/main.ts). This can publish private paths or block delivery once the username is listed.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize local paths in link labels and titles even when the destination requires no rewrite.

findings.title: Recognize local file URLs before comparing directory roots
findings.detail: A file:// destination points into the worktree but never starts with the configured filesystem root, so the entire link survives unchanged. The probe printed: FAIL: local path remains: [source](file:///factory/data/work/run/src/main.ts). These links still expose the owner's local layout and remain broken on GitHub.
findings.suggestion: Parse local file URLs and compare their decoded filesystem paths against the worktree and data-directory roots before producing relative links or placeholders.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer emits [source](file:///factory/data/work/run/src/main.ts), or a file URL to a log beneath the data directory. Publication retains the absolute local URL.

findings.title: Home-relative paths from the original request remain unchanged
findings.detail: Matching only literal configured roots misses the ~/.limitless spelling explicitly shown in the request. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/publication-review-582.ts" tilde` exited 1 with output: `FAIL\nexpected: [test/a.ts](test/a.ts)\nactual: [test](~/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts)`. Bare home-relative data paths also remain unchanged, publishing the local data layout and broken links.
findings.suggestion: Recognize home-relative aliases for the configured roots before classifying paths, while retaining complete directory-boundary checks.
findings.failure_scenario: With worktree /Users/owner/.limitless/work/run, the report contains [test](~/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts) or ~/.limitless/runs/log.txt.

findings.title: Local file URLs still expose absolute worktree paths
findings.detail: A Markdown destination beginning file:// never matches either root. The whole link is consumed, so the absolute path inside it receives no further processing. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/publication-review-582.ts" file` exited 1 with output: `FAIL\nexpected: [test/a.ts](test/a.ts)\nactual: [test](file:///Users/owner/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts)`. This publishes the username and data layout, or blocks delivery once the username is privately listed.
findings.suggestion: Parse local file URL destinations into filesystem paths before applying the shared worktree/data-directory classification.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer reports [test](file:///Users/owner/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts), with the corresponding absolute worktree configured.

findings.title: Links with relative destinations shield absolute paths in their labels
findings.detail: The regex consumes an entire Markdown link, but the callback examines only its destination. If that destination needs no rewrite, it returns the complete original match, preserving absolute local paths in its label or title. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/publication-review-582.ts" label` exited 1 with output: `FAIL\nexpected: [test/a.ts](test/a.ts)\nactual: [/Users/owner/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts)`. Thus an otherwise valid relative link can still publish the owner's username.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize local paths in link labels and titles as well as destinations, preserving ordinary links without local paths.
findings.failure_scenario: A report uses the absolute filename as its link label and a repo-relative destination: [/Users/owner/.limitless/work/run/test/a.ts](test/a.ts).

findings.title: Rewriting image destinations removes image rendering
findings.detail: The matcher explicitly accepts Markdown images through its optional ! prefix, but reconstruction always emits a normal link. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/publication-review-582.ts" image` exited 1 with output: `FAIL\nexpected: ![screen.png](screen.png)\nactual: [screen.png](screen.png)`. Embedded screenshots consequently become text links.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the image marker when reconstructing a sanitized worktree image destination.
findings.failure_scenario: A report contains ![preview](/Users/owner/.limitless/work/run/screen.png). Publication changes it into [screen.png](screen.png).

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside push and merge helpers
findings.detail: The ownership check precedes calling mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits `gh pr view` before issuing `gh pr merge`, and can await reconciliation and retries before further attempts. Likewise, pushExistingBranch awaits rev-parse, transport preparation, ls-remote and merge-base before pushing. Neither helper receives an ownership guard. A reclaim during those awaits still allows the old worker to merge or push before its heartbeat notices. The added tests defer the helpers' completed results, so they miss this command-issuance race.
findings.suggestion: Pass a claim-validation callback into both helpers and invoke it immediately before every merge or push attempt, including retries. Add deferred preflight-response tests.
findings.failure_scenario: Pause mergePullRequest's preflight `gh pr view`, reclaim the entry as new-owner, then release the OPEN response before the heartbeat fires. The old worker issues `gh pr merge`. The equivalent ordering during pushExistingBranch's ls-remote also permits a stale push.

findings.title: CI inspection still writes after claim loss
findings.detail: Adding ownership to the `current` callback does not guard every write within ciDecision. inspectCi writes default-branch settings and can emit ci.main_red before checking current(). Its requestRerun helper also calls finishCiFailure or reject after awaiting the rerun response without checking current(). Consequently, an inspection already in flight can write outcomes and feed records after this worker loses ownership.
findings.suggestion: Guard CI inspection's post-await writes with ownership validation in the same store transaction, including rerun-response handling and default-branch observations.
findings.failure_scenario: Defer the CI job-rerun POST response, reclaim the land entry, then return HTTP 201 before the heartbeat. requestRerun records `rerunning` despite the lost claim; a rejection response can instead record rerun_rejected and emit a fix trigger.

findings.title: A stale worker still removes the reclaimed worker's checkout
findings.detail: LandClaimLost unwinds through land's unconditional finally block, which calls discard. Every attempt uses the same `land-${entry.id}` worktree path. If the new owner has recreated that checkout, the old worker removes its worktree registration and recursively deletes its files. Preventing database writes therefore still leaves a destructive side effect after claim loss.
findings.suggestion: Make checkout cleanup ownership-safe, preferably by giving attempts distinct worktree paths so stale cleanup cannot delete a newer attempt's files.
findings.failure_scenario: Reclaim an entry while its old worker awaits CI, let the new owner recreate the entry's checkout, then release the old CI response. assertClaim throws, but the old worker's finally block deletes the new owner's checkout.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge helper before issuing commands
findings.detail: The ownership check before mergePullRequest does not protect the actual merge command. That helper awaits `gh pr view` before issuing `gh pr merge`, and its retry loop can await reconciliation and retry delays before issuing another merge. If another owner reclaims during those awaits, the old worker still merges before its next heartbeat. The new check after mergePullRequest only prevents recording the result.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into mergePullRequest and invoke it after preparation awaits and immediately before every merge attempt, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: Pause the helper's pre-merge `gh pr view`, reclaim the entry as new-owner, then release the OPEN response before the old heartbeat fires. The old worker issues `gh pr merge` despite losing ownership.

findings.title: Guard the actual push after the helper's preparation awaits
findings.detail: The transaction checks ownership before entering pushExistingBranch, but that helper subsequently awaits commit resolution, transport preparation, ls-remote and an ancestry check before issuing git push. A reclaim during any of those operations leaves the old signal active until its next heartbeat, allowing the stale worker to push. The added preparation test pauses remoteBranchSha outside this helper, so it does not cover this remaining window.
findings.suggestion: Provide pushExistingBranch with an ownership guard checked after its preparation awaits and immediately before issuing the push, covering any transport retries as well.
findings.failure_scenario: Allow pushApproved's ownership transaction to complete, defer pushExistingBranch's internal ls-remote, reclaim the entry, and release ls-remote before the heartbeat. With the remote still at approvedSha, the stale worker pushes its merge commit.

output.summary:
Found a reproduced descendant-recovery gap and an unsafe Linux identity comparison across reboots. Process tests passed 19/19; cleanup tests passed 8, while 3 integration tests were blocked by the missing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dependency. No repository files were modified.

Confirmed a crash-recovery gap with a real subprocess reproduction. Eight cleanup tests passed; three integration tests could not run because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js is missing. Also found unsafe Linux identity matching across reboots.

findings.title: Recovery clears ownership without discovering descendants missed before the crash
findings.detail:
Recovery kills only persisted members, then deletes the invocation record without rescanning. A member can fork after the live cleanup's snapshot but before SIGSTOP; the live cleanup normally catches that child in its next sweep, but recovery never does. Reproduced with `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/review-cleanup-race.ts"`. Output: `owned pids: [ 14217, 14549 ]
recorded pids: [ 14217 ]
records after recovery: 0
unrecorded descendant survived recovery: true`. Recovery reports success while an invocation descendant remains able to write to the checkout.
findings.suggestion: Persist sufficient invocation discovery metadata and resume the discovery/freeze/kill sweep before clearing ownership or allowing another invocation.
findings.failure_scenario: A marked parent forks between the initial process snapshot and its freeze. The daemon crashes after freezing that parent but before rescanning. Startup recovery kills the recorded parent, leaves its unrecorded child running, and permits subsequent commands.

findings.title: Include the Linux boot identity in durable process ownership
findings.detail: Linux processBirth returns only /proc/<pid>/stat starttime, measured in ticks since boot. Persisting that value introduces a cross-reboot hazard: both PIDs and starttime values can repeat on another boot. Recovery treats an unrelated process with the same pair as owned and sends SIGKILL. findings.title: Decode filename credentials before redacting diagnostics
findings.detail: The new diagnostic emits percent-encoded credentials unchanged. redactCredentials matches registered credentials literally, while redactPrivate only checks the private-string denylist. A focused probe registering a synthetic credential and passing its percent-encoded filename through this exact expression returned {"encodedCredentialRemains":true,"decodedOutputContainsCredential":true}. Previously this refusal emitted a generic message without the filename.
findings.suggestion: Decode supported filename encodings before credential redaction, or suppress filenames containing encoded registered credentials. Add coverage for encoded credentials in refusal paths.
findings.failure_scenario: A newly committed file has a percent-encoded registered credential in its filename and content that exceeds the private-text decoding depth. Diagnosis includes the recoverable encoded credential in the publication error, which can then enter logs or persisted feedback.

findings.title: Check private filenames after terminal normalization
findings.detail: The filename is checked for private strings before redactGateOutput strips terminal escapes. Stripping those escapes can reconstruct a configured private string, which then enters audit events, persisted findings, and model prompts. A direct `bun -e` probe calling auditDiff returned `"file":".tmp-gate/private-host.example.txt"` and failed with `error: auditDiff exposes configured private string`. The probe configured `private-host.example` as private and supplied a filename containing an ANSI color escape between `private-` and `host.example`.
findings.suggestion: Normalize the filename with redactGateOutput first, then check the normalized value for private strings before returning it. Add a regression test for a private value split by terminal escapes.
findings.failure_scenario: private-strings.txt contains private-host.example, and an added file is named .tmp-gate/private-<ESC>[31mhost.example.txt. The raw filename passes privateMatches; terminal normalization reconstructs and exposes private-host.example.

Found three eval accounting defects. All 19 workload tests passed. CLI and HTTP checks were blocked by incompatible Zod and a missing MCP SDK dependency. Read-only probes confirmed cache-data loss and statistics changing after restart recovery.

findings.title: Combined review usage is attributed to a single provider/model
findings.detail: Review evals can invoke multiple finders and verifiers across providers. The runner combines their usage and costs into the trial totals, but this fallback assigns the entire total to details.provider and t.model_id. Other participating providers receive no workload, and the first finder receives their spend. Replay evals can attribute spend to a finder that was never invoked.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish combined review trials from single-target trials. Attribute only measurements supported by stored call evidence, and expose unavailable attribution explicitly instead of assigning combined totals to the first finder.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel uses finder provider A and verifier provider B. Its combined $3 spend is reported entirely against A's model, with no eval workload reported for B.

findings.title: Implementation grading failures change provider successful share
findings.detail: The runner overwrites EvalRound.status with error or timeout when implementation grading fails operationally, even when the provider invocation returned ok. Using that round status reports a successful provider call as unsuccessful. The probe documented in the next finding returned successfulShare: 0 despite details.invocationStatus being ok.
findings.suggestion: Use invocation outcome evidence for provider successful share. For a single recorded round, details.invocationStatus supplies that evidence; avoid interpreting grading outcomes as provider outcomes for other cases.
findings.failure_scenario: An implement invocation returns ok, then its grading command times out. The stored round status becomes timeout and this endpoint reports provider successful share as 0 rather than 1.

findings.title: Single-round evals discard their stored cache measurements
findings.detail: Any nonempty rounds array forces cache-read, cache-write and input tokens to null, even for a single round whose exact split is stored on the trial. One such trial also makes those provider totals null through summarize(). Exact probe command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; import {computeProviderStatistics} from "./src/db/stats.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); const run=s.createEvalRun({role:"implement",models:["m"],k:1,maxUsd:10},[]); s.recordEvalTrial({evalRunId:run.id,modelId:"m",effort:null,caseId:"c",trial:0,cacheKey:"k",harness:"fake",status:"error",output:null,pass:false,score:0,details:{provider:"p",invocationStatus:"ok",cacheReadTokens:20,cacheWriteTokens:5,rounds:[{provider:"p",modelId:"m",round:0,effort:"default",status:"timeout",pass:false,reason:"grading timeout",tokensIn:100,tokensOut:10,costUsd:1,costEquivUsd:2,durationMs:60000}]},tokensIn:100,tokensOut:10,costUsd:1,costEquivUsd:2,durationMs:60000,createdAt:1}); const t=computeProviderStatistics(s)[0].eval.totals; console.log(JSON.stringify({successfulShare:t.successfulShare,inputTokens:t.inputTokens,cacheReadTokens:t.cacheReadTokens,cacheWriteTokens:t.cacheWriteTokens})); s.close();' Output: {"successfulShare":0,"inputTokens":null,"cacheReadTokens":null,"cacheWriteTokens":null}. The token measurements should be 75, 20 and 5.
findings.suggestion: Preserve trial-level cache splits when they can be attributed unambiguously, including single-round trials. Keep unknown values only where the persisted evidence genuinely cannot supply the breakdown.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round implement eval stores 100 prompt tokens, 20 cache-read tokens and 5 cache-write tokens. Its historical statistics report all three requested input/cache measurements as unknown.

findings.title: Do not attribute multi-provider review totals to the trial target
findings.detail: The fallback assigns the entire trial's tokens and costs to details.provider and t.model_id. Review panel trials combine results from additional finders and verifiers, potentially using different providers and models (see combined() in src/pipeline/review.ts and sendTo() in src/evals/runner.ts). Consequently, this reports other providers' work against the first finder. Verifier-only replay trials can even attribute all spend to a finder that made no call.
findings.suggestion: Handle composite review trials explicitly. Use stored attribution where available and represent unresolvable composite spend as unknown rather than assigning it to the first finder.
findings.failure_scenario: A review trial uses a finder from provider A and a verifier from provider B. Both calls' costs are combined in the trial, but the endpoint reports all cost under A and no workload under B.

findings.title: Preserve known cache measurements for single-round evals
findings.detail: Any nonempty rounds array forces both cache measurements to null, even when the trial contains exactly one round and stores its exact cache totals. Reviewed the diff and eval persistence paths. All 19 workload tests passed; targeted probes confirmed two accounting defects. HTTP and CLI checks were blocked by missing MCP SDK and incompatible Zod dependencies. No files changed.

findings.title: Panel usage is attributed entirely to the primary finder
findings.detail: Review panels combine finder and verifier usage into trial totals, potentially across providers. This fallback assigns all those totals to details.provider and t.model_id, silently charging other members' work to the primary finder. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/provider-stats-review.ts"` seeded a panel trial with provider alpha and a beta-verifier member; output was `[{"provider":"alpha","cost":1,"models":["m"]}]`, with no verifier attribution.
findings.suggestion: Handle multi-model review trials separately. Derive attribution from available stored evidence and mark any unallocatable usage explicitly unknown rather than assigning it to the primary finder.
findings.failure_scenario: A review eval uses an alpha finder and a beta verifier. Their combined tokens and costs appear entirely under alpha's finder model, while beta's workload is absent.

findings.title: Preserve known cache-token totals for implementation evals
findings.detail: Whenever details.rounds exists, both cache measurements are unconditionally replaced with null. The runner persists cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens on the trial, so even an ordinary single-round implementation eval loses measurements requested by this change. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/provider-stats-review.ts"` seeded one round with 100 prompt tokens, 20 cache-read tokens and 10 cache-write tokens; output was `{"inputTokens":null,"cacheReadTokens":null,"cacheWriteTokens":null}` instead of 70, 20 and 10.
findings.suggestion: Retain trial-level cache totals wherever attribution is known, including single-round trials and aggregates whose rounds all use the same provider/model. Reserve null for measurements that genuinely cannot be allocated.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed single-round implementation eval has fully recorded cache splits, but the endpoint and CLI report its input and cached tokens as unknown.

findings.title: Preserve spend recorded after the last completed round
findings.detail: When rounds exist, the implementation discards the trial's cumulative counters entirely. The runner persists cumulative spend after a failed session-resume attempt before recording that round's evidence (runner.ts:1149). During this interval, or permanently after interruption, stored spend exceeds the round totals. A targeted `bun -e` probe seeded a running trial with costUsd=3 and one recorded round costing 1; its output was {"persistedCost":3,"reportedCost":1}. Tokens and API-equivalent cost are lost the same way.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile round totals with cumulative trial counters and retain any persisted remainder, marking attribution unknown where necessary.
findings.failure_scenario: Round one finishes; a subsequent session-resume attempt consumes tokens and fails. The runner checkpoints cumulative usage, then the daemon stops before the next round evidence is written. Historical statistics permanently omit the checkpointed attempt's spend.

findings.title: Do not report composite review trials as single model invocations

Found two reproducible defects in redaction and excerpt construction. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency; direct Bun probes reproduced both findings.

Inspected the diff and rerun compatibility paths. Two isolated behavioral assertions failed. The targeted repository tests could not start because the entities dependency is missing.

findings.title: Preserve exact-value redaction for short image credentials
findings.detail: Image redaction now receives surrounding log text, so credentials shorter than eight characters no longer satisfy redactCredentials' exact-value rule. The previous implementation redacted the extracted image value directly. The raw image and signature subsequently enter ci_failures. Command: bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("REVIEW_TEST", "abc123"); const r=ciSignature("test", "Image: abc123\nerror: broken", ""); if(r.image!=="[redacted]") throw new Error(`Expected redacted image; got ${JSON.stringify(r.image)} and signature ${r.signature}`);' Output: error: Expected redacted image; got "abc123" and signature ["test","error: broken","abc123"].
findings.suggestion: Apply exact-value credential redaction to the extracted field as well as context-aware redaction.
findings.failure_scenario: Register the six-character credential abc123 and inspect a failing log containing Image: abc123. The returned image and persisted signature contain the credential.

findings.title: Budget the tail after redaction to retain the failing test
findings.detail:
The tail budget counts raw characters, but redaction can expand eight-character credentials into ten-character markers. The final slice then discards the stack location and chosen failure line from the end. Command: bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; registerCredential("REVIEW_EXPANSION", "abcdefgh"); const r=ciSignature("test", "error: assertion failed
"+"abcdefgh
".repeat(400)+"at test/example.test.ts:4:13
(fail) actual failure", ""); console.log(JSON.stringify({length:r.excerpt.length,hasLine:r.excerpt.includes(r.line),hasLocation:r.excerpt.includes("test/example.test.ts")})); if(!r.excerpt.includes(r.line)) throw new Error("Excerpt omitted the chosen failure line");' Output: {"length":2000,"hasLine":false,"hasLocation":false}, followed by error: Excerpt omitted the chosen failure line.
findings.suggestion: Bound the redacted tail from its end, reserving space for the selected failure line before assembling the excerpt.
findings.failure_scenario: A Bun assertion block contains many occurrences of a registered eight-character credential before its stack and (fail) line. Redaction expands the block, and truncation removes the actual failing test from the excerpt.

findings.title: Redaction expansion can remove the selected failure from the excerpt
findings.detail: The tail budget measures characters before redaction. Replacing eight-character credentials with ten-character markers expands the tail; the final slice then removes its ending, including the chosen failing test. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-682.ts"` (isolated probe executing the extracted implementation). Output: `FAIL Bun excerpt retains selected failing line after redaction: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the excerpt budget after redaction while preserving the selected failure line.
findings.failure_scenario: Register credential `12345678`, then classify `error: broken\n` followed by `12345678 ` repeated 300 times and `\n(fail) real failure`. The signature selects `(fail) real failure`, but the 2,000-character excerpt omits it.

findings.title: Publication windows bypass exact-match redaction of short credentials
findings.detail: Short credentials are redacted only when the complete redaction input equals the credential. The new padded publication input includes surrounding log text, so an image value that previously received exact-match redaction now remains plaintext in the signature and persisted ci_failures fields. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-682.ts"`. Output: `FAIL exact short runner image credential is redacted: Expected values to be strictly equal: + 'abc123' - '[redacted]'`.
findings.suggestion: Preserve exact-field redaction for short credentials alongside the contextual redaction needed for crossing credentials.
findings.failure_scenario: Register credential `abc123` and classify `Image: abc123\nerror: broken`. The returned image and serialized signature contain `abc123`; the previous implementation returned `[redacted]` for the image.

Reviewed the diff and worker lifecycle; source-extracted probes confirmed two event-reporting defects. Targeted worker tests could not start because entities is missing; agent-test tests encountered an incompatible installed Zod version. No repository files changed.

Reviewed the diff, surrounding lease and harness code, and isolated failure paths. Found result corruption and missing failure reporting. Targeted tests could not run because @simplewebauthn/server is missing and the installed Zod lacks prefault. No files were modified.

findings.title: Report event rejection as a job failure
findings.detail: A rejected event POST aborts the job controller, but the catch block only posts failure when jobSignal is not aborted. Consequently, rejection stops the harness without failing the coordinator job; it remains leased until expiry. A source-extracted runAgent probe (`bun -`, with the event POST rejecting) returned {"aborted":true,"posts":["/worker/agent-jobs/job/events"],"failureReports":0}. The new rejection test only checks that the job is not done, so it misses this requirement.
findings.suggestion: Track reporting failures separately from cancellation and send a bounded failure notification using a signal that survives the harness abort.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects an event batch with HTTP 400 or 413 while the agent lease remains valid. The worker aborts and removes the local job without posting failure.

findings.title: Bound event batches by the coordinator's byte limit
findings.detail: Batching limits event count and elapsed time but ignores the coordinator's 1 MiB event-body limit. Both harnesses allow 20,000-character tool results, so valid output can exceed that limit before reaching 200 events. A source-extracted readJson probe (`bun -`) with 60 such events returned {"events":60,"bodyBytes":1203670,"limitBytes":1048576,"rejectedAs":"BodyTooLarge"}. Such sessions lose the batch and abort despite valid harness behavior.
findings.suggestion: Split batches by serialized UTF-8 byte size as well as count and time, preserving sequence order. Handle an individually oversized event explicitly.
findings.failure_scenario: Sixty tool-result events containing 20,000 ASCII characters each arrive within 250 ms. The worker posts their approximately 1.2 MB batch, receives HTTP 413, and aborts the session.

findings.title: Gate-specific redaction modifies agent structured results
findings.detail: sanitize uses redactGateData, which enriches objects resembling gate results rather than merely redacting credentials. A valid structured agent result containing {"ok":true,"output":"answer"} acquires an unsolicited confinementError field. Verified with `bun -e 'import { redactGateData } from "./src/gates/output.ts"; console.log(JSON.stringify(redactGateData({ structured: { ok: true, output: "answer" } })));'`, which outputs `{"structured":{"ok":true,"output":"answer","confinementError":false}}`. The shared call helper also applies this transformation.
findings.suggestion: Use credential-only redaction for agent events and results at both sanitize and the HTTP call boundary; reserve gate-specific enrichment for gate payloads.
findings.failure_scenario: A session produces structured JSON with ok and output fields under a schema that forbids additional properties. The worker posts altered JSON containing confinementError, breaking equivalence with local invocation and potentially failing downstream schema validation.

findings.title: Rejected event batches suppress the job failure report
findings.detail: A rejected events request aborts the job controller here. When runAgent catches that rejection, its `if (!jobSignal.aborted)` guard skips POST failure. The coordinator therefore retains a leased job until expiry instead of immediately recording the rejection and releasing its agent slot. The added rejection test checks only that no result is posted, so it misses this state. An isolated execution of the extracted runAgent with an events refusal produced `{"calls":["/worker/agent-jobs/probe/events"],"aborted":true,"failurePosted":false}`.
findings.suggestion: Track event-delivery failure separately from cancellation, abort the harness, and send a bounded failure notification using a signal independent of the aborted job controller.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator rejects an event batch with HTTP 400 or 413 while the worker still holds the lease. The harness stops, but no failure is posted; the job occupies coordinator capacity until lease expiry and its recorded failure reason becomes lease expiry rather than the actual rejection.

findings.title: Retrying a job silently discards its new event batches
findings.detail: Each execution resets seq to zero, but failAgentJob preserves existing events when requeuing the same job. The coordinator deduplicates by (job_id, seq), silently ignoring the retry's overlapping batches. A focused probe executing runAgent twice with the actual event INSERT SQL stored only the first attempt's event.
findings.suggestion: Make event sequence allocation survive attempts, or introduce an attempt identifier into event storage and deduplication.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker A uploads batches 0–3 and then fails. Worker B leases the requeued job and uploads batches starting at zero. Its first four batches are acknowledged but discarded, leaving events from the failed attempt alongside the successful result.

findings.title: Event rejection aborts execution without reporting failure
findings.detail: A rejected event batch aborts the job controller. The catch block then skips POST failure because jobSignal.aborted is true. The coordinator still considers the job leased until expiry instead of immediately recording and retrying the reporting failure. A focused runAgent probe rejecting events with 413 produced only the events request and no failure request.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish reporting failures from cancellation and fencing. Abort the harness, then send a bounded failure notification using a separate signal when the coordinator still holds the lease.
findings.failure_scenario: An event batch exceeds the listener's 1 MiB limit and receives 413. The harness stops and its checkout is discarded, but no failure reason is reported; reassignment waits for lease expiry.

findings.title: Report rejected event batches as job failures
findings.detail: When an event POST is rejected, this handler aborts the job controller. The catch block at line 533 then skips POST failure because jobSignal is aborted. The worker discards the checkout and forgets the job, while the coordinator retains it as leased until expiry and records an expiry reason instead of the actual rejection. The new rejection test only asserts that the job is not done, so it permits this behavior.
findings.suggestion: Track event-reporting failures separately from coordinator cancellation. Abort the harness, then send a bounded failure report with a live signal when the worker still holds the lease.
findings.failure_scenario: A running harness emits events and POST events receives HTTP 400 or 413 while the lease remains valid. The harness stops, but no failure is posted; the coordinator waits for lease expiry before retrying the job.

Reviewed restart, reconciliation, adoption and reporting paths. An isolated executor probe reproduced a restart failure during local fallback. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies, including entities, are missing.

findings.title: Retire the done-job handle before starting local fallback
findings.detail: A done report with failed confinement or cancelled status starts local fallback while agentJob still names that report. If the local session edits files and shutdown interrupts it, resume processes the same done report and calls adopt before falling back. workerPublication.adopt rejects the dirty worktree, ending the run NeedsHuman. An isolated `bun -` executor probe using the adoption cleanliness condition produced: `Fallback before shutdown: {"status":"cancelled"}` followed by `Resume: NeedsHumanError Coordinator HEAD or worktree changed during worker session`.
findings.suggestion: Durably mark the worker result consumed before local fallback starts, so resume continues the interrupted local session without replaying worker adoption.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker reports confinement failure without changes; local fallback edits a file; the daemon stops before implementation-ready; the restarted round retains the done-job handle and fails adoption because the local edits made the worktree dirty.

findings.title: Make reused-result accounting idempotent
findings.detail: Returning a stored result repeats its full usage and costs in a new invocation. RunContext.invoke records those fields and refreshes totals before the implementation-ready checkpoint. A crash at that checkpoint leaves the original charged invocation and durable job handle; resume returns the report again and charges another invocation. Store.refreshRunTotals sums both rows without deduplication. An isolated `bun -` executor probe returned `{"firstCost":2,"resumedCost":2,"sum":4}` for the same done job.
findings.suggestion: Associate result accounting with the durable job or original invocation and record it once. Preserve invocation attribution while preventing resumed invocations from charging already-recorded usage again.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker result costs $2. Its invocation is finalized, then the daemon dies before implementation-ready is saved. Resume reuses the done result, and the run reports $4 plus doubled tokens despite only one worker session.

findings.title: Persist the transition to local fallback before starting it
findings.detail: A completed worker job remains in agentJob when its cancelled or confinement-failed result triggers local fallback. If that local session writes files and shutdown interrupts it before implementation-ready, resume reconciles the same done job and calls adopt again. workerPublication.adopt rejects the local session's dirty worktree, ending the run NeedsHuman instead of resuming implementation. An isolated `bun -` probe executing the transpiled executor produced: `Before restart: daemon interrupted local fallback`, `After restart: NeedsHumanError: Coordinator HEAD or worktree changed during worker session`, `Local sessions: 1`.
findings.suggestion: Durably record that the worker result has been consumed and execution has transitioned to local fallback, so resume does not adopt that result again over partial local edits.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker reports a cancelled session with sha equal to parentSha; the coordinator starts local fallback; the local harness writes a file; a deploy interrupts it before implementation-ready; the restarted coordinator attempts adoption of the old done job and rejects the dirty worktree.

findings.title: Validation retains setup artifacts that grading deletes
findings.detail: The generator runs hidden tests directly after setup. gradeImplement instead resets tracked changes and runs git clean -fdq before injecting hidden files. Consequently, validation can accept a case whose reference solution fails actual grading. The new test fixture itself relies on an untracked ready file. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/replay-validation-probe.ts". Output: generator hidden exit: 0; grader hidden exit: 1; error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'ready'; 0 pass; 1 fail.
findings.suggestion: Share the grader's checkout restoration and hidden-test execution sequence with generator validation, including scratch/environment behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup creates an untracked file required by a hidden test. The implementation fails at base and passes at head during generation, but the grader deletes the file and rejects even the reference implementation.

findings.title: The CLI never attempts to retrieve production complexity
findings.detail: Only an injected lookupRun can obtain triage complexity, but the CLI never supplies one. Thus the requested generator always assigns medium, even when the referenced production run is available on the factory host. The injectable helper is tested, but the advertised command cannot use it.
findings.suggestion: Wire a best-effort lookup through the existing daemon API or a read-only run store, retaining the documented default when the record is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a replay for a PR whose footer identifies an available production run with small complexity. The CLI stores medium and reports lookup not configured.

findings.title: An interrupted publication permanently blocks the next case ID
findings.detail: Hidden files are written to their final directory before cases.json is replaced. If the process stops between those operations, the directory remains without a corresponding case. On restart, next is derived from cases.json, so the same ID is selected and rejected by this existence check. Because next advances only after acceptance, every subsequent valid PR also encounters that directory.
findings.suggestion: Add recoverable publication staging and reconciliation for hidden directories absent from cases.json, without overwriting files belonging to existing cases.
findings.failure_scenario: The generator is interrupted after creating hidden/impl-013 but before renaming the updated cases.json. Subsequent invocations exclude all valid PRs with Hidden destination already exists: impl-013 until someone manually removes the orphan.

findings.title: Wire production complexity lookup into the CLI
findings.detail: The CLI supplies only `cache` to generateReplayCases. Since complexity is obtained exclusively through the optional lookupRun dependency, the documented command always records medium, even when the production run record is available locally. Providing an injection point exercised by tests does not implement lookup for users of the generator.
findings.suggestion: Supply a best-effort production run lookup from the CLI, retaining the explicit default only when the record cannot be found.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a replay for a factory PR whose Run footer identifies an available run with complexity small. The CLI writes complexity medium instead.

findings.title: Recover hidden files left by interrupted publication
findings.detail: Hidden files are written directly into the final case directory before cases.json is replaced. If the process stops between those operations, the directory survives without a corresponding case. Every later invocation selects the same next ID and refuses because that directory exists, blocking unrelated PRs as well. The catch cleanup does not run after process termination.
findings.suggestion: Stage hidden files separately and add recovery for an interrupted publication, verifying ownership before removing or reusing an orphaned destination.
findings.failure_scenario: Terminate generation after hidden/impl-013 is created but before cases.json is renamed. Restart generation: impl-013 remains the next ID, and every otherwise valid PR is excluded with 'Hidden destination already exists'.

Consequently, an accepted case can fail even when replaying its exact solution. The new test fixture itself depends on an untracked `ready` file. Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-JBAncB/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-JBAncB/claude-501/replay-validation-probe.ts`. findings.title: Connect production complexity lookup to the CLI
findings.detail: The advertised generator command never supplies lookupRun. Therefore replayProduction always records medium, even when the PR contains a run ID and the configured factory has the corresponding production record. Supporting lookup only through a programmatic injection leaves the CLI's required production-complexity extraction unimplemented.

structured.summary: Reviewed the diff and surrounding generator/grader code. Found two defects. A real-git probe confirmed a validation mismatch. The targeted test file could not load because dependencies are absent (`entities` missing).

findings.title: Validate the filesystem state the grader actually uses
findings.detail: Validation retains setup-created untracked files, but gradeImplement runs reset --hard and clean -fdq before injecting hidden tests. Consequently, an accepted case can fail even when replaying its exact solution. The new test fixture itself depends on an untracked `ready` file. Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-JBAncB/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-JBAncB/claude-501/replay-validation-probe.ts`. Output: `generator head validation exit: 0`; `grader hidden check exit: 1`; `error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'ready'`; `0 pass`; `1 fail`.
findings.suggestion: Share the grader's preparation sequence with validation, including cleanup before hidden-file injection, so head validation establishes that the saved case can actually pass grading.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup creates an untracked helper or artifact required by a changed test. Hidden tests fail at base and pass at head during generation, but grading deletes that artifact and rejects the exact head implementation.

findings.title: Connect production complexity lookup to the CLI
findings.detail: The advertised generator command never supplies lookupRun. Therefore replayProduction always records medium, even when the PR contains a run ID and the configured factory has the corresponding production record. Supporting lookup only through a programmatic injection leaves the CLI's required production-complexity extraction unimplemented.
findings.suggestion: Provide a read-only production-run lookup through the CLI's configured factory connection or store, retaining the documented fallback when the record is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a replay for a PR whose footer identifies an available run with complexity small. The CLI saves complexity medium and notes `lookup not configured` instead of using the production value.

Found validation and production-complexity defects. A real-git probe reproduced the validation mismatch. Targeted repository tests could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. No files were modified.

Found three defects in replay validation and complexity metadata. Targeted tests could not start because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. A separate real-git fixture confirmed the snapshot validation mismatch. No files were modified.

findings.title: Validate the reference solution under the runner's snapshot conditions
findings.detail: Base validation removes evals/, while head validation retains it and the full repository history. Generated cases always use snapshot mode, so the runner cannot reproduce that successful reference environment. A real-git fixture with a hidden test reading evals/value.json reproduced this: running `bun test ./test/answer.test.ts` returned base exit 1, full-head exit 0, and snapshot-head exit 1 with `error: ENOENT: no such file or directory`. Thus the generator's acceptance condition admits a case whose correct reference implementation fails grading.
findings.suggestion: Additionally validate the reference solution in the same snapshot environment used during grading, and exclude cases that depend on removed files or history.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR changes a test that reads an existing evals/ resource. Baseline gates do not read that resource. Hidden validation fails on the base snapshot and passes on the full head, but the correct implementation fails in the runner because evals/ is absent.

findings.title: Wire production-run complexity lookup into the CLI
findings.detail: The requested CLI supplies only cache access; it never supplies lookupRun. Consequently, even when the PR footer identifies a locally available production run, every generated case defaults to medium. A targeted invocation of replayProduction with a run footer and no lookup confirmed `complexity: "medium"` and `lookup not configured`. The injectable lookup exercised by tests is unavailable through the actual command.
findings.suggestion: Connect the CLI to the existing run-record store or API and pass lookupRun, retaining the documented fallback when the record genuinely cannot be found.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a replay for a PR whose footer names an available run with complexity small. The CLI records medium instead of the production complexity.

findings.title: Handle production runs with large complexity
findings.detail: Production complexity includes large, and replayProduction returns it unchanged when found. ImplementCaseSchema accepts only trivial, small, or medium, so parsing rejects the PR before validation. The new test explicitly expects this rejection, although the request requires preserving production complexity and does not exclude large tasks. This discards precisely the harder examples the generator is intended to collect.
findings.suggestion: Support large complexity through the implement case reader and relevant consumers, or establish an explicitly authorized representation that preserves the production value without excluding the case.
findings.failure_scenario: lookupRun returns `{ complexity: "large" }` for an otherwise valid merged PR. ImplementCaseSchema.parse rejects the case, so neither validation nor publication occurs.

findings.title: Validate equivalent repository contents at base and head
findings.detail: Base validation removes evals/ through snapshotting, while head validation retains it. This can manufacture the required failure. A real-git fixture with an unchanged evals/helper.ts and a newly added test importing it produced actual-base: exit=0, generator-base: exit=1 (Cannot find module '../evals/helper.ts'), generator-head: exit=0. Preparation succeeds when existing baseline checks do not exercise that dependency, and the generator accepts load errors.
findings.suggestion: Check the required fail/pass behavior against the original base and head, and separately verify that the reference solution passes in the snapshot environment used for candidate grading.
findings.failure_scenario: A test-only PR adds a passing test for existing code under evals/. The original base already passes the hidden test, but removing evals/ makes generator base validation fail, so the case is incorrectly accepted.

findings.title: Support the production large complexity value
findings.detail: replayProduction returns the production complexity unchanged, including large, but ImplementCaseSchema only accepts trivial/small/medium. Consequently, finding a valid large run record excludes the entire PR before validation. The new test explicitly expects this exclusion, despite the request requiring production triage complexity and targeting harder cases.
findings.suggestion: Extend the implement case schema and affected consumers to preserve large complexity rather than excluding those replays.
findings.failure_scenario: lookupRun returns { complexity: "large" } for a merged PR whose hidden tests otherwise satisfy both validation requirements.

findings.title: Wire production run lookup into the generator CLI
findings.detail: The CLI supplies only cache, never lookupRun. PR reports do not contain triage complexity, so every case generated through the requested command defaults to medium, even when the footer identifies an available local production run. An injectable hook used only by programmatic callers does not implement complexity discovery for the delivered command.
findings.suggestion: Provide a read-only production run lookup through the existing store or API, retaining the documented unknown fallback when the record is genuinely unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: The user runs the documented generator command on the factory host for a PR whose footer names a locally available small or large production run; the generated case records medium without consulting that record.

Reviewed snapshot creation, execution, reuse, and verification evidence. Found a timeout-result reuse gap. Targeted tests could not reach assertions because dependencies are missing or incompatible: entities is absent, and the resolved Zod lacks overwrite/prefault.

Found two defects in gate result handling. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies were missing or incompatible; socket probes were sandbox-blocked. Focused probes reproduced both findings. Diff whitespace checks passed.

findings.title: Preserve timed-out factory executions for same-tree reuse
findings.detail: The completed predicate rejects every timed-out result, so this condition discards the execution instead of recording its failure. When the implementer finishes without changing the tree, the gates stage finds no record and runs the full suite again, potentially followed by its normal timeout retry. This violates the requested preservation of failures and retries and recreates duplicate suite load. The new timeout test explicitly expects an empty execution table, so it codifies this gap.
findings.suggestion: Apply the normal timeout retry policy to the requested factory gate, persist its terminal result and attempt history, and reuse that outcome for matching keys while retaining its blocking status.
findings.failure_scenario: The baseline passes; an implement-session factory test exceeds its timeout; the implementer returns with the same tree. The gates stage reruns the suite and may retry it again, losing the session-requested timeout from the final gate history.

findings.title: Return failure when confinement invalidates a zero exit
findings.detail: The returned status ignores result.ok and confinementError. runOne can produce ok=false, confinementError=true, exitCode=0 when a command prints a confinement failure but exits successfully. A focused probe executing the extracted runAgentGate function returned status: 0 alongside 'Factory gate run ... FAIL'. Shell conditionals therefore treat this failed factory gate as successful.
findings.suggestion: Return a nonzero status whenever the factory result is not successful, preserving meaningful nonzero process exit codes.
findings.failure_scenario: The test check or setup prints a recognized confinement failure and exits 0. The wrapper prints FAIL but exits 0, so the implementer receives a successful command status.

findings.title: Repeated requests overwrite failures with a clean pass
findings.detail: runAgentGate never looks up an existing execution before running the same snapshot again. putAgentGate then overwrites the previous comparison. An unchanged-tree request can therefore erase a recorded regression and its retry history. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/agent-gate-review-probe.ts". With an injected executor, output included: first request: { calls: 2, verdict: "regressed" }; same-tree second request: { calls: 3, verdict: "pass", firstAttempt: false }.
findings.suggestion: Reuse validated evidence for the same key before starting another execution. If additional attempts are permitted, retain the original failures and classify subsequent success as flaky.
findings.failure_scenario: The first request fails both its initial execution and automatic retry. The implementer requests the suite again without changing files; it passes. The gates stage reuses a clean pass with no record of the earlier failures, which can also qualify for verification substitution.

findings.title: Return failure status when confinement invalidates a gate
findings.detail: The response derives status solely from exitCode, although a gate can have ok=false and exitCode=0 when confinementError is set. The wrapper then exits successfully despite displaying FAIL. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/agent-gate-review-probe.ts". An injected confinement-failed result produced: { status: 0, text: "Factory gate run of check test on tree aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa: FAIL (0s)\nconfinement failed" }.
findings.suggestion: Return a nonzero status whenever result.ok is false, retaining the original nonzero exit code where appropriate.
findings.failure_scenario: A test command exits zero but its output reveals a nested confinement failure. The factory rejects the result, yet the session command returns zero, allowing shell success branches and success-dependent command chains to proceed.

findings.title: Allow factory gate requests for repositories routed locally
findings.detail: The handler is disabled whenever gateExecutor.kind is "lan", even though lanExecutor runs repositories outside workers.repos locally. A direct probe returned {"configuredKind":"lan","freshCheckout":false,"actualExecutionKind":"local"}. Thus a local implement session with local gates receives "factory gate unavailable" instead of the requested factory run. reusableAgentGate has the same overly broad exclusion.
findings.suggestion: Determine the execution route for this repository rather than rejecting the entire LAN executor object, and use the same routing decision for execution and reuse.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure gates.executor = "lan", leave the current repository out of workers.repos, and run a local implement session with agent_full_suite = "gate". Its wrapped bun test request fails despite normal gate executions running locally.
