output.summary:
Reviewed the diff and surrounding restart, cancellation, leasing, and routing code. Found four defects. Attempted `bun test test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts`, but it could not load because the checkout lacks the `entities` dependency; no test assertions ran. No files were modified.

Found four defects in restart recovery, retry state, liveness, and worktree exclusion. Isolated source probes reproduced three failures. The targeted test file could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Running retry jobs cannot be reattached after restart
findings.detail: The resume predicate accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. In-place targeted retries, full retries, and timeout reruns are nevertheless persisted and left running during shutdown. On restart, the engine enters the initial gate path, rejects the retry handle, cancels its running job, and starts the suite again. This omits the requested restart support for targeted retries.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress to resume the recorded purpose directly, and allow matching in-place retry handles to reattach.
findings.failure_scenario: Restart the daemon while an in-place baseline-retry-targeted or regression-retry-targeted job is running. The resumed engine cancels that job and reruns earlier gates instead of receiving its result.

findings.title: Worktree exclusion is not enforced when leasing
findings.detail: The lease transaction checks only the selected job's queued state. The worktree check in lanExecutor.start happens before awaiting slot release, saving the handle, and enqueuing the job. Two concurrent starts can both observe no existing job and subsequently enqueue jobs for the same cwd. Separate executor processes can then lease both because neither lease checks for another running or unconfirmed-stopped job in that worktree.
findings.suggestion: Enforce worktree exclusion atomically at the database lease boundary, including jobs whose stopped flag remains zero.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent executeGate calls target the same worktree and both finish start before either attaches. Both jobs are enqueued; two executor processes lease them and run checks concurrently in the shared files.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor can block a run forever
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID birth identity; there is no heartbeat timestamp or freshness check. After a running job's lease expires, sweep marks it failed, but waitStopped keeps waiting while that executor process exists. A stalled executor never acknowledges cancellation, and this wait has no deadline. Thus lease expiry does not lead to either fallback or a reported stop-confirmation failure.
findings.suggestion: Track executor responsiveness and bound stop acknowledgement. If shutdown cannot be confirmed, report a clear failure rather than waiting indefinitely; preserve the process-stop barrier before fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor stalls after leasing a job while its process remains alive. Its lease expires, but the daemon waits indefinitely in waitStopped and never completes or falls back.

findings.title: LAN configuration bypasses the enabled executor for local repositories
findings.detail: The inplace flag is used only when gates.executor is local. With LAN routing configured, repositories outside workers.repos take lanExecutor's local.start fallback directly, even when executor.enabled is true and a matching executor is available. Those local gates still run inside the daemon and are lost on restart.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local-repository branch through the enabled in-place executor, retaining in-process execution when it is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure gates.executor='lan', workers.repos=['owner/remote'], and executor.enabled=true. Run gates for another repository with a live local executor. They execute in the daemon and restart from scratch after daemon shutdown.

findings.title: Enforce worktree exclusion inside the lease transaction
findings.detail: leaseInplace checks only the selected job's state, allowing two executors to lease different jobs for the same cwd. The start-time scan is separated from enqueue by awaits and checkpoint persistence, so concurrent starts can both pass it. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-probes.ts"` against the extracted WorkerStore implementation produced `same-worktree leases: job-1 job-2` and `concurrently leased jobs: 2`.
findings.suggestion: Make worktree admission atomic and refuse a lease while another job for the canonical worktree is running or has an unconfirmed stop.
findings.failure_scenario: Two starts for one worktree pass the scan before either enqueues. Two executor processes then lease the resulting jobs and run checks concurrently in that worktree.

findings.title: Preserve setup scratch across retry jobs
findings.detail: Each executeGate call creates and deletes its own command scratch. In-place retries are separate jobs, but freshCheckoutFor returns false, causing retryFailures to omit setup. Consequently HOME, TMPDIR, and package-cache state created by setup disappear before the retry. The scratch probe in `bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-probes.ts"` printed `retry retains setup scratch: false`.
findings.suggestion: Retain owned scratch across the initial execution and its retries, or explicitly recreate the setup state required by each retry.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup writes a required configuration file under HOME. A check fails transiently; its retry skips setup and runs with a new HOME, so it fails because the configuration is missing.

findings.title: Resume matching retry jobs instead of cancelling them
findings.detail: The purpose allowlist excludes every targeted retry, full retry, and timeout rerun. Even an otherwise matching live in-place handle is cancelled and its worktree cleaned. The source probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-probes.ts"` produced `matching retry handle resumed: undefined` and `matching retry handle cancelled: true` for regression-retry-targeted.
findings.suggestion: Persist sufficient attempt state to resume retry purposes and route resumed stages back to the recorded attempt.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts during a long targeted retry. The resumed stage cancels that surviving job and starts the initial gates again, repeating completed work.

findings.title: Track executor freshness separately from process existence
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID birth identity. There is no heartbeat timestamp or freshness expiry. A stalled executor remains available indefinitely; after its job lease expires, waitStopped still sees its live PID and waits forever rather than reaching recovery or a bounded refusal.
findings.suggestion: Implement executor heartbeat freshness and bounded handling of expired leases whose owner remains alive, while preserving process-stop confirmation before fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor stalls while holding a leased gate. The lease expires and the daemon attempts fallback or restart recovery, but waitStopped loops indefinitely because the executor process still exists.

findings.title: Running retry jobs cannot be reattached after restart
findings.detail: The resume predicate accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. In-place targeted retries, full retries, and timeout reruns are nevertheless persisted and left running during shutdown. On restart, the engine enters the initial gate path, rejects the retry handle, cancels its running job, and starts the suite again. This omits the requested restart support for targeted retries.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress to resume the recorded purpose directly, and allow matching in-place retry handles to reattach.
findings.failure_scenario: Restart the daemon while an in-place baseline-retry-targeted or regression-retry-targeted job is running. The resumed engine cancels that job and reruns earlier gates instead of receiving its result.

findings.title: Worktree exclusion is not enforced when leasing
findings.detail: The lease transaction checks only the selected job's queued state. The worktree check in lanExecutor.start happens before awaiting slot release, saving the handle, and enqueuing the job. Two concurrent starts can both observe no existing job and subsequently enqueue jobs for the same cwd. Separate executor processes can then lease both because neither lease checks for another running or unconfirmed-stopped job in that worktree.
findings.suggestion: Enforce worktree exclusion atomically at the database lease boundary, including jobs whose stopped flag remains zero.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent executeGate calls target the same worktree and both finish start before either attaches. Both jobs are enqueued; two executor processes lease them and run checks concurrently in the shared files.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor can block a run forever
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID birth identity; there is no heartbeat timestamp or freshness check. After a running job's lease expires, sweep marks it failed, but waitStopped keeps waiting while that executor process exists. A stalled executor never acknowledges cancellation, and this wait has no deadline. Thus lease expiry does not lead to either fallback or a reported stop-confirmation failure.
findings.suggestion: Track executor responsiveness and bound stop acknowledgement. If shutdown cannot be confirmed, report a clear failure rather than waiting indefinitely; preserve the process-stop barrier before fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor stalls after leasing a job while its process remains alive. Its lease expires, but the daemon waits indefinitely in waitStopped and never completes or falls back.

findings.title: LAN configuration bypasses the enabled executor for local repositories
findings.detail: The inplace flag is used only when gates.executor is local. With LAN routing configured, repositories outside workers.repos take lanExecutor's local.start fallback directly, even when executor.enabled is true and a matching executor is available. Those local gates still run inside the daemon and are lost on restart.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local-repository branch through the enabled in-place executor, retaining in-process execution when it is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure gates.executor='lan', workers.repos=['owner/remote'], and executor.enabled=true. Run gates for another repository with a live local executor. They execute in the daemon and restart from scratch after daemon shutdown.

structured.summary: Found four defects in restart recovery, retry state, liveness, and worktree exclusion. Isolated source probes reproduced three failures. The targeted test file could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Enforce worktree exclusion inside the lease transaction
findings.detail: leaseInplace checks only the selected job's state, allowing two executors to lease different jobs for the same cwd. The start-time scan is separated from enqueue by awaits and checkpoint persistence, so concurrent starts can both pass it. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-probes.ts"` against the extracted WorkerStore implementation produced `same-worktree leases: job-1 job-2` and `concurrently leased jobs: 2`.
findings.suggestion: Make worktree admission atomic and refuse a lease while another job for the canonical worktree is running or has an unconfirmed stop.
findings.failure_scenario: Two starts for one worktree pass the scan before either enqueues. Two executor processes then lease the resulting jobs and run checks concurrently in that worktree.

findings.title: Preserve setup scratch across retry jobs
findings.detail: Each executeGate call creates and deletes its own command scratch. In-place retries are separate jobs, but freshCheckoutFor returns false, causing retryFailures to omit setup. Consequently HOME, TMPDIR, and package-cache state created by setup disappear before the retry. The scratch probe in `bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-probes.ts"` printed `retry retains setup scratch: false`.
findings.suggestion: Retain owned scratch across the initial execution and its retries, or explicitly recreate the setup state required by each retry.
findings.failure_scenario: Setup writes a required configuration file under HOME. A check fails transiently; its retry skips setup and runs with a new HOME, so it fails because the configuration is missing.

findings.title: Resume matching retry jobs instead of cancelling them
findings.detail: The purpose allowlist excludes every targeted retry, full retry, and timeout rerun. Even an otherwise matching live in-place handle is cancelled and its worktree cleaned. The source probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-inplace-probes.ts"` produced `matching retry handle resumed: undefined` and `matching retry handle cancelled: true` for regression-retry-targeted.
findings.suggestion: Persist sufficient attempt state to resume retry purposes and route resumed stages back to the recorded attempt.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts during a long targeted retry. The resumed stage cancels that surviving job and starts the initial gates again, repeating completed work.

findings.title: Track executor freshness separately from process existence
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID birth identity. There is no heartbeat timestamp or freshness expiry. A stalled executor remains available indefinitely; after its job lease expires, waitStopped still sees its live PID and waits forever rather than reaching recovery or a bounded refusal.
findings.suggestion: Implement executor heartbeat freshness and bounded handling of expired leases whose owner remains alive, while preserving process-stop confirmation before fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor stalls while holding a leased gate. The lease expires and the daemon attempts fallback or restart recovery, but waitStopped loops indefinitely because the executor process still exists.

findings.title: Executor availability never expires while its process exists
findings.detail: Availability checks only PID birth identity; there is no executor heartbeat or freshness timestamp. A nonresponsive executor remains eligible indefinitely. Once its job lease expires, fallback waits in waitStopped forever because that method also treats process existence as responsiveness.
findings.suggestion: Track executor freshness and apply the requested freshness rules. On expiry, fail closed with bounded stop confirmation rather than waiting indefinitely or starting overlapping gates.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor leases a long gate and then its event loop stalls while its process remains alive. The lease expires, but the daemon cannot complete fallback, cancellation, or restart recovery.

findings.title: Restart attachment excludes every retry purpose
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial, and rebase handles can survive resume. Targeted retries, full retries, and timeout reruns are explicitly rejected even when their stage, round, SHA, environment, release, and lease match. The engine's initial-purpose resume call cancels those surviving jobs and starts the stage's gates again, contrary to the requested coverage of targeted retries.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress to resume the recorded purpose and attach to its existing job. Add a restart test during a targeted retry that verifies its command runs once.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor runs a regression-retry-targeted or baseline-retry-targeted job. Resume cancels that job and reruns earlier checks instead of receiving its result.

findings.title: Unconfirmed cleanup leaves callers waiting forever
findings.detail: When cleanup leaves discovery or cleanup records behind, the executor leaves stopped=0 but continues polling with its registration intact. waitStopped only attempts recovery when the executor process disappears, so a responsive executor that has already abandoned this job can leave fallback and mismatch cancellation waiting forever. No remaining code retries this job's cleanup or reports the unconfirmed stop to the waiter.
findings.suggestion: Persist and surface an explicit cleanup failure, or perform bounded cleanup recovery before acknowledging termination. Ensure waiters receive an actionable failure while keeping the worktree blocked.
findings.failure_scenario: Gate termination fails to confirm that a descendant stopped. The job becomes failed, the executor returns to its idle loop, and the daemon waits indefinitely for stopped=1 despite the executor no longer processing that job.

findings.title: Confinement uses the executor's environment
findings.detail: Passing req.env to executeGate does not preserve the daemon's confinement. cfg.readPolicy captures the executor's environment, and homeReadPolicy derives toolchain allowances and credential denies from that captured environment. For example, a daemon using RUSTUP_HOME under its home can enqueue the correct environment, yet the executor denies access to that toolchain because it allows its own RUSTUP_HOME instead.
findings.suggestion: Carry the daemon's trusted confinement inputs with the job and apply them per execution, preserving credential-path denies as well as toolchain allowances.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon and executor have different RUSTUP_HOME values under the home directory. A Rust gate passes in-process but fails through the executor because the requested toolchain is read-denied.

findings.title: Matching targeted retries are never reattached
findings.detail: The purpose allowlist rejects every targeted retry, even when stage, round, purpose, SHA, release, environment, and lease match. The engine also resumes through the initial purpose, so a restart cancels the surviving retry and repeats the initial suite. An isolated probe of this function with a matching regression-retry-targeted handle returned `CANCELLED\nundefined`.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress to resume the recorded retry and reattach its handle instead of restarting the initial execution.
findings.failure_scenario: Restart the daemon while an executor is running regression-retry-targeted. The resumed stage cancels that job and starts initial gates again, repeating work the request explicitly requires to survive.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor blocks cancellation indefinitely
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID birth identity; there is no heartbeat freshness. Once a leased job expires, fallback waits in waitStopped, which never recovers or refuses while that PID remains alive. discard calls it without an abort signal or deadline. A suspended or wedged executor therefore leaves restart, mismatch cancellation, and fallback waiting indefinitely despite lease expiry.
findings.suggestion: Track executor responsiveness and bound stop confirmation. When stop cannot be confirmed, fail closed with a clear error rather than waiting indefinitely or starting overlapping gates.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor leases a gate and then becomes unresponsive while its process remains alive. After lease expiry or a resumed SHA mismatch, the daemon waits forever for stopped=1 and never completes fallback.

findings.failure_scenario: An executor leases a gate and then becomes unresponsive while its process remains alive. After lease expiry or a resumed SHA mismatch, the daemon waits forever for stopped=1 and never completes fallback.

Reviewed identity routing, token handling, approval checks and key confinement. Found an agent-readable private-key path and incomplete startup readability validation. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies were missing; standalone isolation probes confirmed the key-protection gap. No files were modified.

Found two security defects in identity selection and private-key isolation. Targeted suites could not load because dependencies entities and the MCP SDK are missing; dependency-free probes confirmed the repository-selection error.

findings.title: Protect the configured private key from agent reads
findings.detail: Absolute paths and paths outside configDir are accepted, but the key is never registered with protectPrivateFile or added to readPolicy.denyRead. Tool-enabled agents run as the same OS user, so mode 0600 does not prevent them from reading it. Standalone probes returned `key protected: false`, `external key explicitly denied: false`, and `agent reads restricted to allowlist: false`. This violates the requirement that the App key never reach an agent.
findings.suggestion: Register the configured key's canonical and configured paths with the shared private-file protection mechanism before agents or gates start, retaining protection for the provider's lifetime.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure private_key_path as an absolute path such as ~/app.pem outside the config directory. A tool-enabled editor reads that file and obtains the App private key.

findings.title: Confirm the daemon can read the key during startup
findings.detail: The validation checks stat metadata and the file owner's read bit, but never checks readability by the daemon. A regular 0600 file owned by another user passes this check even though readFileSync will fail. Startup succeeds, and the first configured GitHub operation fails later with the generic signing error, contrary to the required startup refusal.
findings.suggestion: Verify actual readability during configuration validation and report an actionable startup error when the daemon cannot read the key.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator installs the key using sudo, leaving it owned by root with mode 0600. The unprivileged daemon accepts the configuration but cannot obtain an App token when work begins.

findings.title: Argument values can silently select the owner's identity
findings.detail: githubRepo searches every argument for --repo or -R, including option values. mergePullRequest passes the PR description as --body, so a description equal to --repo makes githubRepo return the following --match-head-commit argument instead of the repository in the PR URL. The provider then selects the owner's login. Confirmed with: sed -n '105,114p' src/integrations/github-identity.ts | bun -e 'const js = new Bun.Transpiler({loader:"ts"}).transformSync(await Bun.stdin.text()).replace("export ", ""); const repo = new Function(`${js};return githubRepo` )(); console.log(repo(["pr","merge","https://github.com/o/r/pull/1","--body","--repo","--match-head-commit","abc"]));' Output: --match-head-commit.
findings.suggestion: Pass the repository explicitly from repository-aware callers, including mergePullRequest, rather than deriving authentication from arbitrary command arguments.
findings.failure_scenario: An App-configured repository has a PR whose entire description is --repo. Factory merge inspection uses the App, but the actual merge runs with the owner's credentials.

findings.title: Private keys outside the config directory remain readable by agents
findings.detail: The configuration accepts absolute key paths and relative paths escaping configDir, but never adds the resolved key to the confinement deny list or protectPrivateFile registry. configureReadPolicy only protects configDir and existing credential locations. A mode-0600 key elsewhere is readable by agents running as the same user; the dummy GH_TOKEN does not protect the key file. This violates the requirement that the key never reach agents or gates.
findings.suggestion: Register the configured key's canonical and configured paths as private before launching agents or gates, using the existing private-file protection mechanism.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure private_key_path as /opt/factory-key.pem, owned by the daemon user with mode 0600. Startup accepts it, but an agent can read that path because it is outside the protected config directory and other credential denies.

findings.title: Validate key paths consistently at startup and exchange
findings.detail: Startup uses statSync, which follows symlinks, while signingKey opens with O_NOFOLLOW and rejects them. findings.title: Validate key ownership and readability before startup succeeds
findings.detail: Startup only checks stat metadata and permission bits. It never verifies ownership or opens the key. A regular 0600 file belonging to another user therefore passes configuration loading, although signingKey later rejects it or cannot open it. The daemon can start with unusable App authentication, contrary to the required startup refusal.
findings.suggestion: Share the descriptor-based key validation with configuration loading so startup checks ownership and actual readability, while retaining validation when signing.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator configures a root-owned 0600 private key after copying it with sudo. The unprivileged daemon accepts the configuration and starts, but every App GitHub operation fails when it first attempts to read the key.

findings.title: Authentication retries can still finish as a stuck implementation round
findings.detail: The captured fixture contains structured system/api_retry authentication failures, but the parser ignores them. If the CLI stalls or times out while retrying the rejected login, runClaude returns timeout/stuck without failureClass. Context.invoke can return that as a task result, and the engine commits and runs checks on unchanged code. Even an already-parsed assistant authentication rejection is lost because timeout/stuck returns precede this classification. A targeted probe confirmed the retry event is ignored: `bun -e 'import { ClaudeStreamParser } from "./src/harness/claude.ts"; const p = new ClaudeStreamParser(() => {}); p.feed(JSON.stringify({type:"system",subtype:"api_retry",error_status:401,error:"authentication_failed"})); console.log(JSON.stringify({authenticationFailed:p.authenticationFailed}));'` outputs `{"authenticationFailed":false}`.
findings.suggestion: Track structured authentication rejection during API retries, clear it when subsequent successful session activity proves recovery, and preserve authentication classification when an unrecovered rejection ends through timeout or idle termination. Keep explicit caller cancellation authoritative.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude emits system/api_retry with error_status 401 and error authentication_failed, then waits through retries until the invocation or idle timeout fires before an assistant/result event. The unauthenticated attempt returns timeout/stuck, bypasses authentication fallback, and consumes an implementation round.

Found four lifecycle and re-approval defects. Targeted tests could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency. Isolated bun probes reproduced the ordering, repeated-event, failed-write, and disabled-queue behaviors.

findings.title: Persist lifecycle events before their status disappears
findings.detail: Comments are derived from current status, and become durable only when the poll reaches their POST. A failure or needs_human transition followed by resolution before polling is permanently omitted. Earlier comment failures can also prevent recording these events. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review-probe.ts". The probe executed the transpiled lifecycle function with fake dependencies and produced {"failureComments":0,"labels":[]} after running → failed → resolved between polls.
findings.suggestion: Record publication-safe lifecycle events durably when transitions occur, then let polling deliver and checkpoint those events independently of current status.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails and the owner resolves it before the next queue poll, or before polling recovers from an earlier comment failure. No failure comment is ever posted.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates incorrectly require queue enrollment
findings.detail: lifecycleManaged requires githubQueue.trusted and repository membership, and the reconciler runs only from startIssueQueue. Consequently, CLI, MCP, label-triggered and comment-triggered runs outside enabled queue repositories receive no lifecycle labels. Legacy notifier comments do not implement the required label changes or durable retries. The request explicitly covers every start path without imposing queue enrollment.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission and cover all supported issue-linked runs.
findings.failure_scenario: With githubQueue disabled, an owner starts limitless run with Closes #7. Starting, failing, cancelling and merging the run never update issue #7's lifecycle labels.

findings.title: Use timeline order when label timestamps are equal
findings.detail: The new guard compares timestamps strictly and discards timeline ordering. GitHub label events can share a second-resolution timestamp, so a trusted priority application ordered after failure is rejected. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/issue-approval-review-probe.ts". The probe executed the extracted eligibility function with failure followed by trusted priority at the same timestamp and returned {"eligible":false,"reason":"factory status requires priority re-approval after failure"}.
findings.suggestion: Determine whether the trusted priority event follows the latest failure event using timeline order, including timestamp ties.
findings.failure_scenario: The failure label and a subsequent trusted priority application occur within the same second. The issue remains ineligible despite the required re-approval.

findings.title: Failed CLI-linked issues can be picked again when label writes fail
findings.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation can remove in-progress and then fail to add failed. Selection proceeds in the same poll. latestIssueRun only finds issue source references, so a failed CLI or MCP run linked through Closes #n supplies neither a claim nor a latest-run re-approval barrier. An isolated bun probe produced {"eligible":true,"priority":1} after rejecting the failure-label write.
findings.suggestion: Include all linked start paths in the existing durable latest-run eligibility check, so re-approval does not depend on a successful GitHub write.
findings.failure_scenario: An approved issue is implemented through a CLI run containing Closes #1. The run fails, removing in-progress succeeds, and adding failed fails. The queue immediately starts another run using the original approval.

findings.title: Lifecycle events are lost or suppressed across status episodes
findings.detail: Events are inferred only from the current status, and comment checkpoints are keyed by status for the entire run. A needs_human transition resolved before the next poll is never recorded. After one needs_human comment completes, subsequent needs_human episodes skip their comments at line 114. An isolated bun probe traversing running → needs_human → running → needs_human posted only the first reason; a between-poll episode posted nothing.
findings.suggestion: Durably record lifecycle events and their reasons when transitions occur, with a checkpoint per event episode, and let polling deliver those records.
findings.failure_scenario: A run requests human help, resumes, and later requests help for a different reason. The issue receives the needs-you label again but no comment explaining the new reason. A restart or resolution before polling can also erase an unobserved event entirely.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates require opting the repository into queue admission
findings.detail: lifecycleManaged rejects repositories outside githubQueue.repos or without trusted queue accounts, and reconciliation is only scheduled by startIssueQueue. Consequently CLI, MCP, label-triggered, and comment-triggered runs receive no lifecycle labels unless queue admission is enabled for their repository. The request requires lifecycle updates for every start path and does not impose this prerequisite. An isolated bun probe with githubQueue=null produced zero lifecycle writes.
findings.suggestion: Schedule lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission and manage issue-linked runs regardless of whether their repository accepts automatic queue picks.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner starts limitless run with Closes #1 in a repository that is not configured for automatic issue picking. No in-progress, needs-you, or failed labels are ever written.

findings.title: Timestamp comparison ignores the order of same-second label events
findings.detail: Re-approval requires createdAt to be strictly greater than the failure timestamp. GitHub label events can share a second-resolution timestamp even when the trusted priority application follows the failure event in the timeline. The requested event-order rule should accept that approval. An isolated bun probe with ordered failure and trusted approval events sharing a timestamp returned {"eligible":false,"reason":"factory status requires priority re-approval after failure"}.
findings.suggestion: Use timeline order to distinguish label events whose timestamps tie, retaining the trusted-actor check.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory applies failed and the owner reapplies a priority label later in the same second. Both events have the same createdAt value, so the issue remains ineligible despite the later approval.

Found missing lifecycle events, omitted reasons, suppressed fallback comments, and incomplete start-path coverage. Targeted tests could not start because dependencies are absent (`entities` was the first missing package). Dependency-isolated probes exercised the lifecycle function with fake collaborators.

Reviewed the diff, persistence, polling, and notifier paths. Dependency-free probes confirmed lost transitions, omitted reasons, and missing fallback comments. Targeted tests (`bun test test/issue-queue.test.ts test/github-notifier.test.ts`) could not start because dependency `entities` is unavailable.

findings.title: Transitions between polls are permanently lost
findings.detail: Lifecycle effects are created from the current run snapshot, rather than durably recorded when transitions occur. If a run fails or reaches needs_human and is resolved before the next poll, its notification is never checkpointed or delivered. The legacy notifier also suppresses these managed runs. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts"`. Output for `failed then resolved between polls` contained only the started comment and `"failedCheckpoint":null`.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle events durably alongside run transitions, then let polling deliver those recorded effects.
findings.failure_scenario: After one poll, a run transitions running → failed → resolved before the next poll. GitHub never receives the failure notification, including after a restart.

findings.title: Failure and needs-you comments never include the reason
findings.detail: Both comments contain only fixed status text and a UI link, even when the reason is safe to publish. This omits an explicit requirement. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts"`. With error `Gate failed: typecheck`, output was `Limitless run run-1 failed: see https://example.com/runs/run-1.` and the effect was marked done. The added tests explicitly assert that reasons are absent.
findings.suggestion: Include the recorded reason after credential redaction and publication checking; use fixed text when the check blocks it.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails because typechecking failed, or needs owner input for a specific decision. Issue watchers receive no explanation despite the reason containing no private information.

findings.title: Publication rejection permanently suppresses the required fallback
findings.detail: When publication checking rejects a body, the catch marks the comment done without posting anything. The delivery-time check repeats this behavior. The request requires a fixed public fallback instead. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/issue-lifecycle-review.ts"`. With a publication checker rejecting the UI URL, output was `"bodies":[]` and `"needsHumanCheckpoint":"done"`.
findings.suggestion: Checkpoint and deliver a checked fixed fallback that excludes the rejected text and URL; mark it done only after successful delivery or deduplication.
findings.failure_scenario: The configured UI hostname matches a private string. A needs_human run receives its label but no comment, and later polls never retry a fallback.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates require issue-queue enrollment
findings.detail: lifecycleManaged restricts all effects to githubQueue.repos with a nonempty trusted list, and the reconciler runs only through startIssueQueue. Consequently, CLI, MCP, label, and comment-triggered issue runs outside that queue receive no lifecycle labels or durable comments. The request specifies these updates for any start path without requiring queue enrollment.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle delivery independently of queue admission and cover issue-linked runs in repositories using the other supported start paths.
findings.failure_scenario: With github.queue unset, an owner starts `limitless run` with `Closes #7`. The PR gains the closing directive, but the issue receives no in-progress, needs-you, failed, or cancellation updates.

findings.title: Persist lifecycle events when transitions occur
findings.detail: Events are derived only from the current status during polling. Neither updateRun nor resolveRun records lifecycle effects. A transition that ends before the next poll disappears permanently, including across a restart. findings.detail: After mergeForDelivery succeeds, run.baseSha points to the fetched base, while lastVerifiedSha still identifies the pre-merge implementation. Workflow changes introduced only by the newer base then appear as factory edits or deletions, causing a DeliveryHeadError and preventing the verified-work draft.
findings.suggestion: Check the fallback SHA against its recorded verification baseline, or an appropriate common ancestor, while retaining the independent workflow check on the exact outgoing SHA.

Delivery then encounters an error before opening the PR and attempts its pre-merge verified-work draft. Comparing that commit with the updated run.baseSha reports the base's workflow change as an ungranted factory change and refuses the draft.

findings.suggestion: Persist the rejection checkpoint while retaining a recoverable run status, then mark needs_human after rollback completes. Alternatively, explicitly recover terminal runs with unfinished rejection cleanup. Exercise this through scheduler restart.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after the rejection updateRun commits but before reset, or immediately after reset before clean and the rollback state save. On startup, the run remains needs_human and is never scheduled; the checkout, headSha, and pending merge fields remain partially rolled back indefinitely.

output.summary:
Reviewed the diff, transaction handling, webhook routing, and queue polling. Isolated probes reproduced two defects. The targeted test suite could not load because dependencies were missing; git diff --check passed.

Found two command-filtering defects, reproduced with isolated tests against the actual queue implementation. The repository test file could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is missing; direct imports also encountered missing entities. No repository files were modified.

findings.title: Identity lookup failure disables the factory-author exclusion
findings.detail: An identity error becomes null, so bot is null and the factory-author comparison cannot match. Slash commands still proceed, including commands authored by the factory bot when that login is trusted. This violates the requirement that factory-authored commands never run. Isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/q1c-review-probe.ts"` produced `{"author":"factory[bot]","body":"/limitless do it","runs":1}` with an identity lookup that throws.
findings.suggestion: Leave comments retryable when the posting identity cannot be established, or retain a verified bot identity that still permits excluding factory authors.
findings.failure_scenario: The queue trusts factory[bot], its unedited slash command is newer than the enable boundary, and the posting-identity lookup fails after the issue query succeeds.

findings.title: Marker substring silently rejects valid owner requests
findings.detail: Any occurrence of `<!-- limitless-` rejects the entire command, even when a trusted human is asking to change or remove that marker. Body content does not establish that the factory posted the comment. Isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/q1c-review-probe.ts"` produced `{"author":"owner","body":"/limitless remove the <!-- limitless- marker","runs":0}` for an otherwise eligible comment.
findings.suggestion: Exclude factory comments using verified authorship or recorded comment identities rather than an arbitrary substring in the request.
findings.failure_scenario: A trusted owner posts an unedited command after the boundary whose request contains the factory marker prefix, such as `/limitless remove the <!-- limitless- marker`.

findings.title: Do not discard owner commands that quote factory markers
findings.detail: The substring filter rejects valid requests mentioning factory markup anywhere in their text. Factory authorship cannot be inferred from a marker quoted by a trusted human. Reproduction command: bun test "$TMPDIR/comment-command-review.test.ts". The test "owner request quoting a factory marker is actionable" failed with "Expected: 1; Received: 0".
findings.suggestion: Use posting identity to exclude factory comments rather than rejecting arbitrary marker text inside a trusted user's request.
findings.failure_scenario: After the enable boundary, the owner posts an unedited '/limitless fix handling of <!-- limitless-status -->' command. Every poll silently skips it.

findings.title: Preserve the factory-author exclusion when identity lookup fails
findings.detail: Identity errors are swallowed and bot becomes null, disabling the factory-author check while slash commands remain actionable. A factory bot included in trusted can therefore start a run despite the explicit author exclusion. Reproduction command: bun test "$TMPDIR/comment-command-review.test.ts". The test "identity failure must not admit the factory bot" failed with "Expected: 0; Received: 1".
findings.suggestion: Leave commands retryable when the posting identity cannot be established, or retain a previously verified bot identity for the exclusion.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory bot is trusted, a post-boundary slash command exists under its login, and identity resolution fails after the issue query succeeds—for example during token refresh. The poll admits the bot's command instead of excluding it.

findings.title: Valid requests containing a factory marker are silently discarded
findings.detail: The substring check rejects a command whenever its request mentions `<!-- limitless-`, even when a trusted human authored it. This adds an exclusion beyond the requested author, edit, and boundary checks. An isolated probe using the actual queue implementation, run with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-comment-filter.ts"`, printed `ordinary command runs: 1` and `trusted request containing marker runs: 0`.
findings.suggestion: Identify factory comments by a structured marker in its expected position or recorded posting identity, rather than rejecting marker text anywhere in the request.
findings.failure_scenario: After the enable boundary, the trusted owner posts an unedited `/limitless Fix parsing of <!-- limitless-status --> comments` command on an open issue. Every poll skips it.

findings.title: Identity lookup failure disables the factory-author exclusion
findings.detail: Catching an identity error and substituting null makes `bot` null, so the factory-author comparison cannot reject its own comments. Slash commands still proceed and can be permanently consumed. The isolated probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-comment-filter.ts"` printed `factory slash command with unavailable identity runs: 1`. A production trigger is an identity refresh failing after the issue query succeeds.
findings.suggestion: Keep factory-author identification available independently of token refresh, or leave commands retryable when the posting identity cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory App login is in the trusted list, its unedited slash command is newer than the boundary, and identity lookup fails after the comments are fetched. The poll creates a run for the factory's own comment, contrary to invariant 2.

findings.title: Queue routing silently swallows pull request comment commands
findings.detail: The new branch intercepts every issue_comment delivery in queue repositories, including PR conversation comments. The queue queries issues only, so these commands never run. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/q1c-review-probe.ts". Output: builder accepts PR comment: true; {"status":200,"body":"Issue queue poll requested","runs":0,"hints":1}.
findings.suggestion: Exclude payloads with issue.pull_request from queue interception and preserve their existing webhook behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner posts /limitless fix this PR on a pull request in a configured queue repository. Its webhook is acknowledged but no run starts.

findings.title: Identity lookup failure disables factory-author exclusion
findings.detail: An identity error becomes null, making bot null and allowing slash commands from the factory bot when that login is trusted. This violates the requirement to exclude factory-authored commands. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/q1c-review-probe.ts". Output: identity failure: 1 runs.
findings.suggestion: Leave commands retryable when the posting identity cannot be established, or retain a verified bot login independently of token refresh.
findings.failure_scenario: A healthy issue response contains an unedited slash command by a trusted factory bot, but the subsequent identity lookup fails. The poll creates a run from the factory's own command.

findings.title: Substring filtering discards valid requests containing marker text
findings.detail: Any occurrence of <!-- limitless- causes the entire command to be skipped, including literal text in a legitimate owner's request. Probe command: bun "$TMPDIR/q1c-review-probe.ts". Output: normal: 1 runs; marker: 0 runs.
findings.suggestion: Identify factory comments using verified authorship or a precise generated-comment structure rather than an unrestricted substring.
findings.failure_scenario: A trusted owner posts /limitless remove the <!-- limitless-status --> marker after the boundary. The unedited command is silently skipped on every poll.

Found two durability/finalization defects. The classifier and storage tests passed (34 tests), including Homebrew SQLite migration coverage. Pipeline tests and the replay probe could not load because the checkout lacks the entities dependency.

Reviewed durability, classification, attribution and restart paths. Found a completed-result replay gap across deployments. Targeted tests produced 34 passes; worker and pipeline tests could not load because the checkout lacks the entities package.

findings.title: Record the gates stage's round instead of the implementation round
findings.detail: Initial verify-change execution calls oneRound(ctx, -1, null), while ctx.state.round remains 0. Observations therefore receive round 0, but the completion callback finalizes round -1 and skips them. They eventually receive interrupted terminal classifications instead of the completed stage's classification. Targeted command: bun -e 'import {Store} from "./src/db/store.ts"; const s=new Store(":memory:"); s.db.run("INSERT INTO failure_observations (run_id,repo,stage_id,round,sha,handle_kind,handle_id,phase,name,command,observed_at,timed_out,confinement,duration_ms,failed_files,output_tail,signature,setup_eligible) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)", ["r","o/r",1,0,"head","local","h","check","test","bun test",0,0,0,1,"[]","error: failed","sig",0]); s.transaction(()=>s.observations.finalize("r",{round:-1,sha:"head",stageId:1,comparisons:[{name:"test",verdict:"regressed",blocking:true,result:{name:"test",command:"bun test",ok:false,exitCode:1,durationMs:1,output:"error: failed"}}]}),true); console.log(JSON.stringify(s.failureObservations().map(({round,class:c,history})=>({round,class:c,history})))); s.close();' Output: [{"round":0,"class":null,"history":null}].
findings.suggestion: Capture the active stage's round for observations and add an initial verify-change integration case that verifies completion finalizes its rows.
findings.failure_scenario: A verify-change run's initial gates stage fails, or times out and subsequently passes. Its stage completes at round -1, but its observations remain unfinalized at round 0.

findings.title: Replay completed in-place results before applying execution compatibility checks
findings.detail: The evidence replay path still requires executor.canResume(). The production in-place implementation requires the job request's releaseSha to equal the current release, even when the job is already done and has a stored result. After a deploy, this rejects a completed handle, clears it, and starts another execution without recording the previous result. The new tests replace canResume with an unconditional true, so they miss this production path.
findings.suggestion: Record a completed job's stored result before deciding whether its execution environment can resume. Keep compatibility checks for continuing live work.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place gate finishes with a failure, the daemon stops before the evidence checkpoint, and a newer release resumes the run. The stored result is discarded; if the replacement execution passes, the original failure has no observation.

findings.title: Replay completed in-place results before enforcing execution compatibility
findings.detail: Resume still gates completed in-place jobs on canResume, which requires the original release SHA, environment and daemon port to match. After a deploy, it rejects the stored handle, clears it and re-executes without recording the completed result. This violates the required replay-before-re-execution guarantee. The new tests mask this by supplying canResume: () => true. A targeted probe of the production predicate returned false for a done job from an older release. Exact command: bun -e 'const s=await Bun.file("src/gates/lan.ts").text(); const f=s.slice(s.indexOf("(h, env, daemonPort) => {"),s.indexOf("\n      : undefined,")); const js=new Bun.Transpiler({loader:"ts"}).transformSync(`const f=${f};`); const workers={releaseSha:"new",job:()=>({in_place:1,state:"done",request:JSON.stringify({releaseSha:"old"})})}; console.log(new Function("workers",`${js}; return f({id:"done-job"});`)(workers));' Output: false.
findings.suggestion: Replay and checkpoint a validated completed job's stored result before applying compatibility checks needed for continued execution. Add a restart test using the production resume predicate with a changed release SHA.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place primary execution finishes with a failure, then the daemon stops before the evidence insert. A new release resumes the run. Its different build SHA causes canResume to reject the completed job; a passing replacement execution leaves the original failure without an observation.

findings.detail: Initial verify-change execution calls oneRound(ctx, -1, null), while ctx.state.round remains 0. Observations therefore receive round 0, but the completion callback finalizes round -1 and skips them. They eventually receive interrupted terminal classifications instead of the completed stage's classification. findings.title: Replay completed in-place results before applying execution compatibility checks
findings.detail: The evidence replay path still requires executor.canResume(). The production in-place implementation requires the job request's releaseSha to equal the current release, even when the job is already done and has a stored result. After a deploy, this rejects a completed handle, clears it, and starts another execution without recording the previous result. The new tests replace canResume with an unconditional true, so they miss this production path.
findings.suggestion: Record a completed job's stored result before deciding whether its execution environment can resume. Keep compatibility checks for continuing live work.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place gate finishes with a failure, the daemon stops before the evidence checkpoint, and a newer release resumes the run. The stored result is discarded; if the replacement execution passes, the original failure has no observation.

findings.title: Replay completed in-place results before applying execution compatibility checks
findings.detail: Completed in-place jobs still pass through canResume, which requires the stored request's release SHA, environment, and daemon port to match the current daemon. After a deployment or environment change, this rejects even a job with a durable result. The following branch clears its handle without observing that result, then permits a fresh execution. This violates the requirement to replay an unrecorded completed result before re-execution.
findings.suggestion: Record a completed job's stored result before applying compatibility checks needed to continue unfinished execution. Preserve its original execution identity.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place gate finishes with a failure, and the daemon dies before the evidence checkpoint. A new release resumes the run. canResume rejects the old release SHA, the handle is discarded, and a passing fresh execution leaves no observation of the completed failure.

findings.title: Do not assign a later execution's timeout history to earlier observations
findings.detail: earlierStage only changes history when the final result passes. Otherwise, an older non-timeout failure inherits rerun_failed from the resumed execution's timeout rerun. classifyObservation then returns unclassified for that ordinary regression because its regression rule accepts only no_retry or retry_failed. Targeted command: bun -e 'import { observationHistory,classifyObservation } from "./src/gates/failure-class.ts"; const r={name:"test",command:"test",ok:false,exitCode:1,durationMs:1,output:"failed"}; const c={name:"test",verdict:"regressed",blocking:true,result:{...r,firstAttempt:{...r,timedOut:true}}}; const history=observationHistory(c,true); console.log(JSON.stringify({history,class:classifyObservation({confinement:0,setup_eligible:0,timed_out:0,history},c)}));' Output: {"history":"rerun_failed","class":"unclassified"}.
findings.suggestion: Derive history relative to the observed execution. An earlier ordinary failure followed by a failed resumed execution should retain a history that classifies it as regression.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-timeout regression is recorded, followed by a crash before stage completion. On resume, the initial check times out and its timeout rerun fails normally with output naming a changed file, preventing another retry. Finalization incorrectly classifies the original regression as unclassified.

findings.detail: Completed in-place jobs still pass through canResume, which requires the recorded release SHA, environment and daemon port to match current values even when the job is already done. This violates the new requirement that an unrecorded durable result replay before re-execution.
findings.suggestion: Separate replay eligibility for completed results from compatibility checks for live execution. Record the completed job's evidence under its original handle before discarding or replacing that handle.
findings.failure_scenario: An in-place primary gate completes with a failure, then the daemon stops before the evidence insert. A new release resumes the run. Reviewed install, deploy, rollback, recovery, and executor release handling. Confirmed a service-kind misclassification with a targeted probe. Targeted test files could not run because installed dependencies lack entities and Zod's prefault API.

findings.title: Do not classify migration kinds by canonical labels
findings.detail: isExecutor returns true when old.label is dev.limitless.executor even if old.kind is explicitly daemon. installedUnits permits arbitrary labels, so this is a valid recognized daemon. On replacement failure, restore consequently shuts down and disables both daemon labels, restores the old plist without bootstrapping it, and recovery continues treating its journal as an executor journal. This leaves the daemon unavailable instead of restoring it. Targeted command: bun -e 'const s = await Bun.file("src/cli/service.ts").text(); const body = s.split("const isExecutor = async (state: Migration) =>")[1].split("const reconcileExecutor")[0].trim().slice(0, -1); const f = new (async function() {}).constructor("state", "EXECUTOR_LABEL", "installedUnits", "opts", `return (${body})`); console.log(await f({old:{kind:"daemon",label:"dev.limitless.executor"},label:"dev.limitless.daemon"}, "dev.limitless.executor", async()=>[], {}));' Output: true; expected false.
findings.suggestion: Use the recorded recognized kind when available. For older journals, resolve kind through installedUnits or inspect the backed-up plist rather than inferring it from a label.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon plist uses Label dev.limitless.executor with serve arguments and a daemon marker. service install recognizes it as a daemon, replaces it, and the replacement fails health checking. Restoration misclassifies its migration as executor and leaves the previous daemon unloaded and disabled.

Reviewed the diff, queue admission, linkage tracking and repository resolution. Found a compatibility regression for existing mixed-case repository registrations. Targeted tests could not load because dependencies were missing or incompatible (MCP SDK, entities and Zod).

findings.title: Preserve existing repository identity when canonicalizing queue keys
findings.detail: The lowercased repo now reaches factory.createRun, but resolveRepo and Store.getRepoBySlug still look up slugs case-sensitively. An existing mixed-case registration is bypassed, causing another registration with default settings. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/queue-repo-review.ts". This dependency-free probe executes the extracted resolver with an injected store and remote response. Output showed repoCount:2, mergePolicy changing from "none" to "auto", defaultBranch changing from "release" to "main", and "error: Canonicalized queue request bypasses the existing repository and its settings".
findings.suggestion: Reuse existing GitHub repository registrations case-insensitively before creating a new record, or preserve the configured spelling for run creation while canonicalizing internal queue keys.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository is registered as Owner/Repo with customized settings, and its queue configuration uses Owner/Repo. After upgrading, queue requests use owner/repo and create a second repository record that loses those settings.

findings.title: Avoid querying ownership separately for every historical run each poll
findings.detail: Every poll now loads all historical run prompts across all repositories and calls decision for each. linkedIssues then issues a recursive issueLinkOwner query per run, including unrelated and unlinked runs. A dependency-free in-memory SQLite probe executing the extracted methods with 10,000 terminal runs and 20,800-byte prompts measured synchronous initialization at 244, 231, and 223 ms. This introduces history-dependent event-loop blocking before the first await, even when the queue has no candidates.
findings.suggestion: Batch ownership and linkage resolution, restrict observations to relevant repositories, and avoid loading every historical prompt solely to compare subsequent publications.
findings.failure_scenario: A long-lived daemon accumulates thousands of runs, including runs outside the configured queue repositories. Every queue poll synchronously rereads their prompts and performs one recursive query per run, delaying other daemon work.

findings.title: Canonicalized requests bypass existing mixed-case repository registrations
findings.detail: The lowercase repo now flows into issueRunRequest and commentRunRequest. Factory.createRun passes it to resolveRepo, whose existing-repository lookups use Store.getRepoBySlug with case-sensitive equality. An existing registration such as Owner/Repo is therefore missed, and resolveRepo creates a second registration after calling GitHub. The new record loses the existing repository's mergePolicy and other registered settings.
findings.suggestion: Make repository resolution reuse existing GitHub registrations case-insensitively while preserving their IDs and settings, or resolve the canonical queue key to the existing registration before creating requests.
findings.failure_scenario: Before upgrading, configure queue repository Owner/Repo and register it with mergePolicy 'none'. After upgrading, the queue submits owner/repo. resolveRepo misses Owner/Repo and registers owner/repo using cfg.githubMerge instead, so queued work can use a different delivery policy.

findings.title: Preserve slow-regression classification across stage restarts
findings.detail: A restart creates a new stage ID. findings.title: Resumed executions lose the slow-regression flag
findings.detail: A restart creates a new gates stage ID. When a completed durable execution is reattached, observation insertion conflicts with its existing row and preserves the original stage_id. This filter therefore excludes that execution's observations, leaving observedHandles empty. The selector can return true and perform a successful re-check without recording slow_regression, causing the failure to be classified as flaky instead of load.
findings.suggestion: Identify observations using the resumed execution identity rather than requiring the current stage ID.
findings.failure_scenario: A LAN post-merge primary failure is observed, then the daemon stops before the selector runs while the execution handle remains persisted. After restart, the same completed handle is reattached and its slow-regression re-check passes.

findings.title: Preserve retry history when post-merge gates rerun after restart
findings.detail: Restricting earlierStage handling to initial observations drops D0a's cross-stage recovery semantics for rebase observations. If restart causes a fresh primary execution that passes, the earlier failed observation is finalized with no_retry and class unclassified. The isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-rebase-finalize.ts"`, using the actual finalizer and migrations with privacy/confinement helpers stubbed, printed `{"history":"no_retry","class":"unclassified"}` and failed with `AssertionError: actual 'no_retry', expected 'retry_passed'`.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a fresh passing execution after restart from resuming an already-recorded coordinator confirmation, and preserve retry_passed for the former.
findings.failure_scenario: A post-merge primary failure is inserted and gate-result clears its handle durably. The daemon stops before saving postMergeGates.result. On restart, gates execute again at the same round and SHA and pass; finalization incorrectly records the earlier failure as having no retry.

findings.title: Resumed observations are excluded from slow-regression tracking
findings.detail: A resumed gates stage gets a new stage ID, while the primary observation retains its original stage_id: reinsertion uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Filtering by ctx.stageId therefore excludes that observation, so the selector never persists slow_regression=1. A passing re-check is then classified as flaky instead of load. Focused reproduction command: bun -e 'const s=await Bun.file("src/pipeline/engine.ts").text(); const a=s.indexOf("const observedHandles ="); const f=new Function("ctx","sha",s.slice(a,s.indexOf("ctx.checkCancelled();",a))+"return observedHandles"); const row={run_id:"r",purpose:"rebase",sha:"s",stage_id:10,handle_id:"job"}; const handles=f({run:{id:"r"},stageId:11,store:{failureObservations:()=>[row]}},"s"); console.log(JSON.stringify(handles)); if(handles.length!==1) throw Error("resumed primary observation excluded");'. Output: [] followed by 'error: resumed primary observation excluded' (exit 1).
findings.suggestion: Select the primary observation using its durable execution identity across stage restarts. Add a restart test between observation insertion and slow-regression selection that verifies a passing re-check produces slow_regression=1 and class=load.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after recording a completed durable post-merge primary failure but before selecting its slow-regression retry. On restart, the same handle resumes in a new stage; its retry passes, but the original observation remains slow_regression=0 and is finalized as flaky.

findings.title: Recovered held leases never enter the renewal loop
findings.detail: The loop visits only the in-memory handles map, populated exclusively by an applied operate() write. Neither startup recovery nor reconciliation adds handles. Confirmed leases therefore receive no renewals after a restart, and an unconfirmed first acquisition reconciled to applied is also omitted. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts". The restart probe failed with Expected: 2, Received: 1 writes; the reconciliation probe failed with Expected: > 1, Received: 1.
findings.suggestion: Populate renewal tracking from confirmed held rows after recovery and reconciliation, without manufacturing an anchor.
findings.failure_scenario: Acquire a lease, recreate the manager using the same store, start with active() returning true, and advance a renewal tick. No renewal occurs, so the lease eventually expires.

findings.title: A pending first acquisition blocks another run before reconciliation
findings.detail: The cross-run guard rejects any row with an intent before reconcile() runs. A never-confirmed acquisition whose write did not apply consequently cannot be dropped and forgotten by the next run's acquire operation. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts". The cross-run probe failed with Expected: "held", Received: "refused".
findings.suggestion: Reconcile pending intents on never-confirmed rows before deciding whether another run is refused, and forget the row when reconciliation drops its acquisition.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A's first acquisition returns unconfirmed without changing the absent ref. A ends. Run B repeatedly calls acquire on that ref; every call returns refused even though reconciliation would establish that A never acquired it.

findings.title: Intent reconciliation bypasses release expiry revalidation
findings.detail: reconcileLeaseIntent can replay a release through client.write without a beforeSend hook. Calling it here, in the loop, or through startup recovery therefore bypasses the manager's time predicates for that same-generation write. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts" --test-name-pattern 'pending release'. The probe failed with Expected: 2, Received: 3 writes: reconciliation sent the expired release.
findings.suggestion: Provide the required time validation for release replay in both reconciliation and startup recovery, including a fresh send-time predicate.
findings.failure_scenario: A release returns unconfirmed while the ref remains at the confirmed held tip. Ten minutes pass. The next operation reconciles the intent and sends the same-generation release without sampling GitHub time or checking whether that generation remains renewable.

findings.title: Recovered and reconciled acquisitions never enter the renewal loop
findings.detail: The loop visits only `handles`, which is populated exclusively by the immediate `applied` write branch. Confirmed leases restored at startup, and acquisitions confirmed later by reconciliation, never enter that map. Consequently, the loop neither calls `active` nor renews them, allowing active leases to expire. Temporary command `bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts"` demonstrated both cases: restored ownership produced `reads: 0, writes: 0, active: 0` and failed `Expected: 1, Received: 0`; a reconciled acquisition likewise failed the expected active-hook call.
findings.suggestion: Register confirmed held ownership after startup recovery and successful reconciliation, or derive renewal candidates from persisted confirmed rows. Preserve the requirement not to manufacture anchors during reconciliation.
findings.failure_scenario: Restart with a confirmed held lease, or let an initial acquisition return unconfirmed and resolve on a loop tick. Start the manager with an active hook returning true. Subsequent ticks never renew that lease.

findings.title: Cross-run rejection bypasses pending-intent reconciliation
findings.detail: An intent belonging to another logical run causes an immediate refusal before `reconcile` executes. Even when GitHub now confirms that the previous acquisition never applied, the new operation cannot drop and forget it. This violates the required reconciliation-first ordering and can keep a failed acquisition blocking the next run. Command `bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts"` reproduced a pending run-A acquisition against an absent ref: run B returned `refused: live` with zero client reads, failing `Expected: "held", Received: "refused"`.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile pending intents before applying the cross-run ownership guard. Return wait while unresolved, and forget a dropped never-confirmed acquisition before deciding the new request.
findings.failure_scenario: Run A's acquisition remains uncertain after a failed send and unreadable confirmation. GitHub becomes readable and reports the ref absent. Run B calls acquire before a background reconciliation tick; it is refused without checking GitHub.

findings.title: Release recovery bypasses the lease-time send guard
findings.detail: Both startup recovery and normal reconciliation receive the raw client. `reconcileLeaseIntent` can replay a pending release through `client.write` without `beforeSend`, bypassing all manager time checks. A release that direct mutation would reject as expired is therefore sent during recovery, including after suspend or a slow commit. Command `bun test "$TMPDIR/lease-review.test.ts"` seeded an unchanged held tip and pending release, advanced time by 11 minutes, and observed one write with the row confirmed released; the assertion failed `Expected: 0, Received: 1`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same fresh GitHub-time decision and send-time revalidation to release replay, covering startup recovery and per-operation or loop reconciliation.
findings.failure_scenario: A release intent is persisted but not sent. The coordinator restarts after the generation expires. Recovery finds the original held tip unchanged and writes the expired generation's release without sampling GitHub time or validating before send.

findings.title: Require successful browser setup evidence before converting blocks
findings.detail: A preview plus the absence of browser_unavailable is treated as successful browser setup. That warning only covers browserMcp configuration failures and remote dispatch. After configuration succeeds, the MCP subprocess can fail to launch or initialize; the harnesses forward those diagnostics as stderr/status/tool errors without emitting browser_unavailable. A verifier can therefore correctly report an infrastructure block and have it converted to unclear, suppressing the environment retry and sending an implementation feedback round instead.

findings.title: Use fixed diagnostic codes for question delivery failures
findings.detail: The question publication error path passes the caught exception to logFailure, which interpolates String(error) and only redacts registered credentials. Configured private strings are not protected here. Identity lookup, POST, or recovery failures can therefore publish private exception content to diagnostics, contrary to requirement 2's explicit prohibition on exception output.
findings.suggestion: Map publication failures to fixed diagnostic codes without interpolating exceptions. Cover identity, POST and recovery failures with exceptions containing configured private strings.
findings.failure_scenario: A waiting run has a safe question, but its identity lookup or gh request throws an error containing a hostname listed in private-strings.txt. The question delivery catch logs that hostname unchanged.

findings.title: Use fixed diagnostics for publication failures
findings.detail: Delivery, identity and recovery errors still reach logFailure as arbitrary exception text. That helper only credential-redacts literal registered values; it does not inspect configured private strings or supported encoded credentials. This violates the fixed-code diagnostic requirement. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/q4-review-probe.ts"`, using injected dependencies, produced `exception output reaches diagnostics: true`.
findings.suggestion: Log fixed failure codes on publication error paths and discard exception output.
findings.failure_scenario: A question POST or identity lookup rejects with an error containing a configured private string, such as a private key path. The exception text is written to lifecycle diagnostics.

findings.title: Recover uncertain POSTs before suppressing their checkpoints
findings.detail: The stored body is inspected before pending.page recovery. If inspection fails, the effect is marked done without searching for its factory-authored marker, even when GitHub may already have accepted the POST. The injected probe command `bun "$TMPDIR/q4-review-probe.ts"` produced `after inspection fails: {"recoveryCalls":0,"state":"done","commentId":null}`. Requirement 4 explicitly requires recovery before closing an uncertain checkpoint.
findings.suggestion: Recover uncertain effects using the independently generated marker and checkpointed identity before applying suppression to any potential new POST.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question comment but its response is lost. Before restart, the private-string configuration changes to match its body, or inspection becomes unavailable. Reconciliation closes the pending checkpoint without recovering the existing comment.

Reviewed the diff, lifecycle recovery, privacy checks and command reservation. The targeted issue-queue tests could not load because dependencies are missing. An isolated source-transpiled lifecycle probe with dependency doubles confirmed repeated oversized POST attempts.

findings.title: Recover uncertain POSTs before suppressing their checkpoints
findings.detail: Body inspection runs before marker recovery. If publication policy changes after GitHub accepts a POST but before local acknowledgement, inspection failure marks the checkpoint done without recovering the accepted comment. This violates the required recovery ordering. An isolated `bun -` probe returned recoveryGETs=0 and checkpoint state=done, page=0, with no commentId.
findings.suggestion: Recover uncertain POSTs using the independently generated marker and checkpointed author before applying checks that decide whether another POST is allowed.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question comment, its response is lost, and private-strings.txt subsequently gains a string present in that body. After restart, the accepted comment is never recovered before its checkpoint closes.

findings.title: Use fixed diagnostics for question delivery failures
findings.detail: The new question delivery path forwards arbitrary exceptions to logFailure, which prints String(error) with credential redaction only. Configured private strings and exception output can therefore enter diagnostics, contrary to the publication requirements. An isolated `bun -` probe with a posting-identity error returned privateTextLeaked=true and logged the protected private-key path.
findings.suggestion: Log fixed failure codes for identity, recovery and POST errors without including exception messages or command output.
findings.failure_scenario: A waiting run reaches posting identity lookup, which throws a GitHubIdentityError containing a configured private-key path also listed in private-strings.txt. The path appears unchanged in lifecycle diagnostics.

findings.title: Bound publication bodies to GitHub's comment size limit
findings.detail: Question text is concatenated without a size bound; needs-human reasons are similarly unbounded. A valid stored question can therefore exceed GitHub's 65,536-character comment limit. The resulting permanent HTTP 422 leaves the effect pending, so subsequent polls recover and retry the identical rejected body indefinitely. Command `bun run -` with an isolated lifecycle source probe and fake gh produced `POST body characters: 66168` three times, followed by `{"posts":3,"recoveryReads":2,"questionCheckpoint":"pending"}`. Repository tests could not load because dependencies are missing.
findings.suggestion: Inspect complete original fields first, then bound the complete outgoing body while preserving its envelope, IDs and UI instructions. Use safe UI-only text when necessary, and test oversized individual fields and combined question sets.
findings.failure_scenario: A waiting linked run has one 66,000-character unanswered question, or several questions whose combined body exceeds 65,536 characters. GitHub rejects every publication attempt; the questions never appear on the issue and the effect retries every poll.

findings.title: Bound publication bodies to GitHub's comment size limit
findings.detail: Question text is concatenated without a size bound; needs-human reasons are similarly unbounded. A valid stored question can therefore exceed GitHub's 65,536-character comment limit. The resulting permanent HTTP 422 leaves the effect pending, so subsequent polls recover and retry the identical rejected body indefinitely. Command `bun run -` with an isolated lifecycle source probe and fake gh produced `POST body characters: 66168` three times, followed by `{"posts":3,"recoveryReads":2,"questionCheckpoint":"pending"}`. Repository tests could not load because dependencies are missing.
findings.suggestion: Inspect complete original fields first, then bound the complete outgoing body while preserving its envelope, IDs and UI instructions. Use safe UI-only text when necessary, and test oversized individual fields and combined question sets.
findings.failure_scenario: A waiting linked run has one 66,000-character unanswered question, or several questions whose combined body exceeds 65,536 characters. GitHub rejects every publication attempt; the questions never appear on the issue and the effect retries every poll.
